Subprocess probes run via execFileP/getTmuxPaneMapAsync/isProcessClaudeAsync/findTmuxTargetAsync (session-store; sync variants remain for boot paths), concurrent polls coalesce on ONE in-flight sweep (_sweepInFlight), and lock-entry ORDER is preserved through the parallel probe (claimJsonls' mtime fallback + firstRunning depend on it). Profiling knowledge that cracked it: a BLOCKED loop shows in a V8 CPU profile as a long SAME-NODE consecutive sample run (SIGPROF keeps delivering in interruptible waits), NOT a giant timeDelta — stall detectors must check both shapes.**
- **HOST-CAPABILITY PLUGINS (⚙ → Plugins, `src/plugins.js` + `src/lib/plugins-ui.js`)** — three built-ins with one shape (def + install + start/stop + status + boot replay from `enabled`+`desiredUp` in data/plugins.json, every change broadcast as `plugins-updated`): **Tailscale** (join a tailnet), **Public URLs (frp)** (publish a forwarded port through the shared relay), and since 2026-09-07 the **OpenCode background service**. The third one is the pattern for "a harness needs a background daemon": it is **OFF by default** (the owner's rule after the 2.369.42 runaway — VibeSpace never starts a third-party daemon on your machine until you say so), there is nothing to install (it runs YOUR `opencode` CLI) and nothing to configure (a free loopback port); Start/Stop and one "run it whenever VibeSpace runs" switch. `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0/1` remains an ops override and the card then says "forced by the environment" and disables the controls — and `=0` also STOPS a serve this instance inherited from a previous (SIGKILLed) server rather than adopting it, so the locked card never describes a daemon that is actually running. Disabling it STOPS the process — including one adopted from a previous server — and nothing respawns it. The keeper, its resource guard and every fact stay in the shared module (`src/opencode-serve.js`); the plugin is only the control surface.
- **Relay (frp) — one relay token PER INSTANCE (lane relay-token-per-instance, design q-051 — the owner's decision 2026-10-20: 「每实例独立 token、不进保险库」):** every instance logs in to OUR frps relay with its OWN token, bound to its OWN public names, revocable. PURE `src/relay-token.js` holds the model; the record is `data/relay-token.json` (0600, atomic, the old bytes overwritten — `src/secret-file.js` replaceShredding) and is NOT a vault entry: a restart re-publishes the public mirrors without the second password, and a stolen token reaches that one instance's public names only (impersonate its address, take its bandwidth), never the hub — the named exception row in `src/vault.js` SECRETS_AT_REST says so with the decision and its date. **Identity:** the first start (or boot replay / unlock) of a relay configured the shared way MINTS — and a frpc an older build started, which survives the hub upgrade detached, is restarted onto the identity once — `{instanceId 'vi-<12 hex>', label, token 'vsrt_'+base64url(32 B), prefixes ['pf-','vibespace-instance'], subdomains}`; frpc.toml gets `user = "<instanceId>"` + `metadatas.token = "{{ .Envs.VIBESPACE_RELAY_TOKEN }}"` (frp's env template — the value rides the frpc child's env only; never argv, never a log line, never the status JSON, never a For-you text). frpc's env is BUILT, never the hub's inherited (lane frp-spawn-env-allowlist): `RT.relayEnv` keeps PATH, LANG, TMPDIR and `http_proxy` (measured on frpc 0.70.0: it runs on an empty env, never reads HOME, and `http_proxy` is the one proxy name it dials through) plus the two relay variables — nothing else the hub holds (an agent conversation's session tokens, the cluster's `VIBESPACE_FRPS_TOKEN`, cloud keys) reaches it. A fleet pod mints nothing: the cluster injects `VIBESPACE_RELAY_CLUSTER_TOKEN` and the pod logs in as its own name (`VIBESPACE_INSTANCE_NAME`) — ONE cluster row at the relay binds the names by pod name (owner Q2). **The relay side** = `tools/frps-login-plugin/` (frps `[[httpPlugins]]` Login / NewProxy / CloseProxy): a registered token ⇒ in, `bad_token` / `revoked` otherwise; NewProxy re-checks the identity, the proxy name (without frps's `<user>.` prefix) must carry one of the row's prefixes (`name_not_yours`), a subdomain / custom domain is the FIRST claimer's for good (`name_in_use:<holder label>` for anyone else, a legacy login included); everything else fails closed (`table_unreadable`, `bad_request`, `unknown_op`). **The grace (owner Q1: 7 days, ends early after 24 h with no `legacy` audit line):** a login without `metas.token` — an older build — or with an id the table does not know yet is the shared token's KNOCK (frps checks its own `auth.token`), one `legacy` audit line per use; after it ⇒ `legacy_token_retired` / `unknown_instance`. The plugin's opt-in `--knock-file` VOUCHES a registered instance's login to frps (frp's privilege key for frps's own token) so it needs no shared token even during the grace; the file is re-read on change, so emptying it before `auth.token = ""` keeps registered logins working through the grace's end (q-052) (UNCONFIRMED against a real frps — the rollout's canary checks it). **The knock on the hub:** the shared token (the vault's `frp:token`, the plaintext override before a setup, or the cluster's `VIBESPACE_FRPS_TOKEN`) is still sent as frps's `auth.token` while it is readable; a LOCKED vault no longer stops the relay of an instance with its own token — frpc starts without the knock. The hub reads frpc's own log (≤ 16 KB tail, once a minute): a login that succeeded without the knock records `relayKnocklessAt` (the relay no longer asks); the relay refusing the knock (`token in login doesn't match…`) restarts frpc without it, at most once per 10 min. **Retirement (RETIRE_ID `2026-10-relay-token-per-instance`):** only after the instance's own token PUBLISHED (a proxy ran) AND a knockless login succeeded does the shared token leave the instance — the vault entry dropped at that moment when unlocked, else at the next unlock (the vault's open hook) — never before: the relay is never lost. Setting the shared token again re-arms the knock. **The card** (Plugins › Public URLs): a readout line (own token id · what the relay answered · the knock waiting for the vault) and the chip's sheet — the identity, its names, the registration line(s) with Copy (`relay-admin add <id> <sha256> <label>`; after a rotation also `relay-admin rotate …`; revoked: `relay-admin revoke <id>`), Mint / Rotate / Revoke… (a revoke keeps the id — owner Q3: the names follow it — forgets the token and stops frpc; start / publish are refused `relay_revoked`, never the shared token in its place) / 「The relay no longer asks the shared token」 / 「Send the shared token again」 (`config({ relay: op })`). **Alerts:** a publish the relay refused with `name_in_use:<holder>` / `name_not_yours` is ONE For-you item per name (origin plugin · frp — the plugin declares `reminders`; kind notice, urgency high): a leaked token or a cloned data/. Tests: test-relay-token + test-frps-plugin (fast), test-frp-plugin ① (the restart legs) + ①p (the hub launched from a planted, polluted env), test-vault-law ⑧, test-key-file-law RANDOM32. Rollout + relay-admin: tools/frps-login-plugin/README.md, deploy/frp/README.md.
- **PERMISSION RULES — the READ-ONLY "where does this rule come from" view (2026-09-07, owner ruling 10)**: Session Properties grows a "Permission rules" section (button "Show rules…", never auto-loaded — the codex rung asks the session's own agent, so a panel that re-fetched on every broadcast would re-ask on every broadcast; the tree you loaded then SURVIVES those broadcasts — the window keeps the record and repaints it, and the button says "Reload rules" — because Properties re-renders continuously while the session works and the answer you clicked for used to disappear within a second. Change the question underneath it — the session moves to another cwd — and the tree is dropped back to "Show rules…" rather than relabelled onto a different question), and Manage Agents grows a "Permission rules…" row (per named account, and a "Rules & checks" button on the machine's own CLI row). One tree per SOURCE: the layer's own name for itself, its FILE as a copy-path button (nothing else is clickable — there is no edit control anywhere in this feature and no write route behind it), a per-layer note, then its rules with `allow`/`deny`/`ask` badges in the harness's OWN words (untranslated: you must be able to grep your settings.json for what you saw). claude shows the documented hierarchy — managed (+ every `managed-settings.d/*.json` drop-in as its own source) / user / project / project-local — where a MISSING file, an UNPARSEABLE one ("the CLI ignores a settings file it cannot parse") and one with no `permissions` block are three different honest notes. codex shows `config/read`'s layers + origins, i.e. which layer WON each key, including the file-less `sessionFlags` layer (the `-c` overrides THIS session was spawned with — the reason the session-scoped read goes through the session's own agent), and only this session's own directory trust level (a real store had 378 origin keys, most of them other people's projects). A TABLE-valued key such as `sandbox_workspace_write` is attributed **per member**, because that is how codex keys it (measured on 0.153.4: the table itself is never in `origins`, its leaves are) — so `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access` set by this session's own `-c` flag shows up under "this session's own -c flags" while the rest of the table stays with the file that set it, instead of the whole table being reported as an unset packaged default. A key no layer set at all still says so; if the agent's answer had to be capped, the rules say "origin unknown — the answer was capped" rather than borrowing that sentence, and an answer too big even for that is refused out loud with its size. **codex answers only for a LIVE session**: an instance-wide codex read would need a fresh `codex app-server`, which was measured connecting to chatgpt.com even with no credentials, so Manage Agents shows a disabled row naming that measurement where the button would have been, and asking anyway returns a refusal that quotes it. OpenCode shows its resolved permission config with a note saying the serve reports NO per-key origin — the honest answer instead of a fabricated file attribution. Harnesses that cannot answer say why, with a typed reason: a shell session has no section at all, a REMOTE session says the rules live on that machine (every harness, including a live remote codex one — its agent runs over there and only that machine can vouch for what it can answer), a stopped codex session says a stopped session's rules are recorded nowhere, and a session whose agent predates the feature says "Terminate + Resume". ≤768px: one column, full-width copy-path tap target, no sideways scroll (measured at 375×667).
- **LOCAL ORACLES — human-triggered, zero-network CLI checks (2026-09-07, owner ruling 6)**: the same Manage Agents menu offers per-account read-only checks that run ONLY on your click (never on a timer, never at boot), under the sanitized spawn env with that account's own config dir, and show their output in a modal — typed JSON when the CLI offers a JSON flag, monospace text otherwise, always with both streams (`codex login status` answers on stderr). Shipping: **Login status**, **Configured MCP servers**, **Feature flags** (all codex). The three the design proposed — `claude auth status`, `claude agents --json`, `codex doctor --json` — were MEASURED and REJECTED (5 / 5 / 16 connections to vendor endpoints; the first still reaches api.anthropic.com with no credentials and with every traffic-suppressing env set), so claude's menu shows them as disabled rows carrying the reason rather than an empty menu. A fourth was caught the same way after it had already shipped: the codex instance-scope rule read spawned `codex app-server`, measured at 7 connections including chatgpt.com — that capability is now off, and codex's menu carries its disabled row too: "we measured these and they phone home" is a more useful fact than "there is nothing here". §ban-safety detail + the measurement method: kb-design-lessons §9.
- WS message dispatch is wrapped in try/catch (ws-handler handleMessage) — a malformed client message once crashed the whole server (array extraArgs hit .trim()); handler errors now log + reply an error instead of killing the process. extraArgs accepts string|array.


#### Day one lands on the person's files (lane door-day-one-landing, 2026-10-23 — two naive-user studies on fleet pods)
Day one asks ONE thing — what to work on — and lands in a chat on the folder that holds the person's files. Everything else waits until it is needed. The verdicts live in PURE `src/day-one.js`.
- **The welcome (tour step 0)** says what VibeSpace is for in one plain sentence, «An assistant that works on your files — ask it in plain words.», and shows three example asks. There are no theme or language chips (⚙ keeps both) and no feature pitch. The empty desktop's welcome (`#welcome`, public/index.html) says the same sentence.
- **«Protect this workspace» (step 2)** shows only where nothing protects the workspace yet (`tourSteps`). Where SSO or a sign-in password is already set (a provisioned pod), the step and its SSO sentence are gone: the person has just signed in. The tour's dots count the steps it will show.
- **The connect step (step 1)** stays. The owner's ruling: the Claude sign-in is per person and never skipped.
- **The start step (step 3)** «Start your first chat» shows the home's folders as chips, the one holding the most files first and CHOSEN («work (23 files)»), with the field filled with it. ONE primary «Start the chat» opens a chat there. A terminal is a link, and typing a folder still works.
- **The New Session dialog's folder field** is the caller's folder (a folder's «+», a Task Group) or EMPTY. It is never the folder the last dialog held, which belonged to another area. Its hint is words («Type a folder, or pick one below»), not a grey `/home/<user>`.
- **The chips** (`folderChips`, painted by `src/lib/folder-chips.js`), in order:
  - a Task Group's own folders (pinned, as before);
  - the home's folders WITH files, most first (≤ 4);
  - «Last used: …»;
  - the home's other folders;
  - the other recent folders (≤ 8 in all).

  The home's folders come from `GET /api/home-folders`: this machine only, a bounded count, a mount named but never walked, 10 s cache. A remote machine's chips stay its recent folders.
- **The vault's second password** is asked ONLY once a secret is stored. The hub's vault facts say `secretWaiting`: a store minted its first key file, a key file or a device link token sits beside the data, or a store was refused for want of a vault. The page asks at the broadcast where that turns true, with no reload, and saying why («A credential was just stored here — …»), or at a load while it holds. Day one stores nothing, so day one never asks. «Later» = 3 days on this device (localStorage `vs-vault-later`).
- **A sign-in terminal** (the tour's guided login, Manage Agents' Log in, an add-account login) carries `purpose: 'sign-in'`. It is a window the person sees, but no session row: the sidebar skips it, and the claude it runs is no discovered row.
- **A chat's window title** follows its first message once one exists (the card already did), instead of the generated «Session N».
- **Git's name and email** default from the Claude sign-in's account (`~/.claude.json` oauthAccount) at a local spawn. This happens only where git has no identity, and never over one (`src/server/git-identity.js`).
- **The left rail** carries each door's word under its icon (68 px) for the first week, or until every door was used once. The record is localStorage `vs-rail-labels`; the chrome suites preset it `done`.
### Terminal Management
- Multiple simultaneous sessions via dtach (survive server restarts)
- Attach to external tmux sessions (read/write, closing doesn't kill)
- Multi-device sync (output broadcast to all connected clients)
- Global settings (toolbar ⚙ / the phone's ⚙): the ⚙ menu TREE (2.369.124, docs/design-gear-menu-hierarchy.md; 2.369.131: All Settings… is a DIRECT row after Manage agents…, System monitor… / Ports… under System) — Appearance ▸ (theme, font size, font family, UI scale, UI font size, All Settings, Customize UI, Language ▸ with ✓ on the current choice; the head's caption shows `Dark · 14px · 100%` and follows a change made inside the panel at once — r2) · Manage agents… · Tools ▸ (Usage, Background Work, Desktop apps, Plugins, plugin windows) · Communication ▸ (For you, Channels, Outbox) · System ▸ (Report a problem, Diagnostics, Restore a previous layout, Backup & migrate, Integrations — keys beside the password since 2.369.266, under Communication before, Change password, System monitor, Ports) · Update VibeSpace… (direct, its vX → vY label is the update indicator) · Help ▸ (Welcome tour, All Settings) · Sign out. Desktop = a cascading flyout opening to the LEFT on 120 ms hover intent / click / Enter / ArrowLeft, arrow-key navigation with a roving tabindex, Esc closes one layer at a time; phones and hover-less pointers = an inline accordion, one head open per level, rows ≥ 44 px. A plugin row with `parent:'tools'|'comm'|'system'|'help'|'appearance'` lands in that head; without one it stays at the top level as before.
- **Diagnostics — an incident's errors name their line** (lane vault-chip-zone-errors, 2.369.339 — two errors reached inc-mvi50qdh-ygmh as «bundle.js?v=…:1», which names nothing in a one-line bundle): the console ring's `uncaught` / `unhandled` entries keep the error's first 3 frames (≤ 400 chars, the bundle's line:column, the origin cut — src/lib/incident-stack.js); `node scripts/symbolicate.mjs data/incidents/<id>/bundle.json` maps them to src/ file:line:col on the hub's checkout — the map is rebuilt in memory with the build script's own flags and refused unless byte-identical to the served bundle; no map file is ever kept, and express.static answers no `*.map` path (src/server/static-public.js). A full console ring is 224 KB of a capture, the hub takes 50 MB.
- **Diagnostics — Claude builds without a record table** (lane cli-2-1-308-records, 2.369.342): ⚙ Diagnostics report gains ONE section (src/lib/cli-registration-words.js `diagnosticsSection`, PURE, en/zh/ja) when the server saw a claude build this release has no record table for — a row per build: «claude <v> is not registered — records may show as new fields until the next release», where it was seen (the hub's claude / a conversation's records), and what to do (the draft's file + its changes against the newest pinned build; else Manage agents ▸ claude ▸ 「生成记录草稿」 / `node scripts/claude-cli-dump.mjs --auto` on the machine that runs it). Absent while every build is registered. Manage agents' claude row (this machine only) says the same line with the 「生成记录草稿」 button until the draft is taken (`hubRegistrationRow`), then the draft's words.
- ⚙ → Update VibeSpace… progress (`_runSelfUpdate`): pull/build log, "Restarting the service…" while the server is down, then (2.369.210, B-0ece) the reload waits for the new server's boot phase — `GET /api/boot` `ready` — with "VibeSpace is starting… (N sessions reconnected)"; the stale-tab auto-reload waits the same way. The boot splash waits for `ready` before it restores the layout, and its first-paint requests retry 1 → 2 → 5 → 10 s, then show the reason in words + Reload now (a `boot-stuck` telemetry event names the request; the server records its own after 90 s of a boot step not finishing).
- **Plugins = a list; their configuration = All Settings › Plugins (lane plugin-settings-p0, 2026-10-13 — the VS Code plugin model, docs/design-plugin-settings.zh.md):** the ⚙ → Plugins sidebar shows one row per plugin — name, one-line description, a status chip (已关闭 / 已连接 / 运行中 / 「N 条待处理」 — the LLM chip's tooltip says 「今天：判断了 n 条 · 命中 m 条」 and what was spent), the on/off switch, Install / Uninstall… (manifest plugins; Install for a built-in not yet downloaded) and ⚙ that opens the Settings window AT the plugin's section (desk: tree node + scroll; phone: that section alone until you search). Every configuration row of every plugin lives in that section — DERIVED from one PURE table per plugin (src/plugin-settings.js; manifest `contributes.settings[]` through the same validator), searchable ("threshold" / "阈值" / "Dropline"), values only in data/settings.json (`plugin.<id>.<key>`; the legacy `decision.threshold` / `decision.attentionBlock` keep their spelling and moved from Channels). A section ends with LINK rows: "On / off and status" → the Plugins list, "Key and provider" → Services › Integrations (keys never become settings), frp's relay token (a plugin-held secret, written to the plugin, never shown). The server reads rows through the host handle (h.setting / h.settings); a `plugin-config` row (frp relay fields, Tailscale mode) re-applies through the settings write hook (`applySettings`). Boot migration 2026-10-plugin-config-to-settings moved the old plugins.json `config` values once. The chip opens actions, never settings: Voice → Connect + the proposal cards; Tailscale 「Log in…」 → the sign-in link.
- **Tailscale never takes over the container's DNS (lane tailscale-plugin-pod-dns, 2026-10-19 — the owner's fleet pod lost github.com and its update when the plugin's kernel-mode tailscaled rewrote /etc/resolv.conf):** every `tailscale up` and every start of the plugin's daemon carries `--accept-dns=<verdict>` — false on a cluster instance, a cluster-managed resolv.conf and userspace networking; true only on a machine of your own in kernel mode with the new row **Let Tailscale set this machine's DNS (MagicDNS)** on (All Settings › Plugins › Tailscale, default off). A resolv.conf Tailscale already rewrote is healed at start / boot (`tailscale set --accept-dns=false`; tailscaled puts the saved resolver back), logged once. Tailnet names still reach ssh hosts: the hub answers `<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net` (or `<host>`) from the plugin's own `tailscale status --json` (ssh `HostName` + `HostKeyAlias`). The running Tailscale row says whose resolver is in use: 「DNS：集群解析器（Tailscale 名字经插件解析）」 / 「DNS：本机解析器（…）」 / 「DNS：Tailscale MagicDNS」.
- **A Settings row never squeezes its words (lane settings-multiline-row, owner 2026-10-14):** a row whose control holds a textarea (the json rows, 「我在乎什么」) STACKS — words on top, the box across the row, its buttons under it at the right; any other control that would leave the words < 40 % of the row wraps under them at the right (style.css flex-wrap + `min-width: 40%`, no container query); gates test-settings-view §11 + test-settings-row-layout (heavy, 600 / 760 / 1200 / phone).
- The Settings window (2.369.132): a TREE of five groups over the categories (Appearance & layout / Sessions & chat / Harnesses / Services / Spending; Plugins and Other trail by rule), foldable on desktop and flat on the phone; each harness section is three sub-blocks — Global (written into the CLI config file), Per session (passed to the CLI at spawn), VibeSpace (server-side) — from the rows' declared apply kind.
- Per-terminal overrides (window ⚙): theme, font size, font family — each with Default option
- Dynamic font list: Google Web Fonts + client local fonts (queryLocalFonts) + server fallback (fc-list)
- Bell notification: 🔔 icon on window title when terminal receives BEL while not focused, cleared on focus
- Pin-to-bottom: default on, scroll up freezes terminal (output queued), scroll back to bottom or click ↓ button flushes queued output
- Idle detection: OSC 0 title parsing — ✳ (U+2733) = idle, braille spinners = working. Window title bar + taskbar blink orange when Claude finishes and waits for input (cleared on focus)
- Clipboard image paste: Ctrl+V with image in clipboard → saves to temp file → sets server X clipboard via `cat | xclip` pipe → sends Ctrl+V (0x16) to PTY → Claude Code checks clipboard and reads image
- CJK support: Unicode 11 addon for correct fullwidth character width calculation + CJK monospace font fallback chain
- Multi-device sync: terminal size uses min(all clients), larger clients show padding. Editor open/close broadcasts to all clients with session targeting
- Ctrl+G external editor with split-pane CodeMirror (screen not cleared). Press Ctrl+G again to Save & Close. Auto-focuses editor on open.
- Minimum contrast ratio: auto-enabled at 4.5 (WCAG AA) for light terminal backgrounds, disabled for dark. Adjusts any RGB foreground color that doesn't meet threshold.
- **Phone key row (2.369.125, docs/design-mobile-gaps.md #10)**: a **Copy screen** key copies the visible terminal text (xterm has no touch selection) with a toast naming the line count; the row wraps to two lines so every key — incl. paste and ^C…^\ — sits inside a 390 px viewport at ≥ 36 px; icon keys are SVG (the 📋 emoji is gone).

- **A silent conversation is reconnected by itself (lane-dead-bridge, 2026-09-30).** A local session (chat or terminal) that has sent the server nothing for `session.deadBridgeMinutes` (Settings → Session, default 3, 0 = off) while its CLI demonstrably kept working — its wrapper's buffer file was written, or an OTel api_request row arrived for its conversation, after the last byte — is re-attached through the one local healer; at most 3 times an hour per session, and a re-attach that brought nothing doubles that session's wait. At every boot (1.5 s after the restore's attaches connected) the attach clients a crashed / killed previous server left attached to our sockets are ended (never a dtach master, never an attach whose parent is alive); a crash now ends the server's own attach clients like a clean shutdown does. Whatever a re-attach releases is counted through the late-record rule (records stamped > 2 min before they arrive never move the pool or the readings — lane-hot-switch) and, when the output was lost for a minute or more, ONE card from VibeSpace in the chat says: "The connection to this conversation's output was lost at HH:MM and restored at HH:MM — N records caught up (they are shown, not re-run)." The journal carries `[bridge] …` lines for every sweep, heal, catch-up and card. Essay: kb-file-structure.md (src/bridge-liveness.js + src/server/bridge-watch.js), kb-bugfix-invariants.md.

### Chat Mode
- **What this conversation asks of you is a card in its chat (lane chat-needs-you-card, .359; the owner 2026-10-26: «这个界面里是不是应该有个地方能让我看到需要approve？»):** every open For-you item the conversation filed or that addresses it — an agent's ask with its chips, a channel watch / access request, a machine's «ask me each time», a vault run / grant / paste, an app install, a browser takeover, the pool's cross-provider ask — stands inside the record that filed it (the tool card whose output names it, else the CLI call before it, else the record at the filing), drawn by the For-you row with the tray's own verbs; answered anywhere (the tray, a phone, another page) it becomes the one line «✓ approved · 2 min ago — …»; the status bar's «waiting for you · N» names what waits and lands the newest card (a ≥ 24 px chip, 44 on touch; it counts the cards drawn — the chip and the cards change together). Several waiting: ONE card is open — the newest, or the one the person opened — and the others fold to one line (the question · its age; on a touch screen the sheet's 44 px row); a tap / click / Enter opens one in place and folds the other. S1's helper asks, the permission card and the proposal / API / wall cards keep their own cards (never drawn twice); a job's ask keeps its form. After a filing the agent says «Filed for you: … — answer it on the card in this conversation or in the For-you tray (<id>)».
- **What you typed is what the bubble shows (lane phone-refusal-wrap, .355; the naive-user walk's P2-15):** your own message keeps its line breaks — «a⏎b⏎c» is three lines in the bubble, as it was in the box (CSS pre-wrap on the user's own paragraph — never `<br>` nodes (the AX budget: a `<br>` per line is 4 accessibility nodes, pre-wrap's newline 2; the first cut's marked `breaks: true` was redone in lane ci-355-red); For-you words in their own window keep marked `breaks`); the AGENT's markdown keeps the markdown convention (a single newline is a space — a model wraps prose at will). Both through the one sanitizer.
- **A status-bar panel fits the screen (lane phone-refusal-wrap, .355; P2-17):** every panel a status-bar chip opens (the model picker, effort, health, tasks…) is bounded by the room above its chip — under the window's top and the phone's top bar — and scrolls inside (chat-status-bar.js dropdownRoom → `--dd-room`). At 385×571 and 594×368 the current model, Effort and the model lock are reachable; before, the 621 px picker rose above the top bar with no scroll.
- **可用工具 — the harness's own tool switch at New Session (lane new-session-form, .346):** the row exists only where `capsOf(backend).toolAllowlist` declares one. Claude: a chip per tool cycles default → ✓ (`--allowedTools`) → ✗ (`--disallowedTools`) → default; Bash never takes ✗ (deny beats allow in Claude Code — it would block the `Bash(vibespace-…:*)` allow rules every reporting CLI rides; the chip says so and the PURE `toolAllowlistArgs` drops a forged one). Codex: sandbox + approval over the permission mode's own default (the chat wrapper's `CODEX_WEBUI_TOOLS_PICK`; a machine without codex-linux-sandbox keeps its forced danger-full-access). The pick is meta `toolPick` and the conversation's own config `tools` (latched when its id exists), so a resume / an inbox reopen re-passes it; a live permission change re-resolves from the mode.
- **The status bar shows what the conversation's harness REPORTS, per declared row (lane agy-status-bar-facts, .342; the owner 2026-10-21: «agy 的 chatview 缺少很多信息啊 什么 context 啊，cache rate，产物啊啥的下面都没有了»):** each chat descriptor declares `ui.statusBar` (src/status-bar-facts.js) — context (the window `reported` by the stream, or a per-model `table`), cache hit rate, odometer (the conversation's token total + the thinking share, Σ), model, the turn's time. claude: context / ⚡ / model; codex: + Σ; opencode: context / model (ACP has no cache field — the old ⚡0% is gone); antigravity: all five, the context % against the model's DOCUMENTED window (the descriptor's table; a slug not in it ⇒ «window unknown» with the token count). What a harness lacks is ONE dim «not reported» chip naming it (claude: token total, turn time) — never a blank. The bar gates on the row, never an id.
- **The effort menu is the harness's own (lane effort-menu-per-harness, .338; the owner 2026-10-21: «antigravity 也是这几个档位吗？»):** the status bar's effort chip, its menu and the New Session dialog's effort row offer the levels THIS conversation's CLI takes. `GET /api/session-options?backend=<id>` answers each harness its declared `ui.effortLevels` (antigravity: agy --effort's low|medium|high|xhigh|max; claude: the CLI's parsed levels; codex: the model catalog) and its OWN `ui.effortExtras` (claude's ultracode never reaches another backend). A harness with `effortLevels: null` (opencode) has no effort chip, row or menu. A level the CLI does not take is refused by name (`effort_not_supported` with the levels, on a create and on a mid-session pick), never dropped. The chip's title says which fact it shows: per turn (codex), as last commanded (claude), or as asked at start (antigravity, whose CLI reports none). «?» appears only when nothing was asked, and its title says the CLI's own default applies.
- **A direct vendor read says so on its card (lane bypass-witness-hint, owner 2026-10-13: "这个怎么没显示成读取过 channel 的卡片？"):** a shell call that reads Lark / Slack / Gmail / Microsoft 365 with the agent's OWN client (a vendor host, SDK or CLI in the command text, heredoc bodies included — PURE `vendorBypassOf` in src/agent-tool-rules.js, a censused table) has no witness box, so the card carries ONE muted line instead: this read bypassed VibeSpace's channels — no channel card, read marker or budget record — and `vibespace-channels read` would have them. Display only; nothing is blocked. There is no owner-facing channels how-to page (the manual is the agents' JSON at /api/agent/docs/channels), so the line names the door instead of linking. The channel digest's read line (src/channel-filter.js, the injection that teaches `vibespace-channels read`) also says: never your own SDK or script — no card, read marker or budget. (Not the drain's reply hint in agent-routes: test-stash-strip's r5 byte-identity and tail sweep are calibrated to its exact bytes.)
- **A card shows an expander only where there is something to open (lane ci-351-reds, the owner 2026-10-24: 「这俩为啥无法展开」):** a tool card's ▸ belongs to a `<details class="chat-diff">` — the caret (and its hover tint) is `.chat-diff > .chat-diff-summary` in public/chat.css, never every `.chat-diff-summary`. So a summary-only result is a static line: an Antigravity read answers «N lines, M bytes» (never the file's text) and its card says «✓ N lines · size» under the clickable path — no ▸, nothing toggles; the «Stopped before it finished» / «Terminated with the subagent» lines likewise. A claude Read keeps its fold (▸ → ▾, the file's text). Chrome leg: test-agy-status-bar-chrome ④ (real clicks; RED control = the old caret rule).
- **Deliverables: the files the agent writes for you are cards and an Artifacts list (lane artifacts-model):** derived from the harness's own write record (claude Write / Edit, codex apply_patch, an ACP diff — never a tool the agent must learn), ONE card per file in the chat, born at the first write and patched in place on every later change ("BRIEF.md · Changed 3 times · 2min ago"); one click opens it beside the chat. An **Artifacts · N** chip in the status bar lists documents first, code folded behind "Code (n)". A new document the agent writes opens beside the chat by itself (setting `artifacts.autoOpenDocs`, on). Your own save in an editor opened from the chat counts on the row and the agent hears one "[Doc edit] <path>: +a −b lines" note on its next turn. Survives restarts and rebuilds. docs/design-artifacts.zh.md ⇒ kb-file-structure "src/artifacts.js".
- **The automatic open is QUIET (lane artifacts-auto-open-quiet, owner 2026-10-08):** a doc the agent wrote opens beside the chat WITHOUT the focused window, the caret or the keyboard owner — `app.openFile(…, {quiet:true})` → openDoc / FileViewer → `createWindow({quiet})` (a split shown beside the chat with the chat's pane still active; a chain already split or the tab placement ⇒ a pulsing tab; a free window not focused). `_onArtifactCard` is the ONLY quiet caller; a user's own open (card, chip row, Artifacts window) focuses as before. The phone (≤768 px) opens nothing — the card + the chip only (a minimize there is the synced truth). The switch `artifacts.autoOpenDocs` (key + default unchanged) is in Settings → Chat AND the Artifacts chip's popover ("Open new documents automatically"); the first quiet open on a device shows ONE toast "… · Turn off" (localStorage `vs-auto-open-taught`). PURE verdicts: src/lib/artifact-auto-open.js; suites: test-artifacts-auto-open (fast), test-artifacts-chrome ① ③ ⑨ (heavy).
- **Artifacts: a helper's deliverables (lane artifacts-handover, .224):** a Task / workflow agent's writes (its sidechain transcript) are the PARENT's rows with "By subagent <name>", born at the Task's end, the same at a rebuild; another conversation hands its own artifacts over with `vibespace-msg send <agent> "…" --artifact <path>` (≤ 20, the message's reach, same machine — never copied): the receiver's chat card says "Handed over by <helper>" (移交自), its chip counts it, the helper's row says "Handed to …"; a handed-over design opens in the user's Design window and its home lists it "via <helper>" (`vibespace-design open --for <conversation>` = the same door).
- **Artifacts: Services — a site or service the conversation runs (lane artifacts-services):** a Background Work job the conversation owns that listens on a TCP port is a row under its own "Services" head (after the documents) with its link (http://<the instance's host>:<port>/); its card is born at the first listen and patched in place (a moved port, stopped); a click opens the Web view, ⋯ = copy URL / open in a new tab / show the job; a stopped job's row stays 24 h greyed ("stopped at …"), then goes. Derived from the jobs engine at every read — the agent declares nothing.
- **Artifacts: Services — the link (lane artifacts-services-url, .225):** a service row links where the user can REACH it: the port's PUBLISHED forward (Ports panel → its public URL, "Published" / 已发布) else through this VibeSpace's own proxy (`/proxy/http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`, "Through this VibeSpace" / 经本实例代理; the Web view opens it in proxy mode) — never the instance's host with the raw port; the url prints LTR, end-truncated. ⋯ adds Show in Ports (publish from there) and Copy the machine-local address. A publish / unpublish patches the card in place.
- **A machine's commands fold into one line; a PowerShell -EncodedCommand reads as its script (lane machine-card-fold, 2026-10-04):** consecutive "Machines · <machine>" cards of the SAME machine (vibespace-exit run / pull / push) fold with the run they sit in (the Bash fold toggle) under ONE head — "WIN-DESK1 · 6 commands · 2 files · last: exit 0 · 19:39–19:42" (zh/ja too; the time span has its own span, so a 390 px head cuts the counts, never the time); another machine's card starts a new fold; a FAILED card (non-zero exit, timeout, refusal, a copy that did not land) stays on screen and turns the head red with "N failed". A `powershell … -EncodedCommand <base64>` line is shown as the decoded script on the card (head "PowerShell: <first line>"), in the machine's Commands… list, in `vibespace-exit runs` and in the "ask me each time" approval; the raw line is behind "Show full command". Inside an open fold of ≥ 2 such cards each call is ONE line (lane machine-card-compact, the owner: "如果整体已经显示了是win-desk1 每个指令没必要都展示吧") — the command ("PowerShell: <first line>", or "pulled <there> → <here>") and its outcome ("exit 0 · 1.4 s"), no header and no machine name — the open group is ONE framed list (thin dividers between rows, ~40 px rows on a phone, ~30 px on a desktop); a click or Enter on the line opens THAT call's script, "Show full command" and output in place (the per-message fold state); a failed call stays on screen as its line in red with its first error line; a lone Machines card (a run of one, another machine between) stays the full card. A script that cannot be decoded, or that carries direction controls / invisible characters, is refused at the door like a plain command.
- **A `vibespace-exit` call is a machine card in history too (lane exit-calls-in-history, 2026-10-04):** after a reload / page-in / resume the agent's `vibespace-exit run / push / pull` Bash calls draw as the same Machines card the live chat showed (the words, the command, the output heads), fold per machine with the compact rows, and `list` / `runs` / `use` / `url` are one-line lookups with their output behind a click (URL secrets cut); live, the card upgrades the agent's own Bash card in place — one card per call. A line it cannot prove (an expansion, a pipe, a second command, an output whose last line is not the CLI's) stays a Bash card.
- **Messages from other agents and jobs arrive folded (lane peer-card-fold, 2026-10-02):** a peer card longer than one line (or 160 characters) shows its head + ONE preview line (markdown markers gone) + Show; Show opens it in place (headings as bold text, never page headings); the open state is per window by message id and survives patches, folds, rebuilds and trims; `chat.foldPeerMessages` (default on) turns it off. Gate test-peer-card-fold (+ -ui heavy).

- **A helper's permission request is a card you can answer (lane S1, B-6e95 — both naive-user studies' T9: "帮手要权限时没有任何地方能点'允许'").** A helper (sub-agent) runs in the parent's process and asks on the parent's stream (`can_use_tool` with the helper's `agent_id`, measured on 2.1.281). The ask is a permission card INSIDE that helper's Agent card in the parent chat — "Helper “<description>” needs your approval" + what it wants (the url / command / file) + the same Allow / Always Allow / Deny (lane L's words and widened rules) — and the SAME request sits on the helper's tool card in its View Log, which opens LIVE while the helper runs; answering in either window answers the parent's stdin with the helper's request id and settles both. The "waiting for you" chip names who waits and a click scrolls to the card and flashes it (paging it in from anywhere in the conversation); it also stands on a waiting ask after a server restart. An ask unanswered for 60 s is filed in For you (origin Agents; a click lands on the card; it clears itself when the ask is answered or withdrawn). A helper stopped while waiting reads "No longer waiting — the helper was stopped", its card's chip "stopped" (never "⟳ running"), and a helper stopped mid-run keeps its title and says "Stopped before it finished". A card holding a waiting ask never folds. Pending asks survive a restart (the rebuild + the task replay); a withdrawn one stays withdrawn. src/helper-ask.js (PURE) · src/server/helper-asks.js (inbox, routing) · docs/kb-bugfix-invariants.md.
- **Bypass answers the CLI's own checks (lane bypass-no-prompts, owner 2026-10-10).** In a conversation whose mode is `bypassPermissions` no permission card ever forms: the CLI's own safety-check asks (measured 2.1.288: "This shell -c script runs rm and could not be checked", `safetyCheck`, not classifier-approvable, not stopped by a PreToolUse allow) and any other `can_use_tool` — a helper's, the WebFetch provenance re-ask — are answered ALLOW at once with the exact input, and the chat shows a quiet line "Auto-allowed (bypass): Bash — <the command's first 120 chars>" (a warning if the CLI then refused it). Session Properties counts them; the server console ring (the incident bundle) carries each. AskUserQuestion is never answered. Setting `permissions.bypassAnswersAsks` (default ON; OFF = the card). Never in any other mode — the mode is read per ask. src/server/bypass-auto-allow.js · test-bypass-auto-allow.
- **What VibeSpace says to the ASSISTANT is not conversation, and VibeSpace speaking is never "another agent" (lane S3, naive-user study 2, 2026-09-26).** The Stop hook's bookkeeping nudge, the session-start tools intro, the per-turn reminder and codex's nudge turn render as ONE grey line each ("VibeSpace reminded the assistant to update its status"; the text behind the expander), fold under the 'note' kind of Settings → Chat → Card kinds that collapse (on by default — the nudge folds with the vibespace-status call it asked for), and Settings → Chat → "Show VibeSpace notes to the assistant" off hides them entirely (the assistant still receives them). The nudge itself asks for the bookkeeping calls only: "do not restate your answer; end with at most one short line". A helper's launch ack reads "Helper started: <task>", a Stop task result "Stopped: <task>" (raw record behind the expander). A browser handback, a Background Work event, a channel wake or VibeSpace's own auto-resume / usage-limit card is a card titled "VibeSpace · <what happened>" ("VibeSpace · you handed control back after 17 s — the page is now …"; the words the assistant was given folded under "What the assistant was told"), and the words the assistant receives open with "VibeSpace (this workspace, not another agent) reports:". Which card is a notice is decided by the PATH the message took (S3 verify F3) — never its first sentence or its sender's name: a real agent's message that opens with that sentence keeps its "Message from “name”" card, and an agent or session named "VibeSpace" / "Background Work · …" (any case or spacing) reads "Message from an agent calling itself “VibeSpace”"; a held message drains to the assistant as `from "<name>":` unless VibeSpace sent it. A new For-you item pops "Added to For you (bottom right)" — the corner measured off this device's button — and the assistant is taught to name it — since lane agent-context-owner-facts (B-7960 b, 2026-10-20) by its LABEL in the owner's language and its CURRENT place, both DERIVED (src/tray-words.js trayWords over `chrome.arrangement` / `taskbar.position` / `chrome.zoneAlign` / `taskbar.showUserTodos` + the owner's last page in user-state `ownerPage {lang, phone}`, bound by src/server/owner-facts.js): «the “待你处理” (For you) tray at the top right», never a literal place, never "your inbox"; the SessionStart paragraph, the reminder, the session intro, the stop nudge, vibespace-ask's answer (`tray`), vibespace-app's answers and vibespace-vault's locked line all say the hub's words. (src/lib/chat-run-summary.js, src/notification-senders.js, src/server/conversation-deliver.js; gates test-chat-hygiene + test-chat-hygiene-ui.)
- **The CLI's "Stop hook error" notice is hidden by default (2.369.127).** A Stop-hook BLOCK (VibeSpace's own bookkeeping nudge included) makes the CLI post `system/notification` key `stop-hook-error` on the live stream; `chat.showStopHookErrorNotice` (Settings → Chat, default off) hides that card — the "Stop hook feedback" and hook summary cards stay — and the server never toasts it when the nudge itself just fired. On: a red immediate notice. It is also a hook card, so "Show hook cards" off hides it too.
- **Unknown harness records, whole (docs/design-unknown-records.md, 2026-09-21 — owner rulings (a) the fall-back card 2.369.120 + (b) "known types with unknown parameters must be recorded and flagged").** ① THE SCHEMA ORACLE: `src/record-shape.js` declares every known record shape per harness AND carrier (claude stream rows verbatim from the installed binary's zod union, transcript camelCase twins, codex rollout payloads/events/items); both normalizers judge every record AFTER routing. THE CARD IS THE UPDATE SIGNAL (owner 2026-10-15 「那个红色是有理由的啊，就是为了知道什么时候有更新啊」 — lane drift-card-restore reverted .276's hiding): a known record that GREW a field draws ONE "New fields on a known record — Claude Code 2.1.297 · system/init +{…}" card per shape per session (red border, dim head, merged on new fields or values, the CLI build the init frame named, one line saying the CLI may have updated and that registering the new version ends these notices, the redacted sample behind "Full record", folds under the 'unknown' kind — off by default, so it stays in the flow); an undeclared enum VALUE is the same card headed "An undeclared value on a known record". Every grown field is ALSO a row of the drift ledger (per conversation + shape: fields, CLI build, count, the latest redacted sample), listed by ⚙ Diagnostics "Records that grew a field". When such cards show up in every chat, the cure is pinning the new build (below) — never hiding the card. Telemetry `harness-shape-drift` once per process per shape (Diagnostics "Harness drift" table). The oracle is pinned per CLI build (2.1.281 · 2.1.288 · 2.1.296 · 2.1.306 · 2.1.307 · 2.1.308, one tracked dump each — 2.1.308 is 2.1.307's code rebuilt on a newer Bun runtime, its dump equal to 2.1.307's, nothing declared; a build the hub has not installed is dumped from the npm package's linux-x64 binary in a scratch prefix — never on PATH, never run as a session — lane cli-2-1-306-records; a build the hub HAS installed is read with strings over a 0644 copy — lane cli-2-1-307-records). Since 2.1.307 the dump also reads ONE LEVEL DOWN (`nested`: the seven objects the shapes judge inside a record — rate_limit_info, compact_metadata, …): the flat union never saw a field added inside one, so rate_limit_info.overageEnabled (2.1.296) drew a red card on every rate-limited chat until lane cli-2-1-307-records declared it. The three fields the product already depends on (init.messaging_socket_path / task_started.owned_by_subagent / task_progress.workflow_progress) are declared with a note and never flagged. scripts/test-record-shape.mjs re-reads the INSTALLED claude's union every run — the day the CLI adds a subtype, a type or a field, the build goes red with the name printed. ② `system/notification` (the REPL's own queue: stop-hook-error, fast-mode-overage-rejected, model-deny) = a dim priority-coloured notice card, keyed dedupe per turn; `immediate`/`high` ALSO toast every client through server-notice (one implementation in session-brain for the parse and the device feed). ③ codex `item_completed` McpToolCall = the MCP tool card ("tool (server)", fold kind mcp, result as output, failed = error) — no more red card per MCP call; the wrapper's `_stdin_ack` is skipped. ④ History-only rows: `local_command` → the /command bubble; `away_summary` → the "Recap — while you were away" card (markdown through DOMPurify); `turn_duration` → the message-meta popup's "Turn: 3m18s · 66 messages [· budget n/limit]" row on the turn's last message; `api_error` → declared card-less (the transcript rows are NOT consumed — a days-old 401 must not evict today's pool member; the live-feed consumer for 401/403 is forward-compat for a stream record the census never observed, r3 2026-09-21); `microcompact_boundary` → declared card-less. ⑤ Chrome signals: `vcs_state_changed` → the session card's git chip ("push · fix/x"), a `session-vcs` push that re-lists every open File Explorer rooted in that cwd, and a "git push" row in the Session Properties timeline — card-less; `code_change_published` (+ the transcript's `pr-link` row, the same fact) → ONE small "PR #608 pushed" card with an escaped, never-auto-opened link + PR chips on the session card (session meta `prLinks[]`, restart-safe); `background_tasks_changed` (the full live set of BACKGROUND tasks) → the status bar's "N background tasks" chip and the reconcile that SOFT-closes a backgrounded task card the set no longer names (`finished`, outcome not reported — drawn neutral; a foreground Bash is never closed by it, and the real outcome record that follows overwrites it — r3 2026-09-21); `task_updated {patch:{status:failed}}` closes the task card at once (overriding a level-set soft close). Invariants: a routed name never renders the red card again (test-unknown-records pins the three lists exactly); a field is never deleted from known, only moved to ignored with a reason; an unknown TYPE is the fall-back card only, never doubled as drift; every harness string is escaped and no url is fetched or auto-opened.
- **A claude build the release does not know, said ONCE + its record draft (lane cli-2-1-308-records, 2.369.342 — THE TREADMILL, built: the hub's claude auto-updated 2.1.296 → 2.1.307 → 2.1.308 in ten days):** src/server/cli-registration.js. A version not in SCHEMA_CLI_VERSIONS, seen as the hub's CLI (oat-file-sync's --version tick: boot + 20 s, every 15 min — `onCliVersion`) or on a conversation's drift card (`global.__vsCliSeen` in message-manager `_noteDrift`), is said ONCE per build: one journal line «[cli-registration] claude <v> is not registered — records may show as new fields until the next release …» + one `cli-unknown-version` telemetry event, the build kept in data/cli-registration.json (a restart does not repeat it; a release that registers it drops it). `GET /api/cli-registration` = {newest, hub, unregistered[{version, sources, firstSeen, draft}]}. **The record draft** (`POST /api/cli-registration/draft`, human-triggered, one at a time): `process.execPath scripts/claude-cli-dump.mjs --auto --data data --bin <the hub's claude>` on serviceEnv, 120 s bound — strings over the INSTALLED binary, NEVER run (the version is the versions-dir name or the bundle's own `VERSION:"x.y.z"` stamp), written to data/claude-cli-dumps/<v>.json = the recipe's dump + `draft` {takenAt, against, diff: newKeys / fields / nested / sentences, changes}; a draft already taken is kept. It never registers anything (that stays a reviewed commit). test-cli-registration.
- **Session-start card + a live command list (§2.6 of docs/design-harness-features.md, 2026-09-07)**: the claude `system`/`init` frame is kept WHOLE, and four things follow.
  - **A dead MCP server is no longer invisible.** The init card (previously rendered as nothing at all) is one collapsed line — "Session start · N skills · output style: X" — and, when the frame reports trouble, an always-visible health strip in warning colour: every MCP server whose status is not `connected` (statuses are shown verbatim: `failed`, `needs-auth`, …), every `--mcp-config` entry the CLI skipped, and every demoted plugin. Expanding lists skills, plugins (with versions), MCP servers, sub-agents, tool count, output style and the CLI version + betas. The card never claims the opposite ("all healthy"): upstream omits the error keys entirely on some lanes, so an absent key is not evidence of a clean load.
    **How often it appears, measured (round 2, a round-1 claim corrected).** A conversation carries one init record per spawn — every resume, every server restart, every wrapper respawn. Measured on this instance's own `data/session-buffers`, which are a ROTATING window (so these are snapshots, independently reproduced by the reviewer): at 2026-09-07 05:34, **62** init records in 13 conversations, **62 of them carrying a health issue**, and **33 byte-identical ones in a single conversation**; a re-measure at 05:40, after the ring buffers had rotated, gave 30 records / 14 distinct frames / 30 with issues / 6 max. Both agree on the shape — 2×–33× redundancy at a 100% warned rate — so round 1's "one quiet line" was in fact up to 33 warned lines in a single rebuilt history. The card therefore renders **once per DISTINCT frame**: an init whose frame equals the previous init's is marked a repeat and draws nothing, while its side effects (model, permission mode, command list, memory dirs) still apply. A frame that CHANGED always draws — a server that went `connected` → `failed`, a skill discovered mid-session, a CLI upgrade.
    **Who renders nothing.** Producers whose init record carries no frame at all: codex and OpenCode/ACP, whose normalizers build `{model, permissionMode, slashCommands}` only. NOT "old claude CLIs" — in the CLI's own zod schema `tools` / `mcp_servers` / `skills` / `plugins` / `output_style` / `claude_code_version` are REQUIRED (verified on 2.1.238, 2.1.239 and 2.1.257), so every claude session gets a card and the gate must never be described as a version test.
  - **Terminal-bound slash commands are gone from the chat composer.** The frame's `terminal_slash_commands` is upstream's own "subset whose UX is bound to the local terminal … Phone/remote UIs should hide these"; `/doctor` and `/color` used to sit in the completion and do nothing when picked.
  - **The command list follows the session.** A mid-session `commands_changed` push (e.g. skills discovered as the agent works in a subdirectory) REPLACES the completion list — a command that disappeared upstream disappears here — live and on the next attach alike. Same behaviour for OpenCode/ACP's `available_commands_update` and codex's wrapper-served list: one path, no local/remote twin. **The newest frame wins, and that is an ORDERING rule (round 3)**: a conversation re-inits on every resume / wrapper respawn, so a push followed by a later `init` is ordinary — the window that attaches after the restart shows the list the NEWEST init declared, not the pre-restart push, exactly like the window that watched it happen. (An init that names no list at all does not erase the push before it — an absent list is not an empty one.)
  - **Agent-memory cards follow the CLI's own directories.** Read/Write/Edit on the dirs the frame names (`memory_paths{auto,team}`) render as memory operations; the built-in path patterns remain the fallback for older CLIs and other backends. A custom memory directory used to render as an ordinary Write on a long dotfile path. The dirs are learned from the attach payload BEFORE the history slab is rendered (round 2): the attach tail almost never contains the init card, and a rendered card is not re-rendered on a later status change, so learning them after the render loop left every memory card in that window misclassified for its whole life.
- **Review / rename-writeback / fork-from-here are capability-gated (§2.13)**: the Review chip and its detached-review poll, the codex thread-name writeback **and the sidebar rename that triggers it**, and the per-message "fork from here" button **and its click handler** (BOTH HALVES of every one of them — a control drawn on caps whose action still gates on a backend id is a dead control, and an action ready on caps whose trigger still gates on an id never fires) all read `backend-caps` rows (`review`, `renameWriteback`, `forkAtMessage`) instead of a backend id; a click that cannot proceed because the session id is not known yet says so in a toast. `forkAtMessage` is deliberately separate from `fork`: claude can branch from ONE message (`--resume-session-at <uuid> --fork-session`), codex's `thread/fork` branches the whole thread — so the per-message button appears only where it can actually work.
- **Codex sub-agent chatter is ATTRIBUTED (B-7473, 2026-09-06 owner report "根本没区分出这是subagent消息")**: in codex 0.153 multi-agent v2 a root conversation is mostly ORCHESTRATION — spawns, encrypted inter-agent mail, lifecycle events, and the children's reports. VibeSpace renders it in two shapes, never as the root agent's own reply:
  - **Sub-agent report card** — an inbound PLAINTEXT payload (in practice the children's `FINAL_ANSWER`s): the markdown body rendered exactly like assistant text (DOMPurify), under a "water_research · FINAL_ANSWER" head with a tinted left strip and a "sub-agent report" tag.
  - **Compact collab rows** — encrypted inbound mail, outbound `send_message`/`followup_task`, `spawn_agent`, `wait`, and started/interacted/completed lifecycle, one line each with an SVG direction icon; CONSECUTIVE rows coalesce into one message ("3 messages · water_research (FINAL_ANSWER), energy_research (MESSAGE)"). The hover title carries the envelope and says *payload encrypted upstream* when the body was withheld — an encrypted blob never reaches a rendered string.
  **Fold kinds (B-7473 integration 2026-09-06): the ROWS are `collapseKind:'agent'` (orchestration noise, in the default `chat.collapseKinds`), a REPORT is `collapseKind:'report'` and is NOT in the default set** — a child's written answer is the content the owner opened the window to read, and folding it by default hid it behind a one-line summary. 'report' is offered in the settings list so a user who wants the quiet view can tick it (then the header adds "N sub-agent reports"). A fold header reads "N sub-agent messages · N agent ops" and lists "N sub-agents: water_research, interior_research" — **the agent NAME is clickable everywhere it appears** and opens that child's rollout read-only in the existing sub-agent viewer. 0.153.4 puts `agent_thread_id` on every SubAgentActivity item, so the click needs no server call; older rollouts fall back to `GET /api/subagents?backend=codex&threadId=<root>` (the local session tree's `source.subagent.thread_spawn`), and a remote conversation's children are honestly reported as "not on this machine" (toast) instead of a silent nothing. Live and rebuilt views agree: the wrapper's live twin and codex's rollout twin of one message dedupe by id, else by (author, payload) within the turn — **and that content leg only fires when there IS content (B-7473 integration 2026-09-06): an encrypted message has body '' and msgType MESSAGE for every message, so the (turn, author, type, body) key collapsed every message an agent sent in a turn into one (101 of 140 when the verifier measured, 120 of 168 on a re-measure of the same still-growing rollout — all with distinct ids and distinct blobs, so the id leg never fired). Encrypted mail dedupes by id, with the fernet blob's first 32 chars as the content discriminator.** **One agent = one identity (round-5):** codex names a child BARE in the outbound call arguments and absolutely everywhere else, so before the fix the same sub-agent appeared as two chips, the "N sub-agents" count over-reported, and an outbound row had no thread id and so no click-through (measured on the owner's real rollout: 36 identities for 20 children, 98 of 409 rows unclickable → 20 / 20 / 408 of 409 after). **And a child's errors are all shown:** a repeated `errored` used to collapse into the first one, so a later, differently worded failure vanished — errors now dedupe on their own message.
  **Sub-agent lifecycle is ONE row shape, never a card (B-7473 integration 2026-09-06):** started/interacted/completed/interrupted are collab ACTIVITY rows (the old standalone "Sub-agent" tool card is retired), and a lifecycle record whose own id IS the tool call that caused it (0.153.4: started → `spawn_agent` 18/18, interacted → `send_message`/`followup_task` 214/214) draws NO second row — the call's own row already said it — while still teaching the agentPath → thread-id map the click-through uses. A terminal record synthesises `subagent-completed-<uuid>`, twins nothing, and always draws its row.
  **A CHILD's failure is the child's (B-7473 integration 2026-09-06):** the app-server relays an `error` notification for every thread it hosts and `ErrorNotification` carries `threadId`, so a sub-agent's error used to surface as the ROOT conversation's failed turn + error card. It is now a collab activity row ("water_research errored", the message on hover). The wrapper's thread gate is INVERTED — any notification NAMING another thread is foreign unless allowlisted, instead of a method whitelist that goes stale.
  **LIVE PROGRESS ON A CONTINUOUS BURST (2026-09-07, owner: “这种互聊如果连续发生是不是应该界面里展示下连续数量，这样我好知道对话没卡住”):** dozens of encrypted one-line rows over minutes, with no assistant text between them, look exactly like a wedged turn. Three surfaces now say otherwise, all derived from the rows themselves (nothing stored, nothing counted server-side): the coalesced card's HEAD (“Sub-agent traffic · 47 messages · 3 agents · last 4s ago”), the RUN HEADER / floating run bar / run footer (“… · 3 sub-agents · 47 messages · last 4s ago” — the surface a reader with the run folded actually sees), and the SPINNER line (“Sub-agents working — 47 messages **this turn**, last 4s ago”, which yields back to the server's own activity label the moment any other record lands, and returns when collab traffic resumes). The three are three SCOPES of the same traffic — the card head counts that card, the run header that run, the spinner the whole turn — so they can show different numbers at the same instant; the spinner is the one that floats free of what it counts, so it is the one that says “this turn”. The age TICKS at 1s granularity under a minute then whole minutes, from ONE interval per chat window that no-ops while the window is hidden; a lifecycle event (started/interacted/completed) counts like a message, encrypted and plaintext count alike, and the normalizer's dedup twins (an id re-read, a repeated (thread,kind) lifecycle) are never counted twice. When the turn ends — or the card stops growing because something else arrived — every age FREEZES to the absolute span (“over 4 min 12 s”), and a reload / read-only view shows those frozen totals with nothing ticking. Each row's hover title now leads with its time and says whether that clock is the ROLLOUT RECORD's own timestamp or the moment VibeSpace saw the line. Two properties the readout must never cost you: the **Stop button is untouched by the ticking** (the label is a text node of its own, so the button never blinks out from under a click and keyboard focus on it survives — an interrupt swallowed by a rebuilt button would be a silent failure), and a burst that starts and ends **while the window is on another desktop** still shows its frozen span when you come back, never a “last 0s ago” on a turn that finished minutes ago.
- **Design window (lane design-window, 2026-10-02)**: window type `design` = one conversation's `designs/<slug>/` folder on a canvas — each artboard a plain HTML file in its own sandboxed frame (`allow-scripts` only; since .331 loaded through the hub's frame host — the design policy as a header, never the app page's), placed by `design.json` (or in a row), pages + notes from the manifest; Fit / zoom (wheel pans, Ctrl/⌘+wheel zooms at the pointer, pinch on a phone) / pages / a list of artboards; double-click (tap on a phone) = one artboard ENLARGED and live; **the three views' fit rules (lane design-focus-whole — owner 2026-10-23 「预览和演示（放大）图周边差了一圈」: the enlarged Duo board 951×585 filled the pane's width at 1.76× and lost its bottom 98 px):** the canvas Fit = the page whole (`fitView`, ring `FIT_PAD` 40 — room for the name strips; never past 100 %); the focused view = a SCREEN whole, contained and centred with the same `FOCUS_PAD` 16 ring on all four sides (≤ 2×, its frame the artboard's own height), a TALL PAGE (h/w > `PAGE_RATIO 2.4`) at fit-width, its top at the pad, its frame cut to the pane and its document scrolling inside — a row that declares `"print": "fixed"` is a screen at any height; Present = whole, `PRESENT_PAD` 0, scaled up to fill (≤ 400 %). The line is a census, not taste: 63 artboards in 11 design.json files on the hub (2026-10-23) — the tallest screen 390×844 / 375×812 (h/w 2.165), the shortest page 390×960 (2.462); a 20:9 / 21:9 phone (2.22 / 2.33) stays a screen. The pads live once, as design-canvas-model.js constants. The phone uses the same rule (a 390×844 screen on a 390-wide phone is now whole too — fit-width cut its bottom 22 px). Zoom past contain keeps the frame's own height (never cut); Fit (or `0`) = contain again; repaints the changed artboard in place when a file in the folder changes (the hub's watch while the window is open); Comment = click an element → a composer with its quote line → the agent receives `[Design comment] <file> › <path> ("<text>"): <words>` as your own message; Print = the open artboard with its page size; Publish… = one self-contained page on `/p/<id>` (same URL on republish). A failure is said in words (a named card, a chip), never a blank canvas or a greyed button. Essay: kb-file-structure `src/lib/design-window.js`.
- **Design canvas chip (2.366.0; re-pointed by lane design-window 2026-10-02)**: status-bar chip (SVG, next to the goal chip; live windows only; count = this session's designs + published pages) → popover with a brief, a public-link toggle and Create (never disabled) → a VISIBLE message `[VibeSpace design request] <brief> — Make it with vibespace-design (manual: vibespace-docs design): new → write plain-HTML artboards under the printed dir → add → check; say the directory.` (+ ` [--public requested]`); the agent's `new` opens the Design window on your screen; the popover lists this session's designs (Open = the Design window, Publish… = its dialog) above the pages published from this session (Open / Copy link / Public↔Private, live on `page-published`); the Claude CLI kit line and its Retry are gone. The three canvases published by the old kit stay hosted and listed as pages; they do not open in the Design window. Essay: kb-file-structure "The design chip, re-pointed".
- **The Pages chip's two groups (lane pages-chip-groups, 2.369.240, B-aa28 — owner 2026-10-08 "可以，不过要分组")**: the design chip's popover lists pages in TWO groups under a head each, never mixed — "Published by this conversation" (the pages store's rows for this session / conversation; a design's page stays on its design row) and "Shown here" (a page ANOTHER conversation published whose `/p/<id>` link appears in this conversation's text — observed by the artifact registry, never declared; name + the publisher conversation's live name, or "no longer published" once it is taken down; Open / Copy link). The chip's number = designs + own + shown; the tooltip spells the split. Task Group pages are not listed. The shown rows also appear in the Artifacts list as kind page. ≤ 50 shown pages per conversation (the newest-mentioned kept).
- **One attach per double-click (B-0cc8, 2.369.240)**: a second click on a sidebar row while that conversation's attach is still in flight (< 15 s) raises the window the first click opened and sends nothing (it used to build a second window and a second attach).
- **Taking a published page down / choosing who may open it (B-f694, 2.369.202 — 生活方式助手 2026-10-01: an agent could only overwrite its public page with a placeholder; deletion lived in the UI)**: `vibespace-page unpublish <page>` and `vibespace-page visibility <page> public|private`, `<page>` = the published file's path (made absolute by the CLI; the server keys it as host + path, like publish), the page id or its `/p/` link (relative or absolute). Routes `POST /api/agent/pages/unpublish` / `…/visibility` (session or job token, `pageAuth`): the page must be in the caller's LIST scope (its session or conversation — what `vibespace-page list` shows); anything else is 404 "not among the pages this conversation published", never a hint that it exists. An unpublished page's id is kept in the store's `gone` list (id + time only — a private page's name never reaches an anonymous viewer; newest 5000), so `/p/<id>` and `/raw` answer **410 "This page was unpublished — …"** (UI deletion too, and across a restart); an id never published stays 404. A republish without `--public` keeps the visibility set. Permission: both verbs are HELD (never pre-approved); `visibility` also rides the `permissions.ask` rule beside `publish` (the same exposure as `--public`), `unpublish` none. The chat status bar's Pages list gains **Unpublish** behind a danger confirm (the explorer's *Publish page…* dialog already had it). The Pages list's own routes (`POST /api/pages/publish`, `POST` + `DELETE /api/pages/:id`) are the USER's: an agent token (`vsst_` / `jbt_`) is refused there 403 `agent_forbidden` with the `vibespace-page` verb to use (verify r1: on an instance without a password — the default — another conversation's token took a page down or made it public there, with no ownership check and no ask). Gates: test-published-pages §11, test-agent-tool-rules (ask list + card labels).
- **Context-full guidance + guarded compaction (2.365.0)**: a `prompt_too_long` result error is normalized with `errorKind:'prompt-too-long'` (message-manager `classifyResultError`, live + history) and rendered as a guidance card (chat-renderers `appendContextFullCard`): explanation, **Compact now** (sends `/compact` via `ChatInput.sendText` — null-safe; view-only windows drop the button), and the "Conversation too long → rewind in terminal mode" escalation. A `/compact` send sets `session._streamingKind='compacting'` + a descriptive label (ws-handler), broadcast to all clients and carried in the attach meta; while the kind is active the chat-input Stop button is a two-step confirm (armed 4s as "Cancel compaction?"). Reason: the CLI's only "Compaction canceled." path is an abort, and large-conversation compactions run 1–2 minutes — a reflexive Stop threw the attempt away (userN incident). Do not regress: the kind resets with the label at turn end (session-stdout), and every streaming-label broadcast carries it (API-retry relabels must not drop the guard).
- **Present, Print all and the downloads in the Design window (lane design-present, 2.369.203, design 003 §2.6 S7; owner Q2: no PPTX)**: ▶ Present on the bar shows the current page's artboards one at a time, full-screen (on the user's press; a refusal leaves it filling the window), each whole and fitted to the screen, in READING order (rows top to bottom, each left to right — `presentOrder`); → ← Space / Home End, a click or a swipe step (the frames stay shielded — a click never lands inside an artboard), a counter + the artboard's title in a chrome that fades after 2.5 s, Esc or × ends and the canvas view comes back exactly. The published page presents through the same canvas core: its ▶, or the link with `#present` (the /p/<id> shell hands exactly that fragment to its frame and allows the frame fullscreen). Print with nothing open on a page of several (or ⋯ "Print all artboards on this page") = ONE print document, one PDF page per artboard at its own size (named @page; each artboard in its own script-only frame — Save as PDF keeps the text as text). ⋯ Download HTML = the publish bundle as a file (`GET /api/design/bundle`, nothing hosted; it opens offline and presents); ⋯ Download folder (.zip) = the File Explorer's zip.
- **The Design window's changes strip (lane design-changes, 2.369.203, design 003 §2.2)**: one agent turn for many changes. In Comment mode a double-click on a text edits it IN PLACE (Enter keeps the words as a preview, Esc puts them back); the composer gets "Add" beside "Send" (the comment becomes a chip) and a Style… row (text colour, background, font size, spacing — previewed inline in the frame). The chips collect in a strip at the stage's top ("3 changes · Send all", each removable — × undoes its preview), kept per design on the device; Send all = `POST /api/design/changes` ⇒ ONE `[Design changes]` message (one belted line per chip) down the comment's own sender. Nothing writes a file (owner Q1 2026-10-02: no hand edits). Files: src/lib/design-changes.js; design-pick.js (edit / nudge / undo), design-canvas-model.js (editFence, frameSay), design-canvas.js (listen / tell), design-model.js changesVerdict / changesText, design-engine.js `changes`.
- **The Design window, the agent's side (lane design-docs-removal, 2026-10-02)**: an agent learns it from ONE tools-intro line and `vibespace-docs design` (the CLI manual, then VibeSpace's own craft rules: look at the project's tokens and components first, name static vs prototype, one whole HTML page per artboard at 390 or 1280 wide with real copy, re-read before every edit, `add` / `sync` last, say the folder at handover). `vibespace-design new <slug>` makes designs/<slug>/ in the conversation's folder and opens the window; every verb but `publish` runs without a card, `publish` asks. A user's comment arrives as a `[Design comment] <file> › <path> ("text"): …` message — one written while the conversation was not running waits and is handed over with its next turn. The Claude CLI kit behind the old /design flow is gone (its `vibespace-page` verb, the chip's kit line, the server module); a one-shot migration deletes the kit's extracted files. The three canvases published through it stay on `/p/<id>` and in the chip's pages list, and do not open in the Design window.
- **Design systems + the Design window's home (lane design-systems-home, 2.369.203, design 003 §2 S5 + S6)**: the agent makes a design system with `vibespace-design new <slug> --kind system` (system.md + tokens.css + component artboards, built from what the user points at); `new --system <name>` (or the `design.defaultSystem` setting) copies its tokens.css into a new design, and every read of a folder holding tokens.css WARNS on colours / font sizes outside it (`not_token`, `token_drift`). The Design window opened with no folder (⚙ Tools ▸ Designs…, the chip's All designs…) lists every design and system — name, conversation, folder, last opened, published link — with a find, Open, Rename, Show in Files and Remove from the list (the folder stays); the chip's brief form has a Design system select. src/lib/design-home.js, src/design-tokens.js.
- **Ask first + the visual check (lane design-ask, 2.369.203)**: the agent's `vibespace-design ask` puts ≤ 8 questions on its own design — the Design window shows them as a form over the canvas (pills, Decide for me, Other…, Skip, Later); Continue sends ONE `[Design answers] …` line as the user's message (or it waits in the stash). The chip's brief form ticks "Ask me a few questions first". `vibespace-design preview <file>` gives the agent's browser a 15-minute sandboxed address to look at an artboard before the hand-over; ⋯ Copy hand-off prompt points another agent at the folder and its HANDOFF.md. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md
- **Tweaks — the free knobs (lane design-tweaks, 2.369.203, design 003 §2 S4)**: the agent declares 3–8 knobs in design.json (`tweaks`: a colour, a range, a choice, a switch — each ONE CSS custom property or ONE root `data-` attribute its CSS reads); the Design window's **Tweaks** button opens OUR panel (a bottom sheet on the phone). Moving a knob restyles every artboard at once with no agent message; VibeSpace keeps the values in the design's `user.json` (written only on the owner's act) and bakes them into what the window shows, `preview` serves and `publish` puts on the page — another device's window restyles in place, without a reload. Reset = the agent's defaults; a design without knobs offers **+ Tweaks** (ONE `[Design tweaks]` message asking the agent for some). `vibespace-design show` / `check` tell the agent what the user set; the agent never writes `user.json`. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md §src/lib/design-tweaks.js
- **An agent-opened Design is placed, never popped to the front (lane design-window-placement, 2.369.323)**: when an agent opens or syncs a Design (`vibespace-design new|open|add|sync`), its window is PLACED as the right split beside the conversation that started it — the conversation on the LEFT half, the Design on the RIGHT, both on that conversation's desktop — and never comes to the front, takes your focus or switches your desktop; its taskbar entry pulses. A design the agent re-opens or syncs is shown (its tab chosen) without being raised. Your own doors (a chat card, the Designs home, the gear menu) still bring it forward, and Settings → Desktop apps → “Agent-opened windows come to the front” (default OFF) restores the old behaviour for designs too. Same rule as the agent browser (lane agent-window-no-steal); PURE `agentWindowPlacement` in src/lib/desktop-app-placement.js. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md
- **An agent's Design never re-arranges the desk you are using (lane agent-window-no-pop, inc-mvhebl4n-rkvr)**: the Design opens as the right split beside its conversation ONLY while you are in that conversation (its window is the active one); on another desk it is placed there, unseen. Anywhere else no window opens and nothing moves — the conversation shows a card above its composer (the design's title + **Open** + ✕) and its taskbar entry the badge; pressing Open opens the Design and brings it to the front. A design whose window is already open just pulses its taskbar entry. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md
- **Search cards show their query in the title + codex web searches are complete cards (2.369.43, owner report: every codex web_search card read `{"query":"","action":null}` / "(empty)")**: every search-kind card — claude WebSearch (query) / WebFetch (url), codex `web_search` (query, or the action's queries/url), ACP search tools — carries the query as a muted `.chat-tool-query` chip in its header (escaped, ~90 chars, full text in the tooltip), so a fold of "3 web searches" expands to readable titles without opening Input. Codex: the v2 WebSearchItem is an empty stub at item/started and complete only at item/completed, and a 0.153 rollout persists the search ONLY as `event_msg web_search_end` (which the normalizer used to skip — rebuilt histories rendered no search at all).
