  built in that window would be `disabled` forever, so `_setQueueSupported` —
  the one writer — schedules a single rAF-coalesced pass over the rendered
  elements and re-runs the chip renderer for every message carrying a queue
  state. It runs in BOTH directions: losing the capability makes the chips inert
  again rather than leaving a control that cannot work.
- **The chip joins on `webuiMsgId`, stamped on the message.** The normalizer's
  `userMessageIds` map is server-side only; the bubble carries the id itself so
  the client can match it to a queue row (without it every chip click answered
  "That message is no longer queued").
- **A dead or disconnected window SPEAKS.** Every queue action goes through one
  liveness check that toasts ("This session is not live — reconnect…") instead
  of swallowing the click, and the strip is dimmed under
  `.chat-input-disconnected` so the state is visible before the click.
- **THE CHORD: `Alt+Enter` = steer (2026-09-07, owner "顺便加入一个 queue 的快捷键,
  不支持queue的就不显示").** `Enter` already sends as QUEUED while a turn runs —
  our default, and the one the web/desktop Codex apps use (the TUI's
  `Enter`=steer / `Tab`=queue is a terminal keymap we deliberately do not copy).
  What was missing was the OTHER mode by keyboard, so: **`Alt+Enter`, and
  `Alt+Enter` only** — `Tab` is the slash-command completion and `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter`
  keeps meaning send/queue; both would have been silent redefinitions of a key
  the user already relies on. It must be tested BEFORE the plain-Enter branch,
  which checks only `!e.shiftKey` and would otherwise swallow it as an ordinary
  send. **A steer NAMES A QUEUED ITEM** (`turn/steer` takes the app-server's
  queued-submission id — there is no "send this text as a steer" verb anywhere),
  so the chord SENDS on the one ordinary send path and converts the item the
  harness reports back, with the SAME `queue-op` frame the strip button and the
  chip send: no second wire shape. `_steerAfterSend(msgId)` parks the msgId in a
  MAP (two quick chords must both land) and `_setQueue` drains it; an 8s timeout
  that expires **while the turn we sent into is still running** says so in chat
  rather than letting the user believe an injection happened — and says nothing
  once that turn has ended, because the message then runs next, immediately,
  which is what "now" asked for.
  **WHICH turn, never "a turn" (round-2 verifier's MAJOR).** The silence guard
  first tested `_typingSince` for truthiness, and that flag is RE-ARMED by the
  NEXT turn. The only way the timer survives to fire is that the msgId never
  appeared in the published queue — which is exactly what a NOT-busy wrapper
  does: it runs the message as its own `turn/start` (it only
  `thread/queue/add`s while a turn is active). That new turn re-armed the flag,
  so the guard was false precisely in the case it existed for and the window
  apologised for a message the agent was visibly running. `_showTyping` now
  stamps `_turnEpoch` on the same null→armed transition that sets
  `_typingSince` (a TIME is not an IDENTITY — the turn that ends and the one
  that starts next can arm in the same millisecond), `_steerAfterSend` captures
  it, and the timer stays silent unless the SAME epoch is still running. The
  epoch advances only where the flag arms, so a relabelled turn ("running
  Bash") is still the same turn and still gets the honest apology.
- **It is a CONTRIBUTED command, `chat.steerNow`** (contributions.js Ph1), so a
  plugin can see it, rebind it and run it. The command is registered ONCE for
  the app (`registerCommand` rejects a duplicate id by design — a per-view
  registration would throw on the second chat window); the per-view part is the
  KEYBINDING, carrying the view's AbortSignal and a `when` that scopes the chord
  to the window the keystroke happened in (`steerTargetView` resolves the target
  from an explicit `ctx.view` — the composer route hands itself in — or from the
  mounted view whose container holds the event target). The composer's own
  `Alt+Enter` routes through the SAME id, so there is exactly one definition of
  what the chord does. It is the FIRST core `registerKeybinding` chord (the
  palette / command-mode chords stay where they are: their modifier-lenient
  capture-phase checks are load-bearing).
- **THE HINT, and what gates it.** While a turn runs the composer carries a
  one-line hint under the box — `Enter queues · Alt+Enter injects now` — each
  segment drawn only where the harness backs it. The PURE
  `composerSendModes(caps)` (agent-meta.js) is the ONE decision:
  `allowSteerChord` = `steer`, and the queue segment is gated on **`queueOps`,
  not `queue`** — claude's CLI really does hold a mid-turn message, but it
  publishes no queue and takes no operation on it, so there is no strip, no live
  chip and nothing to act on; a line announcing "it is queued" with nothing on
  screen to show it is a promise we cannot keep. Hence: codex = both segments +
  the chord, opencode = the queue segment only, **claude and shell = no hint and
  no chord at all** (the owner's rule, verbatim). The caps it reads are the live
  intersection (`_queueCaps()` = harness row ∧ the RUNNING wrapper's advert),
  the very object the strip's Steer buttons read, so the chord, the hint and the
  strip can never disagree — including the late-capability ordering that once
  shipped a permanently dead chip (`setQueue` repaints both faces).
- **≤768px: no chords, a BUTTON.** A phone has no Alt key, so the same verb gets
  a small bolt button beside **Send**, shown while a turn runs on a
  steer-capable session. The split is deliberate: **JS owns only the capability**
  (the `.hidden` class on both surfaces), **CSS owns the viewport** — the hint is
  `display:none` under the 768px media query and the button is `display:none`
  above it (the shape `.chat-attach-btn` has used for the mobile upload button
  since 2.234.0), so the two faces can never both appear and neither can
  contradict the capability. Measured at 375×667: the button sits beside Send,
  the textarea keeps ≥2 rows visible and nothing overflows the input area.
- **Session Properties carries the same sentence, gated the same way** ("Sending
  during a turn"), from the HARNESS row rather than the live intersection — a
  properties panel describes what this KIND of agent does and is opened on
  stopped sessions too. It shares the panel's **"Config overrides"** section
  with the response-style row, and that header is created **at most once, on
  first demand** (`cfgSection()`): the panel's old `cfgSec || section(...)`
  idiom appended a NEW header per lazy row, which was invisible while exactly
  one such row existed and printed the header TWICE the moment this one joined
  it — a codex session with no saved override, i.e. the common case (round-2
  verifier's minor). Pinned by the real-browser leg ⑨f of test-queue-steer,
  which counts headers for codex / opencode / claude / shell (2 lazy rows / 1 /
  1 / 0) and proves its own probe can see a duplicate.
- **Removing a queued agent-to-agent / job message gives it back.** It was
  already reported delivered, so `remove` re-reports `peer_message_result
  ok:false` with the text and sender and the delivery ladder re-stashes it for
  next-turn injection — the same rule the ACP wrapper's Stop already obeyed.
- **STOP CLEARS THE QUEUE ON EVERY HARNESS (owner decision 2026-09-07 — the
  2026-09-06 divergence is closed).** Stop means stop: whatever was queued
  behind the running turn is dropped, and each dropped entry's bubble reads
  `Removed`. On ACP the queue is ours, so the wrapper simply drops it (plus the
  loud "Stop also dropped N queued messages" notice). On codex the queue belongs
  to the app-server, which DRAINS it when the turn ends — including a turn
  ended by Stop — so the wrapper `thread/queue/delete`s every item **before**
  it sends `turn/interrupt`; clearing afterwards loses that race and the queued
  message runs the instant Stop lands (that was the old behaviour, and the codex
  suite's negative control reproduces it). **Both wrappers emit the SAME frame,
  a `queue_op_result {op:'remove', ok:true, reason:'stopped'}` per dropped entry,
  BEFORE they republish the emptied queue** — a bare empty republish would clear
  those chips, which the client reads as "it ran", the exact opposite of what
  Stop did. Nothing is silent on either side: a codex `thread/queue/delete` that
  fails reports `ok:false` (the item is still queued and WILL run) and lands in
  the wrapper journal, and a dropped agent-to-agent/job message goes back to the
  delivery ladder (`peer_message_result ok:false` / `peer_result ok:false`) so it
  is re-stashed for next-turn injection. A message queued and then *drained by a
  turn ending on its own* is a different thing and still clears its chip — it
  ran. (codex-side difference kept deliberately: no extra "send it again" notice
  — every dropped codex item has its own bubble whose chip flips to `Removed`,
  while ACP's notice also covers entries with no bubble.) **Superseded by the
  2026-10-24 amendment below: ACP's notice is retired, the toast is the one
  notice on every harness.**
- **…AND WHAT STOP DROPPED COMES BACK INTO THE INPUT BOX (owner 2026-10-24,
  «可以丢弃但是把内容回填到输入框» — lane stop-refills-composer, .353).**
  The queue is still dropped — nothing queued runs after Stop — but every word
  the person queued is put back into the composer, once, on every open window,
  in queue order (oldest first, a blank line between messages, IN FRONT of
  whatever draft was there), and ONE toast says it: «Stop put N queued
  message(s) back into the input box», plus «K attached image(s) were not put
  back — attach them again» (attachments are named, never restored — the draft
  is text; the bubble still shows the picture), «M message(s) came back
  shortened» (a message over 20 000 characters) and «K more queued message(s)
  were too long to put back» (past 100 000 characters in one Stop). What the
  person was typing when Stop landed is never lost: the words land in front of
  the LIVE box (unsaved keystrokes kept, the caret moves with the text), and a
  save already on its way to the server keeps them too (the server belt). An
  ACP / Antigravity message that the turn had claimed but not yet sent (Stop
  inside the context fetch) comes back as the oldest row and its bubble reads
  `Removed`. A peer / Background Work / notification message is never put into
  the box — it goes back through its own delivery ladder. ACP's «Stop also
  dropped N queued messages — send them again» notice is retired (it is no
  longer true). A codex row the app-server drained mid-sweep, whose own turn
  is the one Stop interrupts, comes back too (2026-10-25, lane
  codex-interrupted-putback, .354 — the owner: «可以 按照你推荐来», a duplicate
  send is cheaper than a lost message): the toast adds «, N had already
  started and was stopped — put back too», its bubble's chip reads «Started,
  then stopped» and its card «That message had already started — Stop stopped
  it and put it back into the input box.» The TURN decides, never a clock: the
  app-server's `userMessage` item names the turn the row entered (the sweep
  waits up to 1 s for it); a drained row whose turn already ENDED ran to its
  end and still reads «no longer queued — it already ran», as does one whose
  turn was never named. If a queued message was being EDITED when Stop landed, the rewrite
  stays first in the box and the put-back (the original text among it) sits
  below it — the person deletes whichever they do not want. **Claude Code
  too, since 2.369.354** (lane claude-wrapper-queue — the owner, 2026-10-25):
  measured on CLI 2.1.308 the CLI ran a message it had queued itself right
  after Stop, so VibeSpace's chat-wrapper now HOLDS a message sent mid-turn (it
  reaches the CLI only when the turn ends) — Stop drops it and puts it back as
  on every other harness, and nothing runs after Stop. A `/goal` set mid-turn
  still goes to the CLI's own queue.
- **Stop only claims what Stop actually did (round-2 review, three fixes).**
  ① The app-server can DRAIN an item between the sweep's `thread/queue/list` and
  its `thread/queue/delete`; it answers `{deleted:false}` (a verdict, not an
  error) and that message is *running*. It is reported `ok:false, reason:'gone'`
  — "no longer queued — it already ran" (since .354, when its turn is the one
  Stop interrupts: `started: true`, and it comes back — above) — so the bubble never reads `Removed`,
  and an agent-to-agent message on that path is NOT re-stashed (it really was
  delivered; giving it back would deliver it twice). ② While the sweep runs the
  ONLY truthful publish is its own closing one: the latch sits on the wrapper's
  single publish choke point, not just on the queue re-read, because a
  `turn/started` (the drained item's own turn!) re-publishes the CACHED list
  with no RPC at all and used to resurrect the just-removed bubbles as
  `Queued`. ③ Stop is a safety control, so the sweep is BUDGETED — ~2.5s per
  RPC, ~6s overall — and when the budget expires `turn/interrupt` goes out
  immediately while everything still queued is reported `ok:false` ("it stays
  queued and will run"). A wedged app-server used to hold the Stop button for
  15s per RPC per queued item.
- **A SECOND Stop is normal, and it is the SAME Stop (round-3 review).** A
  double-click — or a second attached client's Stop, which nothing coordinates
  — used to start a second sweep on top of the running one: it listed the queue
  the first was still deleting and then reported those very items "no longer
  queued — it already ran", the exact falsehood the round above exists to
  remove (and on that verdict a queued agent-to-agent message is deliberately
  NOT handed back to the delivery ladder, so the duplicate also lost a promised
  message). Both halves of Stop are now single-flight: a second frame RIDES the
  running sweep, and `turn/interrupt` coalesces per TURN while its RPC is
  unanswered — keyed on the turn plus a live call, never on a time window, so
  an answered interrupt whose turn is somehow still running still accepts a
  genuine retry. What a riding Stop clears is what that sweep listed; anything
  queued after the list is not swallowed, the sweep's closing publish still
  lists it. **The button says so too:** clicking Stop disables it and it reads
  "Stopping…" until the turn ends or an 8s fallback (deliberately longer than
  the 6s sweep budget) re-arms it — a Stop that can stay dead would be worse
  than a duplicate frame. A label repaint no longer hands the live button back
  mid-flight (that was the actual DOM bug: the streaming status line re-renders
  on every label change).
- **A steer whose delete is REFUSED says so (round-3).** `turn/steer` never
  dequeues, so the wrapper deletes the queued copy — and if that delete answers
  `{deleted:false}` the app-server had already drained the item, i.e. the
  double run the delete exists to prevent has just happened. It is reported
  `ok:true, reason:'steered-not-dequeued'` (the same verdict the failed-delete
  path uses): the chip still reads `Steered` — it was — and a notice warns that
  it may run a second time. r2 read this verdict in the Stop sweep but not
  here, and answered a bare success.
- Measured facts behind the codex implementation (0.153.4, live app-server):
  the removal verb is `thread/queue/delete {threadId, queuedSubmissionId}` —
  **there is no `thread/queue/remove`**; `thread/queue/changed` carries only
  `{threadId}`, so every change drives a re-`list`; `turn/steer` does **not**
  dequeue the item even when it carries the same `clientUserMessageId`; and an
  `add` on an idle thread starts a turn by itself (the app-server drains its own
  queue, we never call `turn/start` for it).

- **OPENCODE: ROLL BACK, ASKS, A SERVE TERMINAL, LIVE UPDATES (S9 remainder, B-eac2, 2026-09-07)** — everything the serve exposes that the store-facts slice left on the table. All of it needs the opt-in **OpenCode background service** plugin (⚙ → Plugins, default OFF).
  - **Roll back to before a message.** Right-click a USER message's colour strip in an OpenCode conversation → *Roll back to before this message*. It asks first (it is a real filesystem change): OpenCode restores the working tree to the snapshot taken before that message and stages every later message for removal. The conversation then SAYS so — a line at the boundary — and the popup offers *Restore rolled-back messages* while it is staged. Sending a new prompt makes it permanent (OpenCode's own semantics; there is no v1 "commit" call). Both actions broadcast, so a second browser sees the new state without a refresh.
  - **The agent's questions are the same card every harness uses.** An OpenCode `question` tool renders as the AskUserQuestion card (options, custom answer, multi-select, one page per question) and is answered/dismissed on the serve's own route — so it works on a conversation with no live process here, and a pending one survives a page reload. An ask that is no longer waiting says exactly that instead of showing a Submit that could only fail. Honest limit: `opencode acp` — the mode VibeSpace's own live OpenCode sessions run in — does not offer the `question` tool at all, and question events are per-process, so this lane fires for turns the serve drives.
  - **"Open terminal in this session"** (session card menu, local OpenCode conversations). Opens a shell the OpenCode SERVE owns, in the conversation's own directory, as a normal VibeSpace terminal window — same xterm, input, resize and window actions. The serve's port never reaches the browser; VibeSpace bridges the stream server-side.
  - **Live, not polled.** The session list for OpenCode conversations no longer refreshes on a 10-second timer: it refreshes when something CHANGES. Two sources, because one of them is blind: the serve's own event stream (instant for anything it does) and a watch on the OpenCode store file (the only way to notice a `opencode` TUI or another serve writing the same database — measured: their events never reach our stream). If both go down the timer comes back, deliberately, so a broken lane can never freeze the sidebar. And the change is PUSHED: every open browser learns about it (a couple of seconds at most) instead of waiting for its own list poll, so a conversation someone started in a terminal shows up on its own.
  - **A conversation someone ELSE is driving shows as `external`** (the yellow state the sidebar already had) — but only on positive evidence: the serve reports it busy, or its row changed while we were not the ones changing it. It decays back to "stopped" by itself. VibeSpace never shows a running agent it cannot see — and **your own actions are not "someone else"**: rolling a conversation back, restoring it or answering its question moves the same row, so those writes are recognised as ours and the conversation stays "stopped" (a change made past them, by a real TUI or a second serve, still turns it yellow immediately).
  - **Any machine.** All of the above take a machine id: this one, a paired device (the daemon runs the same code where the store is), or an ssh host (a shipped single-file runner). The serve terminal is the exception and says so — its stream is loopback-only on the machine that owns it.
- **Harness settings — the dedicated per-harness configuration area (2.369.123, docs/design-harness-settings.zh.md; owner D1–D4).** The Settings window's Claude / Codex / OpenCode sections are DERIVED from each harness descriptor's declared table (src/harness-settings.js): every row says what it is for — an apply chip under it reads "Applies to new sessions · --brief", "Read by VibeSpace · pool engine", or "Written into the CLI config" with the target `~/file → key`, a FRESH receipt for this machine ("✓ this machine: ~/.claude/settings.json → cleanupPeriodDays = 36500 · written 3 min ago" / "⚠ … is 30 (wanted 36500) — written again at the next start or setting change" / "? … will be created at the next start — or press Apply" (a working Apply beside it; lane hooks-create) / "? ~/.claude not found — the CLI has not run on this machine, so nothing is written" / "⚠ … not valid after a hand edit — not touched" / "Leaving the CLI's own value alone") and a human-triggered "Check machines…" that lists every registered host's state ("⚠ userW-mac: … is 30 (wanted 36500) — written at the next tool install or session start on that machine" / "? not checked — reinstall the agent tools" for a helper that predates the plan). The same chips sit on Manage Agents → Machines under the integration rows (that is where the user looks for WHICH machine; not a second editing surface). Values stay in data/settings.json under the same keys (zero migration). Receipts are never persisted (a hand-edited file would make a stored "applied at" lie); the last local write is kept in memory only. No fan-out on change: the next Install or the next session spawn on that machine applies it (the ssh prelude and the dial run-cmd carry the same `VIBESPACE_CLI_CONFIG` plan as Install, so a host only ever spawned into now gets the keys too); the card shows "differs" until then. **Managed CLI-config rows today:** `claude.transcriptRetentionDays` (default 36500 → `cleanupPeriodDays` in ~/.claude/settings.json; Claude Code's own 30-day sweep deletes the conversations this product keeps; 0 = leave alone) and NEW `codex.historyPersistence` (default 'save-all' → `[history] persistence` in ~/.codex/config.toml through a comment-and-format-preserving TOML setter — verified against codex-cli 0.154.0's embedded config template; 'none' means codex writes no rollouts and this instance shows no history for those sessions; '' = leave config.toml alone). A hand-broken file (invalid JSON, a TOML shape the setter does not understand — inline table, array of tables, multi-line string, a root scalar named like the section, dotted keys plus a header for the same table) is refused by name and never overwritten; a symlinked config (the dotfiles pattern) is written through and STAYS a symlink, its mode survives, a dangling link is refused (2026-09-21); a value outside a closed enum's options (an API/import write — the Settings window cannot produce one) never reaches a config file: the default rides and the boot log names the refused value; a missing settings.json is reported, not created; the temp-server guard (`hookRegistrationSafe`) now covers these writes too. `claude.autoResumeOnLimit` moved back to the Chat category (generic feature; key spelling unchanged). A plugin-contributed harness ships its own table and gets a derived section with zero new code. Gates: test-harness-settings, test-harness-contract, test-claude-retention (kept by name), test-architecture §46.
- **What an ask SHOWS (lane foryou-attachments, owner 2026-10-09 "经常 agent 会让我 review 一个产物/文件/网页，我却没法轻易从 inbox 里打开")**: `vibespace-ask "q" --artifact <path|/p/id>…` (≤ 8; vibespace-msg's hand-over grammar — every path after the flag until the next flag, absolute against the shell's cwd) attaches the file / design folder / published page the agent wants the owner to look at. Each is CHECKED at submit (owner 21:42Z, binding): a readable file on the asker's host, a design with design.json, a published page — any that would not open ⇒ the WHOLE ask is refused (CLI exit 2, one line per bad attachment + "nothing was filed — fix the attachment and run vibespace-ask again"). Filed: chips (an SVG kind icon + the name + the host when not this box) under the question in the tray row AND the For-you window; one press = THE one artifact door (the asking conversation's chat view when this client shows it, else the row's own facts) after an open-time re-check (gone ⇒ a toast that says so). Paths and links WRITTEN in the item's text / detail are clickable too (src/lib/foryou-links.js — the chat's path grammar, src/path-linkify.js): absolute, `~/…`, relative (`docs/plan.md`; a bare filename in backticks), http(s), mailto, `/p/<id>` — resolved against the asker's cwd on its host; the words stay exactly as written, escaped. The attachments also show in the conversation's Artifacts list (a `present` op each).
- **Replying to a For-you item (2.369.169, docs/design-user-inbox-reply.md — chunks 1–4: the server core, the panel, the title-bar mini inbox, the usage set).** A reply to an inbox item reaches its agent as the user's OWN message — the same server path the chat composer uses (src/server/user-input.js, shared with the ws chat-input case), never the delivery ladder and never the spend authorizer — prefixed with a quote of the item (`[For you reply #<id>]`, when it was filed, the text, up to 1500 chars of the detail, the options) so the agent knows which ask it answers. It is sent mid-turn too (the session queues it); a successful send resolves the item `by your reply` and keeps the reply on it. It is refused BY NAME, resolving nothing, when the session is a terminal, its host is unreachable, the item came from a server producer (accounts/jobs) or a job; an agent token can never send one (owner-only route). Agents may file decisions with `vibespace-ask --options "A|B|C"` (≤ 6 one-click answers; an empty label such as `"A||B"` is refused by name, never dropped) — such items sort first within their urgency — and read one of their items in full with `vibespace-ask show <id>`. Every session in the live list now carries its `turn` (running / idle / waiting). **In the panel (chunk 2):** each open item has a Reply button (an arrow icon) that unfolds a one-line box under it — Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, Esc folds it (the text is kept for the next unfold) — and an item filed with options shows one chip per option that replies with that label in one click. The button is disabled with its reason as the tooltip when the agent is not running / is a terminal session / its host is unreachable, and is absent on items from Manage Agents or Background Work. A reply toasts "Reply sent" and the row turns resolved in place with "You replied: …"; a failure toasts "Could not reply: <reason>" and keeps the text. Each row names its agent's conversation with a running dot in front (lane foryou-folds; it was the group title's until the tray became the attention list) — filled green mid-turn, hollow green idle, amber waiting for you, dashed when its host is unreachable, grey not running — that follows the session live without reloading. A reply box being typed into survives every update of the list (another item arriving, another client's ✓): the rows are patched in place, never redrawn. The chat shows the reply as your message with a "For you · reply to #<id>" head and the quoted item folded. The phone's inbox sheet has the same box with ≥ 36 px targets. **In each window's title bar (chunk 3):** every chat or terminal window whose agent has open asks shows a small inbox pill after its title — the number of that session's open items (notices are not counted), coloured by the most urgent one; it disappears at zero and moves onto the window's tab when the window is grouped (and back when it leaves the group). A view-only window of a stopped conversation shows its own count too. Clicking it opens a small popover listing only that session's items, with the same Reply box, option chips, ✓ ✕ ↺ and viewer as the panel; clicking a row does not jump (you are already in that window). Items resolved from the popover stay in place, struck through, until it closes; the pill counts down as you go. Escape closes the popover first and the For-you panel on the next press — the same with the ⤢ item viewer (or any other dialog) open above the panel: one Escape closes the dialog only (r1). The session's name in the popover head, like every item string, is shown as plain text. On a phone window title bars are not drawn, so the phone's inbox is the nav sheet. **Against the flood (chunk 4) — superseded by lane foryou-folds (2.369.318):** the per-agent fold ("{n} more…" after 5 rows), the per-agent "Mark all seen" and the board chip beside the agent's name left the tray with its group heads; the tray is the attention list now — the first 6 rows, folds BY BAND, "Mark all seen" per band (see «For-you tray: the attention list»). What stayed: rows resolved while the panel is open keep their slots, a row once shown is never hidden again under the pointer, a new row arriving into a folded band joins its fold's count, one "Mark all seen" is ONE request (struck in place, one update to every other client, ↺ reopens, a failure is a toast naming how many and why). The For-you WINDOW keeps its session groups and the board chip. Not built (the design's LATER list): auto-resolving an item when you answer the agent in its chat, expiring a stopped session's asks, keyboard j/k/r/d, muting an agent.
- **An ask that names a grant carries the grant; a one-click answer reads as a reply (lane controls-that-lie, 2.369.346 — naive study round 4: «Granted access» only typed two words).** `vibespace-ask "…" --grant browser:<label|id>` files the item with the grant itself (the route resolves the profile from the keeper's list — PURE src/ask-grant.js; a channel / a machine is refused with its own road): the tray and the For-you window draw «Let this conversation use <label>», whose press adds the asking conversation to that profile's «Who can use it» (the owner's GET …/use + whole-list PATCH with its base) and THEN answers the agent «Granted — … `vibespace-browser use <id>`» (or «Already allowed — …»); every `--options` chip reads «Reply: <label>». Gates: test-user-todos-layout ㉔, test-inbox-reply-ui ⑤g, test-approval-census `browser-grant`.
- **A reply to a conversation that ENDED reopens it (lane inbox-reply-dead-session, userW inc-mvfuzlom-nwav 2026-10-19 — the box was greyed out on a stopped conversation).** In the tray, the mini inbox, the phone sheet and the For-you window, a reply box is NEVER disabled (PURE src/inbox-reply.js `replyBoxView`, one view for both surfaces). On a conversation that is not running, its note above the box says 「这个对话已结束；发送会重新打开它并把这条回复作为第一条消息」 (en: "This conversation has ended — sending reopens it with this reply as its first message"), and its send reads 「重新打开并发送」 / "Reopen and send"; the chips stay pressable. The send RESUMES that same conversation by the page's own resume road (the ws create `{resume:true, resumeId}` with its config from user-state — src/server/inbox-reopen.js, PURE src/inbox-reopen.js `reopenCreate`), types the reply as its first input through the typing path, resolves the item, and opens the conversation's window on that page (`{ok, reopened:true, sessionId, conversation}`). A resume that fails says why: `resume_failed` with the create's own words, as a toast and in the box's note. A live session's reply is unchanged. Gates: test-inbox-reply §8, test-inbox-reply-ui ③ ㉑, test-inbox-window-ui ② ⑳, test-inbox-window-model.
- **Notices in the For-you inbox (2.369.118).** An item carries `kind: action | notice` (a producer's declaration: spend-guard's ceiling notices, `vibespace-ask --notice`; older items are actions). Notices sit in their own section under the asks (same append-only slots while open) and never colour the badge — the red/yellow/accent segments count actions only, a grey pill counts notices; the head's "{n} open" counts actions. Gate: test-user-todos-layout ⑤.
- **Attachment preview (2.369.245, lane outbox-attachment-preview)**: a draft card's / a channel message's file opens on a click — a picture in the image overlay, a document in a `viewer` window by URL (`app.openFile({rawUrl})`); ⤓ downloads; HTML / SVG read as text; a gone draft says so.
- **Notices grouped by who filed them, and counts on the inbox tabs (2.369.169, B-328d, docs/design-user-inbox-reply.md §8).** Every inbox item names its PRODUCER (`origin`: spend · login · pool · jobs · channels · browser · agent — a closed set of exactly the producers that file; a filing that names none is refused by the store and fails the census suite, a value outside it is refused by name). The Notices section is no longer one flat list: a strip of filter chips — `All` with the number of open notices, then one chip per producer present with its open count — sits over one group per producer (Spending, Login expiry, Account pool, Background Work, Channels, Agent browser, Agents), each head with its open count, in that fixed order (a producer that shows up while the popup is open joins at the end, nothing moves under the pointer). A chip shows only that producer's notices (the active chip again = all); the choice is kept per device and survives closing the popup — while that producer has a notice: a choice whose group is gone when the popup opens becomes All (kept that way on the device), and a notice arriving later never changes what the strip shows (only a chip click chooses); the asks above are never filtered, and a reply being typed anywhere keeps its text. The two tab labels carry counts: Inbox shows the open asks (coloured like the taskbar badge, with the badge's own words as its tooltip) and the grey notice count; Notifications shows how many toasts arrived since you last looked at that page on this device, cleared when you open it. Items filed before this release carry no producer and are placed by a read-time rule (the old spend notices under Spending, the old channel items under Channels, the rest under Agents) — no migration. The title-bar mini inbox is unchanged (asks only; its badge never counts a notice). Phone: the same sheet, chips ≥ 36 px. Gates: test-user-todos-layout ⑪ (incl. the census), test-inbox-reply-ui ⑰ ⑱ ⑱c ⑲.
- **«Mark all read» on the notices; a notice is read by reading it (lane inbox-fyi-mark-all, 2.369.343 — the owner 2026-10-22: «既然是仅供知晓还让我一个一个确认很弱智»).** The Notices tab of the For-you window (in its bar, right after the tabs, on that tab only) and the notices head of the popup and the phone page carry «Mark all read» (全部已读 / すべて既読): ONE `POST /api/user-todos/notices/read-all {ids}` for every OPEN notice the surface lists (PURE `noticeReadAll` — the window's scope + text filter; the popup's chip in force while open, all while closed), the store's `readNotices` = ONE save + ONE broadcast (an ask among the ids refused, a read one left as it was), so the tab's count, the badge's grey count and the attention list's count drop in the same tick on every client; a 5 s Undo toast (`…/unread` — exactly those back open, their expiry kept); disabled with «No unread notices here» when none is open. In the window a notice that asks nothing (PURE `readOnSight`: no producer button, chips, card or door) is marked done after 1.5 s in the pane with the person IN the window (focus inside, page visible), or at once on ‹ back; the selection stays. Gates: test-inbox-reply §9, test-user-todos-layout, test-inbox-window-model ⑧, test-inbox-window-ui ㉑.
- **The View Workflow window shows what the card shows (2.369.119).** While a run is live, /api/workflow lays the launching session's own progress tree over the disk skeleton (PURE src/workflow-live.js), so the window lists phases, labels, states, the running agent's last tool and live usage — the same data as the chat card; the journal's retry verdicts still win, an agent the tree named before its transcript exists has View Log disabled, and a window opened after the launching session is gone falls back to the disk skeleton with the old note. Gate: test-workflow-live-view.
- **Unknown harness records are the "Unknown event" fall-back card (2.369.119 → .120).** A stream record type or `system` subtype VibeSpace does not handle and has not declared ignored renders — history and live alike — as a red-bordered "Unknown event" card in the flow (harness + `system/<subtype>` or the type, a hint, the whole record behind a "Full record" expander); codex too. It has its own fold kind `unknown` in the run-collapse ("{n} unknown events"), offered in chat.collapseKinds UNCHECKED so it stays visible until the user decides it is noise. The declared-ignored lists live in message-manager.js and are a decision, not a default. Gate: test-unknown-records.
- **Live Workflow detail (2.369.118).** While a Workflow (ultracode) run is live, its tool card shows the phases with agent chips (label · state dot · last tool), a done/total tally and the run's usage (tokens · tool uses · minutes) from the CLI's own `task_progress.workflow_progress` tree, kept field-wise across heartbeats; the card re-renders on every progress edit. Live sessions only — the post-hoc View Workflow window remains the history surface. Gate: test-task-lifecycle.
- **The agent can talk to YOU (owner ruling 8(c), setting `claude.brief`, default OFF).** Claude Code has had a first-class agent→user channel since `--brief`: two real tools, `SendUserMessage` and `SendUserFile`. With the setting on, new claude sessions start with the flag and VibeSpace renders each call as a **highlighted "Message for you" card** instead of a generic tool card — which matters because with `--brief` the CLI hides plain text outside that tool from the message view, so the card IS the reply. A `proactive` status (the CLI's own word for "I am initiating, not replying") wears a chip. `SendUserFile` publishes each named file through the existing published-pages channel: session-owned, **private by default**, and the card carries the RELATIVE link the front end joins with its own origin (never a guessed absolute URL — the 2.366.1 law). Failures are ON the card, per file. Remote sessions render the card with no link (their files are on another machine — an honest absence). The row shows the file's basename with the full path on hover, so a 375px column still fits the size beside it. **Default OFF because it changes how the agent writes**, not because it is unfinished.
- **The agent can talk to YOU (owner ruling 8(c), setting `claude.brief`, default OFF).** Claude Code has had a first-class agent→user channel since `--brief`: two real tools, `SendUserMessage` and `SendUserFile`. With the setting on, new claude sessions start with the flag and VibeSpace renders each call as a **highlighted "Message for you" card** instead of a generic tool card — which matters because with `--brief` the CLI hides plain text outside that tool from the message view, so the card IS the reply. A `proactive` status (the CLI's own word for "I am initiating, not replying") wears a chip. `SendUserFile` publishes each named file through the existing published-pages channel: session-owned, **private by default**, and the card carries the RELATIVE link the front end joins with its own origin (never a guessed absolute URL — the 2.366.1 law). Failures are ON the card, per file. Remote sessions render the card with no link (their files are on another machine — an honest absence). The row shows the file's basename with the full path on hover, so a 375px column still fits the size beside it. **A published file never disturbs a page you published yourself**: the channel keeps its own key namespace scoped to the conversation, so it can neither overwrite the bytes of a page you shared from that path nor flip its visibility, and two conversations that hand you the same `report.md` get two links instead of silently sharing one. **A call the CLI rejected — or a turn that interrupted one — says so on the card in red**, with the CLI's own reason: these cards have no ✓/✗ column, so a failure that only lived in the tool result would have shown you "File for you" about a file that never arrived. **Default OFF because it changes how the agent writes**, not because it is unfinished.
- **Prompt-cache levers (owner ruling 8(c), all default OFF, each mapped to one dumped CLI flag).** `claude.systemPromptSnapshot` (`--system-prompt-snapshot on|off` — record the system prompt once per conversation and reuse it verbatim on every request and resume), `claude.excludeDynamicSystemPromptSections` (`--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` — move cwd/env/memory-paths/git-status out of the system prompt into the first user message, so the cached prefix is identical across machines and users), and `claude.autocompact` (`--autocompact auto|100k–1M` — compaction is what breaks the cached prefix). These are a first-order cost lever for "one subscription, dozens of concurrent sessions", so they exist as measurable switches; **none is on by default** and a value the CLI would reject is dropped rather than passed on.

- **VibeSpace's own tools do not ask per step; a card for them says what it does (lane L, 2026-09-25 — the naive-user study 2: 7–15 "Permission: Bash" cards per browser task, Always Allow never sticking, `close --all` feared).** Setting `claude.allowAgentTools` (Claude section, default ON): every claude spawn carries allow rules for vibespace-browser / -status / -task / -ask / -docs / -msg / -window / -channels / -page and the non-executing `vibespace-job` verbs in its inline `--settings` (nothing written to `~/.claude/settings.json`; `vibespace-job run` / `start` / `access`, `vibespace-exit` and any other command in the same line still ask). **Always Allow now sticks**: it reaches the CLI as `updatedPermissions` (it had been sent under a key the CLI drops — every Always Allow was a plain Allow), and on a card for one of our tools it allows the whole tool (the CLI suggested only the verb, `vibespace-browser click *`); its tooltip names the rules. **A browser-only line wears the agent browser's face** — its glyph, "Agent browser", the steps in words ("Open https://…", "Click @e1 · Read the page") on the card head and in the permission prompt ("Permission: Agent browser"); a line that also runs something else stays a Bash card that says what our part does, "also runs: pgrep", and for `close --all` "Closes only this conversation's browser — browsers of other sessions are not touched." A hovered Allow stays green (it used to turn into a dark button with dark words that read as disabled — the "needs two clicks" report). src/agent-tool-rules.js is the table + the words; gates test-agent-tool-rules / test-new-session-dialog. **r2 (the lane's adversarial verify, 2026-09-25) — the verb tables and the trade-off:** allowed whole — vibespace-browser, -status, -task, -ask, -docs, -msg, -window, -channels; verb-listed — `vibespace-job` (list, show, poll, answers, logs, progress, ask, docs, stop, rm, notify, notify-cron, announce, subscribe, unsubscribe; HELD run / start / access) and `vibespace-page` (list, kit; **publish = ASK**: owner decision 2026-09-25 — it is not in the allow list and the spawn also carries `permissions.ask: ['Bash(vibespace-page publish:*)']`, which beats any allow rule — see the r3 mode table below); held whole — vibespace-exit and the non-agent helpers. **Always Allow on a held verb or tool** allows only that exact command line (the CLI would have saved `vibespace-job run *` — every future shell command through that verb), and where no exact line can be saved (a compound, a `*` in the line) or the verb is an ask verb, the button is not shown and the card says why ("Publishing a page asks every time — Always Allow is not offered."). **The browser face is worn only by the bare tool name** — `./data/bin/vibespace-browser …`, `/tmp/x/vibespace-browser …` or `PATH=… vibespace-browser …` is some other file, so its card stays a Bash card that names it ("also runs: /tmp/x/vibespace-browser"). **The accepted trade-off, stated in the setting — the READ and WRITE twins:** anything the agent can read it can type or upload into a web page without asking — except an UPLOAD (the READ twin) from ~/.claude, ~/.ssh, ~/.vibespace, ~/.codex or VibeSpace's account stores (data/subs, data/codex-subs), which `vibespace-browser` refuses by name (`upload_secret_refused`, before the binary or the server; a symlink into a store counts). **r4 (the round-2 verify's surviving MAJOR) — the WRITE twin:** an allow rule on a tool is a grant on every path the tool can WRITE, and every writing verb (`download`/`pdf`/`screenshot`/`state save`/`record`/`trace`/`profiler`/`network har`, the `-o`/`--screenshot-dir` flags — censused from the CLI help) confines its output to the session's project cwd, the OS temp dir or ~/Downloads and refuses anything else — or any credential store — by name (`write_path_refused`, before /resolve and before the binary; measured red on 0.38.1: `download`/`pdf` wrote `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, `open data:text/html,<a download>` reaches the payload with no external server). The invariant: an allow rule on a tool is a grant on every path the tool can write; the tool confines its writes or the rule cannot exist. **r5 (the round-3 verify's CRITICAL) — THE FRAME RULE:** a path is judged and written in the SAME frame. The browser's daemon resolves a relative word against ITS OWN cwd (the launcher's — the keeper's used to be the server's, the checkout), so the CLI never hands it a relative word: every path slot (exact, measured per verb — `download`'s word after the selector, a lone `screenshot` word only when it holds `/` or an image extension, `record start`'s path never its URL, the upload/`state load`/`--baseline`/`--init-script`/`--curl` reads too) is resolved PHYSICALLY (a symlink before any `..` after it; `~` expanded — the binary never does) from where the agent typed it and handed over ABSOLUTE, in the argv, in every batch line (an argument batch goes over as the binary's stdin JSON) and every stdin element; and every daemon runs in a private `<tmp>/vibespace-browser-cwd-<uid>` (the keeper's runtime and the CLI's own spawn — never the checkout, refused by name). The fence is the SESSION's directory — `VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD`, exported by every spawn path (the local wrapper argv, the remote prelude) — never the shell's cwd (absent ⇒ only `/tmp` and `~/Downloads`); a project inside a dot-directory writes under its own root; `.ssh`/`.claude`/`.codex`/`.vibespace`/`.git` anywhere and VibeSpace's own data dir are refused wherever they stand; `AGENT_BROWSER_SCREENSHOT_DIR` is not passed. The job cards say what they do ("Stop or remove one of its background jobs", "Schedule a reminder that wakes this conversation", "Let others see or control one of its background jobs"). With a user's own `--settings <file>` and effort ultracode there is still exactly one `--settings` flag — the user's file; the ultracode mode stands down and the server journal says so. **r3 (integrator decision 2026-09-26) — the publish ask rule follows the SPAWN mode.** On 2.1.281 an ask rule is checked BEFORE the permission mode, so r2's rule on every spawn made `vibespace-page publish` prompt in a full-access session that had never asked. The law: **our injected rules never change what the user's chosen mode does — they only keep OUR allow list from widening.** So the ask rule rides only a spawn whose mode asks anyway, and the allow list is verb-listed (list, kit — never publish) in every mode:

  | spawn mode (`--permission-mode`, read off the argv) | `permissions.ask` publish rule | what `vibespace-page publish` does |
  |---|---|---|
  | `default` / `manual` (2.1.281's alias of default) | carried | asks every time — even when the user's own settings hold a broader allow rule |
  | `acceptEdits` | carried | asks every time |
  | `plan` | carried | asks (plan mode asks for commands anyway) |
  | `bypassPermissions` ("Never ask (full access)"), or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in the session's own args | NOT carried | runs without asking, as it did before lane L |
  | `dontAsk` | not carried (nothing to add) | refused — it is not pre-approved, exactly as it always was |
  | `auto` | not carried | the mode's own safety check decides, as before lane L |
  | no flag ("Default (Claude Code's own setting)") | not carried | the CLI's own mode decides (a user's `defaultMode`, bypass included, or 2.1.281's auto fallback — unknown at spawn); in its default mode publish asks because it is not in our allow list |

  The mode is `spawnPermissionMode(args)` over the argv the CLI receives: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` wins (2.1.281 `Rvr` makes it the first candidate), else the LAST `--permission-mode` (a user's own flag in extraArgs lands after the session's), else unknown. **The rule follows the SPAWN mode:** a mid-session mode switch (`set_permission_mode`) carries the mode alone and rewrites no settings (no `apply_flag_settings` the product sends names `permissions` — census-pinned), so a session started in `default` and switched to full access still asks for a publish until its next spawn (the mode that spawn is given decides again), and one started in full access and switched to `default` asks for a publish anyway (not allowed) unless the user's own rules allow it. A user's own inline `ask` is kept verbatim in every mode. Gate: test-agent-tool-rules ⑬ (every mode, the argv overrides, the switch, a patched copy that always injects goes red on the bypass leg).


**The phone composer + bottom panel (lane phone-chat-composer, 2026-10-13).** At ≤ 768 px the composer row is [+] [field … mic] [send]: ONE "+" door (a sheet: 图片 / 文件 / 文件夹 — the image, file and folder inputs), the microphone inside the field's trailing edge (the recording capsule takes its place), send 40×40, the field ≥ 72 % / 75 % of the row at 390 / 412, 44 px tall growing to 6 lines. **The mic and ⤢ never share a point (lane voice-everywhere, owner 2026-10-13: a mic tap hit ⤢, the editor expanded, the keyboard opened):** the mic = a 40×40 hit area at the trailing BOTTOM, ⤢ = 40×40 at the field's TOP-RIGHT corner, shown only while the box is ≥ 92 px (both hit areas + 8 px) — judged on the box's own height by a ResizeObserver. The old rule read scrollHeight on `input` only, so a multi-line SEND (value cleared, height reset, no input event) left a one-line field with ⤢ drawn ON the mic. The status bar under it is ONE 40-px row on the composer's surface: search · model · what fits, the rest behind ⋯ (a tap opens the bar in place); effort and style are rows at the top of the model chip's sheet. NEVER-FOLD set (PURE `phoneBarFold`, title-chips.js; lane phone-bar-billing-nofold): search · model · turn state · health · the billing chip (who pays — the phone's stand-in for the title bar's badge) are laid first; the billing chip takes the widest of its three forms (full → compact → icon, full words in its title) that fits beside them, the icon even with no room; only the other chips fold, in bar order. A fold is judged on the runner's fonts (DejaVu, wider), not only the hub's. The desk composer and bar are unchanged.

- **A person's first turns look healthy (lane door-healthy-chat, 2.369.344 — the naive studies on 2.369.342).** (1) A record kind the agent's CLI added (an unknown record, a known record that grew a field or a value) is never drawn in the chat: ONE quiet chip LAST in the status bar, «N record kinds this version added — Diagnostics» (src/lib/chat-bar-words.js), opens ⚙ Diagnostics; the rail's Diagnostics counter counts the day's drift kinds; the normalizer keeps the kinds (`addedKinds`, meta op `record-kinds`, attach `recordKinds`). (2) A permission card says the request in words above the command (src/command-words.js), the command folded under «Show the command» (open on a hidden character); the line above the message box says «Waiting for you to allow: …» and goes to the card. (3) From a Claude conversation's THIRD prompt the card offers «Let it work in <folder>/ without asking»: the answer carries the record's folder offer — allow Bash, Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, saved in the folder's local settings; VibeSpace's ask rules still ask. (4) PageUp / PageDown move the chat after a press in it and from the message box, and a dialog's scroll region (createModalShell). (5) A document opened before its file exists says «Waiting for the file…» and opens when it lands. (6) The cost chip says what the figure is and whether it is billed: «This chat ≈ $0.24 · included in your subscription».

### Window Manager
- **The desktop tier at a small screen (lane desktop-small, .358 — the walk at 951×585…1280×640):** a release never buries a window (every drop — and a resize's release — keeps 80×32 of its title bar inside #workspace; a Quad drop over the taskbar takes the nearest bottom cell; a workspace that shrinks re-clamps; a window whose bar is out of reach comes back wholly inside when its tile, its window-list row or any door names it); the taskbar overflows visibly (tiles ≥ 90 px, ONE «+N» chip listing the cut tiles — the list capped and scrolling — the wheel scrolls the strip) and its desktops fold into one «‹name› k/N ▾» button when their previews would crowd the tiles — its list switches, adds and keeps every preview door (a row's right-click or ⋯: Rename…, Delete, Move up / Move down — the order reaches every client; a window drag held on the button — a title bar or a taskbar tile — springs the list open, a row takes the drop and the list closes with the drag; a desktop deleted on another screen meanwhile is refused by name); every menu opens inside the screen (one placement: below, above when opened low, clamped, scrolling when taller); a chat window under 480 px wide or 300 px high keeps its status bar one row (⋯) and its messages ≥ 45 %; a new window never opens over the title bars on show; a toast never stands on an open menu or a composer.
- **✕ says the conversation keeps running (lane phone-refusal-wrap, .355; P2-2):** closing the window of a conversation that is still running — the phone's ✕, a window's or a tab's ✕, the window menu's Close — shows ONE toast «Closed the window — the conversation keeps running» (a shell: «… the terminal keeps running»; several closed at once: «Closed {n} windows — what ran in them keeps running»). No question: the close stays one tap. In the window menu a running session's Close reads «✕ Close window — it keeps running» and is not red; «Terminate session» stays red.
- Floating windows with drag/resize
- Edge snap zones (Magnet-like)
- Drag threshold (5px): prevents accidental snap when clicking title bar to focus
- Pre-snap size memory: snapping saves original window size, dragging out of snap restores it (persisted in layout)
- Freeform mode (no grid) + custom MxN grid with snap-to-cell (drag + resize snap, Alt to bypass)
- A zone SMALLER than a window's minimum (the .window floor 320×180, or a desktop app's own — Chrome ~512 CSS wide, GNOME Calculator 618 tall at 2×): the window keeps its minimum and overlaps its neighbour, and in the last column / bottom row it slides back INSIDE the workspace (4 px gutter kept) instead of hanging past the edge where #workspace clips it — every snap zone, grid cell / range, preset, layout restore / sync / desktop switch, the workspace reflow (the sidebar opening, a browser resize) for a visible AND a minimized window (r2: a minimized window is placed while hidden, so a restore after the sidebar opened lands inside), and the restore from maximize (r2: the stored box carried to a workspace that changed meanwhile as the same fractions); stored bounds land on whole layout px; a new window's default cascade is kept on the workspace too; a raise by a workspace-CAPPED minimum stays on the client that needed it (never synced); a window the person left hanging off the edge keeps its own edge (inc-muhmqvzf-jodk, 2026-09-26: `_placeWindow` → PURE `zoneBox`; gates test-window-minsize §4 + heavy test-desktop-app-snap)
- Shake-to-bypass-snap: shaking a window vigorously mid-drag latches "grid/edge snap off" for the rest of that drag (mouse-only alternative to holding Alt; cursor-following "Grid snap off" badge + dashed window outline; per-drag, re-enables next drag; `window.js` titlebar-drag path only — reversal-count detector, `layout.shakeBypassSnap` on/off default on + `layout.shakeBypassSeconds` sustained-shake duration default 1s, re-read per drag so it's live-adjustable)
- Built-in presets: maximize, 2-col, 2-row, quad, 3-col (all via grid mechanism)
- Custom grid presets: + button to add, right-click to remove, auto SVG icons, persisted
- Grid overflow: round-robin distribution when windows > cells (`i % totalCells`)
- Window menu: right-click title bar → full menu (Switch-window submenu w/ configurable scope + Rename + Task Groups + Move/Minimize/Close); □ button keeps the classic overlap popup; taskbar item right-click carries Rename/Task Groups too (2.212.0). **Side by side (split UX chunk 2, 2026-09-23):** in a tab group of ≥ 2 the menu has **Show side by side ▸ Beside {name} (on the right)** per other tab (this window left, the named one right, the focus staying on this window — split r1, every user entry keeps the focus on the window acted on — 5 s Undo toast); a split group shows **Unsplit** + **Swap left and right** instead; a chain-less / one-tab window shows neither; a phone is not offered the submenu (one pane shown). A tab's right-click opens that tab's own menu
- Overlap indicator: ⧉/□ icon on title bar shows whether other windows overlap, click opens switcher
- Command mode: `Ctrl+\` prefix key (tmux-style), [CMD] indicator in taskbar, 2s auto-exit. **`v`** = side by side on / off for the active window's tab group (active tab left, most recently used other tab right, undoable), **`V`** = swap left and right; without a group of ≥ 2 tabs a toast says "Group two windows first" (never silent); the armed hint lists `v split`. **`{` / `}`** (split tabs v2, 2026-09-25) move the active tab one place left / right within its own list (its half in a split; stays in command mode) — the same verbs as the registry chords **Ctrl+Shift+PageUp / PageDown** (app.js; inert outside a ≥ 2-tab group, a terminal passes them through only in a group; a regular browser tab may keep the chord for itself)
- Shift+drag: select rectangular cell range in grid mode, window spans entire range
- Layout history (⚙ ▸ System ▸ Restore a previous layout): a rollback point before every change of a desktop's window set, each naming what changed after it. Since 2.369.341 a restore stamps every restored record NOW — a phone or tab that slept through it is refused (stale) and adopts it, so the restore holds — and each point names the write that made it (`writer`: the desktop, the writer's viewport, its evidence by reason) and the refusals since the last one (`refused`)
- Presets (renamed from Layouts): save/restore the workspace's windows, positions, z-order and grid. Sessions matched by claudeSessionId. Non-preset windows minimized not killed. Since 2.369.274 loading one never changes the theme, the fonts or the sidebar (the layer law: those are the device's).
- Active window highlight intensity: `window.activeHighlightIntensity` setting (subtle = shadow only, normal = accent border, strong = border + glow)
- **One workspace, each device its own arrangement (§6b item 10 — THE LAYER LAW, 2.369.274; since 2026-10-13 a phone never rearranges a desktop)**: every field of the shared layout record belongs to ONE layer — the windows and their contents (shared by every device), the desktop arrangement (z-order, boxes, maximize / minimize / snap, the grid — synced between computers), a device's chrome (sidebar, bars) and the legacy preferences (theme, fonts — a computer reads them at its boot). A phone's layout save carries the record's arrangement verbatim and is stamped `viewport:'phone'` (a computer applies such a record as membership only); a window opened on the phone lands at the computer's own default box. A phone applies only the windows and a computer's minimize (hidden, listed under Minimized) — never a computer's boxes, z-order, sidebar, bars or theme. The phone's window on show is LOCAL (this tab's sessionStorage, per desktop): a reload shows it again, another client's record never switches it, and restoring a minimized window from the phone's switcher shows it on the phone only.
- Window close behavior: `window.closeBehavior` setting — **default DETACH for everything (2.108.8, user directive: no per-type exceptions)**; sessions stay alive in the sidebar for re-attach. Ephemeral helper terminals always terminate. (The 2.108.7 shell-only default was replaced by this.)
- Tab groups: drag window icon onto another window's icon to merge into Chrome-style tab group. Tab bar with rounded top tabs, active tab connects to content. Drag tab downward to pull out (follows cursor with snap); a drag that STARTS sideways reorders while the pointer stays near the bar and TEARS the tab off once the pointer is > 30 px above or below the bar (inc-muly2izg-cks3, 2026-09-28 — before, a sideways start stayed a reorder for the whole drag, so a diagonal pull never left the group). Close individual tabs. Tab chain data synced across clients via layout-sync. **Side by side (split UX, 2026-09-23, docs/design-split-ux.zh.md):** the tab merge is the ONE exception to ordinary drag-and-snap — no drag ever splits. After a merge the strip's two-column button pulses once and a 5 s toast offers "Show side by side"; the button (active tab left, the most recent other tab right) is the entry, and in a split the same button is the badge (Unsplit / Swap left and right; the divider's right-click has the same two). The strip is drawn in visual order with a bar between the pane tabs and an owner-colour underline on each; every user-initiated split shows "Side by side: A | B · Undo" for 5 s. Right-clicking a tab opens THAT tab's window menu. **Split r1:** the button's tooltip is re-written on every tab switch (it names the partner the click will use — on a ≥ 3-tab group the most recent other tab changes with each switch); a split taken any way withdraws the post-merge "Grouped as tabs" toast, and its button, if it still runs after the group changed, says "Already shown side by side" / "The tab group changed — nothing to show side by side" (never a silent no-op). **Split tabs v2 (2026-09-25, inc-muhfb5al-jzk6, docs/design-split-ux.zh.md §8 — the owner: tabs all on the left, no reorder, only the right side switchable):** in a split every tab belongs to a SIDE and the strip is TWO HALVES laid on the panes' own columns (a subgrid of the host — they follow the divider live), the glyph over the divider, each side's shown tab highlighted; a tab of the left half shows on the LEFT, of the right half on the right (D19 (a) retired). A horizontal tab drag REORDERS (marker, Esc cancels; the first 8 px decide, vertical = the old pull-out); across the middle it MOVES the tab to the other side (a shown tab stays shown there, the side it left shows its neighbour; the last tab out ends the split) — never a new split. A merge drop lands at the slot under the pointer (in a split: that half). A press inside a pane focuses that pane. A tab GROUP dragged by its title bar only moves (it used to orphan its other tabs when dropped on an icon). Settings → Window: **`window.mergeDropLayout`** tabs (default) | split — the merge lands side by side at once, the dragged window on the right, toast **Undo** (back where it stood) / **Unsplit** (back to the slot it was dropped on — v2 verify r1 ③); a drop onto a chain ALREADY split (either setting) joins the half under the pointer, shown there, with a "Side by side: A | B · Undo" toast (the window back where it stood, the split back to its sides / order / pair before the drop — r1 ④); a pointer drag first SHOWS the tab (a press shows it), so a tab dragged across arrives shown; the right column never renders narrower than the controls + a tab's room and the ⫿ badge steps aside on a tight column (r1 ②); a divider drag survives another client's structural change made during it (held locally, re-sent once — r1 ①; kb-design-lessons §6b item 7); **`window.openLinkPlacement`** split (default) | tab | window — a path / local link opened FROM A CHAT is born beside THAT chat (its own window, never the active one; on a chain already split the side the chat is not on), the same path again shows its tab (a `:line` link moves the editor), the phone keeps its own window. Other clients apply a same-member change IN PLACE (no re-parenting); a member still being replayed asynchronously keeps its chain pending (no free viewer that would break the group on the next save). **A split never moves a tab across the strip** (inc-mv4q1u6b-ksyh, the owner's right tab that went left): the ⫿ button, command mode `v`, the merge toast and the merge-drop split put each tab on the side it already sits on (PURE `splitSideFor`); the button's tooltip names the partner's side.
  - **A split tab group opens on its active window; the ⫿ words follow a rename** (2.369.263, lane split-ux-leftovers, B-9cd4): a chain rebuilt from a record around the focused window (a phone's boot, a remote apply) moves the active mark to its FRAME and names the chain's active tab (PURE `chainFocusOf`, chain-layout.js) — a phone shows only the marked window, and the mark left on a guest's hidden frame was a blank screen until a pick. Chrome text that names a window reads its live name: `setTitle` re-words the strip's ⫿ button (`_labelSplitBtn`) beside the tab label.
- Window type icons: each type has an inline SVG icon (chat bubble, terminal `>_`, folder, document, etc.) shown in title bar, tab bar, taskbar, overlap switcher. Chat/terminal windows with a backend show a composite icon (backend logo + mode badge). Taskbar icons scale uniformly via `transform:scale()`. All session card buttons (star, archive, rename, find, resume, history, terminate) use SVG icons instead of emoji.
- **The title wins over the billing chip (2.369.179, lane G, 2026-09-25; owner: "这个全部->UCI Max占据了绝大部分空间，都看不到窗口标题了")**: on a tab and on a standalone title bar the billing chip shows every word ("≋ 全部 → UCI Max") only when the whole title fits beside it; otherwise the pool glyph + the member's short name ("≋ UCI Max", cut at 8 characters) while ≥ 6 title characters still show; otherwise the glyph alone (its colour still marks pool / API / subscription — a subscription chip gets a crown in that form). The tooltip leads with the full words and the click opens the billing switcher as before. Re-decided per tab / bar on resize (one ResizeObserver per bar), a title or member change, and the owner dots / inbox chip appearing or going; the inbox chip keeps its number at its minimal width ("99+" cap). Phone layout (no title bars) and the sidebar card unchanged. Rule: PURE src/lib/title-chips.js; gates test-title-chips (fast) + test-title-chips-ui (heavy).
- Taskbar: two-row layout with large icon (18px) + title/subtitle. Items show window type icon, starred sessions prefixed with ★.
- Taskbar tab-group stacking (Windows-style): a tab-group host renders ONE stacked item (`_buildGroupItem`/`_buildStackIcon` in taskbar.js) — the unique tab icons offset like a card stack (active tab frontmost; a lone icon gets a faded ghost behind), a count badge, titled by the active tab + "N windows grouped". Click → ACTIVATE the group (lane K, 2026-09-25, owner "这个体验比较差" — the old click was always the chooser): restore + focus + raise its active tab through `activateWindow`, the single button's own path; a click while the group is IN FRONT (host or a tab focused, unminimized, on this desktop — PURE `inFrontOf`) = the `showTabGroupList` chooser (click one → restore+focus group + `switchTab`); HOVER with 300 ms intent on a mouse or a pen (never touch / a drag / another popover) = the same chooser, non-modal, closing 250 ms after the pointer leaves button + chooser — armed by the pointer MOVING over the button once per visit, a press spending the visit until the pointer leaves, the visit kept per group so a taskbar rebuild under a resting pointer (a tab title change) grows nothing (2.369.184, PURE `hoverStep`); Enter/Space = the click rule, ArrowUp = the chooser. Decisions PURE in src/lib/taskbar-group.js (gates test-taskbar-group + test-taskbar-group-ui). The chooser's ONE cleanup (a MutationObserver, whichever path removed it) also aborts createPopover's outside-click close (`pop._closeCtl`) — verify r1's minor finding, pinned by test-taskbar-group-ui (j) (30 hover cycles, document mousedown listeners unchanged; CONTROL 2 = the disposer reverted ⇒ +30) and test-taskbar-group §7/§9. Right-click on the button acts on the whole group; right-click on a chooser ROW = that tab's window menu (the window list's row pattern), the chooser pinned beneath and re-listed from the live chain after the action (a Move closes it). **The five verify-r1 lows, fixed in the same lane (2026-09-25; each reproduced red on a scratch server with a real mouse, now a red→green leg with a control):** ① a reload shows a restored tab group as ONE grouped button with no input — tab-group.js `restoreTabChain` ends with `_notify()` like every other chain mutation (before: separate single buttons until the first window event, so the first click after a reload landed on a single button); ② a taskbar rebuild under an open chooser (a tab title change re-keys the structure) RE-ANCHORS it — `_buildGroupItem` hands the new button to `pop._chooser.reanchor()`: `aria-expanded="true"`, the outside-click close's live exclusion list, and Esc focus / the cleanup's reset / placement read the live anchor (before: the rebuilt button said "false", Esc dropped the focus on body, a click on it closed and re-created the chooser); ③ a PEN hovers like a mouse (`pointerType` mouse or pen with `(any-pointer: fine)`; touch never); ④ right-click on a chooser row (above; before: the browser's native menu); ⑤ the dead `.taskbar-window-list` (nothing produces it — the window list is `overlap-switcher`, a [data-popover]) is gone from `_otherPopoverOpen` and from app.js's autohide conceal guard, and test-taskbar-group §7's PRODUCER CENSUS keeps every class those two guards query produced by the tree, each guard's pre-fix spelling as its control. Gates: test-taskbar-group-ui (k)–(n) + CONTROL 2 (the fixes reverted ⇒ each red), test-taskbar-group §7 pins + the census + §9 `liveExclusion`. active/minimized/waiting is group-aware (`_applyTaskbarItemState`, reads `dataset.groupTabs`). Previously only the host showed and every guest silently vanished from the taskbar.
- Closing a whole tab group asks first (B-a67c, 2.369.203; the owner: "当窗口是tabbed或者side by side的时候，注意点击整体的关闭要有个警告提示确认要关闭x个标签页吗，避免想关闭tab但点错"): the frame's ✕ of a tabbed or side-by-side group, its title-bar menu's and the taskbar group button's "Close group" open the house dialog "Close {n} tabs?" listing every tab by the name its tab shows ("Close {n} tabs" = Enter, Cancel = Esc) and then close every tab — before, they closed only the group's first (host) tab, usually not the one on show. A tab's own ✕ or menu, a lone window and programmatic closes never ask; no setting. One gate: tab-group.js `requestCloseGroup` ⇒ kb-file-structure (tab-group.js).
- Taskbar right-click context menu: Move (full-screen overlay blocks all interaction, restores from maximized/snapped), Minimize/Restore, Close
- Move mode: window restores to original size, full-screen overlay prevents interaction with other UI elements
- Virtual desktops: multiple independent workspaces with per-desktop grid/layout. Ubuntu-style miniature previews in taskbar corner showing window positions. Click to switch, drag window to move between desktops, Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right shortcut. Waiting windows blink yellow in preview. Resizable taskbar (36-120px) with auto-scaling elements.
  - **The phone classes' Desktops door (lane desktop-switch-phone, 2.369.356 hotfix — userW on the Duo's inner display: «如何在这个界面下切换桌面？»)**: the switcher above lives in the taskbar's corner and neither phone class shows the taskbar — the regular class had no way to another desktop, the compact one only a tap on the nav title nobody found. Now ONE **Desktops** button on #mobile-nav (src/lib/mobile-nav.js `_buildDesktopsDoor`, icon `UI_ICONS.desktops`): the compact bar beside the title, the regular class's trailing bar FIRST in its bottom section (before Task Groups; portrait: after the title); the active desktop's number as its badge when there are two or more, «Desktops — <name> (k/N)» as its label. A tap = THE SHEET (src/lib/desktop-switch-sheet.js over PURE src/desktop-switch.js; the phone's `.mobile-sheet` under the nav on the compact class; beside the button, into the conversation column, on the regular class): one 44 px row per desktop — its name, «N windows» (the built ones + the held record's unbuilt ones), the active one marked, up to three window titles greyed and «N not opened on this screen yet» for the held ones — then «+ New desktop» (= the taskbar's «+»); a long press on a row = Rename · Delete (the manager's own verbs; Delete moves the windows to the next desktop, as the taskbar's). A desktop deleted elsewhere meanwhile is said by name, never switched to. A row = `switchDesktop`: the manager's own `switchTo` (the Stage left first, as the preview's click), then the desktop's window on show (§6b guard 10: the one this tab showed there, else its topmost; a lazy replay is waited for). The nav TITLE's window switcher (its `.mobile-desk-tabs` strip) opens in the regular class too (its landscape: a tap on the conversation's title bar) and its tabs take the same road. The door follows every desktop change (`_renderSwitcher` → `updateDesktopsDoor`) and every window change (`updateTitle`). On a desktop the ⧉ window list (taskbar.js `showWindowList`) keeps its active-desktop view and folds «Other desktops (N)» under it: each row «<title> · <desktop>» switches there AND raises the window (a window that desktop's record holds and this page never built is built by the switch, then raised). Gates: fast test-desktop-switch, test-phone-doors ⑥ (wiring pins), heavy test-duo-layout ⑧ (951 + 382 touch) + ⑨ (the ⧉ group, THE DOOR CENSUS with its RED CONTROL).
  - **The desktop doors are ONE table (lane desktop-doors-table, .359)**: Rename…, Delete, Move up, Move down, switch and «New desktop» come from PURE `desktopDoors` (src/desktop-switch.js) on every surface — the taskbar's preview and compact list, the phone sheet, the phone window switcher's tabs; the phone can reorder desktops (a long press: Move up / Move down), a door that cannot act there is greyed with its reason. An OPEN desktop list (the taskbar's compact list, the phone sheet, the window switcher's tabs) follows a change made on another screen: renamed and moved desktops redraw, a deleted one keeps its row greyed with «“name” is no longer there» (its doors and its tap say the same); a door pressed after the list changed is judged then, and a refused one says why. An open list never swaps the row under your pointer (it is updated in place); a rename made on another screen while your Rename dialog is open is named when your name replaces it. An open list that grows stays on the screen: its rows keep their place, what is added past the bottom scrolls, and a very long name is cut short. A list you scrolled stays where you scrolled it, even after the window gets taller.
- Dynamic desktop (Stage) — THE MOVE RULE SPEAKS (inc-muly2izg-cks3, 2026-09-28): windows never move between the Stage and a normal desktop, in either direction (the owner's 2.112.4 rule, unchanged), but a refusal is now SAID: a Stage window dragged by its title bar over a desktop preview marks the preview (dashed, the theme's yellow) and a line beside the pointer says "Windows on the Stage stay on the Stage" / "The conversation stays on the Stage" (a desktop window over the Stage preview: "Windows can't be moved onto the Stage"); the drop puts the window back where the drag began and a toast says what to do instead; "Move to Desktop ▸" on a Stage window holds ONE row saying why; a taskbar item dropped on a preview and command mode's move keys say the same (PURE src/lib/stage-rules.js). A tab torn out of a group on the Stage stays on the Stage in the hero's workspace and is VISIBLE where it was let go (2.369.196 left the Stage's hide on a group member the Stage had not bound — e.g. the agent's live view opened while the Stage was off screen — so the pulled-out window was invisible); the hero's whole group comes back with it on every re-enter.
  - **The shared hero's publish law** (lane stage-hero-key-race, .272 — rel271's Actions mirror): the Stage's hero is shared (`stage/hero`; the 挂机 walk-over — another device's operations win) and every publish is stamped by the page that wrote it. A page follows the shared hero only when another client wrote it since the record the page last stood on, so its own newest pick is never undone by the record that pick replaced. A conversation picked before its session id exists is published the moment the id lands, on the Stage or off it — unless another device picked since.
- Loading screen: inline splash with animated progress bar, waits for workspace restore to complete before fading out
- pointer-events:none on window content during drag (prevents iframe/terminal stealing mouse events)

### Session Management

- **Session Properties = the Task Group window's body shape (lane session-props-scroll, .351).** Root `.task-detail session-props` → ONE scrolling `.task-detail-body` (built once) → every section: padding 10 / 12, 10 px between sections, a 72 px label column (`flex: 0 0 72px`; a longer label wraps, the row aligns on its first baseline). A re-render refills the BODY, keeps its scroll offset, and the history / steps lists hold their old height until their refetch paints. The `.task-detail-body` class IS the contract: never padding / overflow on a window's own root (census test-task-detail-body; Chrome leg in test-task-detail-chrome).
- **The New Session form in two columns (lane new-session-form, .346 — the owner accepted POC v2.2; the folding by the fleet census, SharedContext/vibespace-new-session-field-census.md).** LEFT 「在哪、怎么跑」 = the harness's own flags: 机器和文件夹 (会话名称 ABOVE 工作目录 — the name's empty placeholder, and the name sent when it stays empty, is the folder's own name; it feeds the path field's 由名字 rows), 后端和模型 (the backend as a segmented switch over the hidden `#input-backend`, model + effort, permission, 可用工具 only where `capsOf(backend).toolAllowlist` exists), then 「更多选项」: machine · account · additional arguments · git worktree, each unfolding by itself when the person's own data says so (a paired machine used in the last 30 days, ≥ 2 accounts for the harness, a git folder — PURE `src/lib/new-session-model.js` unfoldReasons; the fold's open state per device, `vs.newSession.moreOpen`). The header's Agent | Terminal switch replaces the Mode row (no Browser kind: no New-Session road to a browser-only session). RIGHT 「能用什么」 (#ns-right, src/lib/new-session-form.js): built-in rows locked on; VibeSpace = Sessions (locked) + the 任务组 chips — SEVERAL, in the order picked (`taskIds`), Channels (a pointer to the accounts below), Browser (ONLY the profiles the picked groups admit — GET /api/browser/admits, the keeper's mayAttach; a pick is judged again at create and never ADDED to «Who can use it», the Agent browser panel keeps that road), vault / automation keys / outside · notifications as read-only facts with their doors; 「账号 · 以你的身份」 = the channel accounts, ONE list: a picked group's / everyone's grant shown ticked and locked, the rest ticks — a tick writes `{principal: this conversation, authority: draft}` through `PUT /api/channels/adapters/:id/access` once the conversation's own id exists (src/new-session-spec.js withCreateAccess; the task binds' own wait rule); 无 | 已选 | 全部 over those ticks; MCP a fact with the Integrations door. The footer says why Create cannot run yet in words («Cannot create yet: Choose a folder first» — the path field's verdict; an empty folder is refused now), else the run's values as chips (a folded row's chip dashed; a chip opens its row).
