Exceptions (例外…) come from grants-unify later — nothing is drawn for them. The path field is lane path-field's component (its contract; a stub of it until L1 lands).
- **The folder follows the Task Group until the person edits it (lane new-session-group-folder-link, .351 — the owner: × a group, pick another, the folder did not change).** The form keeps WHERE its folder came from (PURE `src/lib/new-session-model.js` folderOn*: `{ value, origin, from }`, origin `empty` · `derived-group` · `prefill-cwd` · `typed`). A folder that follows (empty, or derived) is re-derived on every change of the picked groups (add / remove / reorder) and of the machine: the FIRST picked group's first folder (a group without one passes the turn; a `host::/path` folder counts on that machine only), none ⇒ empty. Opened from a group (its folder + its id) ⇒ derived; opened on a folder (a folder's «+», the palette, Files) ⇒ the person's place, kept. Typed, picked from the list, a chip or the picker ⇒ `typed`, never moved by a group change. Emptied ⇒ it follows again: refilled when the person LEAVES the field (or at the next group change), never under the caret. The field shows a derived value through `pf.setDerived(text, { note })` — its line reads «= ~/workspace/studio（来自任务组「工作」）», a typed one «= …» alone. ONE chips row under the field (the path field's own `chips: true`, `#cwd-recent` adopted): the 由名字 chips — `<group folder>/<name>` per picked group + `~/<name>`, live with every keystroke of the name, 新建 once the machine said it is not there, none while the name is empty — then the day-one chips (the picked groups' folders + their sub-folders that hold sessions, the home's folders with files, the last used, recent). A chip is a pick; a 新建 one is ticked and made only at Create (`pf.ensure()`).
- **The v3 form (lane new-session-layout-v3-build, .351 — the owner nodded the Fable POC 2026-10-23; design: /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/new-session-layout-v3/design.md).** THE LEFT ORDER: 会话名称 → **任务组** (a first-class field beside the name: chips in pick order = `taskIds`, the sentence of what membership brings; none = a plain grey sentence) → 工作目录 (its candidates and its derived value come from the groups above) → 后端 (harnesses only) → 模型·强度 → 权限模式 → 可用工具 → 更多选项 (machine · account · arguments · **the harness's own terminal UI** · git worktree, folded by data). THE RULE — one choice, one place: the header's **Agent | Terminal** is the only mode door; Terminal = a login shell with no harness (no backend card, the fold keeps the machine, the right column keeps 「会话」 + one sentence); running a harness in its own TUI (the old Mode Terminal + Claude, ws-create's pty-wrapper) is the fold's tick «Run in the harness’s own terminal UI» (Settings' default mode Terminal ticks it and shows it). THE RIGHT reads the left: 「会话」 says which groups it joined and how many sessions it reaches («Change on the left ↖»), 频道 has one tick per account (a group grant ticked + locked with its 「除了」), then the browser profiles the groups admit, the vault and automation keys as facts. Gone: the shell backend chip, 无 | 已选 | 全部, the MCP empty row, 「对外 · 通知」, the separate accounts card. THE PHONE: a full-screen sheet (header + footer fixed, the footer one sideways-scrolling line), the right column an accordion with a summary per resource, the group picker a bottom sheet, 16 px inputs, ≥ 32 px targets, the backend a native select. Create is PURE `createPlan` (the v2 payload, byte-equal for the same choices).
- **The CLI's own session title (lane session-title-record):** claude 2.1.288 names a session itself a few turns in (`system/session_title_changed`). That title names the conversation in the sidebar row, the window title and the taskbar — below a user's rename and a name given at creation, above the first-message rule (src/session-name.js). It renders no card (known-ignored); it is persisted in session meta (`cliTitle`) and read back from the transcript by discovery on every machine (TT scanner lines). Codex/ACP have no such record — the rung is simply absent.
- **Run a session in its own git worktree (owner ruling 9, claude only).** The New Session dialog and Session Properties each carry a "Run in a git worktree" checkbox — gated on the harness capability row, so a harness whose CLI has no such flag simply has no row (and any tick is cleared, so a stale checkbox can never ride a create). Ticked, the spawn passes **only** `--worktree` (never `--tmux`: dtach is our persistence layer, and a tmux inside it is a second multiplexer nobody attaches to). The CLI creates `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>` on a `worktree-<name>` branch and works there, so the agent never touches the tree you are editing. **If the folder is not a git repository the create is REFUSED with a reason** — the CLI would otherwise exit before the session existed, leaving an instantly-dead window — and the refusal names the escape hatch the CLI itself recommends (`git init`, or a `WorktreeCreate` hook for another VCS). Remote (ssh/dial) sessions carry the choice through the same builder as every other flag, and the preflight asks the session's own machine. The session card wears a small worktree badge and Session Properties shows **the path the CLI itself announced** (both read the fact off the live session list, which is also the `live` half the fork asks — so a fork of a running isolated session asks for a worktree even when nothing was ever saved) (its own init-frame cwd — never a path we compose from a naming rule, which a `WorktreeCreate` hook could put anywhere). The choice survives resume/restart/fork: **a fork of an isolated conversation starts a fresh worktree** (the CLI strips the binding, so the fork asks again — with the standing pick if there is one, else with whatever the run being forked turned out to be), while a plain resume re-enters whatever the CLI recorded — so the flag is emitted on a new session and on a fork only, never on a resume. Because a resume never sends the flag, a resume is never refused for it either: the not-a-git-repo refusal applies to the spawns that actually pass `--worktree`, so a conversation whose folder stopped being a repo still resumes. **Unticking the box sticks**: the checkbox is a tri-state preference, so an explicit "no" outlives a run that happens to be isolated, and a live fact only ever fills in a choice you never made. If the recorded worktree is gone the CLI continues in the plain directory and says so; the badge follows that fact and disappears, while the saved preference stays yours to change. **Resuming an isolated conversation keeps the badge**: a resume starts in the conversation's own recorded directory — which for these sessions IS the worktree — so "the CLI reported the directory we launched it in" cannot by itself mean "not isolated"; the server asks git whether that directory really is a linked worktree, and only retires the badge when the answer is no. When it cannot get an answer at all (no git, an unreachable machine) it changes nothing rather than guessing.

Its confirm names the live sessions it reaches and the open stopped / read-only ones it skips, with an editable note pre-filled per language (≤ 2 000 characters, control characters out). 确定 ⇒ `POST /api/sessions/refresh-note` (cookie only) ⇒ the note is stashed into each LIVE conversation (`fromName` 'VibeSpace refresh', `ref` 'refresh-note'), so it rides that conversation's NEXT turn: free, never a wake, never the spend guard. A note still waiting is replaced, never doubled. Every client's strip above the composer shows it (a VibeSpace notice). Plan = PURE src/refresh-note.js; delivery = stash-handover.js `refreshLive`; UI = src/lib/refresh-live.js. Gates: test-refresh-note (fast), test-refresh-note-chrome (heavy).

So a short name + wide "working" chip → icon; a long name → text. - **★ Task Group (岗位) concept refactor — 2.39.0 (read this before the historical bullets below; it supersedes them where they conflict).** The code's "Task"/`TaskManager`/`tasks.json` was really the user's **Task Group (岗位 — a persistent ROLE)**; the user's "Task" is a **session (活儿)**; the user's "Task Status" is our **session status**. What changed across the P1–P6 refactor + P0 rename (design: docs/design-task-refactor.md; full log: memory `project-task-system`):
  - **★ CHECKLIST REMOVED — 2.121.0 (user decision; supersedes every checklist/plan mention below).** A group-level checklist of agent WORK ITEMS never made sense: agents don't care about other agents' backlogs — work items live at the SESSION level (the agent's own native todo list, already surfaced as the card's Steps per 2.46.0). Removed everywhere: task-detail Checklist section, task-log Checklist tab, `vibespace-task plan-*` subcommands (print a redirect; `/api/agent/task-plan` = 410 responder for old remote CLI copies), injected context Checklist section + teaching line, diff-update checklist deltas, TASK.md, repo export (import still recognizes legacy `## Checklist`/`## Plan` headings as section STOPS, content dropped). Stored `plan` arrays stay DORMANT in data/task-groups.json (update() ignores plan patches, list() strips it, config-bundle import passes it through — nothing destroyed). `_showTaskChecklistPopover` was renamed `_showTaskBindPopover` (it was always the group-BIND popover, unrelated to the checklist).
  - **★ BACKLOG ADDED — 2.122.0 (user decision; a DIFFERENT concept than the removed checklist).** The group's PARKING LOT for **non-immediate** items: decisions the user deferred, work they said comes later — the class that previously had no home (session todo = immediate steps; activity log = past; vibespace-ask inbox = act-now notifications). Field `backlog` on the group: {text ≤500, detail? ≤6000, status open|done|dropped, addedBy/addedAt, resolvedBy/resolvedAt, **priority high|normal|low** (2.369.154)}; NO cap since 2026-09-22 (a bound belongs to a read); contentUpdatedAt bumps on backlog edits. **PRIORITY + OWNERSHIP SELECT EVERY READ (2.369.154, owner 2026-09-22):** `src/backlog-select.js` orders every listing (open by priority, newest first within one) and picks each session's reminders — its ≤5 highest-priority newest CLAIMED items, one `- unclaimed HIGH:` line naming the open high items nobody owns (so they cannot rot), everything else a count; `backlog-add/-edit --priority`; the CLI numbers the sorted list and a number means the item printed under it in the list that session was LAST SHOWN (another session's add never moves it; `backlog-done` prints what it resolved); a high item whose claimants are no longer running counts as unowned; the repo task file escapes a text beginning `! `/`↓ ` and reads markers only in files that declare `backlog_priority: markers`. Agents: `vibespace-task backlog / backlog-add "item" [--detail] / backlog-done <n|text> / backlog-drop` (resolve indexes the OPEN-items list as displayed) — taught to park when the user defers something and to NEVER start parked items unasked. **Injection is SUMMARY-ONLY (user directive, load-bearing): the hook never dumps backlog content** — `renderContext`/`renderMultiContext` take `sessionKey` (threaded from agent-routes) and `_backlogNoteLines` emits a ≤5-line reminder block ONLY for open items THAT session parked, else a single count+pointer line; the FULL list lives in TASK.md (cap>0 renderings), `show`, and the UI; backlog CHANGES arrive as one-line diff events (PARKED/RESOLVED/DROPPED/REMOVED, occurrence-indexed like the retired checklist diff — same duplicate-text bug class, covered by tests). UI: task-detail Backlog section (open items, ✓/⊘, park input, resolved-count link) + task-log Backlog tab (2.369.154: rows in sortBacklog order, a High/Low chip per non-normal row, priority set from the row's right-click `Priority ▸` submenu or the ✎ editor — one whole-backlog write, the broadcast repaints); repo file round-trips `- [ ]/[x]/[-]`. One-time seed migration: the dormant plan's UNCHECKED items → open backlog items (guard `backlog === undefined`; dormant plan itself untouched).
  - **★ THE CONTEXT TABLE — 2.369.346 (lane task-group-context, POC v2.2 + the owner's fourth level; supersedes every `folders[]` / `contextDir` / "context-folder index" mention below).** A Task Group's `ctx` is ONE ordered list of rows (PURE `src/task-context.js` holds the rules): `{ path (as typed), note, tell, tags, share, keys? }` or a reference row `{ ref, note }`. **Resolution:** a rooted path (`/…`, `~…`, `host::/…`) is itself; a RELATIVE one resolves against the row above's folder, then the group's first folder (the first rooted row that is a folder), then home — the first that exists (`resolveRows`, the store's stat behind the mount door; 4 s cache). **Derived, never stored twice:** the 自动发现会话 (`discover`) rows ARE the old `folders[]` (membership by cwd, recursive — `foldersOf`; a rooted folder matches by its string even while absent, as before); the agent 在这里记笔记 (`notes`, ONE row) row IS the old `contextDir` (`contextDirOf`; the `.vibespace/TASK.md` mirror lives there). The wire (`list()` / `view()`) carries `ctx` + `ctxRes` (where each row points) + the DERIVED `folders` / `contextDir` so every older reader keeps working. **告诉 agent — four levels:** 只说明 (path + note) · 文件名 (+ the listing, relative names + sizes) · 文件名 + 关键文件内容 (+ the CONTENTS of the row's key files — default CLAUDE.md, README.md, HANDOFF.md, handbook.md, TASK.md, top level only, editable per row as `keys`) · 内容 (every file's contents); defaults: a folder 文件名 + 关键文件内容, a file 内容. Verbs: 自动发现会话 · agent 在这里记笔记 · 不许 agent 改 (excludes 记笔记; shares only read-only) · 其他任务组可引用 (`share: ro|rw`). A reference row tells the rows group X marked shareable, LAST, read-only here unless X shared them 可写; X's table edits reach the referencing group's gate (`contentAtOf` = max(own content instant, X's `ctxUpdatedAt`)). **The injection (`renderContext` / `renderMultiContext`):** the objective first under «## Objective — the group's standing rules» (the ONE home of rules — study 3 C4), the tools section, THEN the Context block — every row's line «- <path> — <note> (<verbs>)» at its depth in table order, within ONE budget = min(`tasks.contextIndexBytes`, default 10 KB; the room the 9600 B inline cap leaves after the head, the notes teaching and the log's floor); a row that does not fit STEPS DOWN (内容 → 文件名 + 关键文件内容 → 文件名 → 只说明, THE rule `planRows`) and its line SAYS what it needed and what was left (a walk past 400 files / a file past 64 KB "cannot be told whole"; at 只说明 it points at `vibespace-task show --full`, which lists every row's files). Several groups share the room (each its budget and an even share of what is left). **The diff:** the snapshot carries `ctxHash` + row keys; a removed row is named, an added / changed row is re-told at its depth (a 2.4 KB slice); a file under a 文件名 row is a one-line delta, a file told by its CONTENTS changed ⇒ the full delivery; the LITE persisted snapshot keeps the hash only (a changed table ⇒ full). **The one migration** `2026-10-task-group-context-rows` (through the live store): `folders[]` → rows 文件名 + 自动发现会话, `contextDir` → a row 文件名 + 记笔记 (merged when it IS a folder); the old fields stay in the FILE one release (held aside at load in `_legacy`, written back by `_save`, read only by the migration). The OLD write doors (create/update `folders` / `contextDir` — the CLI, a manager agent, an old bundle) still work, as the rows they mean (`applyLegacyPatch`). **The window (task-detail.js):** tabs 设置 · Backlog · 活动记录 · 成员; 设置 = 名称 → 说明 / 常驻指令 → the table (the path field per L1's contract — a STUB until the integrator wires lane path-field's — note, the 4-way 告诉 agent, the key-file chips, verbs, ×; ＋ 添加路径… / ＋ 引用另一个任务组…; the budget bar) → 「新对话会收到」 (GET /api/tasks/:id/context — renderContext's exact output, the group's part shown, «显示全部» the whole) → 更多选项 (value chips); Backlog / 活动记录 = the log viewer mounted (task-log.js `mountTaskLog`); 成员 = rows with ★ (the session star) / 移出 / 「在这里开始对话」. BLUR COMMITS (src/lib/blur-commit.js): a value that resolves takes effect on blur / Enter (after the pointer-up); one that does not keeps its text and says 未生效 across repaints.
  - **Status lives on the session, not the group.** Session STATES = `working/needs-input/blocked/review/done` (`done` added). A Task Group has NO status — only `archived` (a role never "completes"). The `vibespace-task status` subcommand and `/api/agent/task-status` are gone; `done` is reported via `vibespace-status done`.
  - **A session belongs to 0..N Task Groups, derived LIVE** (`TaskGroupManager.groupsForSession({sessionKey,cwd,initialGroupId})` = explicit `sessions[]` tag ∪ auto-include folder match ∪ spawned-into group; archived excluded). A UI bind/drag/folder change reaches the agent on its NEXT turn with no respawn — the old single `session._taskId` is GONE (replaced by `_initialGroupId`, which only covers the pre-bind window). `VIBESPACE_TASK_ID` spawn env + the hook `?taskId=` were removed — belonging is resolved server-side from the `vsst_` token alone. **A conversation opened INTO a group is a MEMBER (lane open-task-binds, .346):** ws-create's `_birthBind` → conversation-ops `settleBirthGroups` binds it into `sessions[]` through the one bind writer once it has its own id (every opener: New Session, an automation's `--task`, a fork's first group), and a folder includes itself (PURE src/task-membership.js `insideFolder`; a stored `<path>/**` is the recursive switch).
  - **Injection covers every belonged group** (`renderMultiContext`), gated per-group by `session._groupSeenAt[groupId]` + a `contextDirSignature` (so a UI edit, another session's `vibespace-task`, OR user-written files in a group's contextDir all re-inject that group next turn). Per-group **`injectContext`** toggle (task-detail checkbox) opts a group out of injection while keeping belonging/board/vibespace-task working. Baseline `vibespace-status` intro still goes to sessions in NO group.
  - **The seen marks persist; the index is budgeted (B-86d3, lane hook-seen-marks).** The gate's marks (`_groupSeenAt`, `_ctxSig` as a DIGEST, a LITE `_groupSnap` — only the items this session parked or claimed, the only ones a diff speaks of — `_preambleSeen`, the intros' build, `_jobsEventsSeenTs`) live in the session meta's `seenMarks` (src/seen-marks.js), written by `persistSeenMarks` beside each hook route's answer (when SENT, only on a change) and restored by boot-restore `sessionFromMeta`. A restart's first prompt therefore re-sends only what changed: unchanged groups are named in ONE `<vibespace-task-unchanged>` line (decided before the blocks), a moved group arrives as its diff, a changed folder (digest mismatch) or a session holding > 24 items re-sends that group whole, the tools / manager intros come again only under a new build. No marks in the meta ⇒ everything once (as before). SessionStart always sends the full context (its source — startup / resume / compact — is not passed). Each group's context-folder INDEX spends at most `tasks.contextIndexBytes` (default 4096; 0 = the 100-file cap only): the newest files that fit in path order + one `… +M more (older) — vibespace-task [--group <id>] show --full` line; `show --full` (GET /api/agent/task?full=1 → `contextIndex`, belted) lists every file. Measured 13 sessions × 3 real-shape groups: restart 121.4 KB → 3.8 KB (nothing moved) / 10.9 KB (the busy group moved); the 158-file group's SessionStart is no longer cut inside its index.
  - **Live sync is a DELTA, the model's facts are read off the loop (lane task-group-fanout).** A store write names its groups; ONE broadcaster (src/server/task-fanout.js) sends, coalesced over 400 ms, only what moved per group (the fields, the Activity entries added / cleared, the Backlog items by id, the members in / out) numbered `{epoch, base, seq}`; the sidebar's mirror takes a frame only when it follows exactly, else fetches GET /api/tasks again (never a stale board); an open Task Group window / log repaints only for its own group (another group's member / title move for the window), the board, Session Properties, the pickers and the browser trace view only when something but a log moved. `session-status-updated` carries the touched keys only. An ARCHIVED conversation leaves every group's `sessions[]` (the one unbind writer; one still RUNNING keeps its groups until it ends — its next turn needs their context; the 2026-10-task-group-archived-members migration pruned the old ones, archived first). The hook's Context signature is read OFF the main thread each turn (≤ 1 s); a group whose folders did not answer in time is deferred whole to the next turn — never told from a fact that was not read, never dropped.
  - **★ WHAT A MEMBER IS TOLD PER TURN — relevance first, existence always, a cut drops the oldest (lane injection-relevance, 2.369.353; the injection audit of 2026-10-24: half of the other sessions' lines logged inside a member's span never reached it — 97 % to the 8-line count — the lines addressed to it among them, a third of the 8 slots its own lines, others' parks never named mid-session).** An update's activity (`diffChanges` → `renderNewActivity`) reads `- New activity (23, 4 of them yours — not repeated) — 8 told (2 addressed to you first), 11 more below by session:`, then ≤ 6 digest lines `  - <session> logged N more — newest: "<first ≤ 48 chars>"` (+ `(K addressed to you)`) and ONE `  - … N more from M other sessions`, THEN the picked lines in time order — existence before text. Inside the same 8 lines / 2200 B: the member's own lines are counted, never repeated (only its own new ⇒ no section, no delivery); the others' rank 0 addressed (its key or uuid head, its NAME — whole or an identifier-like word of it — or a backlog id it parked or claims) · 1 group-wide (ask / blocked / needs-input / waiting on / for-you / urgent, 待你 / 阻塞 / 卡住 / 需要你 / 请你 / 等你, or an open HIGH id) · 2 the rest · 3 a cleared entry (counted, never quoted), newest first inside a rank, a line that does not fit SKIPPED. `bits` stays `N new activity`. **Others' backlog (F2):** `- Backlog: 3 parked (1 HIGH [B-…]), 2 resolved by others since your last update — \`vibespace-task backlog\`` on a turn where they moved it (a restored LITE snapshot judges the others' items by time — after its last activity line). **Every cut drops the oldest (F1):** `renderDiffBlock` (5000 B) and `renderContextDiffMulti` (6500 B, the biggest group first) re-pick through the result's unenumerated `act.pick(room)` before any pop; `renderContext` / `renderMultiContext` take a `cap` and re-pick their logs (the header still counts); prompt-context fits its group blocks into the room left by re-rendering them (the last first) and SessionStart caps its context beside the preamble — capInline's tail cut (it took the NEWEST: every log prints oldest → newest) is the last resort. No persisted-shape change (seen-marks, the LITE snapshot untouched).

- vibespace-task CLI (2.33.0 local, 2.34.0 remote): agents report task-level updates — `progress "note" [--detail]`, `show [--full]` (the `plan-*` subcommands left with the checklist in 2.121.0; `status` left in 2.39.0) — scoped server-side to the session's live Task-Group belonging; taught by the injected context rules. REMOTE (2.34.0): distributed to `~/.vibespace/bin` on the remote and reaches VIBESPACE_API through the ssh reverse tunnel — verified writing back from the devbox.
- Anti-misconfiguration for the agent tools (2.37.0): both `vibespace-task` and `vibespace-status` print usage AND the current state on NO args, list valid subcommands on an unknown one, and validate their enum locally. NOTE (superseded by 2.39.0): `vibespace-task status` no longer exists — a Task Group has no status; a session reports its own state via `vibespace-status <working|needs-input|blocked|review|done>`. `renderContext`'s "How to report back" was rewritten: `vibespace-task` commands are scoped to the session's live Task-Group belonging via the `vsst_` token (with >1 group the agent passes `--group`, validated to be one it belongs to — there is no `session._taskId` anymore), and "run bare to self-check" is the fallback. **Injection ORDER + SIZE are load-bearing (2.68.0, real incident; THRESHOLD corrected 2026-07-13 by empirical test):** hook additionalContext up to ~10KB reaches the model FULLY INLINE (verified: a 9.8KB block's end-marker was seen). The wrap threshold is EXACTLY 10240 bytes = 10 KiB (binary-searched: 10000 inline ✓, 10240 wrapped ✗). At/above 10 KiB Claude Code wraps it in `<persisted-output>` — a ~2KB inline preview PLUS the full content saved to a file the agent can Read (verified at 30KB/60KB). So there is NO 2KB hard cap (the old note misread this); the 2.68.0 failure was a 24KB Activity-log-FIRST payload crossing the wrap threshold → agents got a useless log preview + never Read the file for the tools. claude-mem uses the IDENTICAL additionalContext mechanism — no magic. prompt-context (agent-routes.js) HARD-CAPS the final additionalContext at 9600 bytes (margin under 10240) — tail-truncates the oldest activity-log lines at a UTF-8-safe newline boundary + appends a `show --full` pointer, keeping the tools-first HEAD always inline — the old layout (24KB Activity log first, tool rules last) meant agents saw a pure-log preview and NEVER learned the vibespace tools (observed fleet-wide non-usage). renderContext now orders identity/objective → HOW TO REPORT BACK → context folder → Activity log LAST, with the log BYTE-BUDGETED (total ≤ ~8KB, newest entries win, ≥3 ≤12, "last N of M" pointer; renderMultiContext splits the budget across groups). TASK.md keeps 50 entries.
- Repo task files (2.34.0, P4): a task ⇄ a committable markdown file. Task detail window "Repo file" → Export (frontmatter id/title/kind/status/color + objective + activity log); board "Import…" card reads such a file back into the store (frontmatter authoritative; existing sessions/folders/progress preserved). Server `TaskManager.exportToFile/importFromFile` + `/api/tasks/:id/export|import`. The store stays authoritative — the file is a projection/seed, never live-parsed.
- Task context injection (2.34.0, P2 — hook-ONLY, NEVER message injection): the user's message text is sent VERBATIM; task context + status-override notices ride the harness's OWN native hooks via `data/bin/vibespace-hook.mjs` (registered for BOTH `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit`). Rewriting the user's input to smuggle context (the earlier codex/remote "first message" approach) was RIPPED OUT — it bypasses the CLI and is unstable (user directive 2026-07-05). Hook output MUST be ONLY the nested `{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName, additionalContext}}` shape — an extra top-level `additionalContext` key makes CODEX reject the whole object (its `*HookSpecificOutputWire` schema is `additionalProperties:false`); Claude is lenient but reads the same nested field (2.1.201 binary hints "Did you mean hookSpecificOutput"). **`/api/agent/task-context`** (SessionStart) delivers context, sets `_taskCtxDelivered` (gated `backend!=='codex'`); **`/api/agent/prompt-context`** (UserPromptSubmit) delivers context on the FIRST prompt when SessionStart didn't (codex path) + any pending status-override notice (consumed once). **Per-turn micro-reminder (2.78.0, user request):** when NOTHING bigger is delivered on a prompt, the route returns a ~330-byte `<vibespace-reminder>` one-liner (status/ask/task, `--group <id>` variant for multi-group) so tools stay in the agent's working context on long sessions — the start-of-session rules scroll out and usage decays. Gated by `agents.perTurnToolReminder` (default ON, liveApply); claude gets it via the UserPromptSubmit hook, codex via the wrapper's per-turn inject. BACKEND REALITY (verified live with a codeword-in-objective): **Claude fires + INJECTS both hooks** (terminal + chat, local + remote) — fully works via hooks. **Codex app-server RUNS hook commands but does NOT inject their `additionalContext`** in JSON-RPC mode (0.142.5) — so for CODEX the hook is NOT the delivery path. Instead (2.35.0, research-verified) the **codex-chat-wrapper injects context natively via `thread/inject_items`** (a first-class app-server method that appends a `role:'developer'` message to the thread's model-visible history out-of-band from the user turn): `injectTaskContextForTurn()` calls `/api/agent/prompt-context` before each `turn/start` and, if non-empty, injects it. Verified: codex answered a codeword only in the task objective, AND the NEW codeword after an edit. GOTCHA that cost a debug cycle: the VIBESPACE_* env reached the spawned CLI (argv `env VAR=val` prefix) but NOT the WRAPPER's own process.env, so the wrapper's inject silently no-op'd — the wrapper (always LOCAL, even for remote sessions) now gets VIBESPACE_API=127.0.0.1:<PORT> + token + task id in the dtach process env directly. The `vibespace-hook.mjs` UserPromptSubmit hook stays registered (works for Claude; harmless for codex). **Task-update injection (2.35.0; DIFF-BASED since 2.113.0):** both endpoints track per-session `_groupSeenAt` (the `contentUpdatedAt` last delivered) — so any group change (UI or another session's vibespace-task) reaches the agent on its NEXT turn, no per-turn noise otherwise. Since 2.113.0 an UPDATE delivers only the DELTA, not the full re-render: every delivery also snapshots the group (`s._groupSnap` via tasks.snapshotForDiff) and later changes inject a `<vibespace-task-update>` block from tasks.renderContextDiff (objective/title edits, changed contextDir files, new activity entries — see the agent-routes.js file-structure note for the full contract; toggle `agents.contextUpdateDiffs`). Claude gets it via the UserPromptSubmit hook; codex via the wrapper's per-turn inject. TASK.md: TaskManager writes `<contextDir>/.vibespace/TASK.md` on every change + boot (program-only writer, content-compare guard, atomic). Remote (P3): the ssh spawn opens a reverse tunnel `-R <rport>:127.0.0.1:<PORT>` (remote agent tools/hook reach VIBESPACE_API through it) and the tools + the per-session vsst_ token ship over ssh STDIN as ONE tar into `~/.vibespace/bin` (0700; token = 0600 `.tok-<id>`, referenced via a `VAR="$(cat …)"` shell prefix assignment — **2.126.0: NOTHING secret or bulky in argv anymore**; the old inline-base64 prelude put ~300KB of blobs AND the vsst_ token in /proc/cmdline on the remote, readable by any local user — real user shock report) + the prelude runs `vibespace-hook-register.mjs` to register the hook in the REMOTE's own settings (its local Claude/Codex fires the hook, not ours) — verified end-to-end on the devbox (remote claude answered the codeword; remote `vibespace-task progress` wrote back through the tunnel)

- Archive folders (2.30.0): "Archive project" records the FOLDER (`archivedFolders` in user-state, host-scoped exact-cwd keys) so sessions created there LATER start archived too; unarchiving one session dissolves the folder rule into individual archives; the project button toggles archive/unarchive
- **Invalidating a SERVER cache that a CLIENT also caches must NOTIFY (2.309.0, real report)**: the client's remote-discovery list has no TTL (an ssh scan is expensive), so dropping only the server's copy left a terminated remote session reading as live until a manual ⟳ — invisible AND permanent. `hosts.invalidateDiscovery` fires `onDiscoveryDirty`; the server then computes the list ONCE on the owning machine (the `discovery-claims` device op) and broadcasts the RESULT as `remote-sessions` — clients apply it, they never re-fetch (2.310.0: broadcasting a bare 'stale' put the trigger for a heavy scan on the orchestration side and multiplied it by the client count; one dirty signal must cost one computation). Nothing is computed when no client is connected; an unreachable machine pushes an error and clients keep their labelled last-known list. The hook lives on the ONE invalidation entry point, never per call site — the bug existed because `/api/kill-pid` had a hand-wired refresh and the ws terminate path did not. Test: scripts/test-remote-discovery-dirty.mjs (drift guard fails any new raw `_discoveryCache.delete`). **COLD START serves STALE-while-revalidate (2.320.0, inc-msp2srj2): a cold sweep blocks 10-60s (device bootstrap/daemon self-upgrade/ssh master rebuild — 12.3s measured healthy) and the zone rendered EMPTY the whole window while the persisted last-known list was only consulted on failure; cold `discoverSessions` now returns it instantly stale-marked + kicks ONE background refresh through this same dirty→push channel (no loop: the background pass runs ttlMs:0 which skips the SWR branch); explicit ⟳ still scans. Field rule: a '默认没有/empty by default' report on anything remote = measure FIRST-PAINT LATENCY before hunting for a data bug — slow-to-first-paint and broken are indistinguishable to the user.**
- Multi-client sync: star/archive/archivedFolders/rename/bookmarks broadcast via `user-state-updated`; tasks broadcast via `tasks-updated` — all clients update live. **RULE (2.231.3, real every-create bug): a UI action chained after a store WRITE must never wait on the broadcast echo** — the awaited API response beats the WS broadcast essentially always, so create→openTaskDetail looked the fresh id up in a stale client mirror and toasted 'Task Group not found' on every create; task create/update/import upsert the returned record into the mirror SYNCHRONOUSLY (`_upsertTaskLocal`), delete removes locally, the broadcast overwrites idempotently (same class as `_pendingTaskBinds`)
- Session rename: double-click name in sidebar → set custom name → used as `--name` on next resume (if CLI supports it — detected via `--help` at startup), syncs to open windows
- Terminate button: in session card expand panel for all running sessions (live/tmux/external). Live uses WebSocket kill, external/tmux uses `POST /api/kill-pid`
- Session right-click menu + Properties window (2.49.0): `renderSessionCard` installs a `contextmenu` handler (works on touch via the global long-press synthesizer) building a full quick-action menu (focus/resume-in-mode/history/fork/star/archive/rename/set-status/Task-Groups submenu with folder-derived disabled/copy/find-goto-move/properties/terminate) — same handlers as the expanded buttons. `src/lib/session-props.js` `openSessionProps(app, sessionRef)` (openSpec `openSessionProps`, window type 'task', keyed dedup `_sessionPropsKey`): Identity / State(+Change popover + history timeline via /api/session-status/history) / Billing (auth line + ON-RESUME account select writing sessionConfigs.account) / Config overrides summary / Task Groups toggles (explicit bind/unbind; folder-derived disabled) / Agent steps (/api/session-todos, empty-subject stubs filtered). Live re-render on tasks-updated/session-status-updated/active-sessions/accounts-updated/user-state-updated; ws listener removed in winInfo.onClose (task-detail pattern).
- Per-session config: gear button (⚙) in Resume split button group opens a popover with Model/Effort/Permission overrides. Each row has a checkbox — unchecked = greyed out, uses global default; checked = per-session override. Changing a select while unchecked auto-checks. Model supports combobox (Custom... for specific model IDs). Overrides are PERSISTED per session in user state (`sessionConfigs` map, key `backend:backendSessionId`, synced multi-client like star/archive) — saved on every popover change, NOT just passed at resume time (closure-only overrides were lost on sidebar re-render, which is why config "didn't take effect"). `app.resumeSession()` reads saved config via `sidebar.getSessionConfig()` for any param the caller didn't specify, so ALL resume paths apply it (card click, Resume button, resume-all, chat resume bar, layout restore). Cards with overrides show a purple gear badge (model/effort/permission summary in tooltip, `.badge-config`).
- **OpenCode history needs the background service (2026-09-07)**: OpenCode keeps conversations in its own database, not in files, so a STOPPED OpenCode conversation can only be listed / opened / resumed / forked while the **OpenCode background service** plugin is on (running sessions never need it). It is off by default, so the FIRST time you use OpenCode here — creating an OpenCode session, or opening/forking an OpenCode conversation — VibeSpace shows ONE dialog explaining what the service does (loopback only, your own CLI, stops when disabled) with **Enable & start** / **Not now**. The answer is remembered for the whole INSTANCE (a flag in data/plugins.json that broadcasts), so a second tab or another device is never asked again. Enabling continues the action you were in the middle of: the serve boots lazily and the pending open/fork re-runs once it answers (and if it does not answer, a toast says what state it is in — never an endless spinner). The way back is always visible: ⚙ → Plugins, and a row in the session list that says "Stopped OpenCode conversations are hidden — its background service is off" with an Enable action (shown only once you have actually met OpenCode here, so it never nags). On an instance where OPS forced the service off that row appears WITHOUT the Enable button — it explains the short list, but nothing you could click there would work. A service that is simply off is never reported as an error: only a service that BROKE (parked after crashes, or stopped by the runaway guard) raises the red toast.
- **Antigravity CLI conversations — Google's `agy` as a harness (lane antigravity-harness, 2026-10-20, commit 1 of 3; the owner 「如果有 antigravity cli 就别搞 gemini cli 了」, replacing the parked Gemini CLI lane)**: New Session → Backend **Antigravity CLI** (shown once `agy` resolves on this machine, `ANTIGRAVITY_CMD` overrides) runs ONE `agy` per conversation in its stream-json mode in chat (data/bin/agy-wrapper.js — the same window, queue strip and Stop as OpenCode: agy is NOT ACP, the wrapper writes the ACP journal so the ACP normalizer and consumer serve it unchanged) and the agy TUI in terminal mode (`--model` / `--effort` / `--mode` / `--conversation <the conversation's id>`, so a chat conversation continues in the TUI and back). Model / effort (low…max) / mode (accept-edits · auto · plan · Never ask = `--dangerously-skip-permissions`) are FLAGS: changing one mid-conversation RESTARTS agy on the same conversation and the notice says so; Stop does the same (agy's stream has no cancel). What agy would do silently or fatally, said instead: a tool it SKIPPED because it needed approval (its stream never asks) becomes a permission card 「agy skipped <tool>」 with **Allow and retry** — one turn on the same conversation with every tool approved (agy has no per-tool grant in a run; the card says so), then back to the conversation's mode — or **Keep skipped**; a chat line whose first word is one of agy's OWN commands (`/model`, `/usage` … — the closed list measured on 1.4.3, src/harnesses/antigravity-slash.js) is refused in the chat by name (agy ends its stream on one); a line that starts with a path — the composer's upload puts the file's path first — or any other "/…" is text and is sent (lane agy-slash-guard-paths, .341: the first-character rule refused every message with an attachment as «/home»); a not-signed-in agy is said by name (`auth-required`) in seconds instead of a 60 s hang that would take our next line as its sign-in code. Text only (an image is refused by name). The agy version is recorded on every spawn (it updates itself; scripts/fixtures/antigravity-cli-<version>.json is per version). **Named Google accounts (commit 2):** Agents → Antigravity CLI → **+ Add Google account…** opens a terminal running agy's OWN sign-in (its TUI shows a link; sign in with the account and paste the code back — VibeSpace never sees a token) on that account's private HOME ROOT (data/agy-subs/<id>, 0700); the roster shows each account signed in or not (a stat of agy's login file — never read), a star for the default, and ⋯ → **Sign in again** / Re-check / Rename / Remove. A session picks its account (New Session / card ⚙) or rides the machine's own login. An account session runs agy with HOME = its root and the session bus off (agy otherwise keeps the login in the OS keyring, shared by every HOME — measured), so two accounts never share a login; the root links the person's dotfiles (git, ssh, npm, gh's files keep working for the agent's commands) and keeps agy's own state and settings per account — which is where **Allow <rule> and retry** writes a rule the skipped-tool notice named (the machine login's settings are the person's own file: there only **Allow once and retry**). Named accounts run on THIS machine only (a remote session on one is refused by name; nothing is exported or shipped). Commit 3 = the quota reading (`agy -p /usage`, answered without a turn, through the human-gated refresh). Until then: no quota reading ⇒ auto-continue never arms and there is no pool. Subagents (lane agy-subagent-cards, .341): each invoke_subagent is a CARD read from the account's agy store that opens the sub's own timeline (`sub-<id>`); see Chat Mode «Subagents per harness».
- **Antigravity: the status bar and the Artifacts chip (lane agy-status-bar-facts, .342):** agy-wrapper journals ONE `usage` record per turn — agy's `result.usage` is the conversation's RUNNING total (measured: the sum over every model call of every turn in agy's own transcript), so the live context is the turn's LAST call, read from agy's transcript (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation>/…/transcript.jsonl`, through one gate: the realpath inside the store, O_NOFOLLOW; nothing else in the store is opened). The bar then shows context % of the model's window (1,048,576 for gemini-4-argon / 3.8 / 3.7 / 3.6 flash / 3.1 pro — Google's model pages), ⚡, Σ + thinking share, the model, the turn's time; a reload replays them. The Artifacts chip lists agy's write_file / edit_file (and write_to_file / replace_file_content / multi_replace_file_content) paths; a report in agy's brain dir is a document. No todos: agy reports no plan list.
- **Antigravity: the permission mode survives the journal ring and a Resume (lane agy-harness-fixes-2, .354; the owner 2026-10-25):** the mode is a SIDECAR fact — agy-wrapper keeps `meta.modes` / `agentMode` current and one file per conversation (`<buffers>/agy-conversation-modes/<conversation>.json`); chatStatus reads the sidecar when the ring has cut the journal's head, so the 🔒 chip shows the mode and opens agy's four modes; a Resume started with no stated mode runs in the conversation's own (with «Never ask»: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` again), its window's chip says it (the hub reads the wrapper's `session` record — no longer lost behind dtach's clear preamble — and tells the windows) and one line says so; a stated mode wins. With it: the skipped-tool card names the tool (`command`, never «required»); no card after a stop-check reminder turn whose tool steps all completed, nor under «Never ask»; Steer / Stop leave no stale «Antigravity: interrupted». OPEN (cross-harness): a pick in the status bar's mode chip is not saved to the conversation's per-session config, while model / effort picks are (src/lib/chat-status-bar.js `_onClick` permission branch vs `_onConfigChange`) — so another harness's Resume still forgets a chip-picked mode.
- **Adding a harness — ONE checklist, never eleven surprises (lane harness-add-census, 2026-10-20; the owner 「harness测试改进也做一下吧」).** `node scripts/test-harness-add-census.mjs` IS the checklist: it DERIVES every fence a harness must be in (scripts/harness-fences.mjs) — every literal table keyed by harness id or program across scripts/** and src/** (an object keyed by id, a list, rows carrying `id:`/`backend:`, a regex or string alternation, a switch; a comment never counts; acorn over git ls-files, the i18n dictionaries and fixtures excepted), plus the ROW KINDS no table shows (the cli-registry EXCLUDED row and the peer-text DECLARED_CLIS row for its wrapper, `public/brand/<id>.svg`, the zh/ja keys of its Settings category, the New Session option, its own suite + its `scripts/ci.mjs` row, the kb-features harness tables + a feature entry, the registry's require line), and the RULES a lane meets (the roster count pin, the keyEnvVars strip, the host-literal / alias / wall-clock / changelog-length laws). Its output is «file: add row» — a count pin beside a table is named with its next value. A table that rightly omits a harness is a declared FENCE_EXEMPT row with a reason; a dead exemption or a dead rule needle is red. The first run found twenty-one fences blind to antigravity (the gate's real-program names, six literal-id regex families in test-architecture, the §78 ratchet's own family list, five contract pins, the queue / settings / exit rosters, the search census, the vault's id shape) and one product gap: the chat view's view-id parser knew three backend names while view ids carry every backend (now BACKEND_META's keys). `node scripts/harness-new.mjs <id> --label … --kind chat|acp|pty --wrapper data/bin/<file>` writes the descriptor skeleton (the REQUIRED keys, every hook a TODO naming the contract), the adapter stub, the fixture dir, the own suite, and every row the kinds derive — through the census's own insert functions, one source of truth — then runs the census in a fresh process and prints what is LEFT (the id-keyed tables: caps, META, settings, the suites' rosters). What stays manual: the protocol wrapper when the CLI is not ACP, the accounts / login / usage hooks (creds, quota, billingIdentity), the measured fixture, the stream shapes the normalizer reads.

- **Harnesses — a CLI installed after VibeSpace started is seen without a restart (lane antigravity-card-fixes, 2026-10-20; the owner's 「Antigravity CLI 未安装」 for an `agy` installed five minutes after the hub booted)**: the agent CLIs (claude, codex, opencode, antigravity, any ACP agent) are resolved at boot; `GET /api/backend-status` now re-checks them at every read (`cliCmds.check`, src/server/cli-cmd.js): a resolved path is re-validated (one `access` — an uninstall shows), an unresolved or gone one is looked up again at most once per 30 s per CLI, or at once when a person asked (`?recheck=1`: Manage agents after **Install**, its new **Re-check** beside Install, and an account's ⋯ Re-check). A path found is adopted for spawns too. The Antigravity row's «installed» is that checked path; claude / codex rows already re-ran `which` per read and now also adopt what they find.

#### "Clear content…" — scrub a record's words, keep the record (2026-09-28, the owner's ask)

A right-click (touch: long-press) on an Activity-log entry (Task Group log window), a For-you item (popup and window), a status-history entry (Session Properties), a Background Work job or an agent-group message offers **Clear content…**, and each surface also shows a visible door: the log row's ⋯, a "Clear content…" button in the For-you window's item pane, a status row's ⋯, a button in an expanded job card, a group message's ⋯ on hover. ONE confirm dialog names the record's time and first words. The Activity tab adds **Find…** (the tab's search box; an entry it matches only by its detail opens that detail, and the dialog says "Found in the detail: …") + **Select…** → "Select all shown (N)" → "Clear selected (N)" for "every entry that mentions X" (a cleared entry cannot be picked; any number of entries — sent in parts of 200; the batch ends Select mode). A refusal is worded on the owner's own device ("no such record", …); a cleared job's old run log is withheld and says so. A clear keeps id, time, author and position; the text becomes "[cleared at the user's request]" (the English key in the store, worded 已按用户要求清除 / ユーザーの要請により消去済み by the client, dimmed) with `clearedAt`/`clearedBy`; every derived copy follows (TASK.md, the injected context — never announced as news —, the For-you preview, the current status + a queued override notice, the jobs archive / event ring / held stash / spill files / the job's For-you items, a group's last line and next-turn reports). Owner-only routes (`POST /api/records/clear[-many]`, an agent token refused by name); an agent clears only its OWN words (`vibespace-task progress-redact <P-id>`, `vibespace-ask clear <id>`; a pending fork / a job token never). A group log is append-only: a clear appends a replacement record + indexes it; the original line stays on disk (group logs never roll). Each clear writes one ids-only journal line. Full mechanics: kb-file-structure.md (src/record-clear.js and "Clear content…" in the five stores).

### File Management
- **The Doc window** (2.369.215, lane doc-window): a `.md` / `.markdown` file opens as a rendered page you edit directly (ProseMirror; the editor loads on the first Doc window). A file the rich editor would change (a table, HTML, footnotes, front matter, CRLF, setext headings, escapes) opens Raw with a chip saying why — never a silent rewrite; Raw is one press away. Select text → Comment → a note; the strip's Send all sends every comment to the chat that owns the file (typed if it is running, else waiting for its next turn) as `[Doc comments]` messages of ≤ 20 rows and ≤ 4 KB each — a long set goes as several, headed (k/n), numbered continuously, in order; a failure part-way keeps the unsent in the strip (hot fix 2.369.257). A save writes the serializer's output and leaves the chat a free next-turn note "[Doc edit] <path> — +a −b lines; sections: …". The agent rewriting the file repaints the page in place; with unsaved edits a bar offers Reload | Keep editing, and the save then asks before overwriting.
  - **A stopped conversation still gets its comments** (2.369.263, lane doc-comments-stopped-owner, B-b51a): the comments (and a save's edit note) sent to a document whose owning conversation is stopped wait in that conversation's stash and land at its next turn — the engine remembers the owner it saw live (data/doc-owners.json; an exit unlinks the session's meta). "No conversation goes with this document" only when none was ever seen.
  - **Comments are VibeSpace's, not a browser's** (2.369.259, lane doc-comments-synced — the owner's eighteen comments were in another computer's browser): a document's comments are a server-side draft (the `drafts` store, one row per host + path), shown live on every client and every device (a phone too); a browser's old local copy is folded in once (the server's rows kept, its own added) and removed.
  - **The send says what it will do and what it did** (2.369.260, lane doc-comments-ui, B-8199 — the owner with eighteen comments: "请问我现在该干啥"): each strip row has a ➤ "Send this one" beside its ✕ (ONE POST of that row: it leaves, the others stay, every client follows); Send all previews the send's shape from the page's own `commentsBatches` — "Send all (18 → 3 messages)", one message ⇒ "Send all (3)"; while the ONE POST is out the button is disabled and reads "Sending 18 comments…" and every row's ➤ / ✕ is held; the answer is said by `delivered`: "Sent {n} comments [in {m} messages]" / "Sent 1 comment"; a stash "Stashed {n} comments — the conversation is not running; they are delivered when its next turn starts" (never "Sent"); a part-way failure "Sent {sent} of {n} — the rest are still here"; clipped notes "+ {k} notes were shortened to fit". The toast and the status chip carry the same words (src/lib/doc-window-model.js sendAllLabel / sendWords; gates scripts/test-doc-comment-send.mjs + test-doc-window §15 ⑪–⑮).
  - **Width + leaving** (2.369.239, lane doc-window-width-export): the page fills the window (Fit width, the default) or keeps a centred reading column (Comfortable) — the choice is the device's, a phone is always Fit; a wide table scrolls with its first column held; the ⋯ at the bar's right downloads the .md (unsaved edits saved first), exports one self-contained HTML file, prints / saves as PDF through the browser's dialog, or copies as Markdown / HTML. No .docx export.
  - **Print / export fidelity** (2.369.241, lane doc-print-fidelity): Export HTML, Copy as HTML and Print / Save as PDF render the markdown SOURCE as it stands (unsaved edits included) through the house renderer (marked + the one sanitizer) — never the editor's DOM, so a block the editor shows read-only (raw) prints as a heading / a list; a bare `<id>` prints as text. The print sheet wraps code, cells and long words, keeps no scroll container or fixed height, steps a wide table's type down by its columns and flows onto as many pages as it needs.
  - **Tables, task lists, block patching** (2.369.221, lane doc-editor-wheel): the editor core is Tiptap v3 (chosen by measurement — docs/design-doc-editor-wheel.md). Tables and task lists edit as such (toolbar Table = a 3×2 table, Task list; right-click in a table or its ⋯ = insert/delete row and column, align the column, delete the table — the house context menu; Tab / Shift-Tab between cells). A save rewrites only the blocks you changed and, inside an edited block, only the lines you changed (the bullet, `1)`, `_em_`, a row's padding kept); untouched lines stay byte-identical. Raw HTML and front matter show as read-only raw blocks (edit them in Raw); only CRLF files and files over 1 MB still open raw, and the chip says why. A comment carries its source line (`L12`). An edited paragraph's reference links become inline links.
  - **The editor's face** (2.369.223, lane doc-editor-ui, design 020): ONE toolbar of glyph buttons — block style ▾ (Paragraph / Heading 1–3 / Quote / Code block) | Bold Italic Code | bulleted / numbered / task list | table link image | Raw — that folds into its ⋯ by priority as the window narrows (Raw first, Bold / Italic last), the comments button at its end; Save is Ctrl+S or the save dot. ONE status line under it, only while it has something to say: the raw-editing reason, "Changed on disk · Reload · Keep editing", "N comments" (opens the comments strip — closed by default), and at the right ● Unsaved · last HH:MM / Saved HH:MM. The page reads like a document: a 76-character column, space between blocks and above headings, task lists with their boxes on the row (a done one struck through), tables with a hover handle on the row and the column that opens the table menu, code blocks naming their language, quotes / raw blocks / image captions styled. On a phone: 36 px buttons, the toolbar folds to the style, B, I and ⋯.
  - **Raw blocks read; a literal tag is text** (2.369.246 lane doc-raw-blocks; 2.369.267 lane doc-table-native — owner 2026-10-14 「这下面不是标准的表格吗 为啥显示说是源码？」): what the editor cannot carry block by block — an HTML block (`<details>`, `<div>`), front matter, a tag with attributes, a table row with more cells than its header — rides as a read-only raw block drawn RENDERED (the house renderer + the one sanitizer), its chip saying what it is: 「Markdown 块 · 已按内容显示 · 点此编辑源码」 (en "Markdown block · shown as its content · edit source"; a block that reads as nothing: 「HTML 块 · 无法显示，给出源码 · 点此编辑」); a press opens its source in place. Paired inline tags (`<code>` `<kbd>` `<sub>` `<sup>` `<b>` `<strong>` `<i>` `<em>`, `<br>`) are lossless marks. A LITERAL TAG is TEXT in the editor exactly as in the reading — a placeholder naming no HTML element (`<absent>`, `<case>`, `/p/<id>`) or an unpaired open tag (`PR-<code>-nn`; a close inside a code span closes nothing) — so a standard table holding one is a native, editable table (the owner's 10-column report with `<absent>` cells was a raw block). Unedited blocks keep their bytes; an edit keeps the tag as written. Tall rows in a wide table are its long text columns (measured). Gates: test-doc-wheel, test-doc-window-width §6, test-doc-window §17 (desk PNGs).
  - **Comments on raw blocks** (2.369.258, lane doc-comment-raw-block — owner 2026-10-12 "这个html部分无法批注"): every block of a document is commentable; what the person selected is the quote. A click on a raw block (HTML / front matter / Markdown kept as written) offers Add comment quoting the block ("HTML block: <!-- …", ≤ 200 chars, its first source line); a mouse selection inside its reading or source box quotes the selected text (its own source line). The strip names the block's kind ("L9 · HTML block") and a press on the comment selects the block and scrolls to it (after a reload / an edit above it the block is found again by its quote). While the block's source box is open it is not commentable — a selection there says "Press Finish first" (a toast). The comment keeps ONE extra field `raw {pos, line, kind, offset?}`; the message to the chat is unchanged (`L<line> "quote" — note`). Gates: test-doc-window-width ⑦ (the anchor table), test-doc-window §13 (desk 1100 + phone 390).
  - **Links open and edit** (2.369.261, lane doc-link-bubble — owner 2026-10-12 "markdown富文本编辑器里url无法点击和编辑"): the caret on a link (a click, the arrow keys) or a hover ≥ 300 ms shows a small bar under it — the address (≤ 48 characters, the middle elided; the full one in its tooltip) + Open (a new tab) / Edit / Copy / Remove; on a phone a bottom row of the same four with their words. Edit = a dialog with the address and the link's text, prefilled; the toolbar's Link and Ctrl/⌘+K are the same door — on a link they EDIT it (never remove it), on a selection they link it, at a bare caret they insert the address. Ctrl/⌘+click still opens at once; a read-only editor opens on a plain click (its bar: Open + Copy). A URL pasted over a selection links it; a typed `https://…` / `www.…` / `mailto:…` + a space links itself (`README.md` stays a word); every address goes through safeHref (javascript: / data: refused, and said). In the Doc window's text Ctrl/⌘+K is Link; the session palette keeps the chord everywhere else.
- **The files on a phone** (lane phone-files-door, 2026-10-24 — the owner: 「手机上好像不是很容易找到文件管理器」; before it the explorer's only phone door was the «+» long-press sheet): the nav's 文件 beside ☰ opens the explorer in ONE tap (the one this phone showed last, else a new one at home; its word under the icon for the first week); the For-you page ends with a 文件 card — home, the last folder used, the folders with files, the mounted mounts, the recents — one tap opens the explorer THERE. On a phone the explorer is the page: ‹ back to the phone's home (the back gesture's rule), breadcrumbs under the path bar that scroll sideways (the folder itself in view; a crumb opens its folder), rows 44 px, the path bar at 16 px, «New session here» heading the listing (New Session opens with the folder). Every desktop door's phone twin is one table (PURE src/phone-doors.js, test-phone-doors) — the table is in kb-design-lessons §7a.
- **Diagrams in the editor's Markdown preview and the file viewer (lane chat-mermaid, 2.369.351):** a ```mermaid fence in a .md shown by the code editor's Preview or by the file viewer (a file served by URL — an attachment) draws through the same diagram card as the chat (src/lib/mermaid-render.js; the preview's old CDN `<script>` is gone — every script is served by this origin). The Doc window (a .md's default door) still edits a fence as a code block (follow-up).
- File explorer with upload/download/drag-drop, title shows current path
- Multi-select (Ctrl/Cmd+click toggle, Shift+click range, Ctrl+A) with bulk Compress/Copy/Cut/Delete; Delete key works on selection
- Copy/Cut/Paste file clipboard (`app._fileClipboard`, works across explorer windows; cut items dimmed via `.cut-pending`; same-dir paste auto-renames "(copy)"; conflicts confirm-once overwrite); Duplicate. Big/cross-machine pastes show a live progress row (upload machinery: ring + % + bytes + cancel) via the transfer-op mechanism (2.215.0)
- Archives: Compress to Archive (zip/tar.gz/tar/tar.xz, multi-select), archive viewer (double-click .zip/.tar.* → entry list + filter + Extract All; entry click extracts to temp + opens via normal pipeline), Extract Here / Extract to Folder (skip-existing semantics), folder Download as Zip (streamed)
- Background right-click menu (Paste/New File/New Folder/Select All/Refresh/Copy Path/Properties); Properties dialog (du recursive size, permissions); icon view has the same context menu as list view
- View menu (single dropdown): view mode (list/icon), options (hidden files, mixed sort, bookmarks panel, preview panel), group by (none/type/modified/size), column visibility
- Resizable columns: drag column header borders, absolute widths (Windows Explorer behavior), persist in localStorage. Right-click header for column visibility + auto-fit.
- Preview panel: toggle via View menu, auto-detects layout (horizontal when wide, vertical when tall), supports all file types (text, images, PDF, video, audio, HTML as iframe)
- Path bar: autocomplete (Tab/Enter), submit file path to open it directly in viewer; a RELATIVE name resolves against the folder on show first (its pathField's base 1, then ~ — B-d027, lane phone-files-door 2026-10-24: `payments` typed at ~/work opens ~/work/payments)
- Drag file from explorer to terminal → auto-types shell-escaped absolute path
- View modes: list (with size/modified columns, sortable) and icon grid
- Large folder pagination: first 100 items + "Load more" button
- File type registry (`file-types.js`): single source of truth for extension→viewer mapping. `hasDedicatedViewer()` prevents binary files with viewers from falling to hex. Adding a file type = one line in registry.
- File viewers: PDF, images (zoom + drag-to-pan), video, audio, hex. `FileViewer.renderInto()` shared by viewer windows and preview panel. An .eml's HTML body and a Word document's embedded HTML (altChunk) are frames at the frame host (`kind=eml` / `kind=docx`, lane frame-host-preview): nothing of them runs, no network; an .eml with remote pictures offers "Show pictures" (the mail frame's rule and words).
- Reload from disk (2.341.0, owner report — html rewritten on disk was unreachable without reopening): CodeEditor gets a ⟳ toolbar button + a freshness watch (`_baselineMtime`/`_startFreshnessWatch`/`reloadFromDisk` in code-editor.js) — on-disk mtime baselined at load AND save (self-writes must re-baseline or the watch flags them as foreign), polled every 15s while visible for LOCAL files only (remote hosts are ssh-per-op: tab-refocus check + the explicit button, never a poll); clean editor auto-reloads (scroll/cursor preserved, `_renderPreviewNow()` refreshes a visible preview — that method is the extracted single preview renderer shared with the Preview toggle), dirty editor shows a "⚠ File changed on disk" chip and every reload over unsaved edits goes through showConfirmDialog — edits are NEVER silently discarded (`opts.auto` returns early when dirty). The CM dispatch is guarded by `this._reloading` in the updateListener so a reload doesn't mark the doc modified. Viewer windows get a floating `.viewer-reload-btn` (FileViewer.open) that re-runs renderInto with `container._bustTs` appended as `&_r=` to all five /api/file/raw URL constructions — /api/file/raw streams without cache headers, so a same-URL img/video/pdf can re-serve stale from the browser memory cache; the bust param is the load-bearing part, do not "clean it up".
- Open with LibreOffice (§7.9 of docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md, the owner's ruling 2026-09-27 ②): an office file's explorer menu opens it in LibreOffice running as a desktop app ON THE MACHINE THAT HOLDS IT (Writer / Calc / Impress by extension); a machine without LibreOffice says so in one sentence and offers "Install LibreOffice on <machine>…" (the plan first). When the LibreOffice session ends with the document's mtime moved, the server broadcasts `file-changed` and the code editor's freshness check runs at once (clean ⇒ reload, dirty ⇒ the disk chip). A stale `.~lock.<name>#` LibreOffice leaves after a Stop is removed only when it names that session's own profile. The Word viewer's toolbar (and the explorer's preview of a .docx) carries **Open in LibreOffice** — the same door, the app named by the verdict, the file's real path and machine; on a machine without LibreOffice its click shows the same sentence + install offer under the button (never a greyed button).
- DOCX (the Word viewer, lane docx-viewer 2026-09-27 — src/lib/docx-viewer.js, every decision a PURE rule of src/lib/docx-viewer-model.js): client-side rendering via `docx-preview` 0.3.7 into a **shadow root** (the document's own CSS — style ids, font names, numbering text written unescaped by the library — can neither restyle the workspace nor be distorted by the app's `* { padding: 0 }` / `.file-viewer img` rules). **Pages are paper**: white `var(--paper)` pages with `var(--shadow-window)` on the workspace colour `var(--bg-workspace)`, the document's own colours (Word's automatic black, run and heading colours, a `w:background` page colour) in every theme — the library's grey wrapper (`background: gray; padding: 30px`, UNSAFE flex centring) is neutralised: measured on master at the owner's shape (an 817 CSS px window at DPR 1.75 = the ~1430 px screenshot) the 816 px page overhung its 648 px grey wrapper by 84 px each side — the grey 30 px top padding was the "band narrower than the page" and the page's left 30 px sat behind the pane, unreachable. A sizer carrying the scaled page stack centres the pages and scrolls sideways only when a page is wider than the pane; a zoom wider than the pane opens centred. **Toolbar** (media-toolbar idiom, built once and patched in place): Fit width · 100% · − · zoom label · + (SVG `zoomOut`/`zoomIn`, title + aria-label) · the page count "n / N" (a page = one `section.docx`; the count follows a probe line a third down the pane, the last page at the end of the scroll). Zoom = `transform: scale()` of the stack (text stays selectable, 80 pages never re-lay out per step), ladder 25 %–400 %; Ctrl/Cmd + wheel zooms the pages (exponential, anchored at the pointer), never the browser; the choice is remembered per device (`localStorage['vibespace.docx-zoom']` = `fit` | a scale); default = Fit width = the WIDEST page fills the pane minus 2 × 24 px (a landscape page shrinks the portrait ones rather than being cut off; on a very wide pane fit can exceed 150 %). **Fidelity fixes applied to the parsed document before render:** Word's header/footer inheritance ("Link to Previous" — the library read only a section's own references, so the body section of a paper with a title-page section showed no running head); style-defined tab stops (the library read a paragraph's stops before copying its style's, so the Header style's right-aligned stop was ignored — the page number sat 181 px short; now 13 px, the library's own em/nbsp residual, identical at UI scale 100 % and 125 %); Word's Symbol/Wingdings private-use bullets (U+F0B7) mapped to Unicode (a browser without the Symbol font drew no bullet). Options (`DOCX_RENDER_OPTIONS`): `experimental: true` (real tab stops; the library measures them 500 ms after render with getBoundingClientRect, so the stack is held hidden at NET scale 1 — `scale(1 / uiScale)` — until that pass has run, then shown at the chosen zoom), `breakPages` + `ignoreLastRenderedPageBreak` left true (false merges a new-page section break's title page into page 2 — the library only starts a page at a manual break or a page-size change), `ignoreFonts: true` + embedded fonts registered through the FontFace API on `document.fonts` and deleted on close (Chrome 153 ignores `@font-face` inside a shadow root — measured), `useBase64URL: false` (no CSP on the app page; blob: images revoked on close). **Safety:** hyperlinks through the PURE `linkVerdict` allowlist — http(s)/mailto open in a new tab (`noopener noreferrer`, never navigating VibeSpace away), `#bookmark` scrolls the document (location.hash untouched), javascript:/data:/vbscript:/file:/relative targets lose their href with a title saying why; altChunk HTML parts — which the library renders in a SAME-ORIGIN iframe with scripts ON (measured: a hostile .docx ran script in the VibeSpace origin on open) — are re-hosted in a `sandbox=""` iframe with a no-network CSP. **Refusals by name, not stack traces:** a legacy binary `.doc`/`.dot` is refused before any fetch ("Legacy Word files (.doc) cannot be shown here. Open it in Word or LibreOffice and save it as .docx."); after the fetch the bytes decide (`sniffVerdict`): an OLE container named .docx (password-protected .docx files are OLE) and a non-zip file get their own sentences; a render that throws still shows the reason in the pane, and a superseded render (window closed, the explorer preview moved on) never paints its error over its successor. **Big files:** "Rendering…" is painted before the parse holds the thread; 80 pages: parse ~60 ms, renderDocument ~6 ms, open → ready ~160 ms, no task ≥ 50 ms (the fixture; no worker needed). **Oracle:** the heavy gate compares the rendered text order with `mammoth.extractRawText` of the same file. **Known limits:** docx-preview does not paginate by content (a page = a section / manual page break; a long section is one tall page), field results are Word's cached text (a PAGE field shows its cached number on every page), editing is out of scope (the viewer is read-only). Gates: test-docx-viewer-model (fast), test-docx-viewer (heavy), fixtures scripts/fixtures/docx/.
- XLSX: sheet tabs at bottom (like Excel), click to switch. 5000 row limit. Text selectable.
- PPTX: slide thumbnail sidebar (high-res render scaled via CSS transform, resizable sidebar with drag handle) + main slide view (fit-to-container 16:9). Keyboard navigation (arrows). Responsive resize via ResizeObserver. Text selectable.
- CSV/TSV: virtual scroll viewer — only renders visible rows (~30-50), pages of 200 rows fetched on demand from streaming `GET /api/file/csv` endpoint. Handles arbitrarily large files.
- HTML files: open in CodeEditor with Preview toggle, same as markdown — the preview is an OPAQUE frame at the frame host (`kind=preview`, lane frame-host-preview: never `allow-same-origin`, so the page has no cookie, storage or API), its local folder's files served at `/frame-host/f/<token>/` (relative stylesheets, scripts — module ones too —, pictures and links resolve there; no `<base>` is written into the page); https:// libraries load, the hub's own files never do
- Code editor: CodeMirror 6, follows global theme, auto-format via Prettier (Shift+Alt+F) for JS/TS/JSON/HTML/CSS/MD/YAML/GraphQL + server-side ruff/black/shfmt/gofmt/rustfmt for Python/Shell/Go/Rust. Language selector drives Preview button visibility.
- Upload: Chrome-style popover menu (Upload Files / Upload Folder / active uploads with spinner / upload history). Mac Finder-style inline progress bars in file list. Ring progress on upload button. Upload history persisted via SyncStore and broadcast across clients. Folder upload preserves directory structure. Chinese/Unicode filenames preserved via `fileNames` JSON field.
- Large file warnings (>1MB), binary auto-detection
- CWD autocomplete with `~` support
- Clipboard image paste (Ctrl+V → upload to server → xclip/osascript sets clipboard → Ctrl+V to PTY)
- Folder right-click: "Copy Path", "Sessions ▸" submenu with "+ New session" and all sessions at that path; "Add to group ▸" submenu to link folder to a session group
- File right-click: "Copy Path", Open, Edit, Open as Hex, Download, Rename, Delete
- Download from the file's own window (2.369.212): every viewer (image, video, audio, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, archive, .eml), the hex viewer and the code editor carry a Download button (in the viewer's toolbar — Word: beside "Open in LibreOffice" — else beside the floating ⟳) and the title-bar right-click menu has Download; it saves the file on disk of the machine it lives on (ssh hosts and paired devices included) under its own name; an editor with unsaved edits downloads the saved copy and says so; a refusal is a toast
- Drag folder from file explorer to sidebar group header → links folder to group
- All windows (file explorer, viewers, editors, browser) persist and restore on page refresh

### Agent browser v2 — P0, "零干扰" only (2026-09-13, docs/design-agent-browser-v2.zh.md §3.2)

**What ships, honestly: the half of (1.b) that stops agents interfering with each
other, and nothing else.** There is no registry, no keeper, no live view, no pin
UI and no `vibespace-browser` CLI — those are P1 and later. An agent still runs
the `agent-browser` CLI out of its own shell exactly as before; what changed is
that its session was spawned with **four environment variables**, so that CLI
call lands in a browser nobody else can reach.

Before this, `git grep agent-browser` over the tracked tree returned exactly one
hit and it was a comment. Every agent's browsing went into the ONE profile named
by `~/.agent-browser/config.json`, in that profile's DEFAULT session: two agents
took turns stealing each other's active tab, and `close --all` — the command a
tidying agent reaches for first — closed everybody's browser.

**The four variables** (`src/browser-profiles.js` composes them, `src/server/browser-env.js`
resolves them, `src/ws-create.js` pushes them into the ONE spawn composition so
local and remote both get them):

| Variable | What it isolates |
|---|---|
| `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION=vs-<browserKey>` | the browser CONTEXT: tabs, cookies, storage, history |
| `AGENT_BROWSER_NAMESPACE=vs-<browserKey>` | the DAEMON SOCKET — so a crash, an idle shutdown or a `close --all` cannot cross |
| `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 900000) | the only thing that reclaims a browser in P0 (there is no keeper yet) |
| `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG` (variant D) | a generated config with **no** `profile` key ⇒ a truly ephemeral user-data-dir |

**The fourth one is a decision, not an omission (§3.2.2 / D12).** The CLI's own
precedence is config file < env < flags, so the `profile` key in the user's
config applies to every call that does not override it. MEASURED on the installed
0.32.0: with SESSION + NAMESPACE set **and nothing else**, the chromium child's
resolved `--user-data-dir` is still the shared `default-profile`. That is variant
B, and it is broken twice over — not ephemeral, and N per-session daemons would
each try to launch chromium against ONE user-data-dir. The shipped ladder is
**(D) generated config → (C) per-session scratch dir under `data/` → (N) the
three names alone, ONLY when the machine's effective config names no profile →
`none`, nothing emitted**, each fallback journalled with its reason.

**A FENCED config never lands on (C) (r4).** Rung C is `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE`,
and the CLI refuses `--allowed-domains` beside a profile at the argument check,
so when the generated config could not be written AND the effective config
carried a fence, round 3 landed on C and handed the session a browser that
answered EVERY command `✗ --allowed-domains is not supported with --profile`
where the bare CLI works — while the journal called it a working `D → C`.
Measured with one injected variable (the config writer throwing) on 0.32.0;
reachable only when the config file write fails while a symlink and a mkdir
beside it succeed, which is narrow and said so. `fenced` is now an INPUT of the
PURE ladder (`variantLadder({…, fenced})`), the ORCH half never attempts the C
block under a fence (no symlink, no scratch dir left behind), and the journal
says `C → N` with the fence as its reason (`fencedRungReason`, one spelling) —
a fenced config cannot name a profile (the CLI refuses that combination whole),
so a fenced descent lands on N by construction and the fence stays intact.
And because the C rung replaces no config, a later pin there must ask the CLI's
two files as they stand THEN, project file included — so the rung now records
the session's own directory in `<key>.cwd` beside its link at spawn, and
`repointPin`'s C branch reads it back (round 3 asked the user file alone; a
missing record refuses the pin BY NAME rather than checking half the fence).
test-browser-profiles ⑰ (two patched-copy pre-fix controls) +
test-browser-resources §ⓖ (the binary: the product's N rung browses, round 3's
C rung is refused).

**THE DESIGN'S (A) AND (B) ARE BOTH NAMED REJECTS, MEASURED (r3).** §3.2.2's
table says (A) "SESSION only" has no directory conflict because one daemon owns
the directory. On 0.32.0 it does: with ONE namespace and two `--session` names
against a config naming a `profile`, the second session's chromium dies on
`Failed to create <profile>/SingletonLock: File exists` exactly like (B) —
every `--session` launches its own chromium, so what collides is two of them on
ONE user-data-dir, however many daemons there are. Round 2 shipped that shape
(three names, config profile in force) as its floor and called it "(A)"; the
verifier measured the second concurrent browser failing to launch where today
both start. The floor is now decided by the same fact the collision depends on:
**(N)** — the names alone — is reachable only when the effective config names
no profile (then each daemon gets the CLI's own ephemeral
`/tmp/agent-browser-chrome-<uuid>`, measured), and when it does name one the
floor is **`none`**: nothing is emitted, the session keeps today's shared
browser, and the journal names the profile that decided it. A stolen tab is the
smaller harm than a browser that cannot start. (`browser-profiles.REJECTED_VARIANTS`
carries both measurements; the design's table row is NOT edited here — it is the
owner's document — the contradiction is recorded in this manual.)

**THE GENERATED CONFIG KEEPS YOUR OWN RESTRICTIONS (r2).** That file REPLACES
`~/.agent-browser/config.json` rather than merging with it, so round 1 carried an
ENUMERATED list of seven keys across — and silently deleted the user's browsing
FENCE (`allowedDomains`) plus the whole confirmation/action-policy family from
every local session. Measured end to end on 0.32.0: through your own config a
navigation is refused (`✗ Domain '…' is not in the allowed domains list`);
through the config the product generated from that same file it succeeded. It is
now a **DENY**, and the deny set is the CLI's own: the binary refuses
`--allowed-domains` beside exactly the flags that mean "this is not a fresh,
isolated, controllable context" — `profile`, `restore`, `sessionName`, `state`,
`autoConnect`, `cdp` — which is precisely the property P0 sells, so those six are
dropped and **everything else in your config is carried across unchanged**,
including keys nobody enumerated. Each drop gets ONE journal line naming that
key's own reason, because a restriction removed by OMISSION is exactly how the
fence vanished with nothing in the journal.

**AND "YOUR CONFIG" IS TWO FILES (r3).** The CLI reads `~/.agent-browser/config.json`
and then `./agent-browser.json` in the directory a command runs from, at HIGHER
priority — and `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG` replaces BOTH. Round 2 layered only the
first, so a project-level fence (or `actionPolicy`, `confirmActions`,
`initScripts`…) was still deleted from every local session, and with
`dropped: []` there was nothing in the journal: finding ① unfixed for the second
file. MEASURED on 0.32.0 with a local http server: at the project cwd the bare
CLI answers `✗ Domain '127.0.0.1' is not in the allowed domains list`, round 2's
generated config answered `✓`; the CLI does NOT walk up (from a subdirectory the
fence is absent), and its merge rule is a shallow per-key override with
`extensions` concatenated user-first (`--load-extension=<user>,<project>`, and
its own `--help` says so). `effectiveConfig(cwd)` now layers the file from the
SESSION's own directory with exactly that rule (`layerProjectConfig`, PURE),
journals ONE line naming the file and its keys, and the drop line says what it
carried FROM (both files). The one boundary is stated rather than hidden, in the
journal and in the agent manual: the CLI reads that file per INVOCATION
