Before: the ✕ asked Chrome, the second ✕ stopped it, and the keeper started it again 4 s later — the window's own `lease` (an app lease) was null while the profile had two leases.

### Agent browser — a request for a person is ONE record seen in ONE place: «等你接管» (lane browser-takeover-queue, 2026-10-23; a fleet power user's Lark ask)

An agent that needs the person IN its browser (a login, a captcha, a payment) runs `vibespace-browser ask-human "<words>"`. PURE `src/browser-takeover-request.js` is the record — ONE per lease (browser key × profile; the conversation's own browser = profile null), a second ask re-asserts it — and its state follows the lease's input side: a takeover ⇒ taken, an explicit handback ⇒ done, a handback nobody chose ⇒ waiting again, the person's Done ⇒ done, the agent's withdraw / its lease ending ⇒ withdrawn. The keeper is its ONE writer (data/browser-takeovers.json, broadcast `browser-takeovers-updated`); the announcer files the SAME For-you item (urgent; a dismissal parks it at band 4, never resolves it; a reply reopens it; ✓ = Done) and tells the agent (the handback's delivery names the request; Done without a takeover is told once). While it waits a page verb's /resolve answers `human_asked` and the CLI WAITS (≤ 90 s, long-polls), then runs or says «end your turn». The Agent browser window's first section «等你接管 · Waiting for you» lists every open request the owner may see (keyed rows: Take over = the live view with the input side taken; Done; Reply through the item; Hand back while driving); its title and the rail's Browser badge count the waiting ones; every live view of that lease shows «agent 请你：…» under its bar.

### Agent browser — the live view shows the browser's own window; a takeover drives it (lane browser-x-in-window, 2026-10-23; design q-026 r1 §2.1 B2 — B2 shipped)

On the attach road (the keeper's Google Chrome on its `display-for-browser` xpra session, this machine) the live view draws the display session's X picture through the ONE desktop bridge with the desktop app window's own view (xpra-view.js — its fit, its DPR rule), showing ONLY this conversation's Chrome window, its dialogs and its menus. THE SOURCE IS A VERDICT: PURE src/browser-picture.js `pictureSourceOf(record)` → 'x' | 'screencast' with why; its words ride the mode badge's tooltip («the browser's own window» / «the page's picture — this machine has no display», another machine, not started on VibeSpace's display, the display session gone). Seats on that display: the viewer holding the takeover is `active` (pointer / keys / wheel / paste / IME into X), the ruling pane while nobody drives is `size` (its view sizes Chrome's window with xpra's own configure-window — never input), everyone else `watch`; the agent's verbs stay CDP, the handback is unchanged. Chrome's HTTP sign-in sheet is CHROME'S on this road (the watch answers `Default`; the sheet is drawn inside the window — measured — and typed into by the person who takes over); while it, or a dialog window of Chrome's over this conversation's window (a GTK chooser), stands the agent's page verbs answer `[dialog_open]` by its title. A paired machine's profile, a conversation's own temporary browser and Browse yourself keep the screencast. Gates: test-browser-picture, test-browser-x-picture (heavy), test-browser-prompts ③x, test-browser-keeper ⑥, test-xpra-client §X.

### Agent browser — one stuck page never holds a shared profile's other conversations; a silent page is answered by name (lane browser-shared-profile-freeze, 2026-10-23; fleet fb-8727ee62fb / fb-0898d92d0a)

The browser driver attached over CDP holds its next command until every NEW tab it discovers answers `Page.enable` (measured: 19.8 s for a tab born holding its main thread, 59.8 s for one born with a confirm() — every conversation on the profile at once). So each AGENT lease of a local named profile shared cooperatively (`owner`) gets a url of its own through the in-process CDP proxy (`cdp-mediator` grant mode `scope`, `browser-mediation.leaseRoadVerdict` / `judgeScope`): its driver discovers only its own tabs and the tabs they open; every call passes as written (no census class, no takeover interrupt — that road's pause stays /resolve's); an attach by id admits the tab; a revoke never closes its tabs. The keeper hands the same url in the attach answer and in its own calls in that lease's session (`leaseUrlFor` → `leaseCliOpts` / `attachOpts`); its raw reads stay on the browser's own endpoint, and a `tab <target id>` is looked up there too (another holder's tab: not_your_tab). A mediated profile, an ephemeral browser, a remote one and the user's own Browse-yourself key keep the raw url. After an Update the new server's proxy hands a new url and the agent's next command reaches the same daemon, browser and tab (the boot re-owns them). The conversation's OWN silent page: /resolve asks the tab the verb acts on first (`browser-dialogs.pageAnswers`, one bounded `Runtime.evaluate` on the watch's own session, PAGE_ANSWER_MS 5 s; the lease's pinned tab, else the tabs its agent navigated; settled at the first answer) — every one silent ⇒ the CLI answers `[page_busy]` naming the tab and the way out (`open` of another site leaves it at once — a new page process), the verb never handed to the driver; tab / close / dialog / stop / site-reset / a navigation still run; a held popup of it is named with `tab close <its id>`, closed through the watch's socket and said `close_pending` when Chrome keeps a busy page. Measurement: scripts/measure-shared-profile-freeze.mjs. Gates: test-browser-mediation ⑧, test-browser-stuck ①p / ③p, test-browser-live ⑩ (`BROWSER_LIVE_ONLY=freeze`), test-browser-daemon Ⓓ.

### Agent browser v2 — P5: the action trace, the per-profile screencast, the housekeeping (server 2026-09-18, client 2026-09-21; design §4.5 / §6.4 / §7.1 / §8 step 3, D7 / D8 / D35)

**Every action the agent SENDS to its browser is recorded with a before-JPEG,
an after-JPEG, its POSITION and the COMMAND** (D35, owner 2026-09-13: "记录前后画面
变化以及操作位置，方便用户后面 review"). The recorder (src/server/browser-trace.js)
taps the stream server's own `command` / `result` / `frame` records through the
bridge for every LIVE lease (a tap never starts a browser, never drives, never
counts as a viewer); an observation (`get`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `launch`,
the box probe itself) is never traced; a fill's value and a type's text are
kept as `«N chars»` (the §3.7 audit rule); the target element's box comes from
ONE bounded `get box <selector>`; the after-frame is the first ≥ 400 ms after
the result (else the latest by 1.5 s, marked "nothing repainted"). Entries are
0600 files under `data/browser-trace/<profile|ephemeral>/` and are NEVER
redacted (§12.9) — which is why they have a RETENTION and why every surface
repeats §6.4's sentence. The retention is BY SIZE since 2026-09-27 (the owner:
"记录不要按照 7 天上限，而是按照容量，每个浏览器 profile 最多保留 1GB 记录"):
`browser.traceBytesPerProfile` (MB, default 1024, floor 64) per profile — the
temporary browsers together count as one; over it the oldest sessions' FRAMES
go first and every action LIST stays (the entry says its frames went to the
size limit); nothing is removed for being old; the video recordings keep their
own 7 d / 200 MB. Setting `browser.actionTrace` (Browser, default ON) gates the
whole thing.

**Browser SESSIONS and their REPLAY (2026-09-27, the owner: "最关键是能在聊天界面和浏览器查看界面两个地方都能看到 session 的开始和结束，以及每个浏览器 session 的回放").**
A session is one run of a conversation's browser — the lease granted / the
browser launched or joined, to the lease let go (detach, the conversation
gone, a person's Stop, a backend switch; an idle stop is NOT an end). The chat
shows a VibeSpace card at each start ("Browser session started · work · 14:02")
and end ("Browser session ended · 12 min · 38 actions" + Replay) — live, and
after a reload / a server restart / a read-only history in the place they
happened (derived from the trace's markers). The live view's Actions pane
opens with a Sessions list (each with Replay) and puts "Session k · started …"
dividers between its actions; a stopped browser's view opens straight onto that
list. The replay window (`browser-replay`, one per conversation or per profile)
lists the sessions and the chosen one's actions, draws the after-frame with
the click point / element box, Before / After, ← → Home End, Space plays one a
second; on a phone the list sits above the picture. Also from Session
properties ("Browser sessions (n)") and the Agent browser panel's Replay….
Gates: test-browser-sessions (fast), test-browser-replay-ui (heavy).

**Where you see it (the client half):** ① THE TOOL CARD — a shell tool call
whose command drives the agent browser (`agent-browser …` /
`vibespace-browser …`, claude's string or codex's argv array — the gate is the
command, never the tool name) grows a "Browser actions" row: the after-frame
THUMBNAILS of every action are always there (D7 (c)), the summary says
`N action(s) · M failed` — or honestly why not (trace off / waiting on a running
card / none recorded) — and the button expands the full list (time · command ·
result · where). One batched fetch per render (the union of the cards' windows,
each entry given to exactly the card that was RUNNING when it happened), live
cards refresh on `browser-trace-appended`, and a STOPPED conversation's cards
still find their actions (the ask carries the CLI's conversation id, the route
resolves the key through the bindings store) — a review happens after the
fact. ② THE ENTRY DIALOG — before / after side by side with the click point or
the element box DRAWN on the picture, the command, the position line, the
result and duration, ← / → through the list. ③ THE LIVE VIEW'S ACTIONS PANE —
the timeline of the pane you are looking at, seeded from GET and grown by the
stream's `trace` record. Frames are drawn through `img.src` only; a frame is a
secret of a logged-in page and the UI says so.

**The screencast (D7 (c) — thumbnails always, video opt-in per profile):** a
`record: true` profile gets `record start <file>` under the lease's own session
when its browser is live (≥ agent-browser 0.37.0 — refused BY NAME below the
floor, the refusal shown in the panel), `record stop` on detach / stop; files
under `data/browser-recordings/<profileId>/`, listed per profile, removed by the
same sweep. Default OFF: a 30 fps WebM of a logged-in profile is a secret with a
storage bill nobody budgeted.

**Housekeeping (§6.4 / §8 step 3 / D8 — a cookie jar is somebody's login):**
the sweep's scope is EXACTLY the provider rows that own a directory on this
machine (`cloud:*` / `local-window` / `cdp` / a paired-machine record are
refused `not_ours` by name); the panel lists every profile with a STATE and a
WHY (in-use / live / recent — with the in-flight grace and its age / stale /
kept / not-ours), its size (measured by `du -sb` in a child, cached), its trace
digest and its recordings, and NEVER proposes a deletion; `forget` ARCHIVES
BEFORE IT REMOVES (the directory is renamed beside itself, a ledger row is
filed first; refused while leased or running); the ONE permanent deletion is
the user's click on a set-aside row; the orphans under `~/.agent-browser` (a
Chromium-marker directory no record names — 53–56 of them, 98 GB, on the
design's machine) are listed with size and last use for the user to ADOPT with
a label or set aside. **The panel** is ⚙ → Tools → Browser profiles… (window
type `browser-profiles`, singleton; also the live view's recording indicator):
one row per profile with the state and its why, the size, the trace digest,
the recordings and the screencast checkbox; the ephemeral row; the
unregistered directories with Adopt… / Set aside; the set-aside ledger with
Delete permanently; the sweep line + Sweep now. Gate: test-browser-housekeeping
(fast, 174) + the window-types / contributions census rows.

### Agent browser v2 — P6: hard mediation — the CDP-mediating proxy, per-session CDP urls, `sharing: "instance"` (2026-09-21; design §6.2 / §6.5 / D6, the §10 P6 row)

**What it is.** A profile's CDP endpoint is unauthenticated and confers
authority over EVERY target in the browser (§3.4), so the cooperative lease was
never a boundary between different owners — which is why `sharing:
"instance"` was refused until this landed (D6). Now every (profile,
conversation) lease on an instance-shared profile is handed its OWN CDP url
(`ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/m/<token>/devtools/browser`, served by
src/server/cdp-mediator.js) and every message through it is judged by the PURE
rules in src/browser-mediation.js: `Target.*` is scoped to the tabs that lease
owns (the ones it created through its url, the ones a scoped page opened, a
child auto-attached under an owned session, a target born in a context it
made — and the tab the lease was minted with), `Target.getTargets` /
`/json/list` list only those, attach / activate / close / getTargetInfo of any
other tab are `target_out_of_scope`, a message on a CDP session the proxy never
handed out is `session_out_of_scope`, `Browser.close` / `crash*` /
`Target.exposeDevToolsProtocol` / `setRemoteLocations` / `sendMessageToTarget`
are `method_refused` always, a browser-level `Target.setAutoAttach` with
`waitForDebuggerOnStart` is `auto_attach_pause_refused` (r4: it would freeze
every other conversation's and the user's new tab in the shared browser), and while the USER holds the input side (P3) every
`Input.*`, the navigation family, a file upload and the target acts that change
what the user sees are `browser_paused` — a CDP error by id on the same
session, the typed code as its prefix, which agent-browser prints inside its
own JSON (`"error":"CDP error (Page.navigate): browser_paused: …"`). What it
is NOT: `Runtime.evaluate` / `Page.captureScreenshot` are not refused while
paused (a read is the honest use; the CLI's typed refusal already stops the
cooperative path) — stated, never sold as a DOM-level fence.

**How a session gets there.** `vibespace-browser new <label> --sharing
instance` (or the panel's PATCH) — accepted only where the instance has the
proxy (a keeper built without one refuses with D6's sentence, `why:
mediation_unavailable`) and only on THIS machine (`why: host` on a
paired-machine profile; the proxy serves hub-side urls). A mediated attach
(`use` / the `--` form's `resolve`) answers `mediated:true`, the scoped url as
the wrapper's `cdpUrl` (never the raw one), an env of the session name + a
PER-SESSION namespace `vs-<profileId>-<browserKey>` (its own daemon over its
own url — two sessions in one namespace would share one daemon and one scope)
+ the scoped url + an explicit idle + NO profile directory, and a one-line
`note` the CLI prints ("you see and drive only your own tabs"). `use --print`
withholds the CDP pair as before (§5.1). The raw endpoint reaches no answer,
digest, broadcast, status or lease view; the digest carries `mediation:
{available, port, grants}` (counts only) and every profile / lease view
carries `mediated`.

**The lifecycle.** A grant is minted once per lease for the process's life;
`start` re-points every grant on the profile (live connections close 1012
`browser_restarting`, the SAME url reconnects), `stop` nulls it (503
`browser_stopped` until the next start); `detach` and a dropped lease revoke
the grant (connections close 1008 `lease_gone`) AND close the lease's own tabs
in the browser — measured on 0.32.0 + Chrome 153: a mediated `close --all`
closes the session's daemon side only because `Browser.close` is refused
through a session url, so the tabs would outlive the lease; a backend switch
admits each re-opened tab into its lease's scope; the live view of a mediated
lease asks the SESSION's own daemon for its stream port and a
`--confirm-actions` answer goes to that daemon too; the keeper's shutdown ends
the proxy. Tokens are not persisted — after a server restart a lease is
re-granted lazily on its next `resolve`, exactly as a forwarded port is.
`sharing` cannot flip while sessions hold leases (their env names the kind of
attachment), a profile that is somebody's PIN cannot become instance-shared
(`pinned`, the conversations named), and never on the legacy "Shared (legacy)"
record, which keeps `instance` for admission but is never mediated
(cooperative, labelled legacy). **(Superseded by owner ruling A, 2026-09-26 — below: a pin is a default
attachment, never a directory, so a mediated profile is pinned like any other and the pinned-flip refusal is gone.)**
**A mediated profile is attached, never
pinned**: a pin hands the NEXT launch the profile's directory (P0's spawn env)
and a shared browser has one owner — the keeper — so `setPin` refuses
`pin_refused` by name, a Task-Group / instance default naming one is skipped
at spawn with its reason in the journal (`pinForCreate.refused` → ephemeral),
and the picker does not offer it as a pin target. The panel shows a `shared`
chip with the sentence.

**Measured (do not regress).** Chrome announces `Target.targetCreated`
BEFORE it answers `Target.createTarget`, so the tab a lease is creating is out
of scope for one message — the withheld announcement is remembered and
REPLAYED before the reply (without it agent-browser's target registry never
learns its own tab and `open` hangs forever). agent-browser connects a `ws://`
url directly but DROPS the path of an http one when it rebuilds
`/json/version` — the lease is handed the ws form; the http twins exist for
other CDP clients. Gates: test-browser-mediation (fast, 127) +
test-browser-mediation-chrome (heavy, 30 — the real chrome and the real
binary as two sessions).

**The CDP census — the Chromes it read (src/cdp-census.js; design §6.2.1).**
While the user drives a shared browser the proxy refuses by CLASS, and the
class comes from ONE row per method of each censused Chrome's own
`/json/protocol` (fixtures scripts/fixtures/cdp-protocol-<version>/):
- **153.0.8010.47** (verify S2 r4, 2026-09-27): 664 methods, the first census.
- **154.0.8037.57** (lane-cdp-154, 2026-09-28): +4 −7 — `Ads.getAdScripts` /
  `Browser.getGlobalPrivacyControl` read; `Browser.addMockCamera` /
  `setGlobalPrivacyControl` refused on every lease (whole-browser settings);
  the Shared Storage rows kept, marked `until`.
- **155.0.8059.39** (lane mediation-chrome-155, 2026-10-14; the runner's
  ubuntu-latest moved first, so it was read on Chrome for Testing 155): +3 −0
  — `DOM.setTextMarker` view (a forced spelling / grammar squiggle under the
  page's text: the picture changes, the page sees nothing);
  `DOM.clearTextMarkers` harmless (only this session's markers, as
  DOM.disable does); `DOM.getImplicitAnchorCandidates` read (a popover's
  invokers).
- **156.0.8078.47** (lane chrome-156-drift, 2026-10-22; the runner image
  moved between two runs of the same sha, read on Chrome for Testing 156):
  +11 −1 — the new FindInPage domain view (measured: the find scrolls the
  page to its match and blurs the user's field; stop ends the tab's find);
  `Page.getSubApps` / `getSiblingSubApps` read; the five Private
  Verification Token verbs classed like the Trust Token pair;
  `Storage.getRelatedWebsiteSets` kept, marked `until`.

A newer Chrome's methods with no row are refused BY NAME while the user
drives, and test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑥ prints them and fails until they
are classed. When the runner's Chrome moves before this box's, get that
version's Chrome for Testing build, run `scripts/cdp-protocol-fetch.mjs
--chrome <it>` and the suite with `--chrome <it>`. Gates: test-cdp-census
(fast), test-browser-mediation ⑥, test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑥ (heavy).

### Agent browser v2 — P7: window binding — one group, two panes side by side (2026-09-21; design §4.6 / §3.7, D19 / D24, the §10 P7 row)

**What it is.** A browser window an agent is driving LOSES ITS OWNER the
moment somebody drags it away. Tab groups (src/lib/tab-group.js) now render a
chain in two layouts: `'tabs'` (unchanged) and `'split'` — two of the chain's
tabs shown side by side inside ONE window, the rest still tabs. The chain
gains `layout` and `split {pair, ratio, dir}`; `tabs` and `active` keep
their meanings, a missing `layout` reads as tabs (no migration). PURE
src/lib/chain-layout.js owns the model.

**How it behaves.** Bind = the strip's side-by-side button after a tab
merge (split UX, 2026-09-23 — the title-bar half drop zone this line used to
describe is DELETED: the owner dragged a window left to snap it and landed in
a split, on the side the target bar's half chose; no drag ever splits now, the
tab merge is the one drag exception), or the live view's own bind control (P7
client half). The strip reads in VISUAL order (the left pane's tab on the
left), the same button is the badge in a split (Unsplit / Swap left and
right), and an announced split can be undone for 5 s. The
divider drags (clamped 0.15–0.85, double-click = 0.5, ratio in one kind of
pixel so it lands under the pointer at any UI scale). Moves, minimise,
maximise and desktop switches happen together — it is one window. Clicking a
THIRD tab of a split chain replaced the non-anchor pane in place (D19 (a)) —
**superseded 2026-09-25 (split tabs v2):** every tab belongs to a side and a
click shows it on ITS side, so the chat pane changes only when a tab of its
own half is clicked. **Lifecycle, three paths, one
decision:** closing the browser pane, closing the chat window (host
promotion) and dragging either pane out all collapse the layout to tabs and
move nothing else; a terminated session's history stays readable in its
pane. **Persistence + sync:** layout + split ride layouts.json through
writeLayouts; the multi-client chain key now carries the layout and the pair
order (a remote tabs→split flip used to read as "unchanged"), a remote ratio
applies in place. **Mobile = tabs only:** ≤768px shows the focused pane and
hides the divider by stylesheet; the model keeps the split, so a phone never
writes its own flattening back over the desktop's layout. **Born in the
chain:** `createWindow({intoChain})` opens a window straight into a chain
without painting it standalone (no jump, no autosave churn) — the path the
auto-bound live view takes. **The ownership badge:** a per-SESSION colour
(the webui id's own counter through the task-colour sequence — never the
task-group colour: a session in no group has none, two in one group share
one) with the session's name, drawn on the standalone title bar and on the
tab; a profile shared by several sessions shows N dots, names one per line,
from the digest's `leases`.

**The live view's side (client half).** One `toggleBind()` behind three
surfaces — the live view's bar button ("Snap beside <session>" / "Unbind"),
a title-bar button on the standalone window, and the window menu's row (the
title bar's own menu, so the tab and the phone's long-press reach it); bind
finds the session's own chat/terminal window on this client and calls
`wm.bindSplit`, unbind calls `wm.unbindSplit`. The ownership badge and the
strip's per-pane owner dots are drawn from the digest's `leases` (never
fetched), the viewer first. **Auto-bind** (`browser.autoBindLiveView`,
default ON): when a session attaches a profile (a NEW lease in the digest)
and you are IN that conversation (its window is the active one, or shares its
split frame — lane agent-window-no-pop), the live view opens
BORN inside that window's chain as a split (a conversation you are not
looking at gets its taskbar badge, and its status-bar chip's "Open live view"
opens it) — under a deterministic syncId so
two clients never open two; never on a phone; never for an ephemeral browser
(no lease to see). Settings → Browser → "Open the live view beside the
session when its browser starts".

**The door in every state (lane live-bind-door, 2.369.342 — a daily user:
«sometimes the browser windows a session opens have no side-by-side
button»).** WHERE the door is and what a press does is ONE PURE verdict,
`bindDoor` (src/lib/chain-layout.js), over {human, bound, inChain,
sessionInChain, narrow, sessionWindow}; the law: wherever the act applies a
door that never folds is shown. The table, one sentence per state:
- A free window: the button on its own title bar, plus the bar's icon; a press binds it beside its session's window (`bindSplit`).
- A free window at 420 / 330 px: the same two — the bar's icon is at the badge's rank (`LIVE_BAR_PRIORITY.bind` 1), so the URL and every other act fold first.
- Born beside its chat (the auto-bind's split pane, however narrow): the door rides the view's TAB on the group's title bar (`.tab-door`, built per render by `winInfo._tabDoor`, shown on the active tab and on a shown pane); a press unbinds.
- A non-host tab of the chat's group (after «Unbind — the group stays»): the same tab door; a press SPLITS the group with the chat (`bindSplit` on the same chain), never a refusal.
- The group's HOST: no title-bar button (the group's title bar belongs to every tab) — the tab door while the view is shown, nothing while another tab is.
- No window of its session on this client: the door is shown and a press says WHICH session has no window and offers «Open {name}» (the sidebar card's own attach); a session without a live row is told to open the conversation from the sidebar.
- Browse yourself: no door, by design (no session).
On 2.369.341 (measured) the bar folded bind at rank 3 below a ~446-px bar —
the split pane of a ≤ 900-px group — and the title-bar button lived in the
view's own title bar, never shown while it is a tab of a group: a born-beside
view had no door at all in a narrow pane.

**Do not regress.** `_normalizeChain` at every chain mutation (never a
dangling pair id, never a guessed substitute); `chainSyncKey` at every
layout.js chain site (the pre-fix `tabs.join(',')` key is the silent fork);
the four §6b anti-ping-pong guards untouched; a pane hidden by the narrow
layout is a suspended view (syncHiddenViews derives it); the bind row's
`when` is false for a window without a type (the contributions parity
fixture). Gates: test-window-binding-model (fast, 220; ⑩ the door table + its law over 64 states) + test-window-binding
(heavy chrome, 80; ⑦ the door hit-tested and pressed in every state — a desktop page + a 390×844 phone page on a worktree server
with a fake claude, a fake agent-browser and a fake stream upstream: auto-bind
births the live view inside the chat's chain (one visible window, two measured
panes, the deterministic syncId, frames drawn, the badge in the session's own
colour), Unbind / Snap beside, the divider under body zoom 1.25 within 4 px of
the pointer, a real title-bar drag / minimise / a desktop switch keeping the
panes together, closing the browser pane collapsing to tabs with the chat rect
unchanged, a third tab joining the right side and shown there (split tabs v2 —
D19 (a) retired), closing the chat host (the only tab of its side) ending the
split with no dangling id,
layouts.json carrying layout + split, the phone displaying one pane while its
model and its own save keep the split, a remote same-tabs layout flip applied
where the pre-fix key would not, a ratio-only change in place, a shared
profile's two dots, the strip's per-pane dots) + test-contributions (the
window-menu parity).

### One session, many browsers — the Agent browser window's strip, the per-conversation limit, pop-out / fold-back, grouped chats that follow (lane P, 2026-09-26; docs/design-browser-multiview.zh.md §2 / §3 (b) / §4, D3 / D4 / D5)

**One window, every browser of the session.** The Agent browser window's strip is PURE `browserListFor(status)` over the session's status answer: its attached profiles, its OWN browser (the managed ephemeral record — "This session", full title "This conversation's browser") and each HELPER's browser (a sub-agent's `new-child` handle — "Helper: <its Task's description>" when a witness named it, else "Helper N"). Nothing else ever becomes a tab. Each tab: a state dot (pulsing green = a command is running in the pane you watch; solid = running; HOLLOW = released — "the next command starts it again", or ended), the name (≤16 characters, the full name in the tooltip), who is driving (`agent` / `you`), and a profile's owner dots. It shows with ≥2 browsers (one browser keeps the old look), or with one when the conversation is AT its limit. A browser that starts later becomes a tab AT THE END of the strip (each window keeps its own first-seen order) and NEVER changes the pane you are watching — not even while you drive it (same socket, same takeover). Narrow windows fold the strip by priority into `▾+N` (the tab you look at never folds; a tab running a command outlasts a quiet one; right to left). A helper's tab shows the helper's OWN picture (its own recorded pairs, never the parent's); taking it over pauses THAT helper (`browser_paused` keyed on its handle), never the parent.

**The limit is the conversation's (D4).** The chip at the strip's end reads `own/cap` — this conversation's RUNNING browsers (helpers count) against ITS limit: explicit (the chip's −/+ 1..6, Session Properties → Browsers at once; kept per conversation in the keeper's registry, so a resume keeps it) > its Task Group's default (task detail → Browsers per conversation — for the group's NEW conversations: stamped when a conversation starts, a running one keeps the default it started with, lane P verify) > Settings → Agent browser → *Browsers one conversation may run at once* (3). Red at the limit. Clicking it lists only this conversation's running browsers (never one you are driving), each with Stop — a profile another conversation also uses says "detach it instead" — and the limit stepper (+ *Use the default*). The agent's next browser past the limit is refused `browser_cap` with `scope:'conversation'`, the sentence about this conversation only and the remedy naming the chip and Session Properties. The machine's ceiling (six, shared with desktop apps) stays the hard top: its refusal says "machine ceiling reached", names only the asking conversation's own browsers and COUNTS the rest ("N are in other conversations or desktop apps") — never another session's name, label or lease id. The chip's popover says "Machine ceiling reached" on its own line when the machine is full.

**Released after the turn (B-325a).** A conversation's own browser and its helpers' are stopped 3 minutes after its turn ended (Settings → Agent browser → *Release a conversation's browser after its turn ends*, 0 = never, 30 s floor) — never while the user drives it, never while a live view watches it, never with an unknown turn (**a TERMINAL-mode session publishes no turn at all ⇒ unknown ⇒ its browser is kept until the CLI's own idle timeout — only CHAT sessions are released after the turn**, lane P verify r2). The record and its lease stay, the tab turns hollow, the chip drops by one; the next page verb starts it again through `ensureEphemeral`. A live view NEVER starts a browser of any kind (lane P verify, 2026-09-26): a released ephemeral / helper browser and a stopped attached profile say "Released — the next command starts it again" (a released OWN browser while a profile is attached: "Released — used again only when no profile is attached" — a bare command lands on the attachment); a conversation that has not opened its browser yet says "Not started yet — the next command starts it" (the keeper asks only the launch-free `session info` — `stream status` would spawn a daemon); the pane is picked up by itself when it runs again; one picked up while it is still STARTING waits for the start (a start that fails is what the pane says — lane P verify r2). A conversation's browser is started with the idle timeout its spawn pairs name (the setting only when they name none), so neither the agent's first command nor a live view replaces it after the setting changed (measured on 0.38.1: a client with a different idle restarts the daemon).

**Pop out, fold back (D3).** No new window type: a session may have N `browser-live` windows, all showing the same strip, each with its own selection. Right-click a strip tab → *Open in new window* = one more window preselecting that browser. Fold back: the window's title-bar menu (also its tab / the phone's long-press) → *Fold back into the Agent browser window* (the main window SELECTS the tab it showed and gets the focus; a main window you are DRIVING keeps its browser — said in a toast — and the folded one stays in its strip; folding back the window you are driving CARRIES your control to the main window first — a `pass` from the holder to the other view of the same browser — so nothing is handed back to the agent and nothing is announced; driving in both is refused in words, lane P verify), or drop its ICON on the other window or on the group holding it: the one drag exception folds back instead of grouping two views of one session (every merge drop — icon, tab, title bar — goes through the same rule). The MAIN window is `win-blive-<session>` while it is open, else the oldest other one — closing the main one leaves the next one as the main one.

**Two grouped chats, each with its browser (D5).** Still two panes, never four columns. A new browser's live view is born beside its chat only while that chat is NOT yet side by side (one pane ⇒ chat | browser); a chat already side by side gets its browser as a quiet TAB (on the side that already holds a browser, else on the chat's own side) that pulses once — the shown pair, the window's place and size do not move. In a group with the chats on one side and their browsers on the other, showing a chat makes the other side show ITS browser, and showing a browser makes the other side show its chat — only when the other side currently shows a partnered tab of that kind; a chat you placed there (two chats side by side), a file, a browser whose chat is on the same side, or an ended session: nothing follows. Both live views are already connected, so the follow re-displays and never reconnects. The phone shows one pane and never follows. The follow runs on the client that clicked; the other clients receive the resulting layout.

Gates: test-browser-handles (fast, 152), test-live-strip (fast, 36), test-browser-ephemeral (fast, 139), test-chain-layout (fast, 83), test-browser-pin (181), test-contributions (219), test-session-schema (7); heavy test-browser-live (116), test-browser-multiview (29), test-split-ux / test-window-binding green.

### ONE answer to "which browser is this conversation using", and everything follows it (lane S2, 2026-09-26; naive-user study 2 T4 / T5 / T7)

Every surface that names a conversation's browser — the status-bar chip and its menu, the sidebar card's chip, Session Properties, the live view's title and its strip, the pin picker — prints the same line, computed once on the server over the browser registry (src/browser-fact.js): the browser the conversation uses now ("work", or "no profile (temporary browser)" — never "ephemeral"), and when the pin says otherwise both names in one sentence, amber ("pinned work · running nothing — work could not start — another browser has it open", "pinned work · running Personal — the agent is still on Personal", "work was deleted — its pin was cleared"); raw bp-/bk- ids only in the tooltip. An open live view follows its conversation's browser: when the profile is recreated, adopted, detached or pinned, a view that was showing the conversation's browser moves to the new one by itself (a view you pointed at another browser, a helper's and one you are driving stay), a stale error clears on the next picture or navigation, and Reconnect re-resolves a view whose browser is gone. Every click or key you send while driving has a receipt: when it does not reach the browser within 1.5 s (or the browser refuses it), the bar says "Input is not reaching the browser" and "not delivered — …" instead of "Typing goes to the browser" — and typing into a SHARED profile's browser while you drive now reaches the page (the mediating proxy admits your own input). Deleting a profile conversations pin (the panel's Delete… — owner ruling A (6): every lease released, the browser stopped, every pin cleared, then set aside) leaves each of those chats saying its pin was cleared (a pin left behind by an earlier delete is cleared at boot); the API refuses a pinned set-aside / DELETE without `unpin`. The New Session dialog lists every profile the panel lists (the pick is the conversation's pin — ruling A's default attachment) and follows the registry while open. Session Properties' Agent browser section updates the moment you pin, shows the name on one line, uses the window's own buttons, and Esc closes the window. Gates: test-browser-fact (fast), test-browser-identity (heavy).

### Agent browser v2 — P9 (first half): window targets — a native window as a target, through its accessibility tree (2026-09-21; design §4.9 / §5.1.1 / §6.6, D27 (a) / D28 / D29, the §10 P9 row)

**What it is.** `vibespace-window` puts a native application beside the browser
target: an agent starts an app on a private display VibeSpace owns (the
desktop-app keeper's Xvfb + x11vnc), takes a LEASE on it, reads its
accessibility tree as a `snapshot` with `@eN` refs (the agent-browser habit),
and acts on a NODE through the action that node itself declares. Pixels are
the fallback (`screenshot`), never the primary read (D28).

**The four measurements came first** (§10's P9 row; numbers in
kb-file-structure.md under src/window-targets.js): the RemoteDesktop portal
is reachable from a `systemd --user` background unit on this box (CreateSession /
SelectDevices answered 0, Start raised the consent dialog — D29 (a) viable,
the user's click unproven); Chromium/Electron exports an `Action` on every
node (357/357, buttons 43/43) while gnome-shell's 74 buttons export none and
Qt is unmeasured (not installed); `do_action` → tree-visible change median
0.34 ms on GTK; no maintained node AT-SPI binding exists and the per-node cost
is the same order with or without libatspi's cache (0.34–0.51 ms/node raw D-Bus vs
2,400–5,400 nodes/s through GI), so the helper is python3 + GI in a bounded
subprocess — the boundary the event-loop law demands anyway.

**Scope (D27 (a)).** `list` shows ONLY windows VibeSpace started (the keeper's
live records, every row `origin: vibespace`); the user's own desktop is never
enumerated or addressable. Windows are local-only in this version.

**The verbs and the law (§5.1.1, enforced per verb).** `click <h> @e7` runs the
node's own action (`click > press > activate > doDefault > …`; Chromium's
`showContextMenu` / `clickAncestor` never unnamed); **a node without `Action`
is refused `node_has_no_action` by the engine before any helper call and stays
refused with an injection backend present** — never silently degraded to a
coordinate click (the refusal names the bounds and the audited `--at` path as
the agent's own decision). `type` needs `EditableText` (`node_not_editable`;
the focused node when no ref is named). `key <chord>` has no road on the tree
and `click --at x,y` is coordinates by definition: both are INJECTION, gated by
a RUNTIME probe of the backends on THAT display (`xtest` = xdotool on our
display, the only wired rung; `portal` present-needs-consent, unwired; `uinput`
unwired) and refused `no_injection_backend` WITH the probe rows. The chord
vocabulary is closed (an argv-bound string never passes through).

**The traversal is bounded** (§4.9): a subprocess per call with a wall SIGKILL,
libatspi's per-call timeout inside, a node budget (600 default, 3000 max); an
application that stops answering shows up as an unreadable subtree, never a
stall on the server's event loop. Every snapshot prints its interface CENSUS
(§12.30: coverage is per toolkit and per desktop).

**Leases and audit.** One holder per window (`window_leased` names the holder);
in memory in this half (re-attach after a restart); the persisted lease, the
per-window live pane (`window-live`, needs the xpra transport) and §4.3's three
modes on windows are the second half — `window_paused` is already the word.
`data/window-audit.jsonl` records who / which window / the verb / `by` (node
with role + name + action, point with coordinates, inject with the chord) —
typed text never. `watch` answers the Desktop-app window of the whole private
display, honestly.

**Gate.** test-window-targets (fast, 125): the PURE verdicts with negative
controls, the bounded subprocess over fake helpers (a hung helper killed at the
wall and dead), the REAL leg on this box's own Xvfb + the GTK fixture through the
real helper (refs from the real tree, the census printed, click @ref changing
the app's state as read back from its own tree, the label-drawn button refused
with and without xdotool, EditableText, ctrl+s and a canvas point click landing
on the fixture's witness labels and both refused with the probe when xdotool is
taken away, a PNG of the frame), the engine + routes (one holder, the STATUS
census). SKIPs with evidence without python3-gi / Xvfb / a session bus.

### Agent browser v2 — P9 (second half): the window lease persists, and a window has the three modes (2026-09-21; design §4.3 / §4.9 / §6.6, the §9 `test-window-target` row)

**What it is.** A window target now has what a tab has: a LEASE that survives a
VibeSpace restart (data/window-leases.json — the keeper adopts the window, the
agent's next verb just works), ONE holder per window with a typed refusal for
the second agent (`window_leased` names the holder; a lease whose session is
gone is orphaned and the next `attach` takes it), and the live view's THREE
MODES on the window itself — Watch / Take over / Hand back — because a window's
takeover and handback ARE a tab's: they share `lease.input`, the PURE verdicts
in src/browser-takeover.js, the idle window `browser.takeoverIdleMs`, and the
ONE handback announcer under the ONE spend reason `browser-handback`.

**The `window-live` form.** The Desktop-app window (the P8-1 vnc-display bridge,
src/server/desktop-stream.js) grows the browser live view's bar when an agent
holds the app: the badge with its exact three phrases, Take over, Hand back,
"Agent: <session>", the title "<label> — agent window", and the §6.6 CLASS
MARKER "VibeSpace-started window" (the other class — the user's own desktop —
never appears; the marker is what keeps it distinguishable when it does). In
Watch and while somebody else drives, noVNC is view-only on the client AND the
bridge cuts the viewer's KeyEvent / PointerEvent / ClientCutText out of the
relayed bytes (the FramebufferUpdateRequest beside them still goes through, so
the picture never freezes on a refused click); a window nobody leases behaves
exactly as before (the user's own app, never gated). Each pane names itself with
one viewer id on its stream upgrade (`?viewer=`) and its takeover, so the lease
says which viewer holds it and the bridge hands back (`viewer-left`) when that
socket closes.

**§6.6's second enforcement point.** A takeover STOPS INJECTION of every kind:
while `input` is 'user' every agent verb — snapshot, click @ref, type, key,
--at, screenshot — is refused `window_paused` (the shared wording: when, "do not
retry in a loop", snapshot again when it comes back). What we guarantee is that
WE do not inject; the handback (explicit: announced into the conversation with
"snapshot it before continuing — refs from before the takeover are stale";
idle / viewer-left: zero-spend, the notice rides the next message, one inbox
item) resumes it explicitly. Every audit line carries `origin:'vibespace'`;
takeover / handback lines say `by:'user'` with the viewer and the cause.

**Gate.** test-window-target (heavy, 99): the sieve's strip, the window noun
(browser strings byte-identical), the PURE mode arithmetic, the engine over a
fake keeper with an injected clock, the announcer, the bridge over a fake RFB
server, then the REAL leg — the keeper's Xvfb + x11vnc + the GTK fixture,
`vibespace-window` as a child process for two sessions, a key sent in Watch that
never reaches the fixture's witness and the same key landing after the takeover,
the handback announced, a restart keeping the lease.

### Agent browser v2 — P10: tier 3 — windows on the user's REAL desktop, behind their own switch (2026-09-21; design §7.6 / §7.1's `local-window` row / §4.9 columns 1-2 / §6.6, D27 (b) / D31, the §9 `test-browser-tier3` row)

**Measured first (src/window-desktop.js `TIER3_MEASUREMENTS`, scripts/measure-tier3.mjs):** §12.36 — the installed agent-browser on a STOCK launch reads bot.sannysoft.com 3 passed / 1 failed, nowsecure.nl no challenge, browserscan.net "Robot" (tier 2 = binary absent, tier 3 = the user's own window, banks = the owner's act — each a refusal BY NAME, not a blank); §4.9 columns 1/2 on the user's own session — X11 enumerates only X11 clients (`_NET_CLIENT_LIST` empty here), the Xwayland root grabs black, an Xwayland client's OWN window is readable through `x11grab -window_id`, a native Wayland client has no X window at all yet is on the a11y bus, the ScreenCast portal answers CreateSession/SelectSources from the server's own systemd context and `Start` is the user's click, GNOME's Introspect / ScreenshotWindow are AccessDenied; §12.39 — one `do_action` → a visible pixel change median 3.3 ms (p95 one frame) on the user's Xwayland.

**An app's dialog is part of its window (lane window-dialog-member, 2.369.254 — owner 2026-10-11, JASP's Open on xpra).** A dialog, popup or tooltip the app maps is a MEMBER of the screenshot's plan: members are composed in stacking order bottom→top (xwininfo prints topmost first — measured), the image is their union (its top-left = `originX/originY`, `--at` maps back through it; a window up-left of the main joins only when it overlaps the main window). A top-level mapped while no viewer is attached stays in an unmapped xpra corral (measured): while the main window is mapped, the engine maps that corral before it plans (audited `show-window`). The snapshot's first line says `a dialog is up: "Open" (@e11) — act on it first; its text field: @e15` and the dialog's subtree is listed first; `type` without a ref goes into the dialog's field when the focused node is not editable; `key` (and an injected `type`) focuses the dialog's X window first (`focusedBy: 'window'`). The owner's pane needs nothing new: the xpra client maps every new window and places a dialog inside the pane (`placeInside`). Gates: test-window-targets §DLG, test-desktop-display, test-window-dialog (heavy).

**An app on its own display has an accessibility bus even where the user has none (lane app-display-a11y-bus, 2.369.263 — B-4a59 piece 3):** an app on its own private bus (the portal companion below) is handed the user's a11y bus when there is one (unchanged); where there is none (a fleet pod, a hub without a desktop session) that bus ACTIVATES `org.a11y.Bus` (at-spi-bus-launcher → its own a11y dbus-daemon under the app's 0700 portal/run dir; at-spi2-registryd follows; all reaped with the bus), the bring-up asks GetAddress once (~10 ms), hands `AT_SPI_BUS_ADDRESS` to the app and keeps it on the record (`a11yBus`; `a11y: 'user' | 'own' | 'unavailable: <why>'`). The agent's tree reads of that app (snapshot, the auto-mode probe, the node verbs, the listing) run on THAT bus (`treeEnvOf` in src/window-targets.js), never a global. A machine without at-spi2-core says `unavailable: … (package at-spi2-core)` and the app starts as before. Measured: without it the app warned `ServiceUnknown (org.a11y.Bus)` and the reader died "Couldn't connect to accessibility bus"; the launcher sets no AT_SPI_BUS root property, so the address is the only way in. Gates: test-app-display-a11y-bus (fast), test-app-display-a11y-bus-tree (heavy).

**A sandboxed app's file dialog opens in its own window (lane app-display-portal, 2.369.256 — owner 2026-10-12, JASP's Browse drew nothing in its pane):** a Flatpak/Snap app asks the desktop PORTAL for its file chooser; the user's portal runs on the session bus with the main desktop's DISPLAY, so the chooser drew there. Now a sandboxed app (`flatpak run …`, `snap run …`, /snap/bin/*), a desktop-app BROWSER row (r2, the owner's Chrome on :6 sent its upload chooser to :2: Chromium prefers the portal whenever one answers; known by the row's `browser` fact; its profile already runs `--password-store=basic`, so no keyring is lost), a row with `portal: true`, or every app under the setting `desktop.appPortal` (`auto` default = sandboxed + browsers | `all` | `off`) gets ONE private `dbus-daemon` under its app dir whose only activatable services are xdg-desktop-portal + xdg-desktop-portal-gtk (+ the document portal and permission store, private data/runtime dirs) with the APP's DISPLAY; the app starts on that bus (flatpak's proxy reaches it), keeps the user's a11y bus (AT_SPI_BUS_ADDRESS), and the keeper records `portal: 'on'` (part `portal`, torn down with the app, its FUSE unmounted) or `portal: 'unavailable: <why>'` (the app still starts). The chooser is a window of the app's display ⇒ the pane shows it, the screenshot plan composes it, the tree names it (the companion's pids are in sessionPids). About line: "file dialogs in this window (3 processes)". Non-sandboxed apps keep the user's bus (keyring, notifications). Gate: test-window-dialog ③ (decoy main desktop control; a real google-chrome pressing a file input through the tree, control + fix).

**An app on its own display shows its notifications in its own window (lane app-display-notify-sink, 2.369.263 — B-4a59 piece 2):** an app with its own private bus (the portal companion above) also gets org.freedesktop.Notifications — `src/notify-sink.py` (python3 + GDBus), activated by that bus, journals each notification to the app's 0700 portal dir; desktop-serve reads it and the hub shows a toast INSIDE the app window (the app's name, summary, body, 6 s, a click raises the window), keeps the last 50 under ⋯ ▸ Notifications, and files ONE For-you item ("JASP: Export finished", Show window) when it is critical or no pane shows the window — raising the window resolves it. `desktop.appNotifications` on|off (default on). A machine without python3-gi says `notify: unavailable: <why>`. Every other GUI-bearing session-bus name is in `SESSION_BUS_NAMES`: provided or absent-and-said (a11y → piece 3, secrets → piece 4, polkit → never) — scripts/test-app-display-session-census is the RED census; scripts/test-desktop-app-notify the chrome leg. Ubuntu's `notify-send` CLI is AppArmor-confined to the user bus paths, so it cannot reach any private bus (apps calling libnotify in-process can).

**The switch (D27 (b)).** `window.realDesktopTargets` (Settings → Browser, default OFF, `confirmOn` — the confirmation dialog IS the consent; agents cannot write settings). While it reads `true`, `vibespace-window list` also prints every application on the machine's accessibility bus that is not ours, each a `dw-<pid>` row marked **YOUR DESKTOP** (`origin:'desktop'`, `yourDesktop:true`); `attach` takes the same one-holder lease, persisted with its origin. Turning it OFF drops every such lease at once — at the next verb (`desktop_consent_off`), at the engine's tick and at boot; the user's decision wins before any takeover is even asked for.

**What the class is (tier 3).** No CDP, no automation flag, no process of ours, no directory of ours: the site sees the user's own browser. The channel is the accessibility tree: `snapshot` / `click @ref` (`Action.do_action`) / `type @ref` (`EditableText`) go through NO input injection. **`key` and `click --at` are refused by name (`desktop_injection_refused`) whatever backend the display has** — a chord or a point on the real desktop lands in whatever has focus, possibly the window the user is typing in (§6.6). `watch` is `no_live_view` (they are looking at it). `screenshot` reads an Xwayland client's own pixmap through `x11grab -window_id` on the server's display env and refuses a native Wayland window `capture_needs_portal` by name (the portal's consent click + a PipeWire consumer, not wired — the measurement record's `WIRED` claims say so and the suite goes red if a rung is wired without its ok cell).

**The user's side.** Desktop apps → "Agents on your real desktop": the switch's state, and per window an agent holds a Pause agent / Resume agent (`POST /api/window/desktop/:handle/pause|resume`, the same takeover verdicts as a tab: the agent answers `window_paused` meanwhile). The CLI spells `desktop_consent_off` as THEIR switch (ask, do not work around it).

**The row and the ladder (§7.6 rules 2-5).** `local-window` is wired behind `provider_needs_consent`; it lacks `cdp` / `allowed-domains` / `pin-tab` / `live-view` and each is a typed refusal that says what the class has instead; a tier-3 PROFILE is refused `tier3_is_a_window_target` (escalating to tier 3 creates no record and re-points none — it opens a WINDOW TARGET); switching a profile to it is `switch_refused` naming that act; a site hint's `tier` stays legal only while `backend === null` and a tier-3 `blocked` claim reads "suggests tier 3 (a window on your own desktop — your act …; nothing escalates by itself)" — never "detected"; `hintAction` never answers `auto`. Not in this chunk: the ScreenCast/PipeWire live pane for a native Wayland window (P8's transport), injection on the class (D29), any bank reading (the owner's act).

### Agent browser v2 — r-fix (2026-09-21): the verifier's round on the whole branch

Seven reproduced findings, each fixed where the file's owner suite pins it:

* **A sub-agent on rung D got its own browser only in name.** `childEnvFor` unset the parent's profile symlink on rung C and nothing on rung D — but a PINNED parent's generated config names its directory, so the child's namespace resolved the SAME user-data-dir (the measured SingletonLock shape, or a silent browse in the parent's cookie jar). Now browser-env writes the child its OWN config (`<key>.<n>.json` = the parent's minus `profile`, fence kept, read back and proved profile-less), the env carries `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG=<it>`, the sweep owns it by the parent key; without one a profile-naming parent config is unset. (test-browser-handles 120)
* **Any same-user client could drive a window during another human's takeover.** The pane chose its own viewer id, the bridge's `.set` REPLACED the holder's socket on a duplicate id, and the id was broadcast to every client in `window-leases-updated`. Now the id is a per-socket secret (128 bits, minted per connect, refused 409 on a live duplicate), the lease names a takeover by an OPAQUE tag, and only the taker's own answer carries its tag (`mine` compares tags). (test-window-target 71)
* **An agent could launch an arbitrary executable on a private display.** `POST /api/agent/window/open {exec}` rode the keeper's lease against design-desktop-apps §5 ("an exec is a human's"). Now `open` takes registry ids only — `exec`/`args`/`cwd` ⇒ 403 `exec_is_human` naming `list`'s registry ids as the remedy; the CLI drops the flags. (test-window-targets 80)
* **Installing xpra refused every desktop-app launch.** Inherited from master 2.369.131 by merge: a present-but-unwired rung is passed over with its reason.
* **The mediation sentence promised more than the fence does.** Runtime.evaluate passes while paused BY DESIGN (reads stay open; both mediation suites pin it), so a script could still navigate. The sentence, the CLI's `watch` and the manual now say "input and page-navigation commands are refused; script evaluation and reads are not — do not navigate by script while they drive". (test-browser-mediation 130)
* **`new --adopt <dir>` registered ANY directory** (the user's own Chrome profile, the legacy jar) as session-owned and idle-managed. Now `adoptDirVerdict`: strictly under `~/.agent-browser/` or `data/browser-profiles/`, never the legacy `default-profile`, never somebody else's record; no roots ⇒ refused. (test-browser-handles)
* **The action trace kept key presses and select values verbatim.** A single-character `press`/`keydown`/`keyup` is «1 key» (named keys stay), a `select`'s value/label its length. (test-browser-housekeeping 178)
* **Two heavy suites misbehaved on this box:** test-browser-live's real-chromium leg SKIPs with the vendor's launch error (exit 21 / DevToolsActivePort) instead of failing; test-browser-tier3-chrome's a11y wait is ONE 60 s wall (was 120 × 8 s) and two consecutive helper timeouts SKIP as "the bus is not answering".
* **The seven fast suites the branch broke** (a second counter-zoom literal, the Settings category order test-jobs-triage pins, four usage placeholders the frame census reads as tags, two server.js lines a pin reads by line end, a heavy row's `why` without a category word, the spawnOriginHint line test-codex-effort-meta pins verbatim) are green again; CLAUDE.md's added index lines are heads again with their essays in the kb files (the routing row's full text moved to kb-design-lessons §18).

### Desktop lane E — a window is SHARED with agents, never assumed; tree or pixel mode; "ask an agent to take control" (2026-09-25; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.6, the owner's D1–D7; model src/window-reach.js)

**What changed for the agent.** P9's rule "every window VibeSpace started is addressable" (D27 (a)) is replaced: a desktop-app window is HIDDEN from every agent until the user shares it (D1). `vibespace-window list` shows only what reaches the calling session — a share naming its conversation (or its webui id before it has one), a Task Group it belongs to at that moment (D2: "live now or later" — membership is asked at every verb), or its own `vibespace-window open` (the one exception: shared with the opener only). Every verb on anything else is refused `not_exposed`, and the CLI says "the user has not shared this window with you — ask them (they can share it from the window's ⋯ menu)". The user's REAL desktop (tier 3, P10) is unchanged — its own switch, never this share (D5).

**The user's side.** The Desktop apps dialog has a "Share with agents" row under the machine picker (a summary button + a popover picker: live agent sessions, Task Groups, the mode); what the user sets rides that launch and is remembered PER APP (user state `desktopAppReach`, the desktopAppFrame key) so the next launch of that app proposes it; untouched, the row reads "Hidden from agents (each app remembers its last choice)" and hides for a paired machine (its windows are no agent target). A launched window's ⋯ — now on EVERY rung — and its title-bar / taskbar menu carry "Share with agent…" (the same picker as a dialog: checking shares, unchecking revokes at once; an agent holding the window loses its lease and its next verb answers `not_exposed`; rows another origin wrote are named — "you asked it to take control", "it opened this window") and "Ask an agent to take control…" (D3). A "Shared with N · <mode>" chip appears on the window once anybody is shared (its tooltip names who; a click opens the dialog).

**Tree or pixels (D7, the owner: 像素模式是最接近用户本人操作的方案作为兜底).** Every share has a mode — Auto (default) / Accessibility tree / Pixels — switchable any time; a switch takes effect at the holder's next verb (audited `mode-changed`). Pixels = the agent reads `screenshot` and acts with `click --at` (a pixel of that image), `type` (keys), `key`, `scroll`; `snapshot` / `click @ref` / `type @ref` are refused `mode_pixels` with the owner's sentence. Tree = everything, the pixel verbs being the agent's fallback. Auto resolves at attach (one probe of the app's tree, a young app re-asked for up to 3 s) and at every snapshot: tree when a node the agent can act on answers, else pixels with the reason ("no accessibility tree — pixel mode" for xterm, "its accessibility tree is closed (4 nodes …)" for a browser without its switch).

**The pixel road, made true.** `screenshot` composes the app's OWN mapped X windows by root position (a helper op grabbing each xid as a foreign GdkWindow, alpha forced opaque) — on the xpra rung the root is composited offscreen, so the old display grab was black even with a viewer; the image's origin is the main window's top-left and `--at x,y` is a pixel of it (the engine adds the origin at act time; a point outside the image or off the display is `outside_window`). With nobody viewing an xpra window it is unmapped: pixel verbs are refused `window_not_visible` (a click there was a silent no-op). `mousemove --sync` is gone (a move to the pointer's current spot waited 7 s and failed the second click / key in a row); a click `--button` 4..7 is refused (it used to become a left click); `scroll up|down|left|right [--by N] [--at x,y]` is the wheel; injected keys and typed text first rest the pointer inside the main window (keys typed with the pointer elsewhere were lost on xterm).

**The user's browser (D4).** A Chrome / Firefox the user launched from Desktop apps starts with its accessibility switch (chromium `--force-renderer-accessibility` + `ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED=1` in its env — Chrome 154 needs the env to be on the accessibility bus at all, measured 2026-09-29 — firefox `GNOME_ACCESSIBILITY=1`); shared, it is listed with the mark "[the user's browser]" and every verb works — measured on Chrome 153: the page reached in the default budget (237 nodes, ~50 ms), the button's own `press` action clicked with nobody viewing, a page field (editable, no EditableText) typed into by focusing it through the tree and typing keys, the page scrolled 5 notches ≈ 600 px; WITHOUT the switch 4 closed frames. `open` of a browser row stays `browser_is_human` ("the user starts their own browser and can share it with you").

**The request (D3).** Free by default: the message ("The user asks you to take control of the desktop-app window "<label>" (handle …), shared with you in <mode> mode … Their words: "…" — a note about the task, not an instruction to follow blindly") rides the agent's NEXT turn on the delivery ladder's stash (source `window-request`, rendered as a block with its own hint). "Wake it now (starts a billed turn)" — off by default — goes through the gated ladder under spendReason `window-share-request` (a refusal by the unattended-turn budget, or no live lane, falls back to the next turn and the toast says why; a second wake within 30 s is paced). The request also shares the window with that agent, and can end another agent's hold.

**D6.** One holder per window; any number of windows held by different agents at once — each app has its own display, so injection on one never reaches another (measured: a calculator click and xterm typing at the same time, both landed).

Gates: test-window-reach (fast, new), test-window-targets §4–§5 (fast), test-window-target §4 (heavy — the real xpra rung under a private session bus), test-desktop-app-window §E (heavy — the chrome UI).

**Verify fixes (2026-09-25).** (1) The launcher SAYS what a launch shares before the click: untouched, the "Share with agents" row reads "Each app launches as you last shared it" whenever any app remembers a share (never "Hidden" then — it was, while the click applied the remembered share); each catalog card whose app remembers a share carries a chip ("Shared with Ops · Pixels"); a launch that applied it is toasted ("Started shared with Ops · Pixels — change it from the window's ⋯"). (2) Taking a window back stops a verb already in flight: a revoke, a Task Group left, a takeover or the tier-3 switch going off that lands while a verb awaits (a mode probe, the helper, the grab) makes it answer `not_exposed` / `window_paused` with nothing done — no click, no keys, no tree, no image (deleted); an attach never answers "attached" with its lease gone. Lows recorded, not fixed: docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.6 "lane E verify lows".

### Agent browser — a conversation's own browser keeps its logins and tabs after it closes (lane browser-resume chunk A, 2026-09-30; the owner's ruling 1 "state survives the process"; docs/design-agent-browser-v2.zh.md §3.9)
- **What is kept.** When a conversation's own browser (no profile attached) closes — released after the turn, idled out, stopped by the user, closed by the agent, VibeSpace restarting — its folder `data/browser-profiles/<browser key>` (cookies, site storage: the logins) and its list of open tabs are kept for that conversation; its next browser command starts it again on the same folder. A conversation FENCED to allowed domains keeps its tabs only (the browser CLI refuses a kept profile beside a fence); a helper's browser keeps nothing. No process is kept alive for it.
- **Until when.** Until the conversation ends (a Terminate is NOT an end — Terminate → Resume finds the same key; it ends when no live session carries the key and no binding names it, an hour after the stop at the earliest), the user's **Forget** in the Agent browser panel, an adopt that moved the folder into a named profile, or the size bound: `browser.keptBytesPerConversation` (512 MB — over it the caches go, the logins never) and `browser.keptBytesTotal` (4 GB — over it whole kept browsers go, least recently used first). A running browser is never trimmed or removed, and the kept browser of a conversation that is still running (its browser stopped after the turn) is never removed by the total bound (its caches may go; the sweep reports it). `browser.keepConversationBrowser` off ⇒ today's empty browser for conversations started or resumed after.
- **Which restarts reopen the tabs by themselves (D2).** Recorded now: an automatic stop marks the kept tabs to be reopened at the next start; the user's Stop / the agent's own `close` / `detach` keep them without reopening. (The reopening and the Resume button are chunk B.)
- **Where it shows.** Agent browser panel → **Kept browsers** (tabs, size, since when, why it stopped, Forget); the ephemeral row's Stop says what a stop keeps; three settings rows (Agent browser).
- **Resume + hand back and continue (chunk B, the owner's ruling 2).** A stopped conversation browser's live view shows **Resume** in place of Reconnect when something is kept (the fact's `own.kept`, PURE `ownResumable`), with a status line saying what (tabs + logins / tabs only); the newest browser end card in the chat and the panel's kept row (while a live session carries the key) offer it too. Resume starts the browser on the same folder and reopens its tabs in order, on the tab that was showing (by CDP target id); a tab that fails is named. The agent's next command is told once (`[browser_resumed]`). **Hand back and continue…** (while you drive it, or after you resumed it) ends the takeover and puts your one-line note + the tabs on the conversation's NEXT turn (the stash — "a browser handback" on the strip; a card in the chat says nothing was sent) — no turn is started. After an automatic close the agent's next command reopens the tabs by itself (`[browser_restored]`); after a deliberate one it is told they are kept (`[browser_kept]`) and `vibespace-browser resume` reopens them.
- **Tabs (chunk C, the owner's ruling 3).** On a named profile's ONE Chrome every session sees every tab and the browser CLI itself would close any of them (measured on 0.38.1) — so the agent's `tab` verbs on a shared profile are VibeSpace's: `tab list` names ITS tabs (the tab it was given, its `tab new`s, what its pages opened) and only counts the rest; `tab <id>` / `tab close <id>` of the user's own tab or another conversation's is refused `not_your_tab` before anything runs; closing its current tab is said (its next page verb meets `tab_gone`, and the CLI names this tool's way out). The live view has a **tab row** under the browser strip: one chip per tab (the site's initial on a colour, the title, whose it is: "The agent’s" / "Yours" / "Another conversation’s" / "Nobody’s"); while you drive (Take over) you can switch the agent's tab or close one of them (never its last; closing the one on show moves it to a neighbour first) — the handback tells the agent what you closed and where you left it; your own tabs (Browse yourself) you switch / close any time (never your last — Close ends your browsing); another conversation's tab never gets a control here. **Close all…** at the row's end quits that browser, the confirm naming it. On a "separate tabs" profile the row lists but the agent keeps its own tabs (its proxy fences them).
- **Do-not-regress.** The folder is derived from the key, never read from the store; the store is 0600 and every url/title passes the peer-text door both ways; a registered profile's folder is never removed through the kept store; another conversation's kept folder is refused to an agent's `new --adopt` (`adopt_not_yours`); the fresh-key rule counts a kept key as named; nothing of a running browser is trimmed. Gate: test-browser-kept.

### Agent browser — New profile… copied from a stopped profile ("Copy logins from", lane browser-profile-clone, B-9669, 2026-10-08)

WHY: a long money workflow (a bank site) wants its own profile outside the shared browser's failure domain; before, the only way to a second profile with the same logins was signing in again by hand. The New profile… dialog has ONE more section, **Copy logins from**: "Don't copy" (the default) and every NAMED profile on the machine the new profile runs on, each with its state as words — stopped (pickable), running with no lease (pickable; "it will be stopped first" — submit runs the panel's own Stop, then waits for the browser's exit, witnessed by the recorded pid + starttime and the folder's SingletonLock, ≤ 10 s ⇒ `source_still_running`), leased (names the holder; refused `source_leased` — a browser is never taken from an agent), no folder (cdp / cloud). A paired machine says why it cannot copy (`clone_unsupported_platform` on macOS/Windows; `clone_agent_too_old` — no agent has a copy op yet).

WHAT IS COPIED: the source's folder whole, into the folder the keeper mints for the new profile, EXCEPT two PURE closed tables (src/browser-clone.js): the runtime/lock files (SingletonLock/Socket/Cookie, DevToolsActivePort, lockfile, RunningChromeVersion, *.lock) and the pure caches (Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache, GPUPersistentCache, ShaderCache, GrShaderCache, Dawn*, component_crx_cache, optimization_guide_*). Service Worker, IndexedDB, Local/Session Storage, Cookies, Login Data, Local State are kept. Over 2 GiB (excluded entries not counted) ⇒ `clone_too_big`. The copy is atomic (`<dir>.copying`, renamed at the end; a failure leaves nothing, `clone_failed` + the fs code) and runs off the event loop. The new record carries `clonedFrom {id, label, at}` (the panel fold: "copied from {label} on {date}") and the source's provider + build (a folder is bound to the Chrome that wrote it); never its who-may-use list, pins, leases or notes. A one-time snapshot: logins drift after. A user's act only (POST /api/browser/profiles `{cloneFrom}` refuses an agent token; no agent verb).

DOES THE COPY DECRYPT (measured 2026-10-08, agent-browser 0.38.1 + Chrome 154.0.8037.57, scratch HOME + private runtime dir, headless and the hidden window): yes. The CLI starts every Chrome with `--password-store=basic --use-mock-keychain`, so cookies are `v10` (Chrome's fixed Linux key) even with an unlocked gnome-keyring on the session bus and XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME; the copy is signed in, the source stays signed in, both run at once. No launch flag was added — no profile written through the CLI holds keyring-encrypted cookies.

### Agent browser — a named profile is usable by all my conversations (owner ruling A, 2026-09-26, "A吧"; docs/design-agent-browser-v2.zh.md §3.2.6)

Two naive-user studies failed the same task (a login made in one chat, used from another). Now: **a named profile is usable by every conversation of the owner's** — the UI's new profile, an agent's `vibespace-browser new` / `--adopt`, the card's "New persistent profile from this session's browser" (the adopt stops the conversation's own browser before its folder moves). **One browser per profile**: a second conversation JOINS the running Chrome in its own tab (never a second launch on the directory — the exit-21 SingletonLock); two first commands at once wait for the one launch. **The pin (New Session, Session properties, a Task-Group / instance default) is the conversation's default browser**: its next bare command with no attachment opens the profile through the keeper — nothing is relaunched, the browser it had keeps its pages; a pin that cannot open is refused with the reason and "pinned profile: …" — never a silent temporary browser; the user's pick works even on a profile kept to another conversation, and the user's LATEST choice wins (narrowing takes it from a pinned chat; picking it again gives it back). **One driver at a time**: while another conversation's agent is mid-turn on a shared browser (a command in the last 90 s), a command answers `browser_busy` naming that conversation and the wait bound; while the user drives it from another chat's live view, `browser_busy` says so; no queue. The live view's strip shows a shared profile's tab even when it is the chat's only browser and names who drives it. **The cap**: a shared browser counts once in each chat that holds it and once on the machine; a join never trips the machine ceiling. **The Agent browser window's profile row**: Who can use it (All my conversations / Only <a conversation>) · Rename… · Delete… (warns "N conversations use it", takes it from each, stops it, clears every pin, then sets it aside under "Deleted profiles (kept aside)" until Delete permanently); the mediated chip reads "separate tabs". **Words**: a refusal names a button or a wait, never a command line (`not_owner`: "switch it to All my conversations in the Agent browser panel, or pick it for this conversation in Session properties"). Migration `2026-09-browser-profiles-all-conversations` moves every agent-made (session-owned) record to all conversations. Gates: test-browser-share-model (fast), test-browser-share (heavy, the real 0.38.1 + Chrome).

### All agents — the first choice of every "who may use it" (lane everyone-principal, 2026-10-02; the owner: every place that configures who may use something offers All)

Every place that asks which agents may use something draws the one principal picker with **All agents** (每个会话，现在和以后 / every conversation, now and later) as its FIRST row — above Recent, kept by any search, its chip first, never greyed, never picked by a stray Enter (Enter's fallback and the first ↓ land on the first named row; All is one ↑ above or a click). Surfaces: Channels **Grant access…** (All may see and act — with an authority like any row), **Notify…** (offered while All has access; it wakes EVERY running conversation, a billed turn each — the row and the preview sentence say so — and the daily cap counts per conversation), **Reach & policy → Grant reach to…**, a desktop app's **Share with agents** (the launcher row and the window's dialog — the window's chip reads "Shared with: All agents (N more rows) · Auto"), **Who can use <machine>?** (each list: Nobody / Agents you pick — All agents there IS the old "everyone"), **Who can use <profile>?** (the radios are gone: the picker alone; All agents = every conversation, the profile row reads "All agents"). Rows picked beside All are kept: taking All away restores them exactly. An agent asking for access to a channel conversation All may already see is told "already allowed" — no For-you card. Not offered (by design): a group's members (New group / Invite…) and "Ask an agent to take control…" (one agent). Gate: scripts/test-everyone-principal.mjs.

### One «who may use this» everywhere, with «除了» (lane grants-unify, 2026-10-23; the owner: 「权限系统要 unify 一下，不想引入太多复杂度」)
Every place the owner gives agents something — an Agent browser profile's «Who can use it», an automation key's 授权给… (and its reach), a channel's Grant access… / Notify… / API access, a machine's exit (borrow its network, run commands), a desktop window's share, a Task Group's outside visibility — is ONE row `{to, except}` of the grants store (data/grants.json; src/grant-model.js + src/server/grants-store.js) drawn by THE picker. Two concepts only: 给谁 (the picker's rows: conversations, Task Groups, All agents) and 除了 — after a Task Group or All agents is ticked, a folded «除了（可选）» row opens the same searchable list over that group's members (under All agents every conversation); chips read «除了：…×»; a member with its own row is greyed «有自己的授权» (its own grant counts — rows add, an exception subtracts only its own row). Effect is immediate (each door re-judges on the change: an open exit forward stops, a browser lease is re-judged, a window lease is dropped at the next verb, a channel member left out is never woken and reads nothing there); an exception whose member left the group simply stays. An agent refused this way is told `excepted` with where the owner lifts it. Existing settings were carried over unchanged by the migration 2026-10-grants-unify (each resource judged old reader ≡ new reader before it was written). Not drawn: Reach & policy's «Grant reach to…» (a one-principal grant, not a list).

### Browse yourself — the user as one more holder of a profile's browser (B-6ae8, 2026-09-28; docs/design-browse-yourself.md + the owner's decisions)

The owner: "我能自己打开一个浏览器profile用它浏览吗" — and "我其实也相当于是一个agent而已". **Browse yourself** is the first action on every local profile row of the Agent browser panel (and "Open it yourself" on the switch dialog's empty line when the profile's browser is not running — the "a site blocks my agent, let me get past the check" path). It starts the profile's browser through the same start an agent's first command uses (same Chrome, directory, config, proxy — the logins are there), or joins it when it runs, and opens the user's OWN tab in it; a live-view window opens on that tab already driving (badge "You are browsing") with an **address row** (Back · Forward · Reload · the address — web addresses only; the caret starts there on a blank page).

- **Nothing of the agents stops.** Conversations on the same browser keep working in their own tabs — no confirm, no pause, no interruption, no card. Taking over an AGENT's tab from a conversation's live view is still the takeover (interrupt, tell, remind — unchanged).
- **Recorded like an agent's.** His clicks, key chords, typing (as a length — «13 chars», never the words) and scrolls are trace entries with before / after frames; his browsing is a session in the Sessions list ("You · 14:02 · 4 min") with Replay. The profile row's **Also record my own actions** (on by default) turns that off — then only when he started and stopped is kept.
- **Two ends.** **Close** closes his tab / window only — the browser stays for the agents and closes by itself after the idle timeout when nobody holds it. **Quit the whole browser** stops it for everyone; its confirm names the conversations that lose their pages ("{name} also uses this browser…"), and each one's next command opens the browser again with a new tab.
- **Walking away.** Closing the window without Close (or a dropped connection) keeps his tab: 12 h when HE launched the browser (Settings → Agent browser → "Keep your own browsing tab after its window closes", `browser.humanKeepMs`), 10 min when he joined a browser an agent launched; Browse yourself again (the row now reads **Open your browsing window**) continues where he was. A server restart keeps it too: his tab and the browser survive, the row offers Continue, and his window re-attaches by itself.
- **One window, any device.** A second window of his (another tab, the pushed layout, the phone) watches ("You're browsing this in another window") until he presses **Continue here**; on a touch device a **Keyboard** button raises the soft keyboard.
