### Agents are TAUGHT vibespace-channels on their reach (lane channels-teach, 2026-10-18)

- The SessionStart tools section and the per-turn reminder name `vibespace-channels` when the session may READ at
  least one conversation the user connected (`list` / `search "<words>"` / `read <conv>`, a reply is a proposal, look
  here BEFORE any other connector or file, `vibespace-docs channels`), or only REQUEST some (`list --all` + `request`).
  The reach is the engine's `reachCountFor` (listFor's walk, counted; the built-in Agents adapter never counts), read
  through a 60 s per-session memo on prompts, fresh at SessionStart. No reach / integration off / no engine ⇒ the
  injection is byte-identical. A shell read of data/channels/ as files gets the bypass card line. Gate:
  test-channels-teach; bytes in scripts/measure-prompt-context.mjs (test-prompt-budget).

### An agent's channel search says what it found (lane channels-search-says-hidden, 2026-10-21; a field miss)

- `search "words" --full` prints the SAVED hits first — exactly the plain search — then what the account's own search
  ADDED `(not saved here)`; none ⇒ «the account's own search added nothing beyond the N saved hits above», never «nothing».
- Several words match a stored message holding EVERY one, each anywhere: its text, its sender's name, an attachment's
  name or its conversation's title (`store.search`; the owner's Channels search box reads the same function).
- A match in a conversation the agent may NOT read (in an account it reads or may request something of) is said to
  EXIST — ONE sentence, `HIDDEN_TEXT`, with the user's door (Channels › ⋯ → Grant access…) — never a count, an account,
  a title or a word (the owner: a number leaks too). «nothing matches» only for nothing. PURE `SR.searchAnswer` owns
  the words; gates test-channel-search §S, test-channels-agent-cli ㉒.

### Channels: a Gmail draft is never a message of its thread (lane gmail-draft-not-a-message, .346; fleet feedback fb-9aa1d3bd1e)

- A record's KIND is read off the vendor's labels: a message Gmail labels DRAFT is `kind: 'draft'` (`draftState`
  `trashed` in the Trash / Spam, else `saved`); a record stored before is re-judged at read (`asDraftRecord`).
- The window draws the thread's MESSAGES in order and the account's standing draft AFTER the last one — ONE dashed
  «草稿 · 未发送» row (saved time, its words; no avatar, no To / Cc, no message bar); a binned draft is only «1 条草稿已删除»;
  a draft a later save or a later own sent mail stands for is not drawn (PURE `draftsOf`, the agent's read asks it too).
- Nobody received a draft: no rule matches it (no wake, no For-you, no judge), it is never unread, never the row's last
  line. The agent's `vibespace-channels read` prints it as `[draft · not sent] <words>`, counted apart.

### Communication panel — P3: outbox, approval, receipts (2026-09-16; design §8, §9, §11, §12.3; decisions 7/8/9/11/16/17)

- **A reply is a PROPOSAL.** An agent (`vibespace-channels reply`) or the user
  (the conversation window's composer) proposes; `src/channel-policy.js`
  decides `direct` or `review`: the channel's policy (own > the adapter's
  default > review) is the base and the guards — a link, an attachment,
  off-hours (only when `channels.offHoursTz` is set), draft-only authority —
  can only tighten it; an unreadable policy or guard is review (fail closed).
- **A direct send's receipt is the command's own answer (lane channel-direct-send-sync, 2026-10-21; the owner: an agent that may send directly should learn the outcome from its own command, not from a second message queued for its next turn).** When the policy is `direct`, `vibespace-channels reply` waits for the vendor and prints the receipt INLINE — SENT · vendor id · sent as · what the recipient sees — and the engine files NO «[Channels · Outbox]» receipt message for it (no stash, no wake, no queue row); the Outbox shows that row as sent, read inline. The receipt still travels as a MESSAGE for an approval-gated proposal (the person acts later), a direct send whose CLI timed out or died before collecting (a bounded ≤ 20 s fallback), a Background Work job / another door with no waiting CLI, a reaction / recall, and a later fate change. And a batch of notifications HELD for the next turn now heads by the reason the hub held them — «Messages that arrived during your previous turn» (a turn was running) / «Messages held until this turn (a delivery earlier would have cost a wake)» (idle) — never «unreachable» for a conversation that is taking that very turn.
- **The receipt roads — reply, compose, api (lane inline-receipts-compose-api, 2026-10-21).** The same rule for the two siblings of `reply`. `vibespace-channels compose` (a NEW mail; `compose --caller`, one per caller) sent directly prints its receipt inline and confirms the read, as `reply` does — no «[Channels · Outbox]» message follows; no waiting CLI, or past the hold's window, it messages. A raw API call: a DIRECT write (write-auto / write-all / an always-allowed shape) runs inline and files nothing — its answer IS the outcome. A write that waits for the user (write-ask, a sensitive call) is a proposal: `api … --wait` / `api wait <id>` read its outcome with the card's words (RAN — HTTP n, size · REJECTED by … · EXPIRED · WITHDRAWN · approved but NOT run), and no «[Channels · API]» receipt message is filed for it; a proposal no CLI waits on — or decided after its CLI stopped waiting — keeps its card AND its receipt message on the next turn. One verdict for all three: `receiptRoad` (src/channel-policy.js); a grep-derived census (test-channel-outbox §C) reds a send verb that does not thread `collect`.
- **Two surfaces, one store.** The approval card is rendered inline in the
  conversation window and in the singleton Outbox window (⚙ → Outbox…, the
  panel's Outbox button with the awaiting count) from the same store; approve
  (optionally edited — both texts kept, the receipt says `edited`), reject
  with a reason, or let it expire (24 h). The rail badge counts unread +
  awaiting.
- **The identity row is on every card**: "Will send as you/the bot", and when
  the adapter's `identityMarking` is `marked` or `unknown` a warning with the
  adapter's verbatim sentence (or that it is unverified). The message body
  carries NO honesty line by default (decision 17 overruled): the truth is
  owed to the one approving and the one drafting, never pushed into the
  recipient's message.
- **One "For you" pointer per conversation** (count-free text, count in
  detail, `pendingTodoId` persisted on the row, retracted by the engine when
  the last proposal leaves awaiting-approval; an inbox throw degrades to the
  badge + Outbox window).
- **Approval re-resolves `convCaps` unconditionally** before the send; a
  conversation that no longer accepts messages refuses with
  `send-not-available` + the adapter's reason, the proposal fails, the
  receipt carries the reason verbatim.
- **Exactly-once.** An audit ATTEMPT line before the request, an OUTCOME line
  after; a thrown send is `unknown`, never auto-retried — the user is asked
  to check the platform.
- **The receipt** (`sent`/`edited`/`rejected`/`expired`/`failed`, with
  `sentAs` / `identityMarking` / `identityMarkingText`) reaches the drafting
  agent through the delivery ladder with `noWake` — only into a turn already
  running, else stashed for its next turn — unless the assignment's
  "Wake the agent with each outbox receipt" opted in (decision 8). Every
  vendor-controlled field of the receipt block (title, label, vendor id,
  sentAs) is frame-inert and single-line — the wake block's rule (2026-09-16).
- **Audit** (`data/channels/audit.ndjson`): `draftedBy` / `approvedBy` /
  `sentAs` / `identityMarking` on every outbox line; it never leaves the
  instance.
- **AgentReach** (row menu / window bar → "Reach & policy…"): every grant
  with its origin (you granted / by assignment / you approved a request),
  user rows removable, grants to a live session or a Task Group, open access
  requests (`vibespace-channels request`, one For-you item with the reason)
  approved into exactly one visible grant; everything hidden by default,
  hidden ≡ nonexistent for an agent.
- **The built-in Agents adapter** lists live agent sessions as conversations
  (reach = the msg-acl answer), sends through the delivery ladder as the
  user's own message (policy default `direct`), and marks its identity
  `marked` / recipient-ui.
- **P4 — real external send (§9.4 / §9.5).** Lark and Gmail now send as the
  USER; until the held token carries the send scope(s) the composer's footer
  says what unlocks it (reconnect; on Lark also enable the two dotted scopes
  + publish a version) instead of a greyed control. Lark sends carry the
  vendor `uuid` = the proposal id; Gmail sends are two-phase (a draft in the
  thread, then its send, threading headers off the anchor). A send whose
  answer was LOST is `unknown` — never "failed", never re-sent — and the
  card offers **Check outcome** (only where the adapter declares an
  idempotency mechanism): landed ⇒ sent with the receipt, the For-you item
  retracted; not landed ⇒ failed; else still unknown with the count of
  checks. A proposal the server died on mid-send is `unknown` at boot. **The
  sender honesty line is OFF by default** (Settings → Channels, per-channel
  override on the panel row): when on, an agent-drafted message ends with
  one line naming the agent — the card says so BEFORE approval, the receipt
  after; your own drafts never get one. The panel row shows the platform's
  own attribution of the last real send (the §21-item-3 proof; Lark's
  declaration stays `unknown` in code until an owner-run real send is read).

- **The raw-API call card (lane api-call-card-words, .265)** — the Outbox row, the chat card and the API access dialog draw ONE card per proposal in the card grammar (kb-patterns «The card grammar»): the title says who does what to which named thing (src/api-call-words.js: Lark docx blocks delete / insert / change, docs create, im send / reply, drive upload, bitable rows; Slack chat.postMessage + conversations.create / invite / archive / rename / setTopic; Gmail send / drafts; unknown = vendor + METHOD + last segment). **The three layers of words (lane api-call-words-from-spec, .265)**: (1) hand rows only where the BODY carries the words (a block / row / people count, a title, a channel name); (2) the vendor's long tail GENERATED at build time from its own catalogue (src/api-call-words.generated.js ⇐ scripts/gen-api-call-words.mjs over scripts/api-specs/: Slack 170 + Gmail 79 + Lark 164 methods) as 「{verb} {resource}（{object}）」 (en: “{object}”) — e.g. 「批量删除 文档块的子块（DocFixtu…）」, the object from the path slot or Slack's `channel`; (3) the generic 「调用 Lark API（POST users）」. The agent's `--why` is a quoted line, never the title nor the object's name. A chat is named from the channel index (`conversationName`) and opens its conversation; a document takes the 《title》 the agent wrote in `vibespace-channels api … --why "…"` (new flag, stored as the proposal's `note`), else an 8-char id chip. Sensitivity and tier are chips. Method, URL, headers, body (pretty, 2 KB), size, sha256 and the always-allow shape (「以后放行：…」) live under one collapsed 技术细节; the always-allow button says 「执行，并以后不再问（<the phrase>）」. Approve needs no reason; Reject opens a reason popover. The Outbox's expanded card repeats neither the title nor the row's chip / outcome.

### Communication panel — a3 i18n: the codes cross the wire, the client says the words (2026-09-18; owner "似乎没太做好 i18n"; docs/design-communication-panel-polish-audit.md §1)

- **No English leaves the server as chrome.** The a1 audit found the eight
  surfaces' `t()` coverage at 368/369 and the leaked English elsewhere: codes
  printed raw (`token-expired`, `NO-STORE-ON-PLATFORM`, `rpc-queue`), engine
  sentences shown verbatim (`outcome unknown: …`, `forbidden: …`, the
  store's `the cluster provides no default…`), the built-in row's seeded
  `user: 'you'`, and the adapters' / the registry's DECLARED labels and help.
  Each is now STRUCTURE the client words: `outcome` on a proposal, `whyCode`
  + `whyParams` on a credential, `auth.self`, `authorityWhyCap`,
  `reconcileWhyCode`, `adapterLabel`; the code composers live in the PURE
  modules (channel-caps / channel-policy / channel-filter /
  integration-registry) and every route failure toasts by `code`
  (`src/lib/channel-words.js`). An agent's contract strings (`p.reason`, the
  receipt, the CLI's output) stay English on purpose.
- **A declared string is a key.** `i18nKey(…)` marks a human-visible string
  in a PURE data module (registry rows, adapter OPTIONS); the extractor
  collects it beside `t()` so the dictionaries' census sees it; zh + ja carry
  every one (144 new keys; 45 zh / 24 ja entries re-worded — 发件箱 / 送信箱
  for Outbox, 提案 for proposal, 频道 for channel, 适配器 for adapter, 审批
  for review-as-a-verb; `tc('policy', …)` for the policy mode).
- **Two wording fixes that were product bugs:** an UNTRACKED conversation's
  footer says "Not tracked — messages are fetched once you track it." with
  the Track verb (it said "the send capability is not known yet"); a Task
  Group is named by its `title` (the store has no `name`, so every group
  showed as its id in the Assign / Reach editors — pinned by
  test-channels-e2e ⑮ since r4).
- **r4 (2026-09-21, the verifier's i18n leaks):** the filter validator's
  refusal carries a `code` (+ the rule kind) beside its English contract
  sentence and the editor words it (`filterProblemText`) — "Add rule" no
  longer prints `keyword: value is required` under zh/ja; every "For you"
  item the channels engine files (the pointer, an access request, an
  unknown outcome, the failure headline) rides as `i18n` STRUCTURE the
  inbox words with the device's t() (the English text stays the dedupe key
  and the CLI's contract); the needs-credentials line words a code on every
  path (a self-resolving adapter's `auth.whyCode`), never the store's raw
  sentence; the state-dot tooltip's instant uses `deviceLocale()`.
- **Gate:** scripts/test-channels-i18n.mjs (heavy) drives the a1 driver at
  zh AND ja over all eight surfaces and asserts ZERO Latin-only visible text
  nodes outside a PRINTED allowlist (proper nouns, URLs, ids, the fixture's
  own data by DOM path); a planted English literal turns it red.

### Communication panel — a4 UI design: hierarchy, rhythm, icons, empty states, the stepper, the card, the Outbox views, the phone (2026-09-21; owner "界面很乱，没有层次，你需要用前端技能+实际渲染截图好好设计优化一下"; docs/design-communication-panel-ui.md §4 = the spec, direction A)

- **The panel is a list, not a control panel.** Bar (`{n} conversations ·
  {k} tracked` + the Outbox button: outbox glyph · label · accent count — the
  label hides under a 200px container because the 260px default sidebar
  leaves 172px for the bar, measured) → one collapsible `folder-header`
  section per adapter (chevron · kind glyph · name · 6px state dot with the
  lane in its tooltip · `tracked/total` · ⋯) → rows as bordered
  `session-item-card`s on ONE grid: line 1 = title + the ONE freshness pill,
  line 2 = participants + the needs-you badges right-aligned (awaiting =
  accent-outline pill with a check glyph, unread = accent count, `not
  tracked` as 9px text), line 3 only when assigned. Every adapter verb is in
  the section's ⋯ menu (`channel-adapter`, state-driven; the Sender line is a
  checkable row); a status line exists ONLY when the adapter has something
  to say beyond "connected", wraps at 10px and carries its one verb, amber
  when it needs the user. Under a 180px container the two badges collapse to
  one accent pill carrying their sum (tooltip = the breakdown). A fresh
  instance is `.empty-hint` + the Connect section of full-width `mounts-btn`
  rows with the credential path as the note under each. The panel is a
  NAMED container (`chan-panel`) — the rows are inline-size containers
  themselves, so an unnamed query collapsed the badge pair at the default
  width (round 3); the day separator's date follows the device's language
  (`deviceLocale()`), never the browser's.
- **One colour per meaning (§4.3).** Accent = needs you (unread fill,
  awaiting outline, the card's awaiting pill), green = live evidence / sent,
  neutral tint = an age / rejected, amber = a warning / `unknown` (the one
  outcome that is NOT a failure), red = failed. Text on a tint uses the
  meaning tokens `--ok-text` / `--warn-text` / `--bad-text` / `--attn-text`
  (the raw hue mixed toward `--text`) so both themes clear AA at 9–11px; blue
  left the feature. Every glyph is an SVG from src/lib/icons.js through
  `channel-chrome.js icon()` (chat / mail / robot / more / chevron / check /
  alert / outbox / filter / reach / connect / plus / copy / external / info).
- **The connect wizard is a stepper** (Credential ✓ → Consent → Track): the
  consent page as the ONE primary button beside Copy link, the port-busy
  refusal as a NAMED amber line with the alert glyph, paste-back as a
  collapsed step that opens itself when nothing listens, and a finished flow
  turns into step 3 — the Track picker — in the same dialog.
- **The card is five lines**: state pill · drafter · age → text → ONE meta
  line (why · needs approval · will send as · expires · the sender line) →
  the identity warning ONCE, only when it warns → outcome → a quiet footer
  (reconcile facts, receipt) → reject · edit · approve right-aligned with one
  primary. The inline section shows the cards that need the user plus the
  newest two decided ones and links the rest to the Outbox; the Outbox
  window is a toolbar (summary + Awaiting | All) over cards, All grouped by
  STATE with a dot per head.
- **The editors on the house form rhythm**: short fields paired on a
  two-column grid, rule rows with their own kind selector + ×, Add rule
  under the list, the estimate as ONE bold stat with its honesty as the hint
  under it, the receipt-wake row a `dialog-check-row`; the reach dialog is
  one bordered list (who · neutral level pill · origin · ×) with grants named
  from the roster; one 520px width token for the whole family.
- **Integrations**: an undecryptable row is a state chip + one sentence; the
  Test verdict is one line; the copy button has the copy glyph; field help is
  an info affordance (tooltip + tap-to-show) instead of a paragraph per field.
- **The phone (≤480px)**: rows pad `8px 10px`, every card / composer /
  footer / dialog button is ≥36px tall, the editors' grids become one column,
  the card's three actions stay on one row; nothing scrolls sideways at
  375px (test-channels-e2e ⑫ b).
- **No behaviour change**: the freshness-chip honesty contract, the
  read-mark rule (a user action, never a repaint), frame neutering and
  `escHtml` / textContent on every wire string are byte-for-byte in meaning.
- **r4 (2026-09-21, the verifier's findings on the build, each reproduced
  on the rendered chrome):** the panel REPAINTS IN PLACE — the rail no
  longer tears it down on every broadcast, `draw()` swaps one fragment and
  keeps the scroller where the user left it, zero refetches (a1 D12 was
  still open: 7 teardowns / 7 fetches / scroll 0 for 7 broadcasts); an
  UNTRACKED row carries NO freshness pill (§4.3 — its `not tracked` text is
  the claim; the pill there was the one that truncated ja's negation) and a
  tracked row's pill never shrinks (the title yields first, the pill
  ellipsizes only past the title's floor; ja off words shortened); the
  warning line's alert glyph is a fixed slot beside its sentence (the
  `> span` rule had made it a 124px box); the 200px rail hides the pill and
  the section name (tooltips carry both) and keeps the count; the
  assignment line's `→` became the filter glyph. Gates: test-channels-e2e
  ⑬ (repaint in place) · ⑭ (glyph ≤ 8px from its sentence at 260/340/500) ·
  ⑮ (group title) · ⑯ (every tracked pill whole at 260 in zh/ja/en, none on
  an untracked row).
- **Gates**: test-channels-e2e ⑫ (row grid ±1px, 375px overflow, SVG-only
  glyphs, five distinct state colours + unknown ≠ failed, age pills neutral /
  live green) + the moved legs (the Sender line through the ⋯ menu, reject
  by `data-reject`); test-channels-i18n (zh + ja census over the new chrome);
  test-integrations-ui; scripts/dbg-comm-surfaces.mjs for the BEFORE/AFTER.

### Communication panel — agent GROUPS, g1: the model + the engine (2.369.159; design-communication-panel.zh.md §22, owner rulings D1/D2 + §22.5)

- **A group exists only because somebody made it (D1).** `vibespace-msg group create <name> <member…> [--context "…"] [--quiet]` (an agent), `POST /api/channel-groups` (the owner), or `vibespace-msg send <agent> "…"`, which finds-or-creates the TWO-MEMBER group of that pair (the same pair is always the same group, from either side). No group per Task Group (the owner's spam ruling). Members are keyed by conversation id (a resume keeps them); the owner is the implicit member of every group and is never stored. Reach to invite = msg-acl (`messageable`), judged from the inviter; a miss is the uniform "not found or not reachable" and refuses the whole call.
- **Who is woken is each member's own choice (D2).** `notify` per (group, member): **next-turn** (default) — new messages become ONE report in that member's next turn of ANY origin (the owner typing, a notification's or receipt's wake, a peer message, auto-resume's continue — lane stash-any-turn, 2026-10-05; a turn nobody typed says once to answer each group in its own group), as context, zero billed turns of its own · **mention** — ONLY what @mentions it (by id) reaches it: woken now, its report holds only those, the rest is never queued (B-a354, 2026-10-03 — before it, mention behaved exactly like next-turn) · **always** — every message wakes it · **mute** — nothing (`read` on purpose). An @mention wakes every mode but mute; an invite wakes the invitee unless `--quiet`; `send --wake` = an @ of every other member. A member sets its own (`group notify`); the owner sets anyone's. **A wake is a billed turn**: it goes down THE delivery ladder (`peer-message`), the spend authorizer decides, and a refusal is journaled (`audit.ndjson` kind `group-wake`) while the message stays in the log and rides the member's next report.
- **What a member is handed.** The report holds only messages after its JOIN (the invite context first), newest kept under 2 KiB per group / 4 KiB per turn, with `vibespace-msg read <group> --before <ts>` named when older ones were clipped — never the whole history. It rides `prompt-context` only on a turn a PERSON started (the session's `_userInputAt` vs `_machineInputAt`); a machine-started turn (a wake, a job notification, auto-resume) leaves it for the next user turn, so N agents cannot talk each other into an echo chamber on the owner's money.
- **Membership.** invite (members only, duplicate = a no-op with a word, N invitees = N wakes echoed as a count) · leave · kick (the creator or the owner) · rename · archive (keeps the log) · a direct group that loses a side is archived and the next `send` starts a new one; a direct group takes no third member (make a group).
- **Storage.** `data/channels/groups.json` through channel-store's serialized door; each group's log is an ordinary append-only conversation log `data/channels/msgs/groups/<groupId>.ndjson` (the ChannelRecord shape; system records for create / invite / leave / kick / rename / archive). Every change broadcasts `channel-groups-updated`.
- **The agent CLI (g2).** `vibespace-msg group list` (= `groups`) · `group create|invite|leave|kick|rename|archive|notify` · `read <group> [--before <ts>] [--limit n]` · `send <group|agent> "…" [--wake]`. Every answer ECHOES the wake count — `woke 2 agents = 2 billed turns` (0 said too, refused wakes "not billed"); members/groups named by id OR name, resolved server-side, an ambiguous name refused WITH the candidate ids; every refusal = its typed code + the remedy, exit 1 (2 outside a session, 3 server gone). A Background Work job (`VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN`) speaks as its owner conversation and may list / read / send (into an existing group or direct group) — never create or change membership (`job-token`). The manual (`vibespace-docs msg`) opens with a `## Groups` section in the owner's words; the Reporting-back teaching every Task-Group session gets carries ONE pointer line. Gate: `test-msg-cli-groups` (fast).
- **r1 (the verifier's round).** A wake is paced whatever caused it: an @mention, `--wake`, an invite or an `always` member — one wake per (sender, receiving conversation) per 30 s, keyed by the conversation, never by how the target was typed; a floored wake is said like an authorizer refusal (not billed, the message still lands and rides the next report). A group named like a session never shadows `send <that session>` — the bare name is refused `ambiguous` with both ids. kick / notify by a name two members share is refused `ambiguous`. A next-turn report is never cut after its marker moves: each report's whole text fits its budget (long group names are clipped, the foot shortened), the section fits whole or waits. A focus-in / cursor answer from a terminal is not a person typing. A CJK name followed by CJK text (`@测试请看`) is a mention. A session that has no conversation id yet cannot send (409, try after its first turn) instead of waking the receiver through the pre-groups lane.
- **What was handed over is SEEN in that chat (lane group-report-card, the owner 2026-09-28: "怎么在那个对话里看不到你发了消息？").** Before: a next-turn report rode the member's hook injection and nothing in its chat showed it — the owner looking at the receiver saw no trace of two replies to a peer's urgent question. Now: **before the turn**, the strip above the member's composer lists the waiting group messages ("1 notice is waiting for this agent's next turn: a group message from alpha"; the sidebar card "1 waiting") — with NO "Hand over now" button when group messages are all that waits (a hand-over carries the stash, never a group report; "they ride your next message" stands where the button would be), and beside a stash entry the button stays and the strip says "1 group message rides your next message". **At the turn**, every group MESSAGE the report carried is ONE card in that chat, drawn at the injection (under the owner's message, before the reply): "alpha → <group>" (the sender a link to its session, the group a link to its window), the words the agent was shown (the whole text when its line was whole; the cut words + "Cut short in the agent's report — the whole message: vibespace-msg read <group>" when it was cut), "… and N more (vibespace-msg read <group>)" on the oldest card of a report the budget cut (the same N the agent's pointer says); the owner's own message is "You → <group>"; a system record (an invite, a rename) draws no card. A **wake** (`--wake`, an @, `always`) draws the same card ("it woke this agent" on its head) — the ladder's own card after the post, the codex wrapper's marker on the rpc lane. A message is carded ONCE per conversation (a re-report after a lost marker, a wake over a range a report showed), and every card survives a restart (the report card from the session meta's ring, placed by time; the wake card = the transcript's own record, upgraded in place). A PEER's words — never the VibeSpace-notice head. Its fold kind is `group` in "Card kinds that collapse" (OFF by default — the owner asked to see them). Gates: `test-channel-groups` §7 + `test-stash-strip` ②k (fast), `test-group-report-card` (heavy).
- **Not in g1/g2/g3:** sub-threads, avatars/announcements, cross-instance groups (a remote agent is not a member yet). Gate: `test-channel-groups` (fast).

### Communication panel — THE IM MODEL, g3: the group list first, the owner's own words direct (2.369.159; design-communication-panel.zh.md §22, the owner's clarification "the first screen is the group list — a simple IM")

**The panel is an IM, not a feed of sources.** Every group has at least two members — an agent group is ≥ 2 agents plus the owner as the observer; a Lark chat / Gmail thread is the owner and the other side, with agents as the owner's delegates — and the first screen shows the conversation history of each.

- **The first screen is the GROUP LIST.** ONE list of every agent group and every TRACKED conversation of a connected account (Lark chats, Gmail threads), sorted by last activity; a row = the source glyph · the name · the time, then a source chip (`Agents`, `Direct` for a two-member group, or the account's label) · the last line · the unread count. Archived groups fold apart ("Archived groups (n)"). An UNTRACKED conversation is not in it (nothing has been fetched, so there is no history to show — Track it in its account). The list repaints in place from the two broadcasts; nothing is fetched per event.
- **The secondary sections.** **Accounts** (connect / re-authorize / add another account, each account's discovered conversations with Track, Assign & filter, Reach & policy — everything P0a–P4 shipped) and the **Message watcher** (the built-in agents-as-SOURCES section: follow a live session's messages, assign or filter them for another agent — the "subscribe" shape the owner called a by-the-way feature) sit BELOW the list. Each folds; the fold is the user's, stored in user state (`channelsPanelFolds`) and followed on every open client.
- **New group** (the bar's button): a name, members picked from the LIVE agent sessions grouped by Task Group (each session once; nothing is pre-selected and a Task Group is never added whole — D1), an optional opening context (the first thing each new member reads), and **Wake now** (on by default) with its cost said BEFORE the click: *will wake N agents (N billed turns)*. After the click the toast says what the server actually did (woke N = N billed turns; wakes the spend guard refused are not billed and ride the member's next report). The new group's window opens at once.
- **A group's window.** The log (system records — created / added / left / removed / renamed / archived — in the reader's language, an invite's context under its line), the members chip and ⋯ open the **group detail**: the owner first as **You (observer)** (sees everything, never woken), then each member with its **notify mode** as a dropdown the OWNER may change for anyone (next turn — a report, never woken · when @mentioned — wakes, billed · every message — wakes, billed · mute), Remove (a direct group that loses a side is archived), **Invite…** (the New group dialog minus the name; not on a direct group), Rename…, Archive (the log is kept). The window marks the group read when the owner opens or touches it.
- **The composer sends DIRECTLY, as You.** No proposal, no outbox: `@` opens an autocomplete over the member names, a line under the box says who THIS text would wake ("Will wake beta — 1 billed turn" — the same rule the server applies, parity-tested), and the send's answer is drawn at once with the wake count in the toast. An archived group has no composer.
- **External conversations: the owner's own message goes out directly too.** Where the conversation offers sending AS THE USER, the composer is **Send** — out at once as the owner, no policy and no guard (links / attachments / off-hours still govern AGENT drafts), with the same outbox record, audit and never-re-sent `unknown` underneath. Where only the app/bot identity is offered, the composer PROPOSES (a bot message is not the owner speaking) and says why sending as you is not offered; where nothing is offered there is no composer and the reason is said. The outbox and its approval cards are for replies an AGENT drafts.
- **Unread.** A group's unread count is the OWNER's (messages after the owner last opened it that the owner did not write); opening or touching its window reads it; the rail's Channels badge counts it beside the channels' unread + awaiting proposals.
- **XSS.** A group name, a member name, an invite context and every message are agent-controlled and sync to every client: all of them render as text (a hostile `<img onerror>` group name is asserted as text in the row, the bar and the window title).
- Gates: `test-channels-groups-ui` (fast) · `test-channels-groups-e2e` (heavy: two stub-CLI sessions, every wake through the real ladder into a recording stub — the `always` member woken, the `next-turn` member not) · `test-channels-e2e` ⑩b (the direct send: no approval card, no approve line) · `test-channels-i18n` (zh + ja).

### Communication panel — the OAuth client belongs to the ACCOUNT, account cards work like mount rows (2.369.165; docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md r4 SHIPPED whole — chunk 1: the shared dialog component, chunk 2: the server, chunk 3: the card and the dialogs, chunk 4: D2 on the storage side + the parity census)

- **The choice is stored on the account, like a storage mount.** A channel account (a record in `data/channels/adapters.json`) names its own OAuth client: an env preset by key (`credentialKey: 'cluster:<k>'`, unchanged) or its OWN client (`credentialKey: 'custom'` + `credential {appId, appSecretEnc}`, the secret sealed under `data/.channels-key` — the mounts' `clientId` + `clientSecretEnc` shape). Presets come from the ONE env reader both features share (Google: `VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS` through `drivePresets()`, the storage dialog's own; Lark: `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATIONS`) as `{key,label}` — no value ever on the wire. The account's consent, refresh and status all resolve THAT client; a preset the env stopped offering is named (`preset-gone`), never replaced by another.
- **Sign in before the account exists.** The account dialog's sign-in block runs the storage dialog's consent shape against `/api/channels/oauth/{start,status,callback}` (the loopback redirect or the paste-back); the account is created only by Connect (`connect {flowId}`), with the client that sign-in ran under and the token it minted — a dialog closed half-way leaves nothing behind.
- **Re-authorize = switching the client is allowed and IS a re-authorization** (the mount semantics): the account keeps its old client and token until the consent under the new one lands, then both are replaced together; a failed consent changes nothing. The old "bound to its credential" refusal is gone.
- **Duplicate** makes a sibling account with the same type, client (a custom secret re-sealed), filters (the declared options), push claim and sender line — never the token, the tracked conversations, assignments, reach grants or the message log; the copy is unauthorized and signs in on its own.
- **Remove is refused by name while the account is referenced** (assignments of its conversations, reach grants to the whole account, outbox proposals not yet settled — agent groups do not count): `409 account-referenced` with each reference. **Disconnect** only drops the token and keeps every account's record (the pre-r4 "a further account's disconnect removes it" is gone).
- **Edit's in-place saves:** rename; replace a custom client's secret (same id); another client ⇒ Re-authorize. The Edit dialog prefills the custom secret from an owner-only config route (the storage `GET /api/mounts/:id/config` rule, D3) — the only answer that carries it.
- **The Integrations window keeps only the six browser key rows.** Lark, Gmail and the test channel are not cards any more: `GET /api/integrations` leaves them out and every card verb on them answers `404 binds-per-account` naming where the client is chosen. Their values an older instance saved stay in `data/integrations.json` and are copied once onto the account that used them (`own` → `custom`, reader-side and by the migration `2026-09-channel-custom-client-inline`; this instance had none). No Test verb on an account's client (D7).
- **Chunk 3 — the card and the dialogs (the client, on the storage dialog component `src/lib/mounts-dialog.js`; the dialogs themselves in `src/lib/channel-account-dialogs.js`).** ONE entry at the bottom of the Accounts part, `Connect an account (Lark / 飞书, Gmail)` (the storage footer's "Connect storage"; the per-kind buttons and the ⋯ "Add account…" are retired). The dialog is TYPE-FIRST (`Type` → `Name` → `OAuth client` → `{provider} authorization` → the type's own first option: Gmail's include query, Lark's brand), every later field on a `when:`: `Preset: {label}` per preset + `Custom (own client id/secret)` (no Built-in; presets[0] preselected, Custom when there is none), the registry's `clientHint` as the hint line, Custom unfolding `Custom App ID` / `Custom App Secret` (Gmail: `Custom OAuth client ID` / `… secret`) inline with the registry's help, and for a type whose console needs a registered redirect (Lark) the callback URL as a read-only row + Copy with the console note and the three prerequisites as hint lines; the sign-in runs IN the dialog (the storage block: the cross-browser link row, the paste-back), and `Connect` creates the record. The sign-in page's brand comes from the registry row's `signinName` (Gmail signs in with **Google**).
- **The account card (credential-first, the storage row's grammar).** Head: chevron · type glyph · name (the label, with the login the token names) · the client chip (`Preset: …` / `Custom client`) · the state dot (connected ok · sign-in dead bad · no usable client warn · never signed in / disabled / connected but tracking nothing idle · a consent running attn) · tracked/total · ✎ · ⋯. Under it the HEALTH line in the storage detail-line grammar (`[Gmail] Connected · label:INBOX · last poll 2 min ago · push: exclusive`), or — when the sign-in died or the client is gone — the storage `.mounts-errline` "Couldn’t connect: connected but the sign-in has expired or been revoked — conversations come from cache while every fetch fails; re-authorize to fix (<why code>)" (the mounts' sentence verbatim, D8) with the primary `Re-authorize {product}…` button. Its children are the TRACKED conversations as ↳ rows (the storage child-row arrow); an account tracking nothing says "Login only — no conversation tracked yet; nothing is fetched until you track one. Use Track… to pick conversations under this account." with Track… (today's checklist picker). The ⋯ is the storage row's order (D6): Open conversation window · Track… · Options · Push… ‖ Re-authorize / Connect · Duplicate… · Disconnect · Remove… ‖ Disable; a SOURCE (the built-in message watcher, a scan-only fixture) keeps its old section and its sender-line rows.
- **Edit** (✎): name, the OAuth client (a custom id AND secret prefilled with their real values, D3 — from the owner-only config route), the sign-in facts, the type's options, the push claim, the sender line; buttons Re-authorize {product}… · Duplicate… · Remove… · Save; only what changed is sent; switching the client makes Save open **Re-authorize** with the new client (the account is not re-pointed until that sign-in lands). **Re-authorize** is the storage re-authorize dialog verbatim (who reported the death, Sign in with {provider}, the status line, the link row, the paste-back) with the OAuth client select on top; the fixed-port Lark flow runs in the same dialog (a busy port is said in its status line). **Duplicate**: `{name} (copy)`, the type read-only, client / filter / push claim copied (changeable), the copied / not-copied paragraph, its OWN consent block, `Create & connect` (the copy exists unauthorized from its first sign-in attempt; a dialog closed before that sign-in lands removes it again). **Remove…** (⋯ or Edit) confirms, and a referenced account opens `Cannot remove "{name}"` naming each assignment (conversation → principal), reach grant and pending-proposal count, with the Disconnect sentence and an Open Outbox button. The section repaints in place on every broadcast; the phone draws the same `.mounts-*` classes the storage rows use. The channels' own flow dialog, the wizard's stepper and its credential step are gone.
- **Chunk 4 — the two features agree, and a census keeps them agreeing.** The storage side adopted the account rule (D2, its own commit — see Mounts / Storage above): switching a Drive / Gmail connection's OAuth client opens Re-authorize under the new client, the token lands with it. `scripts/test-oauth-field-parity.mjs` (fast) pins what the two share: ONE component (the module's exports, no second renderer on either side), every shared spelling asserted on BOTH sides (the renderer's own classes through the channel side's import), every re-authorize on both sides = the one `reauthDialog`, switching the client = re-authorize on both sides with the token landing WITH the client, each side's Edit button order (the channel's read off the r4 mockup: Re-authorize · Duplicate… · Remove… · Save; storage: Remove… · Re-authorize · Save), Remove… in Edit on both sides (never a storage row icon), D8's borrowed auth-death sentence, and the design's §4 i18n key list parsed OUT OF THE DESIGN DOC — every key drawn where it belongs as built and carried by zh + ja, a key built under another spelling (`Duplicate…`, the health line in parts, `Include query`) or not drawn (Lark's include-groups option — Lark declares none) says why; the deleted `Add account…` is drawn by no channel file. Each rule has a patched in-memory control.
- **From storage — a storage mount's own client, borrowed (2.369.195, design §2.7).** The owner could not reuse the custom Google client typed once for a Gmail / Drive storage mount (the UI never shows its secret). Connect an account and Re-authorize now list each top-level storage mount holding its own client of the vendor the type signs in with (Gmail ⇒ Google: Drive / Gmail mounts; Lark ⇒ none) as `From storage: {name} (custom client {prefix}…[, {email}])`; chosen, a note says the server copies the id and secret onto the account, the secret never passes through the page, and the consent runs under that client. Server-side the secret is decrypted with `.mounts-key` and re-sealed under `.channels-key` — the account is an ordinary `custom` one (Edit shows it like any custom client, Re-authorize adds scopes). Refusals are named (mount gone / no own client / another vendor's / undecryptable); an agent bearer is 403; one audit line per copy. Route + field: kb-api (`GET /api/channels/oauth/mount-clients`, `fromMount`). Gates: test-channels-engine ⑮, test-oauth-field-parity §9, test-integrations-ui ⑩ (r).

### Communication panel — THE AGGREGATED IM: a linked account is read whole (2026-09-26; design-communication-panel §5 invariant 6, §6.2, §6.5, §7.3 — owner ruling, replacing "tracked is opt-in")

**SUPERSEDES every "Track… / tracked / untracked / Login only" sentence in the sections above** — those describe the model before this date.

- **Every conversation, no Track step.** A linked account lists and fetches every conversation in its scope: every Lark group the account sees, Gmail's Inbox by default (Edit → Mailbox: Inbox / All mail / These labels / A search query; the Labels and query fields appear only for their choice, a hidden field is saved as its default). Discovery walks the vendor's cursor to the end (the old 5-page cap hid conversation 501). Unread counts only what arrived after `linkedAt` (a freshly linked mailbox's backlog is read). Rows: every one carries its freshness pill (short form "19s ago" / "within 30s" / "refresh paused"; the full sentence in its tooltip); bold when unread; first screen 60 rows, an account 30, "Show all N" to expand.
- **The account card's health line** = Connected · the scope in the adapter's own words (the options AS APPLIED — a Gmail record with a custom query reads "A search query", never "Inbox") · push / push + polling / polling · N conversations · M unread · last sync (the last GOOD pass; lane R2 verify: a failed pass is said on its own line from the FIRST failure — "rate limited — retrying in 30 s" — via channel-caps `passStateText`). A Lark sign-in renews itself while the instance runs: no seven-day countdown; "renewals stopped — re-authorize in …" only under a day. While a vendor budget is spent: "Vendor budget reached — {n} {unit}/min for this account; {k} conversations waiting, next refresh in {s} s" (a paced account adds "(at most {r}/s)"). Lane R5 (2026-09-26, the owner: "gmail一直被限速 你可能要控制下gmail默认的读取速度"): reads are PACED PER SECOND (Gmail 40 quota units/s = one thread a second, Lark 5 requests/s — `channels.gmailUnitsPerSec` / `channels.larkRequestsPerSec`, never faster than the minute's budget); a vendor RATE refusal is a short wait said by the vendor's name from the first strike — "Google is limiting the rate · resuming in 12 s" (zh "Google 限速中 · 12 秒后继续"), the vendor's Retry-After else 5 s doubling to 60 s, never a failure count and never "paused"; while conversations are read for the first time the line says "reading for the first time · 120/873 conversations · about 13 min left" (zh "首次读取中 · 已 120/873 个会话 · 约剩 13 分钟"), repainted at most every 5 s (an account card and a source section alike). Lark push without the official SDK says the full remedy (`npm install @larksuiteoapi/node-sdk`, the event subscription, `im:message.group_msg`, the bot in the chats; polled every 30 s – 15 min until then).
- **Refresh.** Per conversation: override (row / window menu Refresh every ▸ Automatic / 30 s / 1 min / 5 min / 15 min / Paused, the check an SVG) > push safety net (a live content-carrying lane ⇒ cold) > tier (hot = open in a window — a 60 s `/watch` heartbeat, 90 s expiry — or a message within `channels.hotRecentMinutes`; warm = within `channels.warmRecentHours`; cold), clamped to [the adapter's floor, 900 s]. Refresh now answers "N new message(s)" / "Up to date". The per-account per-minute budget is in the vendor's unit (Lark 60 requests, Gmail 3000 quota units — settings), most-overdue first, the rest next minute. Arithmetic in the design §6.2 (Lark 55 groups typical ≈ 15.6 requests/min; Gmail polls `history.list` at 2 units, a named thread is due at once).
- **The window.** Images as thumbnails through `GET …/attachment/:id?msg=&inline=1` (set as `img.src`, a click opens the image overlay, a failure falls back to the chip); every other attachment a chip with name · size · download. Everything served `nosniff` + `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `attachment` unless png/jpeg/gif/webp inline; the cache 0600, LRU per account (`channels.attachmentBudgetMB`). Scrolling to the top loads older history (Lark; prepended, never a wake; "Beginning of the conversation" / "Beginning of what this channel keeps" at the start). ⋯ → Search messages… (≤ 64 MB read, ≤ 100 results, newest first).
- **Agents.** `vibespace-channels refresh <conv>` / `read --fresh`: reach first, then `channels.agentRefreshFloorSec` (20 s from the last fetch by anyone), then the budget, then the AGENT SHARE of the minute `channels.agentBudgetSharePct` (25 %, lane R2 verify — the owner's hot rows keep their cadence); refusals carry the number and `Retry-After`. An `ok` is always this refresh's own fetch (concurrent refreshes each run their own pass). `read` lists attachments (metadata only) and `assignedVia`. A file on a message `read --around` showed (older than the saved copy) is fetched from the vendor by its ids — the same budget, share and cache, the message still unsaved, the save says so (2.369.325, B-5f20); ids no read showed in that conversation are refused with ZERO calls (Lark's resource address names no chat).
- **R4 (2026-09-27) — access and notification are TWO operations, access first.** At each grain (the whole account, the conversations a rule matches, one conversation) **Grant access…** lists who may see and act (agents / Task Groups, each `drafts` or `may send`; access alone never wakes anyone, nothing is billed) and **Notify…** lists who is woken (wake per batch / one digest per window, every message or a filter, its own daily cap, the receipt opt-in) — its picker offers only the principals with access there (none ⇒ "Grant access first"); removing access removes the notification. Many principals per grain; per principal the finest grain naming it decides; each notification has its own cap (per (principal, scope)); a number past its bound is clamped visibly. The card line: "访问：A（可发送）, 组 · 工作（起草） · 通知：A 每批唤醒 按过滤器". Agents: `vibespace-channels status` names the access and whether they are notified, `search` looks through what they can see, `compose` proposes a NEW message on an account they have whole (Gmail; review by default). Pre-R4 assignments migrated to one access + one notification row. (The paragraph below is the pre-R4 shape.)
- **Three grains, one editor.** Hand to an agent… (the account), Conversations matching a rule… (participant / title / from-address / kind, any|every; many per account, creation order), Assign & filter… (one conversation). Effective = conversation > first matching rule > account; a new conversation inherits in the pass that discovers it. Reach follows: an account assignment writes one adapter-scope grant (`origin:'assignment'`), a rule's grants are derived at read time (nothing to clean up), both go with the assignment. The pace ledger (daily wake cap) is the assignment's; a digest is ONE block per window for the whole scope. The editor estimates "about N wakes a day" from the matching conversations' last 7 days before you save. Inherited rows: dim "(account)" / "(rule)"; grain lines under the account head.
- **Wire.** Slim digest rows + partial `channels-updated` (`partial`, `changedKeys`) merged in place; the full view on open (`GET /api/channels/:a/:c`). Migration `2026-09-channels-aggregated-im`: tracked ⇒ `refresh.every 30` (by `migration`), never-ingested ⇒ read, `tracked` deleted, `linkedAt` stamped.
- **Gates**: test-channels-aggregate (fast), test-channels-aggregate-ui (heavy, zh), test-channel-caps / -filter / -acl / -store, test-channels-engine, test-channels-gmail-shape / -lark-shape, test-migrations; heavy test-channels-e2e / -groups-e2e / -i18n / test-integrations-ui.

### Communication panel — R3: a picture is a picture; the first screen lists what matters (2026-09-26; design-communication-panel §23 — the owner: "lark图像不能预览吗？" / "开头不要把所有消息都放进来 … 只放重要消息/conversation … 并展示一个小tag表示状态")

- **Pictures.**
  - A Lark picture (on its own or inside a rich text) is a thumbnail through our route, and its "[image]" line leaves once drawn.
  - If it cannot be drawn: when a wait fixes it (budget / back-off / rate limit) it says "retrying in N s" and reloads itself (≤ 2). Otherwise the chip NAMES the reason (budget spent / forbidden / not found / not cached / vendor error, the sentence in its tooltip) with **Retry**. A non-raster file is the download chip "no preview".
  - The fetch: cache first, single-flight, a vendor refusal remembered (no re-ask for 10 min unless Retry), a rate limit waited out account-wide, charged to the budget.
- **VibeSpace's own talk looks internal (2.369.247, the owner 2026-10-09: "这个 VibeSpace 内部的聊天群视觉上很难和其他的外部的区分开").** On the first screen the VibeSpace block — its head and every agent group and agent chat in it — sits on one muted band with a thin left rule; each of its rows wears the VibeSpace mark as its avatar on a grey disc (no colour, no corner badge) and an outlined kind chip (Agents / 私聊). People and vendor accounts keep their coloured discs, pictures and vendor marks, so colour on the first screen means a person or a vendor. Folded, the head alone keeps the band.
- **The first screen is the attention list.**
  - **It splits in two (lane attention-predicate-shared, 2.369.319 — design q-044 decision 7).** 「需要我」 (Needs me) first: the rows a person or an agent waits on, in For you's bands (有人在等 · 有期限或钱 · 要你决定 · 其余的问 · 搁置) — the band's name and count, at most `attention.cap` (6) rows on screen, the rest behind each band's 「还有 N 条 — 展开」 (opens in place). Then 「相关」 (Related), FOLDED by default (user state `channelsPanelFolds.related`, synced): handed over, read by an agent, new since a read, a held wake, replied, and the agent groups (VibeSpace's internal block inside it). The rules below still decide WHETHER a row is listed; its facts decide WHERE (an assigned direct chat a person wrote in sits in 有人在等). A query searches everything, flat, as before.
  - **The Channels badge counts what needs you** — the conversations in bands 1–4 (the server's kept `needsMe` on every broadcast and `?scope=totals`) + an agent group that @-mentions you; never unread + awaiting (measured on this instance: 8 033 → 3).
  - **What lands on it is the owner's POLICY (lane attention-policy, 2026-10-13).** Each fixed rule below is a switch with its meaning in plain words — 有人直接发给我、我还没读的 (direct) · 有人 @ 了我、我还没读的 (at-you — lane attention-rule-at-you, 2026-10-13: a conversation whose unread records of the last 24 h @ the account's resolved self, chip 「@我 · N 条」, ranked after awaiting / unknown and before assigned, the row's preview quotes the mentioning message; a broadcast / a user group / the owner's own message never counts; read-up-to clears it) · 等我批准才发出去的消息 (awaiting) · 指派给某个 agent / 群组、并且它处理过的 (assigned) · agent 读过的（或读过之后又来了新消息）(read / new-since-read) · 为我扣住的唤醒 (held) · 投递状态未知的 (unknown) · 我 24 小时内回过的 (replied) — settings `channels.attention.rule.<code>`, default on. Beside them: the judge's switch (the LLM plugin's own `attention` feature, mirrored — one store), its threshold (a slider 0.50–0.90) and 「我在乎什么」, a preset radio (固定规则 + 判断模型 / 只用判断模型 / 只用固定规则 — it SETS the switches) and the readout 今天判断了 N 条 · 命中 M 条. A rule switched off never lists its row (the row answers with its next rule that is on, else stays under 全部 with its facts); with the rules off the judge may see those rows. ONE block 「需关注 · 怎么判断」: the Settings window (Channels; searching 需关注 / attention finds it) and the ⚙ door on the first screen (a popover on a desk, a sheet on a phone) draw the same rows. The door is the ⚙ System button's own cog ALONE in a 24 px square at every panel width — its words 「怎么判断需关注」 ride the tooltip + aria-label (lane chan-attn-door-icon, 2.369.267: a fleet report — in a Channels window the old 「⚙ How it is decided」 label made a wide button).
  - The agent groups, plus every conversation that: awaits your approval / has a lost send; is handed to an agent or Task Group on its own (by a rule or with its whole account: only once a wake for it was DELIVERED in the last 24 h or is held — D4, 2026-09-27; an 824-thread mailbox handed over must not refill the first screen); was read by an agent in the last 24 h; has a held wake; or that you replied in within 24 h.
  - Each row wears ONE tag on line 2, under the title (N to approve · send unknown · → Agent · Agent read 5m ago · New since Agent · last wake held · replied 3h ago). The agent's name yields when space is tight; the words never do.
  - The header "N need attention | All N" switches views; a Filter box sits under it ("N more in All", "Search messages for …" across every account).
- An agent's read is recorded when it happens, through the agent read route (`vibespace-channels read`). A wake names the agent it reached. The server derives your own replies.

Gates: test-channels-images, test-channels-focus, test-channels-lark-shape ⑨, test-vendor-whitelist §7 (fast); test-channels-aggregate-ui ②b, test-channels-groups-e2e ⑨, test-channels-e2e ⑰, test-channels-i18n (heavy).

### Communication panel — NEW-MESSAGE SEARCH AND SINGLE CHATS (lane lark-search-poll, 2026-09-28; design-communication-panel.zh.md §29 — the owner: "从 lark pull 消息可以通过搜索空格+时间范围来搜索最近所有新消息吧，这样也顺便能解决私聊问题")

- **One search finds every new message.** A Lark account whose sign-in holds `search:message` asks Lark's message search (an empty query + a time window) every `channels.feedEverySec` (30 s) which conversations have new messages — groups, SINGLE chats (which Lark's chat list never names) and thread replies — ONE request per page, 30 hits a page, at most 10 pages a minute (10 % of the vendor's tenant-wide 100/min). A hit is only a MARK: the words come from the chat's own history read; the search's snippet is never stored, logged or shown.
- **Single chats appear.** The first search after the account is connected / re-authorized also lists the single chats of the last `channels.feedBackfillDays` (7) days — as READ, waking nobody (the card: "Found N single chats from the last 7 days"). A new single-chat message afterwards is unread and news. A single chat is titled by the other person's name ("Ann"), else "Single chat" — never its raw id (a push-born row too).
- **The first screen.** A single chat with unread messages (newest within 24 h) wears "DM · N new" (单聊 · N 条新消息) — owner decision 1.
- **Agents.** A whole-account grant INCLUDES single chats — the agent reads them and is woken on them (owner decision 2); a per-chat grant works as on any conversation.
- **Polling relaxes only when the search is PROVEN complete.** While measuring, every conversation is still polled at its own cadence; once ≥ 200 fetched messages were all found by the search (≤ 2 % missed) — measured over at least one full cold cycle (≈ 17 min), so a chat the search never sees has been read on its own and counted — the account CARRIES: an open window stays at 30 s, every other conversation is checked at least every `channels.relaxedPollSec` (300 s — owner decision 4; a cold one stays at 15 min), and the row's chip says "within 90 s" (the search's tick + its overlap). A search that starts missing messages is DEMOTED by itself and the normal cadence returns. Each flip is said on the card with its numbers.
- **The card.** One line says the feed's state ("New messages: a search every 30 s · each chat is still checked on its own until 200 messages show it finds everything (57/200)" / "New messages come from a search every 30 s; each chat is also checked every 5 min" / "Search missed 5 of 60 messages (8.3%) — each chat is checked on its own again" / "Lark is limiting the search · resuming in 12 s" / "Search is off: Lark refused search:message — enable it in the app console, publish a version, then Re-authorize" / "Search is off: Lark ignored its time window — …"), and ONE grants line with ONE Re-authorize for everything the sign-in lacks: "One Re-authorize adds: reading reactions · new-message search and single chats".
- **Consent.** The default consent asks for `search:message` and `im:message.p2p_msg:get_as_user` (the account option "New-message search", on by default; off removes both). If Lark refuses the sign-in because its app has not enabled a scope (20027, on Lark's page), each retry drops ONE optional scope, least valuable first — reactions, then the single-chat read, then the search — each a button naming what it drops ("Sign in without … too").
- **Money.** Every search page is a drain action (rule 21: the minute's budget, the per-second pace, its own minute, ≤ 5 pages a pass, never ahead of a waiting person); a 429 / a refusal of the SEARCH — or the search not answering at all (a 5xx, a timeout: verify r1) — never backs the account off (the per-conversation polling carries on); a sign-in without `search:message` sends ZERO searches. Settings: `channels.feedEverySec`, `feedOverlapSec`, `feedBackfillDays`, `relaxedPollSec`.
- **The search's misses are NAMED, and the row says its state once (lane lark-search-miss, owner 2026-10-11).** Every message the per-chat poll finds that the search's window should have returned is a memo row with ONE class — a type the search does not return (Lark: `system` — 51 of the owner's 59 misses), a chat type it excludes, a bot message, a thread reply (the topic check is their source), a gap, the index lag, unknown; only the lag and the unknown count. The window overlaps by the LEARNED index lag (p95 of the lag misses' age, 30 s – 10 min). The search carries again only after 3 clean polling cycles and never within 6 h of a demotion. The account card says ONE quiet line ("新消息：搜索每 30 秒 + 每会话核对（核实中）" / "（搜索漏 2.5%，索引延迟）" / "（已核实无漏）"); the numbers, the last 20 misses with their class and the topic checks are its tooltip.

### Communication panel — the Channels list opens FOLDED (lane channels-fold-default, 2.369.251 — the owner, 2026-10-11: "能不能让 channels 默认收缩，不然翻找起来很困难")
Every account section (Lark / Gmail / Slack / the webhook door) starts folded unless a row in it needs the person (handed to someone, awaiting them, a held wake, an unread direct message, an @ of them) or the account must sign in again. A folded head says what is inside: the count, "N need attention" in the accent, the unread, and a dot. One press opens or folds; the choice is kept in user state (`channelsPanelFolds['acct:<id>']`, synced like the other folds) and wins over the default both ways. A row that comes to need the person later never opens a folded section; the head's count and dot rise instead. While the filter has text, a section holding a match opens with its matches and folds back when the filter is cleared. Accounts itself folds when every section in it is folded. The first screen stays the attention list; the internal block keeps its own fold. Suites: test-channels-groups-ui (PURE + controls), test-channels-fold-default (chrome).

### Communication panel — a dead sign-in is said where the person looks (lane channel-reauth-visible, .348 — the owner, 2026-10-23: 「对于需要 reauth 的 channel 应该需要更明显的提示」)
When a connected account's sign-in stops working (the vendor refuses its refresh token, Lark answers 20064 because the same user signed in to the same app elsewhere, its OAuth client is refused or missing), the account is in the **auth-expired state** from its FIRST refused pass until a pass goes through again: the Channels rail badge turns red `⚠N` and its tip names the accounts; ONE urgent For-you item per account sits at the top («<login> (<label>): sign-in expired — re-authorize (<why>)») with a Reconnect button; under the account in Channels a red line says «Sign-in expired — re-authorize · <why> · since <time>» with Reconnect (the same Re-authorize dialog — options, access and history kept) — «Re-authorizing…» + Cancel while the consent runs, still shown when the section is folded, the section's left edge red; `vibespace-channels list / read / search` and the hook's channels line name the account to an agent. A restart, a vault lock, another failure or a started consent never clears it; a consent that ends unfinished re-asserts the same item; the first good pass (or removing / disconnecting the account) ends it. The account view's fields: `authState` ('expired' | 'pending' | 'ok'), `authCause`, `authSince`; the record's `signinDead`.

### Communication panel — the account row's notice grammar (lane channel-row-notices, .349 — the owner, 2026-10-23: 「这个提示最好不要常驻了，很丑陋；然后为啥我这里提示需要重新授权，重新授权干啥？」)
Under an account in Channels: **a standing state is ONE short line that can be put away** — a parked push lane says «实时推送未开启 — 消息靠轮询（30 秒–15 分钟）» (plain, no command) with ⓘ and 「知道了」; 「知道了」 is kept per instance (user state `channelsNoticesSeen` {account: the state's sig}) and the line comes back only when the state CHANGES (another code, a new demotion). ⓘ (also on the health line) opens the account's fold: the lane's cause in a few words (its `UNAVAILABLE_CAUSES`), «不会漏消息», where the steps are, a demotion's numbers, and optional consents. The install command and console steps live on the account type's setup card (⚙ → Integrations, «实时推送（可选）», the live lane's `PUSH_SETUP`) and in ⚙ Diagnostics («频道 — 实时推送») — never on the row. **A re-authorization line names its gain and what works meanwhile** (PURE `reauthWhyText(kind, reason, facts)`): read-only «可读，回复需要再授权一次（缺 <scope> 权限）»; Lark's paged consent «继续授权以获取应用下一组权限（next 个），总计剩余 n 个权限 — 下一组：<families>；现在的收发消息不受影响» (from the consent's `nextPageCount` / `morePending` / `morePendingScopes` by `scopeFamily`; shown when an agent holds the account's raw API and the families are known, else under ⓘ; «继续授权一次补齐剩余 n 项权限（共 K 页，逐页同意）» once lark-consent-chain sets `chain`); a countdown «登录将在 {eta} 后到期 — 到期前再授权一次即可» (warn only once overdue); never a bare «需要重新授权». The dead sign-in's red line (channel-reauth-visible) is unchanged.

### Communication panel — people's real avatars (lane channel-avatars, B-5fe1, 2026-10-04)

Lark and Slack authors show their profile picture (panel direct chats, the window's messages, the thread pane) through OUR route `GET /api/channels/avatar` — memoised per account on disk (30 days), fetched in the attachments' one order (memo · remembered refusal · ours only · budget · paced), ≤ 256 KiB, sniffed. Initials meanwhile and for a person with no picture; Gmail and the built-in Agents keep initials (`avatars: null` + why). src/channel-avatars.js.

### Communication panel — rich messages: formatted mail, Lark markup read, bot names (lane channel-rich, 2026-09-28)

The owner's report on the polished Channels window: "lark 有些消息里混入了 <p> 这种 raw tag；gmail 这种富文本 html 内容似乎完全没有按照 html 渲染；lark 里还有标记为 app 的情况，其实是个 bot 应该是有名字的。" Decisions D1–D3 (docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md §27).
- **D2 — a Gmail message with an HTML part is shown FORMATTED by default** in a fully sandboxed frame (`sandbox="allow-scripts"` only, NEVER `allow-same-origin`; its document = our allowlist re-serializer → DOMPurify → our CSP `<meta>` first + our nonce'd resizer, handed in through the hub's frame host since .331 — `GET /frame-host?kind=mail&n=<nonce>` sends the same policy + the host's script hash as a real header, where a srcdoc ran under the app page's). Each such message has a `Formatted | Plain text` switch (per message, kept across a redraw of the window); remote pictures are BLOCKED until `Show pictures` on that message (remembered for the sender for the page session, never globally; the CSP gains `https:` for that frame only; an http picture never loads); `cid:` pictures are fetched by the page through our attachment route and handed in as data:. The parent trusts only a clamped height from THAT frame's window with THAT frame's token; a clicked link opens in a new tab only when http(s)/mailto. Frames are lazy: live only within the viewport ± 1200 px, at most 6. A body the route refuses or one over 2 MiB shows the plain text with one sentence naming why (+ Retry). Gmail keeps the text/html part as the record's `role: 'body'` attachment, written into the attachment cache at ingest (zero extra vendor units). Agents, previews, search and the attention list keep using `text` — agents never receive HTML. Not done: the eml file viewer keeps its own path (unchanged: `sandbox=""` + raw srcdoc).
- **D1 — Lark markup is READ, never printed**: `<p>` / `<br>` / `<b>` / `<i>` / `<a>` / `<at>` / Lark markdown / card elements become paragraphs, line breaks, bold / italic runs, links, chips, rules; a tag outside the reader's CLOSED vocabulary is content, kept as written (a person's speech-control `<emphasis>Hello</emphasis>` / `<break time="500ms"/>` — lane lark-unknown-tags, 2.369.247); script-like elements are dropped with their contents; only a `<…>` named as one of OUR frames becomes `‹…›`. Applies to new records (`rec.text` + blocks) and, at read time, to stored ones (the window, an agent's `read`, search). Code (inline / blocks) is shown as written. Interactive cards render their title, text, rules, notes and button LABELS (never a clickable vendor url).
- **D3 — a Lark bot has a name**: the application API with a tenant token (scope `admin:app.info:readonly` on the app; without it "Bot" + the id's last four — never "app"), cached per app id 6 h with its refusal (said once in the log), a name from a mention taken for free; the row shows a small bot mark (SVG) beside the name; stored "app" rows are named at read time.
- Naive-user verify (2026-09-28): a mail wider than its frame (a 600 px newsletter on the phone) is ZOOMED to fit — never cut; a reply's quoted history (Gmail's `gmail_quote`, Apple Mail / Thunderbird's `blockquote type=cite`, Yahoo's `yahoo_quoted`) is folded behind "Show quoted text" inside the frame, as the plain-text view already folds `>` quotes — a thread reads as its new words; the Formatted | Plain text bar stays above the text in both modes.
- Gates: test-mail-frame (fast), test-channel-record ⑦ ⑧, test-channels-lark-shape ⑤b, test-channels-gmail-shape (D2 leg), test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑩ (heavy).

### Communication panel — THREADS AND REACTIONS (lane channel-threads, 2026-09-28; design-communication-panel.zh.md §28 — the owner: "我发现你似乎不支持 lark 的内嵌回复 (thread) 功能 … 以及 reaction (附加在消息上的表情)")

- **A reply shows what it answers.** One line above its text — `↩ Ada: when is the weekly now?` — a click jumps to that message (it flashes; one not drawn yet is paged up to, at most five pages; one older than everything loaded, or never stored, is said in words). A message inside a TOPIC carries a dim "in thread" (话题中) tag in the main list. **Quote vs topic (owner ruling 2026-09-28):** a Lark reply made without "reply in thread" is a QUOTE — the strip only, no tag, no pane, and the message it quotes grows no chip; the agent reads it as `↳ quotes Ada: "…" (id …)`; zh says 话题, never 线程 (one classifier, `placeKindOf`).
- **A thread opens beside the list** (a side pane on a window ≥ 620 px wide, a pushed view with a Back button on a phone) — never expanded inline, never saved in the layout. The root's chip says "N replies · last 5m"; a Lark topic whose replies were never loaded says "in thread · open to load" (Lark does not list a topic's replies with the group — opening the pane loads them, at most once a minute per thread). The pane has its own composer ("Reply in thread…", "Lands inside this thread"), keeps a draft and a scroll position per thread, and can answer a single reply inside the thread.
- **Reactions** sit under each message as chips (the emoji, the count; yours highlighted; hover / long press = who). A click adds or removes yours (the chip changes when the channel answers — never a guess); Add reaction in the message's hover bar (below) opens a picker (a quick row, search, the channel's own emoji — a custom one is drawn as a picture through VibeSpace, never the vendor's URL; arrows + Enter). Another client's reaction appears on the chip in place. Reaction lists are read only for the messages on screen, at most 20 list calls a minute per account (Settings → Channels: reactions per minute / minutes a list stays fresh / seconds between two loads of a thread), before the per-minute budget, so reading reactions never slows new messages.
- **ONE hover action bar per message (lane reaction-hover, 2026-10-01 — the owner: the `+` under every message "太丑了"; Lark's own shape).** Pointing at a message shows a small bar at its RIGHT edge, its middle on the message's first line: **Add reaction** (the picker, anchored to the button) · **Reply in thread** (opens the thread pane: a message inside a topic is answered there AS ITSELF; any other message starts a NEW thread rooted at it — "No replies yet.", the first reply mints it and the message grows its chip) · **Quote** (the composer shows `Quoted reply — to Ada: "…"` above the box with ✕; the send carries `replyTo` + `placement: quote`) — each only where the conversation offers it (Quote never on a topic's message, never in the pane, never without a composer). An agent group's message carries its ⋯ (Clear content…) in the same bar. The bar is an overlay: the message's height and the next message's place are identical shown or hidden — no line is reserved; a message with no reaction has no strip. Keyboard: the bar is ONE tab stop per message (← → move, Enter acts, Esc closes the picker and gives the keyboard back); it shows while the keyboard is in it (focus-visible — a mouse click leaves no stuck bar). A touch device (hover none + coarse pointer) never draws it: a LONG PRESS on the message opens the same actions as a menu (a link, a picture or a text selection keeps the browser's own; a chip's long press is still its who-list). Gates: test-channel-reactions ⑧ (fast), test-channel-threads-ui (d)(r)(t)(g)(p) (heavy: real hover + press, the five-state geometry at 1280 and 390 px, the pixel compares, the keyboard, thread + quote end to end), test-record-clear-ui ⑥.
- **Lark:** adding and removing works with the existing sign-in; READING who reacted needs the `im:message.reactions:read` permission. OWNER RULING (2026-09-28): the account option "Also read who reacted" is ON by default, so the default consent asks for it beside the five base scopes — an app with every permission enabled needs ONE Re-authorize. An account whose held sign-in lacks it says "Reactions can be read after one Re-authorize (im:message.reactions:read)" on its card (with the Re-authorize verb), on the window's line and on the `+` chip's title (one sentence, `channel-caps.reactReadText`). Lark refuses a WHOLE consent naming a permission the app has not enabled (error 20027, on its own page, never redirected): the sign-in dialog offers ONE "Sign in without im:message.reactions:read" (the same flow, `POST …/narrow`), and the account then says "Lark refused im:message.reactions:read — enable it in the app console and Re-authorize" — never a silent narrower consent. A Deny on Lark's page ends the sign-in by name on the account. Turning the option off silences the line.
- **Agents** read the same structure as words (`↳ replying to A: "…" (id …) · in thread …`, `[thread … · 3 replies · last 5 min ago]`, `reactions: 👍 3 (the account owner)` — never who); `read --thread` shows a thread from what is stored (never loads it), `refresh --thread` loads it; `reply --in-thread` replies inside a thread; `react` / `unreact` PROPOSE a reaction like a reply — the account's "Agent reactions" row (Edit dialog) decides: "You approve each one" (default), "As the channel policy allows" (direct only where the channel sends replies directly and the agent may send), "Off". The approval card reads "Worker wants to react 👍 to Ada: "…"" with Approve / Reject (no edit, never "wake now"); the receipt is one line in the agent's next turn. A reply to an agent's message wakes it only if its Notify… uses the rule "replies to or quotes a message of mine" or "is in a thread I am in, or quotes a message of mine" — OWNER DECISION A (2026-09-28): "in a thread" is a REAL TOPIC only (a Lark topic, a Slack thread) — a quote chain never wakes anyone as a thread; a QUOTE of the owner's (or that agent's) message still wakes, said as "quoted your message" (引用了你的消息); the daily wake cap is unchanged; reactions never wake anyone — reactions on an agent's message reach it as one line in its next turn (at most one per message per hour).
- **Where a reply lands — the PLACEMENT (2026-09-28, the owner: "the boolean is Lark-shaped").** A reply is `chat` (a plain message), `quote` (answers a message, shown in the main list), `thread` (inside its thread) or `thread+chat` (inside the thread AND shown in the conversation — Slack's reply_broadcast). Each channel DECLARES which in its `threads` cap row (`placements` + `rootReply`, its norm for a message outside a thread): Lark chat / quote / thread (norm: quote), Gmail chat / quote, the built-in Agents chat only, the fake all four; Slack (chat / thread / thread+chat, norm thread) and Telegram (chat / quote, norm quote) are fixture rows. An agent's `reply --to <id>` alone follows the norm — a message already inside a vendor thread is answered in the thread, else `rootReply`; `--in-thread` / `--also-in-chat` ask; an undeclared placement (or a quote of a threaded message) is `placement-not-offered`, worded with what IS offered, and creates nothing. The approval card (inline and in the Outbox) says "Quoted reply — to Ada: …" / "Reply in thread — under Ada: …" / "Reply in thread, also shown in the chat — …" (nothing for a plain message); the agent's tool-card row says "drafted a quoted reply / a reply in a thread …"; the receipt says "placed …". A proposal stored before the enum keeps `inThread` as its read alias (= thread) and is sent that way; the registry hands an adapter only a declared placement.
- **An agent's channel search opens as search RESULTS (2.369.212, lane channel-search-view; the owner 2026-10-04: "目前点开似乎是第一条匹配结果的对话框而不是搜索结果展示").** A `vibespace-channels search` card row ("… › NOC  7 search hits") opens the channel search dialog pre-filled with the agent's query and scoped to that conversation ("Search: <query> — <conversation>", one "Search all conversations" control): each hit is author · time · words with the match marked, and a hit opens the conversation AT that message. The card's "+N more" under one search opens the whole search, every conversation grouped under its name. A read / reply row still opens the conversation; the agent's CLI text is unchanged; the touch keeps the query + ≤ 50 hit refs per conversation (ids and instants, never the words).
- Gates: test-channel-placement (the placement table per channel, the caps-row census, the send contract, the engine, the words, controls), test-channel-thread, test-channel-reactions, test-channel-outbox §6, test-channels-engine ⑰⑱⑲, test-channels-agent-cli, test-channels-lark-shape, test-architecture §64 / §64b / §65 (fast); test-channel-threads-ui (heavy, chrome).

### Communication panel — AN ORG-WIDE SLACK INSTALL (lane slack-org-team-id, 2026-10-15 — B-8ca4 + B-091e, parked by lane slack-grid-identity: the fleet moved into an Enterprise Grid; this makes an org-level install work before anyone installs one)

On an Enterprise Grid an admin may install a Slack app on the whole ORGANIZATION instead of one workspace
(`is_enterprise_install: true`; the code exchange answers `team: null`). Such a token is the org's: a workspace-scoped
method must name the workspace (`team_id`), else Slack answers `missing_argument` / `team_access_not_granted`
(docs.slack.dev "Developing apps for Enterprise orgs": always pass `team_id`; a workspace-level token ignores it). THE
RECORD LEARNS THE KIND at every sign-in (paste or consent): `isEnterpriseInstall` (auth.test's flag, the exchange's flag,
or an auth.test whose `team_id` IS the org), `enterprise`, and the WORKSPACE `team` with its source `teamFrom` —
auth.test's `team_id` when it names a workspace (not the org) › the exchange's `team.id` › the first workspace ONE
`auth.teams.list` names. No workspace granted ⇒ the sign-in is refused by name ("an admin adds the app to a workspace,
then Re-authorize"), nothing connected. A re-authorize rewrites the whole record; a record without the field reads as
`false`. ONE PLACE ADDS `team_id`: slack.js `METHOD_SCOPE` names every Web API method the adapter sends `workspace` (16)
or `org` (auth.test, auth.teams.list, oauth.v2.access, apps.manifest.create, team.info {team}); `withTeam`, called by
`api()` alone, adds `team_id` to a non-org method on an org-wide record and hands every other request back untouched — a
workspace-level record sends byte-identical requests. On an org-wide record, `missing_argument` /
`team_access_not_granted` is `forbidden` `org-team-not-granted`: "the app is installed for the whole organization, and
the workspace T… is not granted to it — Re-authorize from a workspace the app is added to"; the conversation's card says
it in zh / ja too (channel-caps `sendWhyText`). Not now: several workspaces of one org under one token (the record would
need `teams[]` and each conversation its workspace). The raw API sends what the agent wrote. Gate:
scripts/test-slack-org-install.mjs (a loopback node:http fake Slack; the METHOD_SCOPE census with a planted call RED).

### Communication panel — A SLACK ACCOUNT BY ITS PARTS (lane slack-grid-identity, 2.369.273 — owner + userW 2026-10-14: the fleet's Slack moved into an Enterprise Grid, every re-authorize was refused as another account)

Slack names a signed-in person by three ids: the person (`user_id`), the workspace (`team_id`) and, once the workspace is in an
