### UI
- **On a phone, a notice never covers what you work with (lane phone-refusal-wrap, .355; P1-5 / P2-1):** on the phone / touch tier the toast stack stands above the composer, and with a dialog open it stands in a room the dialog makes under its title — no row of the dialog is covered; its ✕ is a 44 px target; the port notice says «A program on this machine started listening on port N» with the plug icon of the button that forwards it (no emoji). The New Session footer's refusal («✕ Cannot create yet: Choose a folder first») and its value chips wrap — on a narrow phone (≤ 480 px) on their own row above Cancel / Create; nothing hides behind a sideways scroll. Open: port notices as For-you items with a Forward button.
- 6 built-in color themes: Dark, Light, Dracula, Nord, Solarized, Monokai — all contrast-audited (terminal ANSI colors + UI chrome `--text-dim`/`--text-secondary`)
- Theme editor: floating panel to create custom themes — ~50 CSS variables + 16 ANSI colors, live preview, hover-to-highlight CSS var usage, save/load/delete, multi-client sync via WebSocket. ThemeManager: `registerCustomTheme`, `unregisterCustomTheme`, `setLivePreview`, `extractThemeValues`, `applyPendingTheme`. CSS value sanitization (strips `{}`). Constructor defers custom theme fallback until async load.
- Global settings popover (⚙ in toolbar): theme, font size, font family
- **The top toolbar folds, never overlaps (lane toolbar-fold, 2026-09-30, owner: the green cluster "takes too much width on a low-resolution screen and overlaps other chrome").** Measured before: `.toolbar-right { min-width: 160px; justify-content: flex-end }` let the zone shrink to 160 px and its buttons overflow LEFTWARD over the layout presets, the title and — sidebar open — UNDER the sidebar (21 of 60 states: 1024×768 in every language, 1366×768 at UI 125 %, ja 1280×720). Now lane I's rule: the title is the one flexible item (ellipsis, hidden below 24 px); the create buttons give up their WORDS one at a time in the fold order (glyph + its words as aria-label and tooltip); then they FOLD into ONE ⋯ after the zones by priority (Presets 5 → Desktop / the layout presets 4 → Web view / Apps 3 → Terminal / Files 2 → New Session 1; ⚙, ☰ and the tray widgets never fold); the ⋯ menu (registry menu `toolbar-overflow`) lists the folded items in the ARRANGED order, each row running the same command as its button (the layout presets = a submenu of their own buttons). Customize mode suspends the fold (every element full, the bar wraps). Files: src/lib/toolbar-fold-model.js (table) + toolbar-fold.js (DOM) over live-bar-layout.js `barLadder` + `groups` and bar-fold.js. Gates: test-toolbar-fold (fast) + test-toolbar-fold-ui (heavy rect census, both font sets).
- Resizable sidebar (drag right edge)
- Usage pies in taskbar (two circular pie charts: 5h session + 7d weekly rate limits from Anthropic API, hover for %, click for details)
- **Usage window: who spent it (⚙ → Usage, 2026-09-10).** Every ledger row now says which KIND of transcript produced it — the conversation itself (`main`), one of its subagents, or a workflow agent — so the dashboard answers a question it could not before: on this instance **58.9 % of the last 7 days' cost was workflow agents**, and the top conversation is 72 % agents. Three surfaces: a **By origin** group at the top of the classic cost section (a stacked share bar + one row per origin), a **By session** table with a main / subagents / workflows column each (cost in the selected metric, cost + tokens + requests on hover) and a per-row stacked bar, and **By project** rows whose hover names the same split. `origin` is also an ordinary panel dimension (and a `splitBy`), and the default "Cost overview" preset ships a cost-by-origin donut plus a session × origin bar panel. A fourth origin, **Unattributed**, appears only when the ledger holds rows nobody can name (a transcript that has been rotated away, or a remote machine whose scanner predates the field) — it is never hidden, because it is spend and the other rows are read as shares of the same total.
- **A re-emission costs zero bytes; a machine whose ledger is out of shape is said (lane ledger-dedup-law, B-7f9e, .361 — a fleet shard had reached 23.8 GiB of one harvest window).** A machine's usage is deduplicated as it is WRITTEN (the same events arriving again append nothing); the harvest's progress on a paired machine is kept by the hub (no «change files» ask for VibeSpace's own bookkeeping, nothing re-read when nobody answers); a monthly ledger file over 2 GiB or about 2× its distinct rows PAUSES that MONTH of that machine (round 4 — its other months are recorded as usual; this month's events are held beside the file, at most 64 MiB per machine × month, the oldest dropped past it and counted — once each, however often the machine sends them again, never one already recorded (an event the month's file has is never held; the count a hold ends with is checked against the file, and an open notice that could not check says «some of them may already be recorded») —, and recorded in order once the file is back in shape), says so in For you and in the Usage window («Usage of M for YYYY-MM is held: its ledger file … is out of shape» + «N events of M for YYYY-MM held …»), removes the repeated rows in the background — and when that does not bring it back in shape (the dedup failed, the file was replaced, it is still too big), the notice says what happened, when it is tried again and what to do; when removing rows cannot help (the file is over 2 GiB with no repeated rows, or the month holds more distinct records than the index keeps) it says so and VibeSpace stops trying; one notice per machine × month — re-worded in place when the machine is renamed or a count moves, reopened (never filed twice) when it was marked read; two machines of one name get two notices, each naming its machine's id (kept for as long as the notice is open) — re-judged at every start by the rule that opened it (the holds read back too); a month back in shape stays held until its held events are in the ledger, and a write that fails there (a full disk) is said and retried at the machine's next harvest and at a restart; a device's batch is acknowledged (its cursor commits) once every event of it is recorded or held (a notice the index opened waits for the index — never closed by a quick sample); the update's one-shot pass shrinks files already written that way (the first copy of each row kept — the totals do not change). Round 9: a count of dropped events is said across a restart too (a drained hold's record is read back on its own) and is its hold's — never added twice, and a closed one stays as an «Earlier» line when the month's next hold reopens the notice; one machine's hold that cannot be READ (its file's permissions, a failing disk) is ONE notice naming the file, that month waits (`retryAfter`) while every other month is recorded; the standing item of a background task is a notice — no Allow / Deny on it; it says where to allow it (the machine's Hub automation). Round 10: the «cannot be read» notice names the real file and closes once that file reads — after a restart too; a hold's held events are never pushed out by the events that arrive as its month is recorded again; an older hold's count found at a start is said (an «Earlier» line) before its file goes. Round 11: a held count the store could not keep is tried again once a minute while its machine keeps sending, until it is kept; a file of counts that cannot be read as one is kept and named, never counted as zero.
  - r12: a line of a held usage file that is no record (a crash, a newer build's record, bit rot) never makes its month wait: VibeSpace keeps every other record, moves the file as it was to data/usage-history/_set-aside, and says it once — ONE For-you notice per hold («… had a line that is no record — set aside; nothing waits»: the file, the line, the copy; the owner closes it).
  - r14: the error decides, never the file's age — a held usage file that cannot be read for a moment (too many open files, a network disk that timed out) is kept and read again, its count said then; one the disk refuses (permission denied, a folder in its place, or the same disk error at two starts) is set aside unread, and its month goes on. The notice says what was done: «set aside» only when a copy is there, «read past it» when none could be kept, the line still in the file when its rewrite failed.
- **The usage ledger rebuilds without freezing (B-748f, 2.369.274).** When a repair rewrites the usage records (a shard rewritten, shrunk or gone; a reload after a migration; a Usage summary that met a stale place), the in-memory ledger is rebuilt in a background worker while every reader keeps the figures it had — never a blank Usage window, never a frozen server — and the rebuilt ledger replaces the old one in one step; a Usage summary reaching past the 45-day window waits for it. A rebuild that fails leaves the previous figures, says why once in the server log and retries after a minute (doubling to 15). Code: src/usage-history.js `_rebuildInWorker` ⇒ kb-file-structure.md `### usage-history.js`.
- **A breakdown is fetched when its panel is on screen (B-f95d ②, 2.369.274).** The session × origin and project × origin crosses are as long as the list of every conversation / repo ever (14.5k / 940 here), and the window used to ask for both with every load — All time 9.1 MB instead of 5.1 MB, while the default dashboard draws one of them in its last panel and the other only in the classic view's project hover. Now a session or project cross is asked for (`/api/usage-stats?…&pivot=<a:b>&only=pivots` — the cross alone) the first time a panel that draws it scrolls into view; the panel says Loading… meanwhile, the window stays where the reader scrolled, and from then on that cross rides every refresh with the rest. Crosses over a bounded dimension (day × account) still come with the load. Gates: scripts/test-usage-pivots.mjs (fast) + scripts/test-usage-window-pivots.mjs (chrome).
- **"By project" is the repo an agent worked FOR.** An agent transcript records the agent's OWN directory, so an agent that ran in a git worktree used to be its own project row (272 of this instance's 3,155 agent transcripts). The event is attributed to the parent project and keeps its own directory as `wcwd`; a directory RENAME is handled too (the project directory name is the forward encoding of the cwd, so the right candidate can be verified rather than guessed — without that, $7,828 of one conversation's agent spend sat in a second row under a path that no longer exists).
- **THE THREE BROWSER FACES, NAMED FOR WHO DRIVES THEM (2.369.168, browser takeover C4 = docs/design-browser-faces.zh.md direction B, owner "那就选B吧"):** **Web view** / 网页视图 / ウェブビュー = the toolbar globe's iframe (the globe means nothing else any more; command `Open a web view`; Toolbar setting `Show Web view button`) · **Agent browser** / Agent 浏览器 / エージェントブラウザ = the agent's browser on the window-with-a-dot glyph (rail item, ⚙ Tools ▸ `Agent browser…` 35, the window, `Agent browser (live)` views, the chip `Agent browser · <profile>`, the card commands `Agent browser profile…` / `Agent browser — live view` / `Hand the agent browser back`, the Session Properties section, the Settings category `Agent browser` under Services) · **Browser app** / 浏览器应用 / ブラウザアプリ = a browser in the Apps catalog (sub-label, gated on the registry row's `browser`). The Apps dialog's intro says you drive an app and the agent cannot reach it. Phone '+' sheet: Web view / Desktop app… (when the desktop-apps probe has a backend) / Agent browser (when the profile digest is held: the active session's live view, else a picker over the live sessions holding a browser, else the Agent browser window). Labels and icons only — ids, openSpec actions, settings keys and the rail id unchanged, saved layouts replay as before. Gate: test-browser-faces (+ the label pins in test-window-types / -contributions / -ax-paint / -browser-housekeeping / -profile-blindness, test-architecture §53).
- Embedded browser window (🌐 in toolbar, labelled **Web view** since 2.369.168): iframe with URL bar, proxy mode toggle, layout persistence. `navigate()` accepts `blob:`/`data:`/`about:` URLs verbatim (2.84.0 — the http:// auto-prefix blanked every blob page, incl. the chat html Preview button and the Diagnostics report)
- Browser proxy mode: node-unblocker full URL rewriting (HTML/CSS/JS), strips X-Frame-Options/CSP. Works for noVNC, docs, internal services. Google/Cloudflare sites may trigger reCAPTCHA due to anti-bot detection. **`navigate()` normalizes a bare origin to a trailing slash (2.186.5, real report):** node-unblocker leaves in-page links RELATIVE and relies on the document base, so a pathless origin (`http://host:port`) gave the iframe a base with no `/` and a relative dir-listing link resolved UP A LEVEL, escaped the proxy, and fell to the X-Frame-Options overlay. Running http(s) URLs through `new URL().toString()` adds the `/` (no-op otherwise) so relative links stay inside `/proxy/`.
- Frontend optimization: esbuild minification (2.5MB → 1.4MB) + gzip compression middleware (~420KB over wire, 83% reduction)
- Static file caching: `maxAge=0` with etag validation for cache revalidation
- "N windows" click in taskbar → window list popup (scoped to active desktop)
- **Mobile gaps batch (2.369.125, docs/design-mobile-gaps.md — the top-10 of a 59-feature desktop-vs-phone review at 390×844).** The nav bar carries the **For-you inbox** (badge pills, the popup as a full-width sheet); a **long-press on "+"** opens the create sheet (Agent session / Terminal / Files / Browser / Desktop when available) — the four toolbar entry points that vanish with `#toolbar`; the **window switcher** always shows the desktop tabs with a **"+" tab** (since 2.369.356 in the regular class too; the discoverable door is the nav's **Desktops** button, lane desktop-switch-phone .357 — see Virtual desktops), a tab long-press renames/deletes, a window-row long-press opens the registered 'window' menu (incl. **Move to Desktop**), and a Minimized section is the restore path (a synced minimize is truth on the phone: hidden locally, the next window shown, carried in its saves — r2); the **chat status bar** carries a **search magnifier** (Ctrl+F's touch face, live windows only) and a **long-press on a message** opens Copy text / Open in editor / Fork from here / Message details while the 21×16 hover buttons are hidden; the **file explorer** shows one Name column, a folding bookmark strip, 36 px toolbar buttons and a long-press **Select…** mode with a batch bar; **⚙ System… / Ports… / Channels…** open the rail panels in windows where no rail exists; the **settings nav wraps**; and ONE `@media (max-width:768px)` block lifts every nav / sidebar-header / search / tab / status-chip / dropdown-row / terminal-key target to ≥ 36 px. Gate: scripts/test-mobile-gaps.mjs (heavy chrome, real touch sequences).
- **The phone's back gesture (2026-10-18, lane mobile-back-guard — the owner: 「在手机版上能不能 block 一下那个返回手势啊？」)**: on a phone (app.isMobile) a back swipe first closes what is open, one layer per back, in Esc's order — the floats, a dialog, the window switcher, a sheet (For-you tray / usage popup), then the window area yields to the sidebar (home; the window stays open), then the sidebar's drill-down returns to its list; at home it shows 「再返回一次退出」 and a second back within 2 s leaves VibeSpace (later it re-arms). A desktop browser's back is untouched. Settings › Mobile › 「返回手势先关闭面板，再按一次才退出」 (`mobile.backGuard`, default on). Touch screens also get `overscroll-behavior: none` (no pull-to-refresh / Chrome's own swipe navigation). PURE src/lib/back-guard.js + wiring src/lib/mobile-back.js; the history shape is docs/kb-patterns.md "The history sentinel".
- **A back never costs a load (lane phone-back-reload, 2.369.358 — the owner's Android phone: a back press reloaded VibeSpace, the loading screen, then home)**: the back road's states — at boot a phone stands ONE sentinel above the page's entry (push), KEEPS it on a reload (the entry below stays same-document) and REBUILDS it (the current entry becomes the page's, a new sentinel above) when the tab was discarded and shown again, loaded by a history traversal, or the entry below is another document; a back closes one layer and steps back onto the sentinel (go(1)); at home the 「再返回一次退出」 toast — with nothing of VibeSpace's below the page's entry the next back is the browser's own and leaves; with OLDER VibeSpace entries below (a renderer kill's reload, a second load of the app in the tab) the page re-arms at once and the next back inside 2 s leaves past them all in ONE traversal; the whole tab VibeSpace's ⇒ the tab's first entry, ONE load the diary names; and when the exit's traversal still stops ON an older VibeSpace page (an iframe link followed inside it adds a step the browser's entry list never shows), that page does not start the app — it goes on back, at most 3 hops, and only stays (ONE named load) when nothing is left below or the person taps — or when its own step back never ends (the page before answers with nothing, the person stops the load): then it starts the app within 4 s, never a loading screen for good; a browser that cannot say where a load came from (no navigation.activation) never hops at all. On a slow link the exit still ends where it was going, and one that lands too late to go on files the incident «a slow exit»; a tap while that step back is still loading — also once the page has waited it out — cancels the exit, and the next back after such a wait shows 「再返回一次退出」 again; a chain of slow pages that still ends outside files nothing, and a link to a heading followed meanwhile does not stop the exit from going on; neither does a scroll, from the first moment of the wait on (only a tap that ends on the page counts — also one pressed just before the exit went on to its next step), and a mouse's back or forward button there is the browser's own step, never a tap. The stale-tab reload: once per server version per tab — the stamp written as the reload fires, so a reconnect inside its 800 ms never says the notice early — then ONE notice if the tab still runs the old bundle. A forward press, or a return from another page, never files the «back press cost a load» incident. **What the recorder keeps:** the tab's navigation diary (src/lib/nav-log.js — 60 rows in sessionStorage, surviving every load in the tab): each boot (navigation type, the step taken, the state's shape, history.length, the entries as S/x shapes, wasDiscarded, the referrer's kind), each back (the verdict, the layer, the exit plan), each re-arm (its ms, or the 500 ms push), each exit (skip, load), pagehide / pageshow, each stale-tab step (both versions + the decision), and a `cost` row when a load followed a back press — which files an incident by itself (once per tab per half hour, the toast names it). Never a URL, a title or words; every incident capture carries it (snapshot.navLog). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md "src/lib/back-guard.js + mobile-back.js", "src/lib/nav-log.js"
- **The phone's first screen is the attention list (lane phone-first-screen, 2.369.319 — design q-044 decision 5, accepted 2026-10-19)**: on a phone VibeSpace opens on a PAGE of the attention list over the window area (the For-you tray's bands, rows and fold heads, the notices' grey line); a row's tap opens its conversation, the back gesture returns to the page (HOME while its first screen holds a row, else the conversation list), ☰ still opens the conversation list; nothing on the first screen ⇒ no page (the phone opens where its restore put it). The cap is the list's 6 (never the viewport's); the rows take the tray's two-line preview (whole words need 1161 px at 375×812) ⇒ «For-you tray: the attention list». **Since 2.369.358 (lane foryou-honest, the owner on a phone) the page IS the For-you sheet's rows at the touch scale, the door included:** a row folds to its question (16 px, ONE line) + one 14 px meta line and the whole row opens it in place (ONE open at a time; an answer folds it); its trailing «Chat» door (an SVG, 44 px, «Go to this session») opens the conversation in one tap — decision 5's jump; six folded rows + the heads stay the first screen (q-044 decision 1). A RELOAD keeps the window this tab had on show («每次刷新都是这个»): the page takes the screen only on a cold open, when nothing is on show, or when it was on show itself. Its doors back («切到其他窗口之后又回不来了»): the top bar's For you TOGGLES the page (the page ⇄ the window it covers — never the sheet beside it; the sheet only when the page has no row) and the ☰ drawer's first row «For you · N» (the honest count) opens it; the title tap keeps its switcher.
- **The page's class follows the viewport, live (lane duo-build-1, 2026-10-25 — the iPhone Duo's folds, SPEC-v3 §1.2 / §7)**: folding the Duo from its 951 px inner display to the 382 px cover or the 669 px inner portrait (or any resize / rotation across 768 px) switches the page between the window manager and the phone page WITHOUT a reload, 120 ms after the crossing settles: the chrome is what a fresh load at that size builds (no desktop rail on the phone — B-f5ec; toolbar / taskbar / nav as fresh), the phone shows one window filling the screen (the active one, else the last used — the conversation on screen stays on screen), the desktop puts every window back on its box, every view re-measures (the transcript wraps at the new width — B-1d40), the draft in the composer is the same box with the same words. Nothing is persisted by a switch. PURE src/viewport-class.js + src/lib/viewport-switch.js; heavy gate test-duo-layout.
- **The iPhone Duo's inner display: the list beside the conversation + a trailing bar (lane duo-build-1 slice 2, SPEC-v3 rev 3.3 §2 / §4, 2026-10-25)**: a touch screen 640–1023 px wide (the regular class) shows the conversation LIST as a 320 px column (Sessions · filter · + · ⋯; Folders / Task Groups / Remote; one scroll: the conversations that need you first — a conversation with open For-you questions MARKS them on one line «needs you · N · <its newest question>», whose tap opens the For-you window on them (lane foryou-honest, the owner's B: the inline answers with their chips are withdrawn) —, the running, then the stopped ones arriving as you scroll), the conversation on show beside it (its head = its name + its state word), and in landscape ONE vertical bar on the right edge: on top this conversation's actions (✕ over a viewer or panel, Artifacts with its count, ⋯ = the window's menu without window-manager verbs or Close, Agent browser — live view while it holds a browser), a gap, then the owner's global destinations — **For you (its badge = the honest count; lane foryou-honest) · Task Groups · Files · Channels · Agent browser · Background Work · ⚙** (the owner, 2026-10-25: 「因为 duo 有那个特殊的侧栏，可以考虑把一些电脑版的侧边按钮放过去，比普通手机版访问容易一些效率高一些」 — the five most-used rail doors a phone reaches only through ☰ / ⚙; Remote stays the list's third tab, Ports / Agents / Plugins / System / Diagnostics stay ⚙'s rows: a second ⋯ on one bar would be a second overflow). A destination opens in the conversation column (the list stays) and wears the selected state. Portrait (669×867): list 320 | conversation 348 with the bar lying over the conversation (☰ hides / shows the list — no overlay, not remembered across a rotation). Landscape (lane desktop-switch-phone, the owner 2026-10-25 — 与原文不同, SPEC-v3 §4 kept it static): a ☰ at the conversation's head (`#list-column-toggle`, fixed over the title bar's left 44 px, z 95000) hides / shows the list too — the conversation then takes 0–895; this TAB's choice (sessionStorage `vibespace.listHidden`), kept across a reload and a rotation back, shown by default; a book fold shows the list whatever the choice. The cover (382) keeps the phone page. Heavy gate: test-duo-layout ④ ⑤.
- **Half-folding the Duo (lane duo-build-1 slices 3–4, SPEC-v3 §1.6 / §3 / §5, 2026-10-25)**: only when Safari reports two viewport segments (behind its Device Posture / Viewport Segments feature flags today) does the page re-arrange — like a BOOK (the two columns snap to the two screen halves around the hinge: the list widens to the left half, the conversation keeps the right half, a 20 px seam with nothing tappable near it) or a LAPTOP (the same portrait columns; the conversation's bar moves down onto the composer, the keyboard pushes the composer up; under a tall keyboard the bar steps aside). «Folded» alone never moves anything (the cover held as a tent stays the phone page); a fold that never reports its segments falls back to flat after 1.5 s. The keyboard is read from the visual viewport on every screen size. Heavy gate: test-duo-layout ⑦.
- **No keyboard on load on a touch screen (lane duo-build-1 slice 1, 2026-10-25)**: opening, restoring or switching to a chat on a phone / tablet / the Duo leaves the composer unfocused — the keyboard comes up when the person taps the message box (the restore's autofocus raised a 60 %-high keyboard on the Duo simulator). A desktop with a mouse still puts the caret in the composer. Heavy gate: test-duo-layout ③.
- **The phone's view is its own (2026-10-13, §6b guard 10, docs/design-mobile-gaps.md #59 → A)**: switching windows on the phone (the switcher, a reload, a restore from Minimized) changes only what the phone shows — the desktop's stacking, boxes and minimized windows stay as they are; windows opened / closed on the phone still appear / close everywhere. Heavy gate: scripts/test-phone-desktop-sync.mjs (desktop 1440×900 + iPhone 390×844, real touch, both belts alone, base-tree RED controls).
- **Settings: everyday vs advanced, and only what applies here (B-df40 part 2, 2.369.202).** Rows carry two optional data fields: `tier: 'advanced'` (drawn only while the header's **Show advanced settings** switch is on — localStorage `vibespace.settingsAdvanced`; off, each category ends with "N advanced settings hidden · Show", whose Show turns the switch on in place) and `when` (closed tags `setting` / `fact` / `harness` / `channel`, all clauses must hold). The PURE `src/lib/settings-view.js` decides: a search shows every match with a chip saying why a hidden row is not in use here; a modified row always shows; a false `when` hides the row (never greyed) and an emptied category with its nav item; an unknown fact hides nothing. Facts are built once per open: `vnc` / `desktopApps` from the app's probes (`_desktopAppsKnown` = the probe answered), `harnesses` from /api/home's `cli` field, `channels` from ONE `GET /api/channels/adapters` only when a row asks. Changing a governing row re-draws at once. 77 of 192 rows advanced; Desktop apps is a new Services category. Gates: test-settings-view, test-architecture 44e.

### Desktop apps (docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md, P8-1 — 2026-09-13; HONEST SCOPE)

**Apps that survive a rebuilt machine — Layer 0 (2.369.200, docs/design-app-persistence.zh.md §3.1 + §3.3; owner D3 / D4 / D5):** the Desktop apps dialog has a **Your installed apps** section: the apps installed through VibeSpace (each with Remove…), agents' open proposals (Install… / Not now), **N updates · last refreshed N d ago** + Refresh… (never automatic), "Installed outside VibeSpace — lost when this machine is rebuilt: …" + Adopt… (the DPkg::Post-Invoke tripwire), the package sources (Remove…), and four doors — **Install an app…** (search the machine's package sources → pick → the plan), **Install from a .deb file…** (a path on that machine; also the explorer's "Install this package…" on a .deb — the file is copied into the machine's package cache with its sha256), **Add a package source…** (https + its signing key: the plan shows the key's fingerprint; a source is approved before any package can come from it), **Let an agent help…** (a temporary helper conversation that knows how to install apps — the request + the whole apps manual + the machine's facts as its first message; it can only propose). Every one opens THE install dialog (the same component as "Install xpra on {machine}…"): the plan's facts (packages · download · on disk, where they come from, a .deb's own install scripts, "after this machine is rebuilt, VibeSpace puts it back from its saved packages — about N s after the server starts"), every command, then Install with the log streamed; the run is the plan shown (else `plan_changed`, nothing run) through the machine's ONE package slot. An installed app with a desktop file is a catalog card (`app.<entry>`, its own icon) and an agent can open it (`vibespace-window open app.<entry>`). **An agent only PROPOSES** (`vibespace-app install <pkg> --why …` / `remove` / a source): ONE For-you item (origin **Apps**) with Install… / Not now right on the row and in the For-you window; the outcome reaches the agent free on its next turn (`vibespace-app wait` reads it now). **After a rebuild** (a fresh root filesystem — the marker `/var/lib/vibespace/apps-replayed` is gone), the server puts every entry back after it listens, offline from `~/.vibespace/apps/debs` (rung 1), online only when the machine image changed or rung 1 could not (rung 2); the cards read "restoring…" meanwhile; anything that did not come back is ONE For-you notice naming it. Refusals are said by name (a snap placeholder, a conflict, an install that would remove packages, no such package, not enough disk with the numbers, no passwordless sudo — then the commands to copy). Layer 1 (an app SYSTEM on the persistent volume — zero replay) is the next lane.

**The app system — Layer 1 (2.369.210, docs/design-app-persistence.zh.md §3.2; owner D1 / D2 / D5):** on a pod whose chart sets `VIBESPACE_APP_SYSTEM` (appSystem.enabled), Desktop apps → Your installed apps offers **Set up…** — one click creates a persistent same-release userland on the home disk (rung A: the image's minbase tarball, offline; rung B: debootstrap). From then on every apt / .deb install goes INTO it: after a rebuilt pod the apps are simply there (no replay). Each app is a `sys.<entry>` row that runs its launcher in `~/.vibespace/sysroot/bin` (also at the end of PATH); the launcher enters the app system through the root-owned helper on the same pid (the keeper's handle, group kill and PSS report unchanged). An interrupted install shows **Repair**; after an image change to another release the dialog offers **Migrate…** (Rebase: a new userland, the apps installed again, the old one kept → **Roll back…** / **Delete…**); another processor architecture blocks the rows until migrated. Refresh upgrades the app system. Agents still only propose installs; no session gets new context (D3).

**Apps installed outside VibeSpace — witnessed (2.369.252, lane apps-launcher-witness; owner 2026-10-11, JASP):** the launcher's Apps dialog also lists, in their OWN group "Installed outside VibeSpace (n)" under the engine's rows, what is on the machine without the door — the user's / the system's flatpaks (`flatpak list --app`) and desktop entries (~/.local/share/applications, /usr/share/applications), the user's own first; each card carries its source chip (Flatpak · yours / system, Desktop entry · yours / system) and its command as written; a press launches it through the same door (`seen.<…>` registry ids — never an engine id, never merged); a program that is gone stays listed and says so; a filter box searches both groups; Check again re-lists. The list (src/app-witness.js PURE + app-serve `refreshWitness`, ≤ 5 s, data/desktop-apps-witness.json) refreshes on open when a witnessed directory changed or every 10 min, after an install through the door, and after the install helper's turn. Every install result names its machine: "installed on this VibeSpace machine (linux-box-hub)" / "on WIN-DESK1" (the dialog, the toast, the For-you card, the helper's outcome).

**Apps registered with VibeSpace — Add to VibeSpace…, launch variants, Remove… / Forget (2.369.254, lane app-register-ui = the launcher half; the server + CLI half = app-register-model):** every witnessed card has **Add to VibeSpace…** (an "Add…" beside the card at desk width; its "…" menu / a long press on a phone) — an ADOPT dialog prefilled from `GET /api/desktop/apps/adopt-prefill?seenId=` (label; launch variants as keyed rows, each command ONE line read as argv by `src/argv-words.js` and shown back as chips; a remove recipe — empty = Forget only; a reinstall recipe; the witness line "found as Flatpak · yours: org.jaspstats.JASP"); Add → `POST /api/desktop/apps/adopt` → the card moves into Apps (toast "<app> is now in your Apps"); a refusal (bad_label / bad_exec / bad_args / too_many_variants / needs_root / bad_icon / shadow) is said under the field it concerns, never a toast alone. A registered row (`registered`, `launch[]`, `removable`, `source`) shows its chip + its default command on the card; its "…" lists the variants (≥ 2: the default by its own label, e.g. "Open", the others **Open · <variant>**; the launch POST carries `variant`) above the scale rows, then **Remove…** (one confirm that shows the recipe verbatim: "This runs as you: …" → `POST /api/desktop/apps/:id/remove`; a failure shows the output's last lines; the toast says "Removed" or "Forgotten — the program is still on the machine") or **Forget** (no recipe), and **Show command** (copies the argv line). The For-you card of an agent's registration (src/app-card.js kind `registered`) shows "<agent> registered <label>", the resolved program, every variant as `label — exec args…`, both recipes and the witness line on its face; the digest covers them. Both group heads explain themselves in one line. **Gates:** test-app-register-words (fast), test-app-register-ui (heavy, the contract stubbed in the page). **The three owner routes are REAL since 2.369.255 (lane rel254-verify-fixes — in .254 the launcher called routes its sibling lane never built, so Remove… / Forget always failed):** `GET /api/desktop/apps/adopt-prefill?seenId=` (the PURE prefill, registered before `GET …/apps/:id`), `POST /api/desktop/apps/:id/remove` (the entry's recipe AS THE USER through app-serve's home-remove door — sanitised env, cwd = home, ≤ 120 s, output ≤ 8 KiB back; `no_recipe` / `needs_root` / `changed_outside` / `failed` by name), `POST /api/desktop/apps/:id/forget` (the entry leaves, the program stays and is listed outside VibeSpace again); owner only (vsst_/jbt_ refused). A registered row without a recipe offers Forget; env and cwd are shown on the card's tooltips, "Show command", the For-you card and its digest; a row changed outside VibeSpace is a disabled card with its reason. Gate: scripts/test-launcher-route-census.mjs (fast) — every path the client calls is served or RED.

**The Apps dialog opens at once; "outside" means outside the base (2.369.254, lane apps-dialog-fast; owner 2026-10-11 "打开App界面很卡 … VibeSpace之外的App列表也变得很长"):** an open answers from the LAST witness list (`openAnswer` in src/app-witness.js — answer = the cache, a due walk starts in the background, never a wait); when the walk lands, the machine pushes ONE `desktop-apps-witness {host, witness, rows}` (desktop-serve `hooks.onWitness` → the keeper's broadcast) and the open dialog patches only that group, keyed (the same card nodes, the filter kept); the group head says "listing…" meanwhile. Check again still waits (the person asked), its spinner in the group head. The group lists a `-user` row always and a system flatpak always; a `desktop-system` entry only when the dpkg package owning it (ONE `dpkg -S` per walk) is in the drift set (installed after the apps system's base) — every other system entry is flagged `distro` and hidden behind "n system entries not shown — Show them" (user state `desktopAppsShowSystem`). The cache file keeps `tookMs` + `scope` counts; `vibespace-app status` prints the same list ("Apps installed OUTSIDE VibeSpace"). Measured: the GET with a due 3 s walk 3040 → 4 ms; the dialog's first card 43–177 ms (heavy ⓪, two runs).

**Moving apps into the app system (2.369.211, design 019):** where the app system is usable and root still reinstalls host apps at every rebuild, Desktop apps shows "N apps are reinstalled at every rebuild — move them into the app system" + Move…: per app the install into the app system runs first and only then is its host record forgotten (a failure leaves it replaying, named). Installing the exact packages of a host app into the app system is its move; a partial overlap is named. The drift card's primary act installs into the app system (Adopt on the base is second); Refresh names the host apps it skips; a result names a background service nothing starts and an app-system install with nothing launchable. The index follows root's records after every run (a Roll back's lost apps are named once). An agent cannot propose a move.

**Desktop apps on paired devices — lane C1 shipped (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.zh.md §3.5; D5–D8 decided as recommended):** the machine half of the keeper is ONE shared module (src/desktop-serve.js) that runs where the app runs — in-process for this machine, inside the VibeSpace agent (`desktop-serve` op) on a PAIRED device (D5: always through a daemon — an ssh host gets the agent installed over ssh and is served by it; an agent that predates the op is refused `host_needs_daemon` by name, a failed install is `host_unavailable` naming the reason). The device holds its own record (D8: `~/.vibespace/desktop-apps.json` — the app outlives the hub AND its own daemon: a restarted daemon re-adopts it), the hub reaches it through src/server/desktop-access.js and forwards its loopback picture port over the agent's data plane (nothing listens on a LAN; xpra's protocol is end to end, so clipboard / input / geometry ride it untouched). Measured on a loopback fake device (test-desktop-remote): hello through the forward ~530 ms incl. the ws upgrade, keystrokes → the app's file ~10 ms. **What a person can do today is unchanged**: the launch dialog and the routes still offer this machine only — the machine choice, the bridge's forward and "Install xpra on <machine>…" are lane C2. Records carry `hostId` (`'local'`).

**Desktop apps on paired devices — lane C2 shipped (2026-09-25):** a person can now run a desktop app ON ANOTHER MACHINE. The launch dialog has a "Run on" row (this machine + every paired machine; a machine that cannot run apps is greyed with its reason — offline, needs the agent upgraded, no X11 on macOS / Windows — never hidden; an ssh machine not connected yet "connects when chosen"). Choosing one shows THAT machine's catalog (greyed by its own binaries), ladder and slots; the launch runs there and the window says so ("{app} — on {machine}", an "on {machine}" chip). The picture reaches the browser through the hub: the device's xpra port is forwarded over the agent's data plane (no LAN port, xpra's protocol end to end — typing, clipboard and resize work as on this machine). Stop, Keep running, Scale ▸, windows, the idle stop and the resource report all work for a remote app (the hub decides policy from the input it relays; the device acts). If the machine stops answering, its apps stay listed as "machine not answering" and the window waits for it (they are NOT marked exited); a hub restart re-asks every known and every dialed-in machine and adopts what it runs. **"Install xpra on {machine}…"** (offered when the chosen machine has no xpra): shows the PLAN first — every command, and where xpra comes from (the machine's own apt when it offers xpra ≥ 5, else xpra.org's repository for its codename, pinned to 6.x, with xpra-x11 + xpra-html5 named) — then runs it as root through `sudo -n` with the log streaming into the dialog; no passwordless sudo ⇒ the commands to copy, said by name; macOS / Windows ⇒ no X11, by name. An install that takes longer than 15 minutes is said as such ("still running on this machine — VibeSpace never stops apt halfway"), never as a failure, and no second install starts on that machine until it ends; a link that drops mid-install says so. Since verify r2 (2026-09-25) the install runs DETACHED on the machine (its own session, its log + a pidfile beside the machine's desktop-app record): a hub restart, an Update, a lost link or the agent's own restart no longer kills apt halfway, and opening the dialog again while it runs offers "Follow the install" — "Still installing on <machine> — re-attached", its log from the start — never a second apt; a lost link keeps the machine's slot until the machine, reached again, says the install is gone. A Stop / Keep running / Scale click on a remote app whose machine drops at that moment answers "not answering" at once, not after a minute. The FLEET image gets xpra only through deploy/docker/Dockerfile — now xpra.org's bookworm 6.x, pinned (D7: one protocol version fleet-wide; bookworm's 3.1.3 is no longer installed). Measured on the paired test box (dial pairing to a scratch hub through an ssh reverse tunnel): paired + dialed in 0.8 s, launch → ready 1.8 s, xpra ping round trip through the whole path 7–8 ms on a 6–9 ms link, a key to the app's echo drawn 11–18 ms — with a pty-backed tunnel; a `ssh -N -R` tunnel measured 53–56 ms (+~47 ms per round trip: a session without a pty never sets TCP_NODELAY — the harness's tunnel, not the product; the design note has both). NOT for remote apps: agent window targets (an agent acts on this machine's windows only).

**A Windows / macOS machine's WHOLE DESKTOP — design 014 D1 (2.369.204, lane desktop-vnc-native; the owner's Q1 = yes and option A, 2026-10-03):** a paired Windows / macOS machine is no longer greyed in the Apps dialog's "Run on" row: it reads "its desktop" (ready / set up once / offline) and opens ITS dialog (src/lib/machine-desktop.js) — the state, **Open its desktop**, the one-time setup (the Mac: System Settings → Sharing → Screen Sharing, words only; Windows: **Install TightVNC Server…**), and **Run on its desktop…**. The rung `vnc-native` starts nothing and is no keeper session: the hub probes the machine's own VNC server on its 127.0.0.1:5900 through the agent's existing tcp-connect (src/desktop-display.js `rfbGreeting`, PURE: the greeting + the sign-in types, our version answered, closed before any sign-in), when the launcher lists machines or a window first opens on a link — never on a timer. The window (`machine-desktop.<hostId>`, ONE per machine per page) rides the ONE picture bridge through the ref-counted picture forward (two windows = one forward); the sign-in (ARD: the Mac user's name + password; else the VNC password) is asked in the page every time and handed to noVNC only; the picture is scaled, never resized (`resizeSession` off — the fixed-size rule of app windows does not apply); the window says once that it shows everything on that machine's screen; the machine going offline closes it naming it ("<machine> went offline", close code `machine-offline`). People only: the routes and the bridge refuse an agent token by name (`human_only`). **Run on its desktop…** = the owner's line through the agent's existing run-cmd, DETACHED and WHOLE (macOS: a positional `$1` of a fixed `nohup sh -lc` script; Windows: one PowerShell literal inside `-EncodedCommand` → `Start-Process %ComSpec% /d /s /c "<line>"`), shown before it runs and in the answer; refused by name: multi_line, hidden_chars (every invisible class, named by code point), too_long, empty, not_desktop_machine. **TightVNC (option A):** the agent runs UNELEVATED (a logon task, no admin), so the plan (pinned URL + SHA-256, the frozen flag table: server only, as a service, no firewall exception, no HTTP port, loopback allowed AND only, 5900, VNC auth) runs through a UAC prompt ON THAT MACHINE's screen — someone there clicks Yes and types the VNC password into the elevated window (VibeSpace never carries it); declined ⇒ `no_admin` with the same commands for an administrator PowerShell; the script checks the SHA-256 first and that 5900 listens on loopback addresses only after; done = the 5900 probe. The one-time setups in plain words: docs/machine-desktop.md.

**The Mac's sign-in from any address — lane mac-ard-signin (owner 2026-10-12 "连mac似乎不太成功", inc-mv51w0ow-crw3):** a Mac's Screen Sharing greets `RFB 003.889` and lists ARD (type 30: DH + AES-128 over the Mac user's name + password) first, so noVNC picks it — and encrypts the credentials with WebCrypto, which the owner's http://<hostname>:3456 page (NOT a secure context) does not have: noVNC's async auth threw, nothing reached the Mac, the status said 连接中… until the Mac closed the socket 268 s later. A loopback test never sees it (http://127.0.0.1 IS a secure context). Now `src/lib/aes-fallback.js` (PURE, encrypt-only AES-128/256: importKey raw AES-CBC / AES-ECB + encrypt — CBC answers WebCrypto's bytes, PKCS#7 included) is defined as an own `crypto.subtle` by vnc-view.js before `new RFB` — only for a view that asks a sign-in, only where the page has none; a secure context never sees it. After the sign-in is handed over the chip says "Signing in…" at once; noVNC's `connect` ⇒ "Connected"; noVNC's auth rejecting (an `unhandledrejection` whose stack is noVNC's, listened for only while that sign-in waits), 20 s of silence (`SIGNIN_BOUND_MS`) or the socket closing first ⇒ "The sign-in could not be completed: {why}" in red with Reconnect, the ladder off (no password loop), the words kept through the disconnect — never "Connecting…" past a sign-in. "Open its desktop" (and "Run as its own window…") closes the machine's dialog AND the Apps dialog it was opened from (`closeOpener` = the launcher's own close) before the window opens. Gates: test-aes-fallback (fast: FIPS-197 / SP 800-38A, byte for byte against node's WebCrypto + OpenSSL, noVNC's AESECBCipher over it, tampered-S-box RED), test-vnc-view §ARD, test-mac-ard-signin-chrome (heavy: the page on the box's NON-loopback address with `isSecureContext === false` asserted first, a fixture ARD server that decrypts the block; the base vnc-view.js stays 连接中… there (RED) and connects on 127.0.0.1 (the blind loopback control)).

**A machine's desktop sign-in, REMEMBERED — lane desktop-vnc-remember (owner 2026-10-19 「现在远程桌面密码能保留了吧 就存到 vault 里？」):** the sign-in dialog of a machine's whole desktop offers 「记住这台机器的登录」 (unticked by default; only where the hub can answer the machine's sign-in itself: a Mac's ARD, a VNC password, TightVNC). Ticked, its sentence says the sign-in is sealed in the vault instead of 「VibeSpace 不会保存」; once the machine TOOK the typed sign-in, the page sends it ONCE (`POST /api/desktop/machine-desktop/signin`) and the hub seals it as the per-machine integration row `desktop-signin/<hostId>` (the RemoteApp row's shape; its key is the vault's). From then on the HUB signs in: the machine-desktop target carries `signIn`, and the ONE bridge's RFB relay runs src/server/rfb-signin.js's gate on the first upstream of each window socket — it answers the machine's handshake (ARD / VNC / Tight, byte-for-byte noVNC's crypto) and shows the page a server that asks nothing (security type None), so the window connects with no dialog and the page never holds the password. A refusal (the password changed on the machine) reaches the page as nothing but a fresh plain connection: the dialog says 「上次记住的密码不对，请重输」 with the tick on; the row stays, and the hub never tries THAT row again (a machine's lockout counts failures) until the person signs in anew or forgets it. A locked vault: 「保险库已锁定——先解锁后可自动登录」 verbatim, with where to unlock and what For you holds on their own line below it (the vault's two facts — lane mirror-331-reds-chrome restored the words the .331 merge had run together), no tick, typing still works, nothing stored. The machine's dialog shows 「忘掉登录」 while one is kept; unpairing the machine forgets it (and its RemoteApp sign-in); Manage agents → Machines wears 「登录已记住」. UltraVNC (MSLogonII) and VeNCrypt servers are not answered by the hub: no tick there.

**A Windows / macOS machine's INSTALLED APPS (lane machine-desktop-apps, 2.369.252 — owner 2026-10-11):** the machine's dialog lists what is actually installed on it — enumerated ON the machine by witness through the `desktop-apps-list` device op (src/installed-apps.js, SHARED: Windows = both Start Menus' shortcuts resolved through WScript.Shell + the HKLM / WOW6432Node / HKCU Uninstall keys, in ONE encoded PowerShell script; macOS = /Applications (+ one folder deep) and ~/Applications bundles), bounded at 20 s on the machine, ≤ 500 rows, deduplicated by program. "Installed on {machine} (n)" with a filter; each row = its name + where the OS keeps it (Start menu / Installed programs / Applications); a press fills the command box with its launch line (Windows `start "" "<exe>" [args]`, macOS `open -a "<name>"`) — Run… judges and confirms it like any typed line. The presets stay as "Examples", the owner's own lines as "Recent". The hub keeps each machine's list (data/desktop-apps-hosts.json `installed`) and lists again on Check again, after an install through our door (its row shows at once as "just installed — being listed"), on the agent's hello (at most once a minute) and when the dialog opens on a list older than 10 min. An agent that predates the op is never asked — the dialog says "the list needs {machine}'s VibeSpace agent updated (it updates itself; check again in a minute)". The action row wraps and no button there is ever narrower than its words (Check again was the 24 px icon-button box).

**Desktop apps: a single-app window over VNC — one app at a time (lane machine-app-crop, owner 2026-10-11, route ② of B-bb0b):** "Run as its own window…" in a Windows / macOS machine's dialog (the default for `open -a …` / `start "" …`) runs the line with a launch report, then a `machine-app` window shows ONLY that app: the device follows its window (`window-track`: by the launched process, its start time, or a window new since the run; Windows user32 + DWM bounds; a Mac through its SCREEN HELPER's facts — lane mac-window-list-helper: nothing under node reads a Mac's screen, so the follow needs Screen Recording for vibespace-screen and says so by name without it, re-read every 500 ms; an app's window missing from the list while the app runs and Accessibility is off reads as minimized) and keeps it on top (`window-pin`: Windows topmost, a Mac activates the app through LaunchServices, `open -b <bundle>`); the page crops the machine's whole VNC picture to that rectangle (fit to the pane, the phone included) and sends pointer input only inside it, keys only while focused; the window follows moves / resizes, says when the app closed ("Open its whole desktop" / "Run again"), and several app windows of one machine say which one is on top (one screen). Not persisted; closing it ends the watch and undoes the pin. An old agent ⇒ "update the agent there". The whole-desktop window and "Run…" are unchanged. Gates: test-machine-window, test-machine-app-chrome.

- **What ships in P8-1:** any local desktop application (a registry row or `exec` + args + cwd typed by a HUMAN in ⚙ → Desktop apps… / the toolbar Apps button — never an agent, §5) opens as a `desktop-app` window: the server starts a PRIVATE X display + a picture server + the app for it (DA2: one display per app — isolated, its own idle, its own stop), the browser renders it through the shared picture component (noVNC) over the ONE cookie-authed ws bridge `/api/desktop/<id>/stream`; the raw port is loopback-only and never reaches a browser. N browsers watch ONE display (`-shared`); the window is part of the layout (openSpec replayed on every client and on reload), tab-group capable.
- **The backend ladder (§3, DA1):** `xpra` > `vnc-display` > `desktop-singleton`, each ONE row of the capability table `DISPLAY_BACKENDS` — never an if-chain. **P8-1 brings up `vnc-display` end to end in BOTH spellings** (Xvnc when present — the fleet image, driven in the gate through a shim that honours the keeper's exact argv because the real binary is not on this box; else Xvfb + x11vnc — this box) plus a light WM (xfwm4/openbox) when present; **`xpra` is PROBED and RECORDED only** (the ladder can choose it and says so, the keeper refuses to bring it up by name, the bridge answers 501 by name) — P8-2 wires `xpra start --html=on` and the HTML5 client (D21 (c)); `desktop-singleton` = the app starts on the shared Desktop (D10 fallback). Every fallback carries its reason in §3's exact words: the log prints `[desktop] backend fallback: xpra→vnc-display (xpra not on PATH)`, the record stores `fallbackWhy`, and the window's status chip shows **`vnc-display (xpra not on PATH)`** — the user always knows whether they see one window or a whole display. **(P8-1 state — SUPERSEDED by the P8-2 x1–x3 bullets below since 2026-09-21: the xpra rung is WIRED, brought up, relayed and drawn by us, and is the DEFAULT wherever xpra is installed; the 501 and the by-name refusal are gone.)**
- **The keeper's discipline (opencode-serve's, inherited):** records = FACTS with pid AND starttime (data/desktop-apps.json, atomic); boot ADOPTS a surviving session by pid+starttime+banner and reaps a dead one with its `lastError` kept; a COUNT CAP (6/instance, refused loudly naming the holders) + the RUNAWAY GUARD (>150 % CPU for 5 min or RSS > 2 GB ⇒ stop, park the registry row 1 h, telemetry) — the numbers are `src/keeper-limits.js`, the ONE home opencode-serve now reads too; per-app IDLE from the last INPUT the bridge saw (DA3: `desktop.idleTimeoutMin` 30, 0 = never; the window shows the countdown; "Keep running" is one explicit action); Stop = app → picture server → X, each verified gone. A VibeSpace restart never kills an app (detached, adopted).

- **P8-2 x5 (2026-09-22) — SEVERAL CLIENTS = ONE ACTIVE VIEWER (owner: "直接block掉非active客户端的app界面…" + "仿照terminal…可以手动take over"; design §7.5):** an app window open on several clients has exactly ONE active viewer — the first to attach; its pane sizes the app and only its keys / pointer / clipboard reach it. Every other client shows the overlay (the app's name, "Active on another client", **Resume here**) and NO picture — its resize and its keys reach nothing (the bridge opens no upstream for it). Resume here takes the window over at once (the pane flips before the server answers; the app re-fits to the new pane — measured 648 ms on xpra) and the previous client is blocked; when the active client closes, the most recently active remaining client takes over by itself. Both rungs (xpra and vnc-display). While an agent DRIVES the window every client is Watch: the picture scaled to fit the pane (never cropped), no input, nothing sent that could change the app's geometry; Take over from Watch makes that client the active one. The terminal's size-override made the default for desktop apps; the singleton Desktop window is not governed. **2.369.156 defaults (the round-3 verifier's INFO items — the owner can object):** when the ACTIVE client's connection drops or its page reloads, its seat is held for **5 s** (the others stay blocked) and the same window — or the reloaded page's new window in the same tab — takes it back; only then does the most recently active remaining client take over. On the xpra rung the Watch picture is never scaled UP: a pane larger than the app shows it crisp at 1:1, centred (smaller panes still scale down to fit). Also closed: a blocked pane names the app by its own window title on the xpra rung too (not the launch label); a reconnecting active window takes its seat back at once instead of waiting up to 30 s for the server to notice its dead connection; the hosted upstream xpra page (`/api/desktop/:id/xpra-ui/`) can only watch — it can no longer take the active seat.

Width now lives on `.dialog.desktop-launch` (the .guided-cli-dialog precedent — the THIRD instance of the anti-pattern style.css documents), the Advanced columns are `minmax(0,1fr)` (three nowrap Recent entries turned 1fr/1fr into 126/692px, the latent squeeze), every programmatic focus is `{preventScroll:true}`, and test-desktop-app-window MEASURES a fresh open at 1000×800 / 777×800 / 480×640. Its persistence exposed an older defect: `normalizeUserState` dropped every non-session key, so `desktopAppRecents` had never survived a reload since 2.369.96 (fixed in routes/persistence.js — see its entry).
- **RESOURCES ARE REPORTED, NEVER A STOP (2026-09-25, the owner's ruling after a Google Chrome desktop app was stopped 3 s after ready at a summed-RSS "2.0 GB", its profile deleted, Chrome parked 60 min):** the keeper samples each session's processes once a minute and measures memory as a FOOTPRINT (ΣPss; RssAnon+RssShmem only for a single process; never a sum of VmRSS). Over the threshold (2 GiB; a browser row 3 GiB / 250 % CPU) the window's chip shows the reading ("CPU 12% · 6.2 GB (PSS)", the sentence in its tooltip), ONE notice says "Google Chrome is using 6.2 GB (PSS) — Stop it from the Desktop panel if that is not what you expect" (r2: again only after three samples in a row under 90 % of the line, at most once an hour per session, and re-sent if no browser tab was connected to receive it), telemetry records it — and the app keeps running: no stop, no park, no refused launch. A browser row's profile is removed only by YOUR ending (Stop, a Scale ▸ relaunch, the browser's own exit); an idle-out keeps it. Only the headless OpenCode serve is still stopped for resources.
- **B-bfe6 (2.369.166) — A BROWSER AS AN APP (owner: "应用里面也可以加入一下浏览器"; design §7.7):** the launcher lists Chromium (chromium → chromium-browser → google-chrome, the first on PATH — "Google Chrome" when that is the one) and Firefox (firefox → firefox-esr) under a "Browsers" heading with one sentence, in the section and in each card's tooltip: *This is your own browser window (an app); the Agent browser is separate.* It is a HUMAN'S window on the xpra rung like every app — never an agent's (no automation flag ever reaches its argv) — with its OWN profile: `data/desktop-apps/<id>/profile`, created 0700, removed when the session ends (stop, the browser exiting, a failed start; boot finishes a removal a crash interrupted) unless "Keep the profile after it closes" was ticked; never the user's real ~/.config/chromium or ~/.mozilla and never an agent-browser profile (refused by name). An optional "Open URL" (http/https only — a bad one is refused by name in the dialog and again by the server) opens that page; the window's title bar shows the page title xpra reports. Downloads go to the user's real Downloads folder (HOME is not redirected); Chrome still creates its crashpad directory `~/.config/google-chrome/Crash Reports` and opens the user's shared NSS store `~/.local/share/pki/nssdb` whatever `--user-data-dir` says (measured) — neither holds a cookie, history or login. A SNAP browser (Ubuntu's firefox / chromium-browser) is offered only when this instance's data dir is inside $HOME outside a hidden folder (a snap cannot see /tmp or ~/.hidden) — otherwise it is dimmed with that reason. The idle timeout, the runaway guard and the single active viewer are unchanged. **r1:** a dimmed browser card says a SHORT translated reason ("Snap: cannot reach the data folder"; the full sentence is its tooltip) and the keep-profile checkbox sits left of its text. An AGENT cannot open a browser row: `vibespace-window open chromium` (or any `url` / `keepProfile`) is refused `browser_is_human` (403), and `list` does not offer browser rows — the agent's web road is `vibespace-browser`.
- **2.369.286 — THE KEYS ON STOCK KEYCODES + THE IME ROAD, MEASURED IN A REAL CHROME (lane xpra-ime-mac, inc-mvaddc4m-6m0t; w = End in a Google Docs window):** the keymap the xpra client publishes (`x11_keycodes`, which xpra programs) sits on the STOCK pc105 evdev keycodes, the ones a fresh display already has (w 25, a 38, Return 36; checked against scripts/fixtures/evdev-us-pke.txt). Every key is pressed on that keycode, because an app such as Chrome takes the key's `code` from the X keycode: the pre-lane browser-keyCode map put w on 87, which is code Numpad1, and Google Docs moved the caret. The IME road: compositionend / an `insertText` input ⇒ `typeText` ⇒ `ImeKeymap.plan`. A character on the map is pressed on its keycode (+ shift). Any other character gets a `U<hex>`/Latin-1 row on one of 13 lent keycodes (IME_KEYCODES: stock NoSymbol, no Chrome code), published in a `keyboard-config` BEFORE its press. A batch never moves a slot it presses. A table that moves one waits 150 ms after the last one, because Chrome reads an earlier press with a table sent right behind it. The rest of a long commit follows, keys pressed meanwhile wait behind it, and a reconnect republishes the rows in use. The client offers no `scroll` encoding: xpra 6.5.4's scroll encoder drops every frame it encodes, on both its encoder roads, so XPRA_SCROLL_ALL alone is not enough. This is an upstream bug; re-check when xpra moves (test-desktop-display keeps the row). A Mac viewer's ⌘+key is a tap, because a Mac browser never sends that key's keyup. Option+a stays å; ⌘ follows the primary-modifier rule (the next bullet: it is Ctrl on a Linux or Windows host).
- **THE PRIMARY MODIFIER FOLLOWS BOTH PLATFORMS (lane xpra-mac-modifiers; the owner 2026-10-16 「根据 host+client 两边自动判断」, the follow-up of inc-mvaddc4m-6m0t):** a Mac viewer's ⌘ is Ctrl in an app window on Linux or Windows, so every ⌘ chord works the Mac way (⌘+C / V / X / A / Z; ⌘+click is Ctrl+click). The MODIFIER moves — never a list of letters — and there is no setting or per-window toggle. ONE PURE table, src/lib/modifier-map.js (`PRIMARY_MODIFIER_ROWS`, viewer × host over mac / windows / linux / unknown): a Mac viewer on a Linux, Windows or unnamed host ⇒ meta → control; a Windows or Linux viewer on a Mac host ⇒ control → meta (for the future single-app macOS windows); the same family ⇒ identity. An unnamed host is Linux (every xpra display is); an unnamed viewer keeps its keys. Ctrl stays Ctrl, and Option stays Alt, never AltGr (Option+a still types å). `applyModifierMap` is the only transform; `modifierKeyOf` spells the modifier key itself (a ⌘ keydown goes out as Control_L). Two doors ask the table. (1) xpra-view.js, for keys and the pointer: the viewer comes from navigator.userAgentData.platform / navigator.platform / the user agent, the host from the app record's `platform` (no record names one today). (2) browser-takeover.js's macChord, for the agent-browser live view: its ⌘ rows are the table's, and its Mac editing idioms (⌘← = Home …) stay on top. The ⌘ tap keys off the viewer's own ⌘ (`viewerMeta`, before the map). A fresh press of a key clears that key's tap mark; before, the next plain press of a tapped key lost its keyup and X held the key. Gates: test-modifier-map (rows, doors, no second modifier table under src/), test-xpra-client §3d, test-desktop-xpra-window-open §8 (a real Chrome in the window: a Mac viewer's ⌘+a selects all; a Linux viewer's does not).
- **THE TYPED CHARACTER DECIDES ITS LEVEL — capitals and symbols in an app window, the Agent browser's included (lane browser-uppercase-keys; a fleet user on a Mac 2026-10-22: 「在 Chrome 浏览器里无法输入大写，导致输入密码的时候无法输入大写」 — his Agent browser was an xpra window, and his Caps Lock switches the input method):** the person's own machine has already turned Shift, Caps Lock and its keyboard layout into the character (the DOM `key`), so an xpra window types exactly that character. For a character on a two-level key of the published map (a letter, a digit, punctuation), `keyActionFor` sends `shift` exactly when the character sits on the shifted level (PURE `typedModifiers` in src/lib/xpra-proto.js — `ImeKeymap.plan`'s rule for a composed character), never the viewer's Shift/Caps Lock flags re-read by the US map's Linux rule. X's own Caps Lock is never engaged: no `lock` on any key packet and the Caps Lock key is not forwarded (a Mac sends its keydown when it turns on and its keyup only when it turns off). A chord (Ctrl / Alt / ⌘ / AltGr held) and a one-level key (Space, Enter, the keypad, F-keys) keep Shift as held, so Shift+Space and Shift+← still mean what they mean. Before (measured with xpra's own server keyboard code + a real Chrome): a Caps Lock flag over small letters typed a ⇒ A and Shift+b ⇒ b, a Mac's Caps Lock + Shift + a ⇒ a, a French layout's Shift+& ⇒ ! and & ⇒ 7. The live view (CDP) never had this: its key record carries the character itself. Gates: test-xpra-client §3e, test-live-input §3b, test-desktop-xpra-window-open §8, test-browser-live-input ③.
- **Round 3, Lane A1 (2.369.166) — A COPY YOU MAKE IN THE APP LANDS WITH NO CLICK, EVEN ON PLAIN HTTP (docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.1; the owner: "why does a copy inside the app need a click?"):** on an `http://<hostname>` page (not a secure context — no clipboard API) the xpra pane stamps the user's own trusted copy chord (Ctrl/⌘+C or +X forwarded to the app); the app's clipboard token that arrives within Chrome's 5 s transient-activation window (measured: an async `execCommand('copy')` works 0…4800 ms after the key, fails from 5200 ms) is written by `execCommand('copy')` from a hidden textarea — no click, a "Copied to your clipboard" toast. One chord allows at most one write; a copy nobody made on this page (an agent, a timer, another client), a late one, one after a non-copy key or on a view-only pane keeps the "Copied in the app — click to copy" chip; the browser refusing falls to the chip. The FIRST chip a device needs on plain http also shows a one-time hint "Enable HTTPS for seamless copy" + "How to enable HTTPS" (docs/getting-started.md: Chrome flag / `tailscale serve` / Caddy — no TLS in the product), remembered in localStorage `vibespace.desktopCopyHintShown`, dismissable. Secure pages unchanged (the API). Measured on the real rung with GNOME Calculator: the token ~30 ms after Ctrl+C, the clipboard reads the value with zero clicks. A mouse copy (Edit ▸ Copy) and the RFB rung keep the chip. **A r1:** the keyboard stays in the app after such a copy (the hidden textarea used to take the focus and drop it to the page, so every key after a copy vanished) — measured: the next digit reached the calculator with no click.

- **Lane exit-close-cadence (2.369.271) — THE EXIT IS THE VERDICT (B-8778):** an app's own exit is committed (saved + broadcast) the moment the keeper's window census answers (≤ EXIT_CENSUS_MS), BEFORE the session teardown, which commits again. Before, the broadcast waited for the teardown, and an env with no session bus made every GLib app's close wait ~3 s: GLib autolaunches a bus (`dbus-launch --autolaunch`, a member of the app's session) whose babysitter dies 3 s after a SIGTERM. - **r2 (2026-09-14) — what the round-1 verifier found on this section's own claims, each reproduced on the real keeper and closed with a control:** a picture server whose binary vanished after the probe CRASHED THE SERVER (an unhandled spawn `error`) and left its X alive and unrecorded — every spawn is awaited, every binary re-statted at spawn, every part committed the moment its pid exists; the recorded picture PORT was an assumption (x11vnc keeps the number on `[::1]` when the IPv4 bind loses a race, so a stranger speaking RFB on 127.0.0.1 became the window's picture) — the record turns `ready` only when the 127.0.0.1 LISTEN socket is held by our picture server's session; Stop signalled three pids and left the application's children (a wrapper's `sleep`, a `yes` at 100 % CPU) — every leader is a detached SESSION stamped `VIBESPACE_DESKTOP_APP=<id>`, stop empties the session (group + every member, the env marker identifies a straggler once its leader is gone), verified; the runaway guard sampled one pid and was blind to a launcher whose work is in a child — it samples the whole session set (`live.pids` says how many); a desktop-singleton session was reaped at every boot because vnc.js's `running` is its LAST status() answer (false at boot) — the keeper asks `refresh()` before every verdict; the bring-up was a string switch on the rung — it is a TABLE LOOKUP (`recipes[via]` → `desktop-display.RECIPES[name]`), proven with a fourth rung driven end to end with the keeper untouched; and the bridge counted every browser→server frame as INPUT while noVNC sends a FramebufferUpdateRequest on every repaint, so the DA3 idle stop never fired for a session any tab showed — only KeyEvent / PointerEvent / ClientCutText / the QEMU key event count now (a protocol the sieve cannot follow falls back to today's rule, the direction that never reaps a live user). The suite's own exit sweep used to SIGKILL by bare pid — including its own process — printing ALL PASS then exiting 137; it now sweeps by pid+starttime and the fixture is a throwaway `sleep`. test-desktop-app-keeper 115 / test-desktop-display 63 / test-desktop-apps 98.
- **r3 (2026-09-14) — the round-2 verifier's four, each reproduced on the real keeper and closed with a control:** a Stop that lands while the window still says `launching` (or `POST …/stop` in that window) used to answer `exited` and leave a live Xvfb + a passwordless x11vnc under that record for ever — now `stop()` marks the record stopping, tears down, WAITS for the bring-up it cancelled (bounded by the launch's own deadline), tears down again and only then writes the verdict, a part spawned after the record DIED is killed the moment it is known, the bring-up's `finally` reaps on every exit, and the next boot runs ONE marker census (`VIBESPACE_DESKTOP_APP=<id>` over this store's ids) so even a SIGKILL of the server mid-stop leaves nothing; the runaway guard now counts the work of children the app has already REAPED (`cutime+cstime`), so `yes | head` churn at 110 % trips in ~4 s where round 2 read 0 % — with the honest boundary that a child killed with its whole process GROUP (coreutils `timeout`) is reaped by init and is invisible to any /proc reader over the session (a per-session cgroup odometer is the follow-up); the bridge's RFB table is DERIVED from the shipped noVNC (EnableContinuousUpdates is 10 bytes, not 4 — on a TigerVNC server the idle stop could have reaped a session being typed in; PointerEvent is 6 or 7 by its marker bit; ClientFence is variable); and an identity nobody recorded is NOT proven — a record with null starttimes never makes boot adoption signal a recycled pid (three strangers used to be SIGKILLed by group), the safe direction being 'left alone', while our own stragglers are still found by the marker. BOUNDARY: on a machine with no readable /proc a session cannot be proven ours after a restart and is recorded as ended and LEFT RUNNING.
- **r4 (2026-09-14) — the round-3 verifier's two, each reproduced on the real keeper and closed with a control that fails alone:** a Stop that lands BETWEEN two parts of the bring-up (X and the picture server already recorded, the app's spawn in flight) answered `exited` with the app recorded under it and left `/bin/sleep 3600` alive under that record — r3 settled on the in-flight bring-up only if it was still in the map AFTER the first teardown, and that teardown's own SIGTERM waits (≥ 100 ms per part) were long enough for the bring-up to finish and be forgotten; `stop()` now captures the bring-up BEFORE it signals anything and always settles on that. And the session model counted a session by its session id, so a member that `setsid()`s itself — a daemonising launcher, `nohup … & disown` typed into the app's own terminal — survived Stop AND the app-exit path under `exited`/`failed`, and the runaway guard could not see it either (a setsid'd `yes` read 0 % for 12 s); every teardown now ends with the marker census (`VIBESPACE_DESKTOP_APP=<id>`, the identity those processes INHERITED — the reader boot already used), so `exited`/`failed` mean "nothing of this session's runs" on every terminal path, and the guard's sample unions the same census (ONE /proc environ walk ≈ 50 ms per teardown and per sample, measured over ~3,850 pids). Honest boundary: on a machine with no readable /proc the census is empty and r3's "recorded as ended, left running" stands — the header now says so instead of "no orphans, ever". test-desktop-app-keeper 155.
- **Measured on the dev box (Ubuntu 25.10, Wayland session, x11vnc 0.9.17):** a session = 3 processes / 87 MB RSS with xmessage (Xvfb 1024x768 67 + x11vnc 15 + app 5), 279 MB with gnome-calculator (app 195); ready in ~400 ms; Xvfb answers `-displayfd` in ~40 ms; x11vnc answers a silent RFB client after ~320 ms; x11vnc EXITS under `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` (stripped for every process on a private display); a SIGKILLed server is a CLEAN close to noVNC (the reconnect ladder keys on "still wanted"); the layout autosave fires only after a real pointerdown and not inside the 5 s post-load window (pre-existing, every window type).
- **Not in P8-1 / not verifiable here:** xpra end to end (P8-2); remote machines (every route + fact refuses a non-local `host` by name — the daemon op is P8-2+); `xterm` and the real `xpra` could not be installed on this box (apt locked by a running release-upgrader), so the exit measurements used xmessage / gnome-calculator, a fake `xpra` on PATH for the probe leg and a fake `Xvnc` shim for the fleet spelling of `vnc-display` (the real TigerVNC binary is absent here too) — the fleet image gets `xterm` + `xpra` (package only, nothing enabled); Wayland-only apps cannot run on a private X display (a registry row may say `needsWayland`, refused honestly); the 200 ms / 1 Mbps usability of `vnc-display` is inferred from §4.7's ranking, not measured.

**Desktop v2 P0 — the Desktop picker, one display at a time, the stats strip (lane desktop-v2-entry, design q-030, 2026-10-12; owner: "应该允许选择显示器…不放在应用里，而是作为桌面的子功能…桌面不再直接打开一个本地桌面，而是选择本地或者remote"):**
- **The Desktop button (toolbar `desktop.open`, the phone's Desktop row) opens a POPOVER, not the local desktop** (src/lib/desktop-picker.js; rows by the PURE `pickerRows` in src/desktop-screens.js): 最近 (this browser's last choice — host + display, first, focused, Enter opens it; a reload keeps it), 本机 (the "VibeSpace 虚拟桌面" — the persisted singleton window as before; a Wayland seat (`GET /api/vnc/status` `seat`) says why this host's own screen is not offered — D4: no physical-desktop rung in P0), 远程 (each paired Windows / macOS machine: 就绪 / 先设置 / 离线 + the displays its window mapped last). A 先设置 row opens the machine's dialog (its setup words). The local desktop's replay (`openSpec {action:'openDesktop'}`) still opens it directly.
- **The Apps dialog keeps app launching:** the machine dialog's "Open its desktop" became "打开它的桌面 → 桌面" — it still shows the window at once (inc-mv51w0ow-crw3) and the Desktop picker remembers it as the recent choice. A machine's window stays NOT persisted with the sign-in asked each time (design 014 D1 unchanged); people only (`human_only` on the routes and the bridge).
- **One display of a multi-screen machine:** the window's strip `[机器 ▾] [1 · 2 · 全部] [⤢ 全屏] [已连接 · N ms · F fps]` replaces the line that said what the window is (its words are the status chip's title). The displays = the PURE `screenMap({fb, screens, rfb})` over two sources: the machine's OWN table (device op `display-facts`: a Mac's JXA `NSScreen.screens` in points + backingScaleFactor, Windows' PowerShell `Screen.AllScreens` in DPI-aware pixels) and the server's ExtendedDesktopSize (-308) rects. The union's bbox ≠ the framebuffer ⇒ `unknown` = the whole screen only (never a guess; the chip's title says so); a -308 table of ≥ 2 screens that contradicts the OS table ⇒ the framebuffer's own rects win. A choice = a noVNC viewport crop, scaled to the window, NEVER a reconnect (one RFB session through every switch); 全部 = the whole framebuffer; pointer coordinates carry the viewport offset (Display.absX/absY). Remembered per browser as (host, display key).
- **The noVNC 1.7 facts, measured in the bundle first:** clip and scale ARE exclusive (`_updateClip`: "Disable viewport clipping if we are scaling"); `_handleExtendedDesktopSize` keeps only screen 0's id/flags and skips every rect; `new RFB(target, channel)` takes a WebSocket object. Hence a ≤ 20-line BUILD-TIME patch (src/novnc-patch.js via scripts/build-novnc.mjs — `vsCrop` clips + scales together; the -308 payload handed to the page as a `vsscreens` event); a drifted anchor fails the build; the unpatched mutant reds the crop leg.
- **The stats strip (§4, P0):** the window hands noVNC its OWN WebSocket and reads each send's message types (PURE `clientMessages`): the update round trip = a FramebufferUpdateRequest out → the next one (noVNC sends it the moment the update it asked for is drawn; a gap ≥ 2 s is an idle screen, not latency), fps = requests in the last second (PURE `updateTimer`); browser ⇄ hub = the page's own timing of `GET /api/desktop/machine-desktop/link` minus the hub's time; hub ⇄ machine = one mux PING. A server answering 200 ms late reads as a ~200 ms round trip at ~5 fps (test-desktop-v2-chrome ⑥). NOT in P0: the quality ladder, the keyboard lock (no ⌨ button yet), paste-to-remote, WebRTC, "frame it once" for an unknown layout, TightVNC's share-one-monitor op.

**The machine rows answer at once (lane desktop-picker-instant, 2.369.313; owner 2026-10-19 「这个界面的加载时间怎么越来越长了」):**
- The Desktop picker and the Apps dialog's 「运行于」 draw EVERY machine the moment they open, from what the hub last knew (memory + data/desktop-machines.json — a restart paints too): each row with its last state, a machine never probed 「检查中…」 (that row only, not pressable). The probes run behind it — one per machine, a second asker joins it — and each landed row is broadcast (`desktop-machines-updated`): the open picker / dialog patches THAT row in place (the focused row keeps the focus). A row's title says 「上次检查 N 秒前 · 探测 M ms」. Check again (the machine dialog) probes that machine now and waits.
- An open within 10 s of the last probe asks no machine; a link that dropped since is asked at once; the daemon's hello re-probes its machine. Every probe is one journal line `[desktop] <host> probed in <ms> ms → <code> (<why>)`, and one over 2 s a warn line naming the slow step (dial / forward / greeting).
- The machine dialog's installed apps: the list the machine gave last shows at once while it lists again (`listing`), the new list replaces it when it lands (announced `desktop-installed-updated`); Check again still waits for the machine.

**Desktop v2 P1 — fluid while you work, sharp when still; paste; full-screen shortcuts (lane desktop-v2-latency, design q-030 §4 + §6 P1, 2026-10-12):**
- **The quality ladder** (PURE `qualityPlan` in src/desktop-quality.js, applied by vnc-view `ladder`): a key, a press / drag / wheel (a bare hover is not) or a moving picture (≥ 2 answers to incremental requests carrying ≥ 24 KB in the last second — a blinking caret or a clock is not) ⇒ 流畅 quality 3 / compression 1; still ≥ 500 ms ⇒ 清晰 8 / 2 AND one non-incremental request for the shown display (a still screen sends nothing, so what was drawn at 3 would stay blurry). A slow link (the median rate of the last 5 updates ≥ 32 KB, timed from their first byte, < 2000 kbps; normal again at ≥ 3000) steps one rung down: 均衡 6 / 4 still, 省流 1 / 6 moving, and the strip shows 慢链路. A new rung = ONE SetEncodings (the compression rides the quality write; the first rung rides noVNC's own first SetEncodings).
- **Paste to the machine:** Ctrl/⌘+V in the picture is kept from noVNC (its keydown handler cancels the key, and a cancelled key raises no `paste` — measured in Chrome 154); the browser's paste lands on the focused canvas, its text/plain goes as ClientCutText (CRLF → LF), THEN the V (Ctrl is still down there). Nothing to paste ⇒ the V alone. The 粘贴 button stays (phones). No guard, no log.
