- **Full screen + shortcuts:** ⤢ 全屏 = the window's content (strip + picture); on a secure page `navigator.keyboard.lock()` (all keys) while ⌨ 捕获快捷键 is on (its title: Esc / Alt+Tab / Windows key / ⌘ go to the machine; hold Esc 2 s to leave); off / leaving ⇒ unlock. On http the ⌨ press says VibeSpace must be opened at an https address and nothing locks.
- **The comparison row:** the status chip opens 本次 (browser ⇄ hub · hub ⇄ machine · update round trip · fps · kbps) + the recorded reference of lane picture-path-nodelay (a key press 42.0 → 0.70 ms through the same hops) — words, never a live A/B.
- **D4 (the hub's own Wayland seat):** probed as a report only — /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/desktop-v2-latency/d4-probe.md: xpra 6.5.4's pipewire / portal shadow backends cannot load here (`xpra.codecs.gstreamer.capture` imports `CSC_ALIAS`, absent from xpra-common's `xpra.codecs.constants`); no `shadow` rung.

**Desktop v2 — the machine's pointer at the picture's scale; the HDR chip (lane win-desktop-cursor-hdr, 2026-10-13; owner on the paired Windows desktop: "鼠标如此巨大，而且 HDR 特别白"):**
- **Cursor scaling:** noVNC 1.7 draws the Cursor pseudo-encoding as a CSS `cursor: url()` at the image's own pixel size while the framebuffer is scaled to fit — a 96 px pointer (Windows at 200 % DPI, a Retina Mac) over a screen shown at half was twice too big. The build-time patch hands every pointer image and `Display.scale` to `rfb.vsCursor` and redraws when the scale changes; the page answers PURE `cursorPlan` (css px = fb px × scale, floor 16 px, cap 64 css px, the hotspot scaled; scale 1 untouched) drawn by `scaleRgba` (alpha-weighted box average). The browser already draws a CSS cursor at the device-pixel ratio, so DPR needs no extra factor (measured at DPR 2: 96 px → 48 css px at scale 0.5).
- **Server-rendered fallback:** an image wider than 128 px (Chrome refuses a custom cursor that big) ⇒ `rfb.vsServerCursor = true` and one SetEncodings without the Cursor / VMware-cursor pseudo-encodings on the same session (the machine paints its pointer INTO the picture, which scales with it); a 3 px dot marks the local pointer; every reconnect of that window leaves them out. "The browser refused the size" is not detectable from the page (the computed style keeps the url) — only the 128 px rule decides.
- **The stats row:** the status chip's title and its comparison row say the path — 指针：在这里随画面缩放绘制，为原 N px 的 P% · 按原尺寸 · 由机器画进画面.
- **HDR:** `display-facts` on Windows adds `hdr` per screen (1 / 0 / -1 unknown → true / false / null) from the DisplayConfig API (`QueryDisplayConfig(QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS)` → per path the source GDI name (type 1) + the target's advanced-colour info (type 9): HDR = advancedColorEnabled and not wideColorEnforced). Compiled under portable pwsh 7.4.6 on Linux (user32 absent ⇒ caught ⇒ unknown); NOT measured on a real HDR Windows machine (no owner machines from a lane). The switch bar shows 「HDR 已开 · 画面会偏白」 (title: the remedy — Windows 设置 › 显示 关闭"使用 HDR" / Win+Alt+B) when the shown display, or with 全部 any display, measured `hdr: true`; false / unknown / a Mac say nothing. TightVNC cannot tone-map and we do not transcode — the chip is the whole fix.
- **Gates:** test-screen-map §5 (fast: the plan's truth table, scaleRgba, the hdr field through the parser and the map, hdrShown, the bundle pin); test-desktop-v2-chrome ⑫–⑭ + ⑪ (heavy: the stub's 96 px pointer at scale 0.5 / DPR 2 ⇒ a 48×48 CSS image with hotspot 12 6, 36 px at 0.375, 256 px ⇒ SetEncodings without -239 on the same session and on the reconnect, the HDR chip on 2 / 全部 and not on 1; RED: the unpatched noVNC keeps 96 px).

### Pairing that says WHERE and WHY · exit access with "who can use it" (lane-pairing, B-7007, 2026-09-28)

The owner's MacBook, 2026-09-27: the pairing dialog offered one address the Mac could not reach, every re-open of the row's Re-pair minted a new token, the daemon kept dialing with a stale one, the server said "token mismatch" in its journal and the row said "offline". The fix, as shipped behaviour:

- **The pairing dialog offers an ADDRESS CHOICE.** "Pair a device" (Remote tab) lists every address this server can name for itself — the address the browser is using now (first, chosen), the relay when one is published (or "Publish through the relay and use that address" when the frp relay is configured but not published), this machine's Tailscale / LAN / public IPs, its hostname, a global IPv6 — each with what the server knows about who can reach it ("reachable from your tailnet", "works where this name resolves (same LAN / your DNS)"…), plain-http rows carry a tooltip (fine inside a trusted network; TLS lives in the relay / a reverse proxy), and **Custom…** with a live verdict (the resulting dial URL, or "Just the address — no path or query" in place). BOTH URLs of the command (the installer + bundle, and the dial URL) are the chosen address — never a guess. The dialog never probes: the device does, before it installs anything. The ssh machine's "Upgrade to dial-out" dialog uses the same list.
- **A token is minted ONLY by a button.** "Create pairing" (a new device) and "Generate a new command" (an existing one) are the only mints; the row's pairing icon opens the pairing SHEET, whose head says the device's dial state first (so the user sees whether the old command ever worked), and nothing rotates until Generate — which then says "A new command for "Mac" — the one you generated before stops working now". A device dialed in right now is updated in place as before. No plaintext token is stored (only its hash).
- **The row says why a device is not connected.** One state, read by the machine row's sub-line, dot, badge and tooltip, the Machines card's second line and dot, and the pairing sheet's head: *Connected since 09:41* (+ "— before that 3 attempts failed (token mismatch)"), *Connected, but the device refuses this server's key* (the device holds another command's host token — badge KEY REFUSED), *Last dial: refused (token mismatch) at 23:12 — the device holds an older command; generate a new one* (badge REFUSED; the tooltip names the address it came from), *Offline since … — no dial attempt has reached this server since (is the device on, and on a network that reaches <host>?)*, *Never connected — the command generated at … has not reached this server*, *Offline — nothing recorded yet*. A refusal of a token a Generate already retired is not shown as news. The Machines card's **Dial history…** asks the device itself (the `dial-status` op) for its last 20 dial outcomes ("09:41 · connected", "09:40 · failed (DNS)"); an agent too old to know the op says "Update the agent on this machine first".
- **The device records why.** Every dial outcome lands in the device's `state/dial-status.json` and ONE log line naming the class ("dial-out failed — dns: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND …", "dial-out refused — token-mismatch: <the server's sentence>", "dial-out connected: … (after 12 failed attempts)"); a refused dial gets the server's reason (a 401 with a named header + sentence) and a black-holed address times out in 15 s instead of hanging.
- **The installer checks before it writes.** The command's installer rejects a non-ws:// / wss:// dial address before fetching anything, then runs the daemon's own dial once (`--dial-check`) and stops with the reason and the remedy — "✗ nothing was installed — the device cannot dial mac.lan:3456: dial-check failed — dns: …" / "tls" (wss:// to a plain port — the owner's typo) / "nothing answers" / "not a VibeSpace dial endpoint" / "refused (token mismatch) — generate a new command" — BEFORE the host token, dial.json or the launchd / systemd unit exist. `--no-check` skips it. The check registers nothing on the server.
- **Long device roots work on macOS.** When `<root>/state/agentd.sock` would exceed the platform's unix-socket limit (104 bytes on macOS — the owner's frp-named root made it 106), the daemon listens on a short per-user path (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/vibespace/`, the per-user `$TMPDIR/vibespace/`, or `/tmp/vs-dev-<uid>/`, owner-checked) and writes where to the root's `state/socket-path`; nothing fits ⇒ the log says every candidate's size.
- **Exit access has a WHO.** A machine's exit icon (Remote tab row; the Machines card's **Who can use it…**) opens "Who can use Macbook?" with TWO lists — **Borrow its network** (`vibespace-exit use / url`: the command runs here, only its traffic leaves from the machine) and **Run commands on it** (`vibespace-exit run`: a shell command ON the machine, as you, up to 30 s) — each **Nobody** / **All my conversations** / **Only these** (the principal picker: conversations and Task Groups; a Task Group means every conversation in it, now or later), and **Ask me each time** for commands. The dialog reads the server's lists fresh and saves them with the version it read (a change from another window in between ⇒ "The lists changed while this dialog was open … nothing was saved", redrawn as they are). The row says `Exit: network — everyone · commands — 2 picked (ask me)` and `Last run: ping -c1 … — ops, 3 min ago, exit 0`.
- **Ask me each time** puts "Allow "ops" to run a command on Macbook?" in For you (origin Machines) with the whole command and **Allow / Deny** right on the row (the popup, the For-you window, the phone) — nothing runs until you answer; after 60 s it is refused. An agent cannot answer it.
- **Every run is recorded and said.** The calling chat gets a card "VibeSpace · Machines · Macbook — ran `ping -c1 10.0.0.5` on Macbook — exit 0 · 1.2 s" (or "timed out after 30 s", "you denied it", "no answer in 60 s", "this conversation may not run commands there", "Macbook is offline"; never billed, never in the transcript); every use / run / ask / refusal is a line in `data/exit-audit.jsonl`; the row shows the last run. A command already running when its access is removed finishes (there is no cancel) and says so.
- **Files between machines (lane exit-transfer, 2.369.204; the owner: 「agent有能力在远程机器上生成一个大文件并pull回本地吗？还是只能通过命令行一点一点读？」).** `vibespace-exit pull <machine> <remote> [local]` / `push <local> <machine> <remote>` copy ONE regular file under the `run` grant (its lists and "ask me each time" — the For-you row shows `pull <remote> → <local>`), through the machine agent's own file ops (no shell — Windows the same; no 30 s cap): 8 MiB windows, each compared with the agent's sha256 (an older agent: "size verified"), the file landing as the pull's own `<path>.<8 hex>.vs-part` and renamed only when whole (fix r1: its folder judged again when written and renamed — moved or replaced ⇒ refused, never re-made; one pull per local file, `target_busy`); any failure keeps nothing. Bounded by **Settings → Integration → Largest file an agent may pull or push** (default 1 GB). A pull lands only under the conversation's project, /tmp or ~/Downloads (the browser CLI's write fence); an existing file only with `--overwrite`. Each transfer is one card ("pulled `C:\…\nomad.bin` from WIN-DESK1 → `~/proj/nomad.bin` — 812.0 MiB · sha256 ab12… verified · 41.0 s") and one row in the machine's **Commands** list. Push needs the machine's agent 2.369.204+.
- **The agent's side:** `vibespace-exit list` shows only the machines its conversation may use (`network: yes · commands: ask`); a refusal names the grant it lacks and that the user can change it under "Who can use it" — never another conversation; Background Work jobs can never use an exit. Existing machines keep exactly what they had: "Allow as exit" on ⇒ everyone for both; off ⇒ nobody (migration `2026-09-exit-access-lists`, the old values archived).

- **One card for any install (design 009, 2.369.203)**: an agent proposes a package name, a vendor's download address (`vibespace-app install --from`) or a file (`--file`); VibeSpace downloads and checks it as the user, names the app by its own desktop file (localized zh / ja names, its icon) and files ONE card. A .deb installs through the slot (and comes back after a rebuild); an AppImage is unpacked by VibeSpace's own reader into `~/.vibespace/apps/appimage/<id>/` (never run to install) and gets a row in Apps; Remove… works for every kind. Declined / expired / done ⇒ the download is deleted.

### Channels window: editors size to their text (lane channel-edit-autosize, 2026-10-12 — a fleet user, inc-mv4toyhw-t7ym)
Editing an agent's draft (the proposal card's Edit…, inline in a conversation window and in the Outbox) opens a box already sized to the text — at least 4 rows, at most ~60 % of the window (then it scrolls inside) — and it grows as you type without the list or the caret jumping; a long single line counts by its wrapped width. The composer holding a draft or a quote, the agent-group composer and the thread reply box follow the same rule from their 2-row look. A drag on the box's resize handle wins until the editor is opened again; on a phone the window is the sheet, so the box stays within the screen. One helper (`autosizeEditor`, src/lib/channel-editor-size.js). Gates: test-channel-blocks ㉑ (fast), test-channel-edit-autosize (heavy chrome + PNGs).

### The Outbox at a glance — one row per proposal (B-f467, lane channels-polish, 2026-10-03)

userW (2026-10-03, his screenshot of the All view: a Gmail compose awaiting approval + a sent Lark card): the cards have "no visual centre of gravity — some things I want to see at a glance"; he pointed at the channel list. The Outbox window now reads like that list:

- **One row per proposal** in the channel list's grammar: the conversation's avatar wearing its account badge (B-5fe1), **who receives it and where** in one line (a new mail: the recipients, then the subject; a reply: the recipients the adapter resolved, then the conversation's name — a Lark single chat is the person's name, never `oc_…`), the account in small text when a vendor holds ≥ 2, the time, then the state pill and the first line of the text. An awaiting proposal carries one button, **Approve…**.
- **The full card opens under its row** on a click or Enter (the row keeps its focus; Enter again closes it) — the same card as before (envelope, the whole text, why / policy / identity / expiry, the warning, Approve ▾ / Reject ▾ / Edit…): one renderer, two densities. **Approve…** opens the card and puts the keyboard on its Approve, so the decision is still taken where the whole text, the identity warning and the delivery choice are drawn — the approval rules did not change. A card that just opened is inert for a moment like any card that just appeared.
- The conversation window's inline section keeps its cards; the Awaiting | All segment and the state heads are unchanged.
- Gates: test-channel-outbox B-f467 (7 legs over the real module in the minimal DOM + a pre-fix control), test-channels-i18n ④ (the rows and an opened card in zh / ja / en at 1200 px and on the 375 px phone: nothing overlaps, nothing is cut, phone targets ≥ 36 px), test-takeover-keyboard (the row is a classified control).

### The Outbox window scrolls; its filter means what it says; an API row is a card (lane outbox-window-scroll-filter, 2026-10-22)

The owner, 2026-10-22, the Outbox window at 2.369.342: «1 条待我审批 这一条在哪呢？» and «这个窗口里不能滚动，只能拉长窗口才能看到下面那个要发的消息». The API calls' section sat beside the list and squeezed it — and the one waiting message in it — out of the window; under 「待审批」 it listed 20 calls that had already run or been refused.

- **One scroll container:** the window is its toolbar over ONE list; every section (the message proposals, the API calls) lives inside it and none of them shrinks, so a long list scrolls and never grows the window, and the waiting item is reachable at any window height.
- **One census (src/outbox-census.js, PURE):** the head («1 条等你审批 · 共 177 条提案») and each section's head («消息提案 · 1 个等你决定 · 共 157 个», «API 调用 · 0 个等你决定 · 共 20 个») are one count. 「待审批」 shows ONLY what waits for you, in every section, and the section holding it first; a section with nothing waiting is folded to its head line with 「在「全部」里看」 (it switches to 「全部」 at that section). 「全部」 shows everything newest first, each row with its outcome (no per-state heads any more). The first view is 「待审批」 while anything waits, else 「全部」.
- **The API row is a card:** «actor · action» — the object only by its NAME («大开发 · 删除消息», «杂活 · 上传文件到文件夹»), the policy a chip («删除 · 总是询问»), the outcome a short status («已执行» / «已拒绝» / «已过期» / «已撤回» / «未执行»; a waiting one «等你决定 · N 小时后过期»). Identical consecutive rows are ONE row «×3»; a waiting call is always its own row, its card open. A row opens the card of each of its calls; the object's whole id («对象 id：…»), the answer («返回：HTTP 200 · 36 B»), the URL, headers and body are in its ONE collapsed 技术细节 fold.
- Gates: test-channel-outbox §OW (fast — the census over the owner's shape, the view, the row words, the real window over a minimal DOM, a base-shaped RED control), test-channel-outbox-window (heavy chrome — 600 px, the waiting row first and hit, 「全部」 scrolls, 260 px, the fold; RED control = the base's shape), test-card-grammar.

### Search everything (lane global-search, 2026-10-05 — docs/design-global-search.md)

⚙ Tools ▸ Search everything… (Ctrl+Shift+F, or the last row of the Ctrl+K palette) finds any conversation by what was said in it and any file an agent wrote by its contents. Results are grouped by conversation (3 shown, "+N more"); Enter / a click opens the conversation at that message (a stopped one opens read-only) or the file. Chinese / Japanese / Korean words of two characters work (CJK bigrams); a trailing English word is a prefix. The index is a rebuildable SQLite file on local disk (never data/), built in the background a minute after boot; the System panel shows its size and a Rebuild button. Not indexed: thinking, tool calls and their outputs; files other than text / html / docx.

### Agent browser — the tab list by window (lane browser-tabs-by-window, rel239, owner 2026-10-08 "好做吧")
- The live view's tab row and its Tabs pane group the browser's tabs BY WINDOW: this view's window first ("This window"), then each other holder's window named by its holder ("企业助手's window" — the conversation's live name, never a window number or a session id), then tabs whose window is unread or held by nobody ("Elsewhere in this browser"). The owner's case: profile hanabi-work had two leases, each in a window of its own (lane browser-windows), and the flat "Tabs (4)" list read as two agents in one window.
- ONE fact for both surfaces: the keeper's `tabOwnersFor` reads `Browser.getWindowForTarget` per page (kept per browser run + target, ≤ 24 new reads per record, unread = null, never 0) and the holders' windows (a lease's stamped `windowId` in this browser run; the user's = the window of his own tab); the bridge's `tab-owners` record carries `windows` + `leases`; PURE `tabGroups` (src/browser-tabs.js) orders and names them.
- A window's spare `about:blank` (the blank a session's daemon opens at its first command — measured: 3 blanks, 2 folded on the real 0.38.1 in test-browser-share ③c) folds into its group's head as "+1 blank"; the Tabs button counts "Tabs (2 · +2 blank)". Never folded: a window's only tab, the tab on show, a blank whose window is unread. The pane is keyed now (no `innerHTML = ''`). Gates: test-browser-tabs (BY WINDOW legs + flat / window-id controls), test-browser-resume-ui ⑧ (zh), test-browser-share ③c.

### System window — where the server's memory goes (2.369.241, lane server-memory-census, B-9428 step (c))
The System window (rail panel or window) shows **Server memory** under the Memory bar, for THIS instance only: Main heap · Workers (N) · External / ArrayBuffers · Native / other · RSS, with "used" where V8 says it; the Workers row folds open to one row per worker isolate (`safe-fs#0…3`, `transcript#0/1`, `fs-canary#0`, `search-index`, `usage-index`; one that did not answer in 2 s says "no answer" and is counted, never 0). The note under it: the parts add up to the anonymous resident memory (smaps_rollup); RSS also counts the program and mapped files. Heap parts are the RESIDENT heap (v8 total_physical_size). Sampled every 60 s by src/server/memory-sampler.js — async, a census and never a guard. Telemetry: srv-worker-heap-mb / srv-external-mb / srv-native-mb every 5 min + ONE srv-mem-census event every 10 min (≈ 912 B per 10 min); the journal says `[memory] boot census: …` once per start. A new `new Worker(` in the server process must `trackWorker` it and its script must call `answerMemory` first in its message loop (scripts/test-memory-census.mjs §5).

### Agent browser — the log pipe (2.369.250, lane browser-stderr-pipe, userW inc-mv2qf3xs-7g87)
The browser driver VibeSpace pinned (agent-browser 0.38.1) started Chrome with its error output on a pipe it never read; after about 64 KB (hours idle, seconds when a page logs a lot) Chrome blocked on its next write and the whole browser stopped answering. The pin is now 0.38.2, which reads that output for the browser's whole life. On top of that, every browser the keeper starts runs with Chrome's logging off (`--disable-logging --log-level=3`, unless the user's own browser args set logging), and a browser that still hangs that way (one whose daemon still runs 0.38.1 from before the update) is named: its Browser panel row says the log pipe filled and nothing read it, the journal carries `stderr-pipe-full`, and Restart starts it on 0.38.2.

### Agent browser — it comes back after a server update (lane browser-daemon-survives-update, B-1574)
A page that answers nothing is hung whatever its helper says: an agent's `vibespace-browser restart` asks every page of the browser at that moment (each gets 5 s) and restarts when none answers — or when every page answers but the agent's own commands keep timing out through the browser driver; otherwise it refuses `browser_answering`, naming the pages that answered and those that did not (close those with `tab close`); a page dialog is answered, never restarted away. A browser helper (the agent-browser daemon) that nothing keeps any more — after a server restart, say — is ended a minute after its browser ended or stopped answering, even while a conversation still leases it; its row and `vibespace-browser status` say so, and the next command starts a fresh one. A server restart (an Update included) judges every browser it finds running: the ones whose page answers are taken back as they are, the rest are ended with their Chrome.

**Apps an agent installs are registered (2.369.254, lane app-register-model; owner 2026-10-11, JASP):** two home kinds — `flatpak` (the door: `vibespace-app add --kind flatpak <appId>` installs as the user, held by the CLI card, then records; row from the exported desktop file; remove `flatpak uninstall --user -y`; `search --kind flatpak`) and `registered` (a DECLARATION: 1–8 argv launch variants, remove / reinstall recipes, icon; `vibespace-app register`). THE WITNESS-MATCH RULE: a declaration whose default launch the machine already lists outside VibeSpace (the same flatpak appId, or the same absolute Exec + args as a witnessed desktop entry) makes nothing new launchable ⇒ recorded directly; any other declaration is ONE For-you click. The owner's Adopt turns a witnessed row into a registered app; the launcher launches a `variant`; a gone program shows its reinstall as a user-click rung. **Tightened in 2.369.255 (rel254 verify F2):** recorded directly only when EVERY variant is exactly the witnessed argv, no env / cwd, recipes absent or the witness's own; anything else is one For-you click — "nothing new becomes launchable without your click" now holds. A system .desktop dpkg owns nothing of is LISTED (F6). The `[path]` shown beside a bare-exec line (a card's Details, the For-you item) is ADVISORY — what the name resolved to when it was declared; launch re-resolves the bare name on the server's PATH every time, the same exposure as every bare-exec row (int255, verify r2 R3). The owner's Forget (nothing runs) is only for a kind whose row `forgets` — registered / Flatpak, whose program the witness lists again; an AppImage / uv / npm row is refused `not_forgettable` by name, its Remove… takes its files (int255, verify r2 N1).

### Desktop apps — the private session's secret service (2.369.263, lane app-display-secrets, B-4a59 piece 4)

An app on its own private bus (the portal companion) also gets **org.freedesktop.secrets**: the bus activates src/secret-service.py (python3 + GDBus) — one default collection, never locked, never a prompt (`Unlock` answers the objects, Prompt paths are `/`), `plain` sessions only (libsecret and Chrome ask dh-ietf1024-sha256-aes128-cbc-pkcs7 first and fall back on NotSupported — measured). Measured without it: libsecret ServiceUnknown in ≤ 3 ms, Chrome's basic store (`v10`); with it Chrome keeps its OSCrypt key there (`v11`) and a cookie decrypts after a restart. Items are ONE sealed file `<app dir>/portal/secrets.json` (secret-box's aes-256-gcm under an HKDF per-display key off `data/.app-secrets-key`). THE KEY REACHES THE SERVICE AND NOBODY ELSE (lane display-secret-fd, 2026-10-13, B-6c6d): a 0600 one-shot file `<app dir>/portal/run/secrets.key` named on the service's Exec line, which the service reads and UNLINKS before it owns its bus name (no key file ⇒ it refuses by name in the app's log and libsecret gets an error, never a hang; the display's teardown removes a file an app never asked for), and from there to its sealer over an inherited pipe (`VS_APP_SECRETS_FD` = the fd number). It is never in the BUS env: that env is the environ of dbus-daemon and of every service the bus activates — MEASURED on the .267 shape, the key sat in `/proc/<pid>/environ` of SEVEN processes (the bus, this service, xdg-desktop-portal, -permission-store, -document-portal, at-spi-bus-launcher and the a11y bus's own dbus-daemon) for the display's lifetime, readable by anything of the same uid; measured after, zero. A pipe cannot replace the file here: dbus activation closes every fd above stderr before exec (measured, dbus 1.16.2), while it does pass the daemon's environment on. The app needs no env var: libsecret finds the service by name. ⋯ ▸ Stored logins (n) · Forget all; Settings `desktop.appSecrets` on|off (default on). The passkey store is a separate store. Gates: test-app-display-secrets (fast), test-app-display-secrets-chrome (heavy).

### Desktop apps — a window an agent opens never takes your focus (2.369.254, lane agent-window-no-steal)
A window an AGENT opens — its own desktop-app browser, a second window of that app, the live view its browser start auto-opens — is PLACED, never focused: beside the agent's chat when you are IN that chat (its window is the active one — its split, the chat's frame keeps its place in the stack), on the chat's desktop when it lives on another one (no switch). Anywhere else (lane agent-window-no-pop, inc-mvhebl4n-rkvr) NO window opens and nothing on your desk moves: the chat's taskbar entry carries the badge and its window chip / Agent browser chip opens it. The active window and the caret stay yours; the taskbar entry (the phone's title) pulses once and keeps an accent mark until you go to it. On a phone the shown window is never replaced. Your own launches (Apps "Open", "Browse yourself", "Open its whole desktop") still come to the front. **Setting:** Settings → Desktop apps → "Agent-opened windows come to the front" (`desktop.agentWindowsFront`, default OFF) brings back the old behaviour. PURE verdict `agentWindowPlacement` / `satelliteFocus` in src/lib/desktop-app-placement.js; WM doors `placeBehind` / `markArrived` (src/lib/window.js).

### Desktop apps — one program, one instance (2.369.268, lane app-launch-singleton, fleet inc-mv7hxc2n-2cvr)
An app that RUNS — whoever started it, an agent's too — is OPENED, never started again: its Apps card says 「正在 :2 运行 · 由 agent 会话 X 启动」 (the record's `launchedBy`), its press opens that window (the existing attach path; the POST carries `ifRunning: 'attach'` and the keeper answers the running record `attached: true` — also For you's Open), every live instance is listed under the card with 打开 / 关闭, and 「再开一个」 is offered only for a row that runs twice (`runsTwice`: a browser with its own profile, LibreOffice, a one-process terminal). The Desktop button's popover lists 「正在运行的应用」 (every live app window: where, who, Open, Close). A launch whose app ends within 3 s (`QUICK_EXIT_MS`) is SAID: `quickExit` on the record, its window stays with 「X 刚启动就退出了（code 0）—— 通常是同一程序已在别的显示上运行」 + 「打开在 :2 运行的那个」, ONE server notice, the card's line on the next open, the journal's `exited:` line carries the timing. An installed / witnessed browser of a known family (google-chrome-stable, brave, edge, vivaldi, firefox-esr, librewolf…) launches like the catalog's browser row: its OWN profile dir (never the user's ~/.config/google-chrome — the incident's cause); a browser run through a launcher stays as typed and runs once. The lock fact (Chrome's SingletonLock in the default profile) names the record whose process holds it. PURE: desktop-fit `launchVerdict` (client + server), desktop-apps `appBrowserVerdict` / `runsTwiceVerdict` / `quickExitVerdict` / `quickExitNoticeText`, desktop-browser-app `browserFamilyOf` / `defaultProfileDirOf` / `singletonLockFact`; SHARED desktop-display `profileLockFact`; words src/lib/desktop-app-words.js. Gates: test-app-launch-once (fast), test-desktop-apps, test-desktop-app-window §S (heavy chrome, PNGs).

### Desktop apps — a browser's display that conversations hold: ✕ closes the view, Stop is the person's (lane browser-display-holders, .355)

A2 (the outer ✕ asks the app, a second ✕ within 5 s stops it) is for a USER-held app — no agent lease, no holder. A browser profile's display session (`display-for-browser`, the attach road) carries `holders` from the browser keeper (broadcast on every move); with holders the ✕ is the pane-only close (PURE `outerCloseVerdict` → `why: 'holders'`, before the second-✕ Stop), and the «… press ✕ again within 5 s …» toast never appears. A person's Stop of that display is told to the browser keeper before the teardown: no heal, each holder told once, and the Desktop list's «Running apps» keeps a disabled row «You stopped it · N conversations start it again when they next use it» until a conversation's next command starts it. Details: kb-features «Agent browser — a browser the agents hold is held for its display window too»; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.2 (the holders row).

### Desktop apps — an app that fixes its own window size (lane app-fit-fixed 2.369.204; lane app-window-fit-topleft 2.369.332, B-1f0b)
A window whose app fixes its size (WM_NORMAL_HINTS min = max — WeChat's login, Inkscape's welcome, a GTK dialog) is shown at exactly that size: never scaled, not resizable, no maximize. When that size is LARGER than the workspace in either dimension the window opens at the workspace's top-left (below the toolbar, beside the sidebar) so the most of it shows, and its title bar is held to the workspace's width so its ✕ is always on screen; the rest past the edge is reached with Scale ▸ 1× (measured: the 1000×900 GTK fixture at 2× on an 878 px workspace — 86 CSS px past the bottom at either place; the cascade's x is what the top-left removes). A workspace resize (the sidebar, the browser window) judges it again — this client's placement, never synced to another client; a workspace that fits it again gives its stored place back. On the phone layout the picture scales to fit, as before.

### Desktop apps — one app of a paired Windows machine as a RemoteApp window (rides 2.369.288, lane remoteapp-r1a, design q-024 r1 §1.1–§1.3 — R1a)
The hub runs FreeRDP 3's X client (`xfreerdp`) in RemoteApp (RAIL) mode as an ordinary app on its OWN xpra display — the `remoteapp` row of DISPLAY_BACKENDS (`remote: 'rdp-loopback'`: never a rung for a local app) — connected to the Windows machine's 127.0.0.1:3389 through its agent's loopback forward (the VNC pipe; nothing opened to the LAN). Every remote top-level is an X top-level there, so satellites, window targets and takeover apply unchanged. The password goes ONLY to xfreerdp's stdin (`/from-stdin`, one line, the pipe closed; `/d:` always — without it the line is read as the domain, measured); the certificate is pinned with `/cert:deny,fingerprint:sha256:` and the client gets its own empty config dir (a TOFU certificate stored in ~/.config/freerdp beats the pin — measured). Drives, clipboard, audio, smartcard and extra channels stay off (FORBIDDEN_RDP_ARG_RE, refused by name). One session per machine (rdp_session_busy). The launcher's machine dialog shows «RemoteApp…» beside «Run as its own window…» on a Windows machine; in R1a it answers what the machine still needs (its Windows sign-in + certificate fingerprint — the settings card is R1b). People only: an agent token ⇒ human_only, and the generic launch (POST /api/desktop/apps, the `launch` op) refuses a RemoteApp body (`remoteapp_door`). Why a session ended is read from the client's own words + exit code (rec.rdp.ended). Gates: test-remoteapp, test-remoteapp-token-sinks, test-remoteapp-launch (heavy).

### Desktop apps — the RemoteApp settings card, the sealed sign-in and the certificate pin (rides 2.369.291, lane remoteapp-r1b, design q-024 r1 §1.3–§1.6 — R1b)
- **The card** (src/lib/remoteapp-card.js): a Windows machine's dialog (launcher → the machine) shows «RemoteApp settings…» (never greyed; a launch refused `remoteapp_needs_setup` opens it). Top to bottom: what the machine needs — the facts table read from the machine itself (the `remoteapp-facts` device op, read-only): Windows edition (Home ⇒ 「这台是 Windows Home，没有远程桌面服务；RemoteApp 做不了，「作为独立窗口运行…」（裁剪画面）可用」), Remote Desktop on and answering on 3389 (off ⇒ 「打开 设置 → 系统 → 远程桌面；无需开放防火墙到局域网」), apps allowed as RemoteApps (TSAppAllowList fDisabledAllowList = 1 — else the copyable admin PowerShell line), the graphics card in remote sessions (optional; bEnumerateHWBeforeSW — else 「Blender 这类走软件渲染；要 GPU 请用管理员命令开这条策略」 + its line); «Check again»; an agent too old says the version it has and needs. The fixed console-takeover sentence 「RDP 登录后那台机器的屏幕会显示锁屏；正在它面前用的人会被挤出。适合无人值守的机器」 (no machine name). The Windows sign-in (user, domain, password — sealed on save; the box is cleared, its placeholder says saved). The certificate: 「首次连接」 signs in once with no app and pins what the machine shows; pinned ⇒ 「重新信任」; a launch refused for a changed certificate is said with the same button. Raw strings — the admin commands, the fingerprint, the edition id — sit only in the ONE 技术细节 fold. VibeSpace never runs the admin commands (an HKLM write is the owner's, in an administrator PowerShell there).
- **The sign-in** is the `remoteapp` integration row, ONE record per paired machine (`remoteapp/<hostId>` in data/integrations.json, the password sealed by the store's secret box) — never an Integrations card. A launch and every relaunch read it fresh; the password goes only to xfreerdp's stdin. The pin is the sha256 of the certificate the first connection's `/cert:tofu` stored in its own fresh config dir (taken only when the sign-in succeeded — exit 0); every launch says `/cert:deny,fingerprint:sha256:<pin>`.
- **Fences**: every door of the card and the launch is people-only (an agent token ⇒ 403 human_only — no agent turn can carry the sign-in); one RemoteApp session per machine (a first connection under a live session ⇒ rdp_session_busy); the client's log is scrubbed of password shapes at the session's end (PURE scrubRdpLog); the forward is the hub's 127.0.0.1 listener only.

### Desktop apps — a paired machine's desktop as a low-latency WebRTC stream (lane stream-p1a-transport, design q-041 r2 §2 / §3 P1 part A + P1b — the transport, the player, the input channel; the screen capture is part B)
- **The stats row is ONE component (lane stream-window-fixes)**: src/lib/stream-stats.js — the whole screen's strip and one window's stream mount the same numbers + firewall notice. A page that vanishes without a word is stopped 3 s after its long poll closed (STREAM_LIMITS.goneMs), not at the 30 s idle sweep.
- **The rung** (the `webrtc` row of DISPLAY_BACKENDS — a `remote` row beside the RemoteApp one, off the local ladder; its `needs` = the AGENT's capability `agent:stream-offer`, a fact the hub never probes on PATH): a Windows / macOS machine desktop window (the same window shell as the VNC picture — machine-desktop.js) first asks POST …/machine-desktop/stream/start; desktop-access `streamRung` judges the agent's hello (PURE src/stream-model.js streamRungVerdict: the op, and a SOURCE — the agent's screen once it advertises `stream-screen` (part B), else the instance's fake file `VIBESPACE_STREAM_FAKE_SOURCE`, tests and demos). Not taken (an older agent, no screen source — every real machine until part B) ⇒ the VNC picture at once, no note; the chip's title says «没有串流：…». 
- **The transport**: the agent's werift (bundled into agentd — +2.4 MB) offers ONE H.264 track (constrained baseline 42e01f, packetization-mode 1 — src/stream-h264.js cuts Annex-B into single-NAL / FU-A payloads) + ONE ordered data channel `input`; NACK retransmits, PLI → the source's next key frame, the transport-cc estimate reported (part B's encoder follows it under `maxKbps`). werift runs ICE-LITE with host candidates only and NO STUN/TURN server (its default asks Google's public STUN server even with `iceServers: []` — measured; lite is the off switch); the page is the controlling full agent. The candidates trickle as `stream-ice` pushes; the page's answer / candidates go up through the hub (people only), its long poll (…/stream/watch) brings the agent's candidates, numbers and `ended` down.
- **NAT — direct first, else the hub**: every offer also carries the hub's UDP RELAY (`typ relay`, the lowest priority — ICE takes a direct pair on a LAN / tailnet): the hub's UDP port ⇄ datagrams framed over ONE `tcpForward` on the existing device link ⇄ the agent's loopback shims ⇄ werift (a peer-reflexive 127.0.0.1 peer). Bounded: 4 peers, 1500-byte datagrams, a stalled forward drops (never queues). The strip says «经 hub 中转» when it carries the picture; the record says `path: relay`.
- **The relay paths — the daemon's own UDP leg (lane stream-relay-udp, 2.369.296)**: the owner's Windows firewall blocks every inbound UDP to the agent (default inbound block, no rule for its node.exe, the agent unelevated) ⇒ no direct pair, even for a browser on the same machine; and the relay over the device link carries only what that link carries (measured there: 5 fps / 1.3 Mbps of a 30 fps / 8 Mbps picture). So the hub's relay socket is bound BEFORE the offer and `stream-offer` carries `relayLeg` (its port, a per-session key, the hub's addresses): the DAEMON sends authenticated PINGs from its own UDP socket to that port (at each hub address and the host it dials); the first PONG makes the leg UP and from then on the browser's datagrams and werift's answers ride plain UDP — TURN-shaped, nothing listens on the machine, the firewall lets in the answers to what the agent sent. THE LADDER: direct (host pairs) → the hub relay over the UDP leg → the hub relay over the device link. A PING every 15 s keeps the NAT / firewall state (every 2 s while it carries the picture); THREE PINGs in a row unanswered (2 s each; one late PONG is a lossy leg, not a dead one — lane stream-leg-flap) ⇒ the device link (re-asked 5 s later; a PONG brings it back). The hub ELECTS the path once per session (below). The strip says «经 hub 中转 · UDP» / «经设备链路»; the record: `relay.via` (udp | link) + `relay.leg` (address, pings, forged / replayed / stray drops, the changes) on the hub, `stats.relay.leg` (state, rtt, why) on the agent; a log line at every change. Measured on loopback past a 2 Mbps link stand-in: the leg 30 fps / 8 Mbps with 0 RTP gaps, the device link 7.2 fps with the picture's lag growing 7.5 s in 10 s (it queues).
- **ONE path election per session; a stalled picture comes back by itself (lane stream-leg-flap, 2026-10-20 — the owner's Mac desktop, two displays, went black at «串流 · 2 个显示器 · 0 fps»: the hub had followed whichever path the daemon LAST spoke on and flipped udp leg ⇄ device link three times in 20 s)**: the hub takes the leg ONCE, when it comes up, and leaves it only when it is measured dead — 6 s with no PING flagged UP and no DATA from it while it carried the picture (35 s idle); the device link speaking and a PING not flagged UP are counted (`relay.leg.held` / `quiet`), never obeyed, and the device link's frames always reach the browser. The daemon drops its leg only after three PINGs in a row go unanswered; a socket error is counted (`sendErrors`), never a verdict. A PLAYING picture that decodes nothing for 12 s while the machine says it sends pictures (`stallStep`) ends `stalled`: the window says «串流中断：画面不再传过来——正在重新连接…» and offers the stream again by itself — in ② each pane does, once, then 「重试」 — never «0 fps» for ever.
- **The firewall fact**: after each offer the agent sends a datagram from a second socket of its own to each host address werift offers (Windows' firewall filters that as it filters a browser) ⇒ `stats.directInbound` {verdict: open | blocked | none, program}; while the hub relay carries the picture and the verdict is blocked, the strip says «机器防火墙挡住直连，经 hub 中转» with «复制管理员命令»: the page builds `netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="VibeSpace agent" dir=in action=allow program="<node.exe>" protocol=UDP` from the agent's path (none for a path a shell could act on) — the owner runs it in an administrator prompt; VibeSpace never does.
- **The player**: `<video autoplay playsinline muted>` in the window's pane (object-fit contain); the strip's chip «串流 · RTT · fps» and the numbers «往返 · 抖动 · fps · 解码 · kbps» (getStats once a second — statsOf; lane stream-stats-popup: the numbers ride the chip's title and its details popup); THE STATE MACHINE (streamStep): a sick connection (failed at once, disconnected after 4 s) gets up to 2 CONSECUTIVE ICE restarts (the same session, new credentials), then falls back; the machine ending it (`ended`: stopped / link_lost / ice_failed / idle) falls back at once. Fallback = the VNC picture in the same shell (it signs in then) + the note «串流停了（why）——改为显示 VNC 画面». Phone: the same, full width, the strip one row that scrolls; touch drives the pointer.
- **Input over the data channel (P1b)**: pointer (video pixels → the source's pixel, letterbox aware, + the source's origin on the machine's desktop), wheel (120 a notch), keys as PHYSICAL keys (the DOM `code`; a Mac viewer's ⌘ becomes the machine's Ctrl through THE .287 table — src/lib/stream-input.js is its third door), Ctrl/⌘+V = this computer's clipboard text first, then the V; frame acks (≤ 4 a second) time the picture's way (`ackMs`). The agent feeds THE one injector (src/input-inject.js; the `input-events` op is its twin for a caller with no stream): Windows = a resident PowerShell that compiles SendInput once (absolute over the virtual desktop, scan codes); UIPI stated plainly — before a press it asks whether the window in front is elevated and answers `uipi`, the strip says «Windows 不让输入进管理员窗口——先点一下机器上的别的窗口»; Linux = a recording stub (a file only when VIBESPACE_INPUT_STUB_FILE names one); macOS = input_unsupported (P3).
- **Running the device agent as administrator (lane win-input-elevated, 2.369.327; owner “Windows 上的管理员权限能不能成为默认” — yes, by default)**: the installer registers the logon task at RunLevel Highest BY DEFAULT behind ONE Windows consent (`Start-Process -Verb RunAs` — the person clicks the UAC dialog; the product never elevates silently and never drives the consent UI); a declined consent (or `-NoElevate`, or the pairing dialog’s 「以普通权限安装」) registers it at normal rights and the machine card offers 「Run as administrator…」. The hello-ack reports `elevated` (read live from the daemon’s own token every connection, so it survives a self-upgrade); an old daemon that cannot report it is treated as NOT elevated and never asked to type into an admin window. When the daemon is elevated its SendInput reaches admin windows by the OS’s own rules (UIPI is satisfied — the SENDER is elevated), so the product FENCES it: PURE `injectAllowed({windowClass, elevated, allow})` refuses the UAC consent UI and the secure desktop BY CLASS always (even if an allow-list names them), an optional per-window allow list narrows the rest, and every act injected into an elevated window is one audit line (actor, window class/title, keys/clicks, at). The product writes NO auto-elevation and NO cross-integrity input code — the owner’s one-time task change is the only thing that elevates; the product just reports it and fences it.
- **Lifetime**: a session belongs to the link that asked; a link blip leaves it playing (its media never rode the link) and the reconnect re-arms it; an orphan the hub never re-arms stops after 20 s; the hub stops a session no page polled for 30 s; at most 2 streams per machine. The record (GET …/stream/facts): sid, codec, source, startedAt, state, the agent's last numbers, path.
- **Latency harness**: scripts/probes/stream-glass-to-glass.mjs (a clock page for the machine's screen with a binary band; a viewer snippet that reads the band off each presented frame; `selftest` proves the band) — part B / 主开发 run it on the real machine.

### Desktop apps — the stream's SCREEN source: the paired Windows machine's own desktop (lane stream-p1b-screen, design q-041 r2 §2 采集/映射+编码 + §3 P1; the P0 calibration)
- **What plays**: a Windows agent with `stream-screen` streams its PRIMARY display (an instance that names a fake source keeps the fake — the suites, demos). The agent decides by its own facts (the `stream-facts` op): an SDR display ⇒ the DIRECT road (one ffmpeg: 8-bit DDA → NV12 → the encoder); an HDR display ⇒ the MAPPED road (FP16 DDA's raw bits → the agent's mapping ÷ (SDR white / 80) → sRGB → NV12, in a worker → the encoder). The strip ends «NVENC · 编码 N ms»; the chip's title says «HDR 已在机器上映射（SDR 白点 200 nits）», or «软件编码（没找到硬件编码器）» when only x264 exists.
- **Colour**: exact SDR on an HDR desktop — the owner's calibration patches map exactly (src/stream-plan.js, test-stream-plan; the old 8-bit capture's overexposed greys are its RED control). A highlight brighter than SDR white clips to white by default (8-bit SDR has no code above it); a parametric shoulder (knee, peak) exists for when highlights matter more than exact whites.
- **Windows power throttling** (lane stream-sdr-ecoqos, 2.369.329; B-0485, the owner 2026-10-20 「SDR 路也关」): the agent and its ffmpegs are hidden background processes, so Windows throttles them (EcoQoS: the SDR mapped road measured 3–6 fps at 4K, 19–22 opted out). While a stream runs, every road opts the agent and each of its ffmpegs out (src/stream-plan.js unthrottlePs, the HDR lane's script; same user, no elevation, never a display setting). The agent's opt-out is held by the streams: the last one to end gives it back, a crash included. The stream's details show 「电源限制：关」 (`ecoqos` in the numbers: off / on; a Mac says n/a, no row).
- **ffmpeg on the machine**: ffmpeg ≥ 7 with ddagrab, looked for on PATH, then %LOCALAPPDATA%\vibespace\ffmpeg\bin, then the P0 probe folder; none ⇒ the VNC picture, the chip's title «需要 ffmpeg ≥ 7（含 ddagrab 与 NVENC）——放在机器的 PATH 或 …». Encoders: NVENC → AMF → Quick Sync → x264.
- **Endings, by name**: the capture or the encoder dying, or the display unplugged ⇒ «串流停了（机器的屏幕采集停了）——改为显示 VNC 画面» and the VNC picture. A keyframe request waits for the next GOP key (≤ 2 s); the bitrate follows werift's estimate by restarting the encoder (≥ 5 s apart, ≥ 25 % moves).
- **The real leg**: scripts/probes/stream-screen-real-leg.md (主开发 on the owner's machine: the facts script, the capture + THE mapping exact, the <video> ±2, latency, endings). Part C (a D3D11 shader helper) replaces the CPU mapping.

### Desktop apps — a paired MAC's desktop or one window as the stream (lane stream-p3m-build, design q-041 r3 §1/§3 P3m; the facts: lane stream-p3m-probe)
- **What plays**: a Mac agent with `stream-mac` streams its main display (or a display by id), or ONE window (`source: {kind:'window', id}` on stream/start — needs `stream-window` too; the window shape is the one Windows' single-window lane uses). An older Mac agent (it says stream-screen, cannot capture) ⇒ `agent_too_old`, never asked.
- **The helper**: `~/.vibespace/helpers/vibespace-screen` (+ `.version`, `.state.json`) — ScreenCaptureKit (sRGB: SDR exact, no tone-map, no mapping road) → VideoToolbox H.264 constrained baseline, low-latency rate control, BT.709 / sRGB VUI → FLV (the agent's flvReader). A key is the SAME frame (`key` on stdin); the bitrate follows werift's estimate LIVE (`bps`, ≤ once a second, ≥ 10 %). Sizes: up to 2560×1600 native at 60; a 4K display 2560×1440 at 60 (4K60 is out of reach at low latency), `quality: 'full'` = native at 30. A window = its own pixels (its frame includes the 32 pt title bar).
- **TCC (who is the client)**: the agent spawns the helper `--disclaim`; it re-spawns itself with responsibility disclaimed, so tccd's client is vibespace-screen by path + cdhash — never the agent's node. No grant ⇒ `screen_permission` / input `accessibility_permission` with the Settings pane's link; the strip shows the sentence + «Open System Settings» (copies the link; it opens that pane on the Mac); the next stream start reads the facts again. One disclaimed run per version adds the helper's (off) row so the owner only toggles it. Never a prompt (a background agent cannot).
- **Where it comes from**: built ON the Mac at its first stream when the Command Line Tools exist (both slices at once, lipo, ad-hoc sign — ≈ 5 s on an M4 Pro); otherwise the hub pushes its prebuilt (data/bin/helpers/, from scripts/build-mac-helper.sh / the mac-helper workflow's release assets) over the device link and asks again; neither ⇒ `no_helper` naming both. A new helper version at agent boot replaces an installed one — a granted one is then a new client: `helper_changed_regrant` («turn it off and on») until the facts see the grant.
- **Input**: CGEvent through the helper's `input` — keys as the Mac's virtual key codes, the pointer in global points (the picture's pixels × the source's live scale + origin — a window that moves is followed), a frontmost target at the HID tap, any other app by CGEventPostToPid (not activated) with its streamed window made its key window first (an app's keys land in its key window — measured). Presses keep ≥ 2 ms apart (a burst posted back to back lost all of it — measured).
- **Endings, by name**: window_minimized («restore it to stream» — SCK sends no picture for a minimized window), window_gone, display_gone, screen_permission (the switch turned off mid-stream), encoder_failed, capture_exited.

### Desktop apps — ONE window of a paired Windows machine as a stream (lane stream-p2w-build, design q-041 r3 §1/§3 P2w; the probe: lane stream-p2w-capture-probe)
- **One door for both platforms (int304)**: the start body is the Mac's `source: {kind:'window', id}`, the rung is ONE `want: 'window'` verdict (a Windows agent's or a Mac's `stream-window`; a Mac's also `stream-mac`), the window shape is src/stream-window.js (the Mac's facts become it in src/stream-plan.js windowSourceOf), and «Stream one window…» shows on a Mac too — its picker rows come from the Mac's screen helper. A Windows window minimized is HELD (WGC resumes); a Mac's ENDS `window_minimized` (SCK sends nothing) — each platform keeps what it measured.
- **What it is**: what "share a window" does in a meeting app. The machine's dialog (Remote ▸ the machine) has «Stream one window…» on a Windows machine: a picker of its APPLICATION windows (its agent lists them through the vibespace-wgc helper: visible, not cloaked, not a tool window, no owner, ≥ 64 px, capturable — minimized ones listed and marked; titles are the owner's own windows shown to the owner), a row's «Stream this window» opens it as a `machine-app` window: a WebRTC `<video>` of THAT window only — nothing else of the screen is captured or sent.
- **The helper**: tools/vibespace-wgc/vibespace-wgc.cs (Windows.Graphics.Capture by HWND, C# 5) ships as SOURCE inside the agent (src/agentd/wgc-helper-source.js, generated by scripts/wgc-helper-embed.mjs — the Mac helper's way, int304); the agent builds it with the machine's own .NET Framework csc (every split WinMetadata .winmd + three facades; MinUpdateInterval / borderless defines step down) into %LOCALAPPDATA%\vibespace\helpers\ at the first boot of a version and at first use; a stamp (the source's digest) rebuilds it after an upgrade that changed it. Cannot build ⇒ `helper_missing` with the recipe. Borderless capture is asked (Allowed for an unpackaged exe: no yellow frame on the machine).
- **Colour + road**: BGRA by default — WGC's 8-bit frame of an ordinary window is the exact picture on an HDR display too (99.974 % identical to the mapped FP16) — straight into ffmpeg's BT.709 limited NV12 → the encoder ladder → FLV. The start route's `fp16` (off; no settings row yet — the advanced tier sits at its design ceiling and the road is unmeasured on a real HDR-content window): a window on an HDR display is captured FP16 and mapped by THE table in the agent's worker.
- **Rate + size**: MinUpdateInterval = 1000/fps (33 ms at 30); the helper writes the newest picture at the plan's rate (the last one again while nothing changes; a slow reader drops, never queues); each frame carries its size in a 16-byte head, a size change recreates WGC's pool and restarts the ENCODER at the new size (a key frame). The VibeSpace window follows the source's size: the window's own size on its machine (physical ÷ dpi/96), inside the workspace, aspect kept; its title is the app's.
- **Input**: the stream's own road — the `<video>` sends WINDOW pixels, the agent adds the window's LIVE place (it moves while streamed) and holds a press inside the window; SendInput then lands where the window is visible on its machine, like a person's click there (a covering window takes it).
- **Held, by name (the stream lives on)**: minimized ⇒ a row under the strip — «The window is minimized on … — the stream is paused» + «Restore it» (SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE — never the focus) — shown ONLY while the source says so (src/stream-window.js windowHeldDoor; by style.display — viewers.css's `.file-tool-btn { display: flex }` out-ranks `hidden`, so the old bare button showed at all times; lane stream-window-fixes); a covered Chromium/Electron window that stopped painting ⇒ «… is covered … and stopped drawing». **Ends**: closed ⇒ «“…” closed on …», helper missing / exited, encoder exited — the window says so with «Open its whole desktop» and «Pick a window…». Never minimized, hidden, moved or raised by us.
- **The strip + THE stats row (lane stream-window-fixes)**: the strip says what the window shows, the stream's state (串流 · N ms · N fps; its title the machine's kbps over the window's floor) and «Stop streaming»; under it the SAME stats row as the whole screen's window (src/lib/stream-stats.js over src/stream-model.js streamNumbersOf: RTT · jitter · fps · decode · kbps · the relay path · the encoder + encode ms, and the firewall notice on the hub relay).
- **Stopping, by name (lane stream-window-fixes)**: «Stop streaming» ends it on the machine and leaves the window («Streaming of “…” stopped» + «Stream again» / «Pick a window…»); the picker marks the windows a stream shows now («streaming now», from the hub's sessions — any browser's) with «Stop» (POST …/stream/stop {host, window}); the window's × ends it too. The end's name (closed / stopped / stopped_in_list / viewer_gone) reaches the machine; the window source closes the helper's and ffmpeg's stdin first (the helper releases the window and exits 0), kills after 1 s, and logs one line with both exits. A viewer that vanishes (its tab closed, the browser quit) is stopped by the hub 3 s after its long poll closed unanswered (STREAM_LIMITS.goneMs) — every stream, not only a window's. Measured on a real machine: helper exit 0 in 63 ms, ffmpeg 130 ms; the agent killed outright ⇒ both gone in 410 ms.
- **Titles in any script (lane stream-window-fixes)**: the helper writes ASCII JSON (every character past 0x7E as \uXXXX) through a BOM-less UTF-8 writer — the console's OEM code page (936 on a Chinese Windows) turned CJK titles into U+FFFD and emoji into ??.
- **The rate (lane stream-window-fixes)**: the old rule obeyed werift's estimate at +5 s (the first real use: 300 kbps for a 2698×2078 window, stuck — werift 0.25's estimate counts ~one packet a picture: lane stream-mac-rate below; a correctly fed one spreads p10 6.2 / p50 ~10 / p90 14–17 Mbps around 7.4 sent). Now: a floor by the window's pixels × fps (src/stream-plan.js KBPS_FLOOR — every road's since lane stream-mac-rate: 1000 · 2500 · 4000 · 6000 · 8000 kbps at 30 fps up to 0.3 / 1 / 2.3 / 4.1 MP / larger; ≤ the cap), rateDecision (the median of 2 s of samples vs what the source sent: an echo changes nothing; a shortfall held 2 s steps down, never under the floor; +25 % after 20 s without one) and the intra-refresh wave (NVENC / x264 `-intra-refresh 1` — no periodic IDR, the blurry ↔ sharp pulse; a viewer's PLI restarts the encoder for its key frame). Measured, the same 30 s window: key frames 18 → 2, restarts 5 → 0, still-text PSNR median 29.6 → 45.5 dB.
- **Not yet**: the agent browser's own Chromium windows on the machine still stop painting when covered (the switches `--disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` belong in the machine's own launch, src/browser-serve.js — AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS would replace the config's list); input to a covered or background window (PostMessage) is not built.

### Desktop apps — the POINTER over a machine's picture is the viewer's own (lane stream-cursor, 2.369.305; owner 2026-10-18: the Mac's picture showed no pointer)
- **The rule (Parsec's model)**: the arrow you move over a machine's picture IS the pointer — your browser draws it, with no lag. No source paints the machine's own pointer into the frames: Windows' whole screen (ddagrab `draw_mouse=0`; its default paints it), one Windows window (WGC cursor capture off unless the helper gets `--cursor 1`), a Mac (ScreenCaptureKit `showsCursor` only with the helper's `--cursor`). The agent never passes either flag. The machine's pointer still moves where you point (the input lands there); you just never see a second, lagging arrow under yours.
- **The page**: `.stream-video { cursor: default }` (an inherited `none` never hides your arrow). The VNC rung, when the machine sends no pointer image (none, or a fully transparent one — a Mac's Screen Sharing sent none and painted none, so the picture had no pointer at all), shows your arrow instead of noVNC's `cursor: none` (src/novnc-patch.js `own-pointer` → `vsOwnPointer`; PURE `pointerShown` in src/desktop-screens.js). A machine that sends its pointer's shape keeps that shape as your arrow's look (drawn by the page at the picture's scale — lane win-desktop-cursor-hdr); past 128 px the machine paints it, as before.
- **Words**: the stream chip's title and the one-window view's strip title end with «指针是你的 —— 机器不把它的指针画进画面»; the VNC stats line for the `own` path says «指针是你的 —— 机器没有发来它自己的指针».
- **A Mac's helper**: the change moved its VERSION (its source's sha: vs-4b7bcb1e31e9) — a Mac that had turned Screen Recording on for the previous helper is asked once more (helper_changed_regrant, the strip's existing words).
- **Not yet**: a setting that keeps the machine's own pointer in the picture (a watch-only viewer — the helpers already take `--cursor`, ddagrab `draw_mouse=1`); the machine's pointer SHAPE (I-beam, resize) over the stream — the arrow there is always yours.

### Desktop apps — a Mac's stream: one picture then none, one display, the copied Settings link (lane stream-mac-stall, 2.369.306; owner 2026-10-18 「传了一帧就卡住了」「只有一个屏幕了」「能不能直接在电脑上打开」)
- **The stall (measured on the owner's Mac)**: the helper ran fine (56–58 FLV pictures/s at 1440p60) until the agent's first `bps` (werift's estimate → setTargetKbps, seconds in); the encode loop called VTSessionSetProperty HOLDING its lock, VT waits for the pictures in flight, their callbacks take that lock ⇒ the encoder, SCK's queue and the stats timer parked for good (0 % CPU, no picture, no stats; `sample` showed all four threads on one mutex). Now the rate is set outside the lock (helper vs-054d5cc35456 — a Mac that granted vs-4b7bcb1e31e9 turns Screen Recording on once more). Before/after on the Mac, agent path (stream-host → werift → receiver, rate changes at 4/8/12 s): 182 pictures then none vs 834 over 16 s.
- **The switcher**: a Mac source's offer names the display streamed and the Mac's displays (its helper's facts); over a STREAM the strip's `desktop-strip-displays` lists them left to right (no 全部 — a stream is one display) and a pick restarts the stream with `source: {kind: 'display', id}`. Before, the strip drew the switcher only over the VNC picture.
- **The Settings door**: «Open System Settings» asks the hub (`POST /api/desktop/machine-desktop/settings-open {host, pane}`) → the agent's `settings-open` op (THREE-TOUCH: handler, hello-ack word, the client's gated settingsOpen) → `/usr/bin/open <the pane's deep link>` on the Mac (SP.MAC_SETTINGS by name; measured: exit 0 in 77 ms, no TCC request) — the toast says «已在 <Mac> 上打开系统设置 › 录屏与系统录音». An agent that predates the op is never asked (agent_too_old) and the link is copied, as before.
- **Not yet**: the Mac's bitrate still follows werift's estimate (an echo of what was sent — lane stream-window-fixes' finding for Windows windows); at the 300 kbps floor VT drops pictures at 1440p60 (measured 35–44/s). The window source's floor + median rule should cover the Mac too.

### Desktop apps — THE RATE of every stream: a floor by the picture, an estimate that counts (lane stream-mac-rate, 2.369.310; owner 2026-10-18 「mac画面有了但是压缩的厉害」)
- **What the owner saw (measured on his Mac: 1440p60, the hub's UDP leg, a real Chrome)**: the .309 rule followed werift's estimate (≥ 10 %, once a second): 8000 → 300 kbps at its FIRST estimate (253, 2.2 s in), held 30 s; VT fell to 9–29 pictures/s whenever the screen moved; still blocks vs their sharpest look: PSNR median 30.8 dB (p10 27.4) at 300 vs 38.5 dB (p10 36.2) at 8000.
- **THE ESTIMATE (the cause, every road)**: werift 0.25 notes a sent packet after `await sendRtp` under the transport's CURRENT number — the burst's last — so a picture leaves ONE record (loopback: 14 093 packets, 979 records), and its `packetResults` drops status-vector chunks, adds a phantom per run, renumbers each chunk from the base: ~300 kbps at 30–60 fps whatever is sent (2.3 Mbps sent, nothing lost: 240–390). Now src/agentd/stream-host.js records each packet under ITS header's transport-cc number (a wrapper on the sender's DTLS transport, wired at `connected`) and reads each feedback itself (src/stream-plan.js twccPackets → sendEstimator: min(send, receive) over ≥ 20 packets / ≥ 100 ms). Loopback Chrome: 4.3 Mbps sent ⇒ 4.9–6.4 (werift's: median 41 kbps); a 2 Mbps bottleneck ⇒ 1.9–2.05.
- **THE RATE (one rule, every road)**: src/stream-plan.js KBPS_FLOOR (the window road's table, now every picture's), rateDecision (the median of 2 s vs what was sent: ≥ 0.75 × = an echo, nothing; a shortfall held 2 s steps down, never under the floor; a quiet spell climbs +25 % toward the cap) and rateFollower (the bookkeeping, shared). The roads differ only in step + climb: RATE_RULE (restarting roads — a Windows window, a Windows screen: ≥ 25 % at most every 5 s, climb after 20 s), MAC_RATE_RULE (the Mac's live `bps`: ≥ 10 % once a second, climb after 10 s). A 2560×1440 @ 60 Mac screen: floor 8000 = the default cap ⇒ 8000 throughout.
- **Words**: the whole screen's chip title adds «The machine encodes it at {kbps} kbps — never under {floor} kbps for a screen this size» (a window's already said it).
- **Not yet**: nothing goes UNDER the floor (a link slower than the floor keeps losing — a loss-based step would be the next rung); a LOCKED Mac never starts a capture (ScreenCaptureKit waits, the helper prints nothing, the source waits for its first picture — no end by name); the default cap stays 8000 (the page sends none).

### Desktop apps — HAND a machine's desktop to an agent (lane desktop-handover, 2.369.312; owner 2026-10-19 「把远程桌面的控制权交给 agent」)
- **The door (the owner's)**: while the machine-desktop window's stream plays, the strip shows «Hand to an agent» → a picker of this hub's live agent conversations (one holder) → the strip reads «<agent> is driving · Take back». No agent can ask for it (its verbs answer `desktop_not_handed`, naming this door), none can pass it on; the owner routes are people-only.
- **What the agent does**: `vibespace-window list` shows `md-<hostId>` («A MACHINE'S DESKTOP — handed to you by its owner»); `screenshot md-<host>` = ONE still of the display the window shows (its own pixels; HDR through the stream's mapping), `click --at x,y`, `type "…"` (through the machine's clipboard, like the owner's paste — on Windows the machine's own clipboard text comes back 2 s later, a Mac keeps the agent's text; `--keys` = ASCII keys), `key <chord>`, `scroll`; `detach` hands it back. The SAME records the owner's keyboard and mouse send, into the SAME sink (the stream session's `onInput`). The owner sees the agent's pointer (the labelled arrow, its name).
- **Pause / take back**: any key, click or scroll of the owner's in the window pauses the agent (`window_paused` — never loop) until «Let it continue»; «Take back» ends it; so do closing the window (no window, no hand-over), the stream ending, the machine's agent restarting (`daemon_gone`), the conversation ending (60 s grace). A display switch carries it to the next display (a new screenshot needed).
- **The owner's input PREEMPTS (fix r2)**: on the machine the owner's records never wait behind the agent's — they go first, and one DROPS the agent's unsent records (what the agent held down comes up first: no stuck Shift; its verb answers `window_paused` saying how much went in). One device op carries ≤ 200 records; the hub sends a longer `type --keys` in chunks cut where nothing is held, re-asking the lease between them. Measured: the owner's click 10 ms into a 1500-character type lands 5 ms after it was sent (it waited 6.4 s before). Input during a display switch is said («Switching display — that input did not reach the machine» / 「切换中」, never queued onto the other display) and the next display comes back paused.
- **Fences**: chords that lock / log off / power the machine are refused by name (Win+L, Ctrl+Alt+Del / End; ⌃⌘Q, ⇧⌘Q, ⌥⇧⌘Q); `--at` outside the still; type ≤ 1500 characters; every verb is an audit line (origin `machine`, a type's length only). The user's own Linux desktop (P10 `dw-` rows) still refuses injection by name.
- **Not yet**: a Mac's screenshot (`mac_still_pending` — the helper needs a still verb, which is a new helper version and the owner's Screen Recording switch again; input works now) and its clipboard put-back after the agent's paste (no pasteboard read in the helper yet); the hand-over is not announced into the agent's conversation (the owner tells it in chat; an unasked turn would be billed); a double-click / drag verb.
### Desktop apps — a stream's DETAILS behind ONE summary, pinned to a corner; TRUE full screen with a movable pill (lane stream-stats-popup, 2.369.313; owner 2026-10-19 「做成简单展示，只有点击后才会展开更多细节的 popup … 加入 latency、packet drop、bandwidth 等图表」 + 「全屏模式做成真全屏」)
- **One summary**: both stream windows' strips show the chip alone (串流 · N ms · N fps + a chart glyph); the numbers sentence is its title (hover). The one-window stream's row under its strip is the firewall notice only.
- **The details** (src/lib/stream-stats.js, THE one component): the summary's click opens a createPopover — a table (round trip · jitter · frame rate · decode · received (+ sent) · path · codec · encoder · display · picture size · the machine's rate, floor, estimate · lost / dropped) and three charts over the last 120 s (latency with jitter as a band, packet loss % + dropped-frame marks, received kbps vs the decided rate + floor); hover / tap reads a second. The series is the page's own per-second getStats read (PURE src/stream-series.js — gaps drawn as breaks); nothing new is asked of the agent.
- **Pinned**: 「钉住」 = a small panel in a corner of the picture (top-right first), dragged to another corner, the corner remembered per machine (localStorage `vibespace.streamStatsPin`); it updates each second until the stream ends, the window closes or its ×.
- **True full screen** (src/lib/stream-pill.js): the picture is 100 % of the screen; the strip floats as a pill (grip · summary · 退出全屏 · ⋯ = details, displays, 捕获快捷键) in a remembered corner (`vibespace.streamPill`), hides 3 s after the pointer rests, back on a move; on touch only a tap in its corner wakes it (that tap never reaches the machine). The notices that must not be missed (a Mac's permission switch, the hand-over's words, a refused input) ride the pill and keep it shown. Esc / 「退出全屏」 leave full screen.
### Desktop apps — a machine with several displays: three modes (lane desktop-display-modes, 2.369.312; owner 2026-10-19 「多显示器：每个显示器一个窗口、所有显示器放进一个窗口，或在一个窗口里切换」)

Mapping a 4K frame on the owner's CPU: 25.8 ms whole, 6.3 ms at step 2.

### Desktop apps — a playing stream never drops to the VNC picture by itself; a display is gone only when the facts say so twice (lane stream-fallback-never-silent, 2.369.315; owner incident inc-mvf7z2a3-9sxi 「把 mac 串流成功降级成了 vnc，which should not be possible」)
- **The ladder** (src/stream-model.js endingVerdict, run by src/lib/machine-desktop.js): before a stream's first picture nothing changed (a refusal shows the VNC picture; a replayed window asks first). Once a picture played in the window, an ending is never answered with the VNC picture. The window starts the same display again 1 s later (「串流中断：…——正在重新连接…」, the last picture stays). If the display is gone, it streams the machine's main display once. Then the pane asks 「串流中断：…」 with 「重试」 and 「显示 VNC 画面」; only that press starts the VNC picture. An ending a minute after the last retry starts the ladder again.
- **Gone means gone** (src/stream-plan.js judgeGone, both sources): a capture that died is judged by the machine's facts. display_gone only when two reads that succeeded, ≥ 1 s apart, lack the display. Otherwise the SAME session captures again in place, twice a minute at most (`captureRestarts` in the source's stats), then it ends `capture_interrupted` (「机器的屏幕采集一再中断」). A Mac's helper names every ScreenCaptureKit stop display_gone; measured in the incident as -3805 when a sibling display's capture quit.
- **One session per display**: a ③ switch stops the old session `switched` before the new one starts; ① has one window and one session per display; closing a window stops only its own session.

- **The desktop stream** (the strip — src/lib/stream-mic-strip.js in src/lib/machine-desktop.js, the phone's the same): 「麦克风」 shows once the machine's agent offered the microphone's audio m-line (an older agent offers none — no dead toggle). It is OFF until pressed; a press asks the browser (its own prompt; echo cancellation, noise suppression, gain control, mono) and the track joins the PLAYING stream (no renegotiation). Live = the red dot + where the voice goes: 「你的声音 → 本机应用的麦克风『CABLE Output』」, or 「对方电脑会从扬声器播放你的声音」 with 「安装虚拟麦克风…」 whenever the machine has no virtual microphone (said every time; no default device is changed); a Windows-road machine with no ffmpeg to decode the voice says so instead — 「对方电脑没有 ffmpeg，放不出你的声音——…」 (its receiver's `no_ffmpeg`; lane ci-339-reds). It stops with the window, a lock (the page hidden), a press, its stream's end; a restored window never re-opens it.
- **On the machine** (src/desktop-mic.js): Windows decodes with the stream's ffmpeg and plays into «CABLE Input» (every app that picks «CABLE Output» hears it); a Mac hands the Opus to its own helper (AudioToolbox) and plays into «VibeSpace Microphone» (or BlackHole 2ch). Each OS has its OWN small helper, built on the machine; the screen helper and its permission are untouched.
- **Machines** (the machine's card — showMachineDesktopDialog): one line says the virtual microphone (or that there is none, and the voice plays on its speakers); 「安装虚拟麦克风…」 (Windows: VB-CABLE, donationware from vb-cable.com, one UAC prompt, your default speaker and microphone kept, a restart owed but not needed; Mac: VibeSpace Microphone built on that Mac — or BlackHole 2ch, GPL-3 — behind the administrator password dialog, Core Audio restarts for a second or two); 「设为默认麦克风」 / 「改回」 for apps that only use the default; 「移除虚拟麦克风…」 says what goes away. The plan is shown before anything runs; nothing runs without the person at that machine.
- **Known risk, fixed in the same release** (lane werift-lite-multihomed — the next section): a browser that holds the microphone permission for VibeSpace gathers on every network adapter, and a NEW stream from it to a multi-homed agent did not connect (measured; base reproduces). Both shipped together in 2.369.339; test-desktop-webrtc-chrome ⑱ asserts that such a stream plays.

### Desktop apps — a stream connects whatever adapters the viewer's computer has (lane werift-lite-multihomed, 2.369.339; backlog B-c7d7 — every NEW stream stayed black once the browser was allowed the microphone)
- **Why the microphone matters**: without a media permission Chrome offers ONE mDNS name for a page (the agent never resolves it — `isMdnsCandidate`) and checks from one socket; once the origin holds the microphone permission (a person pressed 「麦克风」 once — Chrome remembers it per origin) it offers EVERY adapter as a host candidate: LAN, Wi-Fi, a VPN, Docker bridges, a tailnet.
- **The agent says it is lite where the browser reads it**: the offer carries ONE `a=ice-lite` at the SESSION level (src/stream-model.js liteSessionSdp — werift 0.25 writes it inside each media section, which no browser reads). Unaware, Chrome took the agent for a full one and nominated pairs before checking them; the lite agent kept the first — on a multi-homed viewer a cross-interface pair whose answers never reached the browser.
- **The agent follows the browser's choice**: it answers every check and SENDS on the pair the browser nominated LAST in this ICE generation (src/agentd/stream-host.js followChoice, on werift's `iceFilterStunResponse` hook; the log says «the browser moved its pair»). Chrome moves its pair as more pairs pass (measured: 0.4 s after the first).
- **Never silent before a picture**: ICE that does not connect within STREAM_LIMITS.connectMs (15 s) is said on the strip — 「串流中断：没能及时连上——正在重新连接…」 — while the view restarts ICE, until a picture plays.
- **Never the fix**: pinning werift to one address, or filtering the browser's candidates at the hub — how many addresses the viewer has is the viewer's fact.

### Desktop apps — the machine's SOUND beside its picture (lane speaker-passthrough-v1, 2.369.340; backlog B-aec9 — the facts: lane stream-audio-probe)
- **The desktop stream** (the strip — src/lib/stream-mic-strip.js `createSoundToggle` in src/lib/machine-desktop.js, the phone's the same): every stream asks the machine for its sound's track; 「声音」 shows once the agent offered it (an older agent, or a machine that cannot send its sound, offers none — no dead toggle). OFF for a machine until the person turns it on, and then REMEMBERED per machine in this browser (`vibespace.streamSound`, the HDR switch's shape); off = the machine captures nothing. The press unmutes the window's <video> IN that click (the browser's autoplay rule) and asks the machine to start (`POST …/stream/sound` → the agent's `stream-audio`); the second press mutes it and the machine's capture ends. Its title says nothing is recorded or stored. A RESTORED window (a reload, a layout replay — `syncId`) never unmutes by itself: it says 「点一下开声音」 until a press, and the machine captures nothing meanwhile. The sound is IN the picture's MediaStream (one msid), so there is one <video>, and Chrome lip-syncs the two by the agent's RTCP sender reports (werift sends one on each track).
- **With the microphone**: the two share ONE audio m-line — sendrecv when both are asked (the viewer's voice goes, the machine's sound comes), no renegotiation for either switch.
- **On the machine**: Windows — the microphone helper's `loopback` verb (WASAPI loopback of the default speaker, AUTOCONVERTPCM 48 kHz float stereo, plus a SILENT render stream on the same endpoint while it runs — without it a quiet machine delivers nothing) → s16le PCM behind a streaming WAV header → the stream's ffmpeg (`-max_size 1920`, libopus 64 kbps, 20 ms) → RTP on a loopback socket of the agent's (the first sender pinned) → the track (src/desktop-sound.js). A default speaker that goes away starts a fresh capture (twice a minute at most). A Mac — the screen helper's OWN SCStream turns `capturesAudio` on (`audio on` on its stdin — no second capture, no new TCC class: it rides 「屏幕与系统录音」); AudioToolbox encodes the Opus; the packets ride the helper's FLV as audio tags beside the pictures; a live switch macOS refuses is answered once by the same capture started again with `--audio`. A Windows window stream carries the whole machine's sound (WASAPI loopback is the endpoint's mix).
- **The rate**: while the sound is on, its ~80 kbps come off the picture's target (src/stream-model.js videoKbpsOf — the estimate counts the picture's packets only); the stats say `audio.videoKbps`.
- **Machines** (the machine's card — showMachineDesktopDialog, `createSoundCard`): a Mac's says 「声音用的是同一个“屏幕与系统录音”授权 · 屏幕助手更新后，macOS 需要你再授权一次」; Windows' says 「声音：Windows 不需要授权」. This release's screen helper is a NEW version (the Swift source changed): a Mac asks the owner to switch Screen & System Audio Recording on once more for it (helper_changed_regrant — the strip names the pane).
- **Not measured here (owner-run, the lane's report)**: the Windows `loopback` verb on a real machine (a tone played there heard in the viewer), the Mac's live `capturesAudio` switch and its AudioToolbox Opus, the re-grant.

### Voice input (Dropline) — 2.369.260 (q-029 P0, docs/design-dropline-voice.zh.md)
- **The plugin** ⚙ → Plugins → «Voice input · Dropline» (`src/plugins/voice-input.js`, `provides:['dictation']`): the key field (secret, `dl_` check), Test = GET /v1/me → «Connected: <name> · <team>», the toggle (refused until a key is saved — OFF by default), the language preference auto | zh | en. **The key tier**: the `dropline` integration row (user key > cluster preset `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATION_DROPLINE_*`); the token lives only in the hub. OAuth + «teach Dropline» are P1.
- **The card's shape** (2.369.262, lane voice-card-polish): header = title + status chip (未连接 / 已连接：{name} · {team} / key 已保存) + the card's own switch; a labelled grid — 账号 (Connect primary, `或粘贴 key ▸` folds the «Dropline key» row: Save + Test on one row, Test only after a save), 语言 (full-width select); then 教 Dropline with its two switch rows (sentence under each). Narrow cards stack (inline-size container).
- **The OAuth tier (P1, 2.369.260)**: «Connect with Fish Audio» on the plugin card opens the consent page in a NEW TAB (scope dropline:api, resource https://api.dropline.fish.audio, PKCE S256); the person allows and types the 6-digit code Fish Audio mails; the hub's callback stores the pair (24 h access, rotating refresh) and the card says «已连接：<name> · <team>» with Disconnect (forgotten here; Fish Audio keeps the grant until removed at fish.audio).
